en: *Continued Lamp: The Orthodox Lineage*, Volume One.
Compiled by the Ancestral Successor Śramaṇa Xingtong of Xichu at Potalaka in Nanhai.
The Linji School.
The Sixteenth Generation Dharma Heir of National Teacher Daokai:
Chan Master Zonggao Dahui Pujue of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture.
He was the son of the Xi family of Xuancheng and possessed [spiritual endowments] from his youth.
He possessed a spirit of vigor. At the age of twelve, he entered a local school. One day, while playing with his classmates, he threw a inkstone at one of them;
by mistake, it struck the master’s hat. He made restitution for the gold and returned home, saying, "For a man of great character, what is the use of reading worldly books?
Why not investigate the supramundane Dharma? He immediately went to Huíyún Monastery on Mount Dōng to serve Huìqí. At seventeen, he shaved his head and received full ordination in the Vinaya.
While casually reading the ancient records of Yunmen, it was as if old habits were being stirred. In the past, I relied upon Chan Master Guangjiao Cheng;

later, I traveled to various regions to follow several elder masters of the Cao-Dong lineage. Having mastered their teachings, I went on to Mount Baofeng to pay my respects to Chan Master Zhantang Zun.
Upon seeing me, the Master marveled at me and had me attend to his robes and sash, pointing out to me the shortcut for entering the Way. My teacher’s spontaneous wit was...

When [Wumen] yielded the hall, Xuedou Chongxian rebuked him, saying, "You have not yet attained awakening; your illness lies in the conceptual understanding of the conscious mind, which constitutes a cognitive obstruction (*jñeyāvaraṇa*).

When Chongxian’s illness grew critical, he instructed the Master, saying, "After I am gone, you should visit Chuan Qin (Qin was Yuanwu); he will surely be able to fully exhaust your potential. Chongxian passed away.
The Master hurried to pay his respects to the Layman Wujin, seeking an inscription for Chongxian’s stupa. Wujin’s gate was lofty and steep, and he rarely [admitted others].
He granted permission. Having attained a single word of accord with the Master, he was invited to stay as a guest. The Master named his hermitage "Miaoxi" (Wondrous Joy).

Later, when he visited again, the Master further instructed him to go see Yuanwu. The Master arrived at Tianning Monastery. One day, he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yunmen:
"What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied, "Water flowing uphill on the Eastern Mountain. If it were...
Tianning was not like this. Suppose someone were to ask, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Tianning would simply say to him: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; within the halls and pavilions, a subtle coolness arises. Under these words, the Master’s past and future suddenly severed;
although the movement of mental phenomena did not arise, he remained seated in a state of pure nakedness. Wuzu said to him, "This was no easy matter."
"You have obtained this field; it is a pity that you died and cannot live again. To have no doubt regarding words and phrases is a great illness. Have you not heard it said:
'Letting go at the precipice, one spontaneously accepts the responsibility; after death, one revives once more—this cannot deceive the Lord.
You must believe that such a principle exists. He then appointed him to reside in the Jue-mu Hall as an attendant who does not manage administrative affairs.
One day, Dayong entered the room of Wuzhuo (who was the place where court officials rested while choosing their trees). Wuzhuo would frequently raise the question, "There is a phrase with no meaning;
it is like a vine leaning against a tree," and ask about it. As soon as Dayong opened his mouth, Wuzhuo would say, "Not so, not so.
After half a year had passed, Dayong finally asked Wuzhuo, "I heard that when you were at Wuzu’s, you once asked this same question. I wonder what Wuzu said."
Moulu laughed and did not answer. The Master said, "The Master ought to have asked this before the assembly at that time;
what harm is there in saying it now? Being unable to refuse, Moulu said, "I once asked: 'What is the meaning of the phrase, "A phrase with no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree"?
The Patriarch replied, "'It cannot be traced, nor can it be painted. Moulu asked again, "'When the tree falls and the vine withers...'"?
"How is it now? the Patriarch asked. Yunwu replied, "I have come along with you. At these words, the Master was immediately relieved and said, "I understand.
Yunwu then cited several karmic causes and conditions to interrogate him; the Master responded without any impediment. Yunwu said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you.

He then composed the *Record of the True Lineage of Linji* and entrusted it to him, appointing him as head of the secretarial office. Before long, he ordered him to share the seat [with the Patriarch] in the meditation hall, where he held the staff.
He used his bamboo staff to test his students; the monastic communities universally accorded him great respect, and his fame resounded throughout the capital.

Prime Minister Lü Shuntú memorialized the throne to grant him the purple robe and the title "Buddha-Sun" (Fírì). During the Jurchen upheaval, their chieftain intended to take several dozen Chan monks as captives;
the Master was among those selected but managed to escape. He traveled to Wú and spent the summer retreat at Hǔqiū, where he devoted himself to reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

When the Bodhisattva ascends to the seventh stage and realizes the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), he thoroughly understands the causes and conditions previously inquired about regarding Zhan Tang’s account of Aṅgulimāla carrying his alms bowl to the house of a woman in childbirth. At that time, Yuanwu was summoned to reside at Yunju;

the Master went there to pay his respects, and on the second day of his arrival at the mountain, he was immediately appointed as the First Seat. At that time, there were many "dragons and elephants" among the assembly.
Yuanwu had long held the position of Seat-Holder (Zuoyuan) and had been waiting for the Master’s arrival, harboring a sense of resentment.

When it came time for the Master to hold the whisk on the winter solstice, Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What is it like when a sword hangs between the eyebrows?
The Master replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven. Yuanwu, from his seat below, gestured with his hand, saying, "Stop, stop! That was a most excellent question, but the answer—"
Even more extraordinary was that Yuan eventually returned to the assembly, and from this point on, the monastic community underwent a transformation.
When Yuanwu returned to Sichuan, the Master established a hermitage at the ancient site of Yunmen behind Mount Yunju to reside there; students gathered like clouds.
After some time, he entered Min Province and built a thatched hut at Yangyu in Changle. Thirteen people who followed him attained the Dharma. He later moved to Yunmen in Xiaoxi.
[The Master] was at Men-an. Later, he accepted the invitation from Chancellor Zhang Wei-gong Xu to Mount Jing-shan. On the day of the opening of the hall, a monk asked:
"The assembly of humans and devas has gathered; the field for selecting Buddhas is opened. The Patriarchal Command is being enacted—how do you proclaim it?

The Master said: "A dull bird flies against the wind. The monk said: "Throughout the entire realm there is no place to seek; clearly, a single point is perfect within the seat. The Master said: "People..."

There is no water that does not flow toward the east. Furthermore, as monks vied with one another to emerge, the Master called them to a halt and said: "Suppose the entire great earth were ground into dust;
suppose each grain of dust possessed a single mouth, and each mouth were endowed with the mark of a broad and long tongue free from all obstruction;
suppose from each tongue issued immeasurable varieties of sounds, and from each sound were produced immeasurable varieties of speech."
Regarding "phrases": each and every phrase contains immeasurable varieties of wondrous meanings.
Suppose as many monks as there are motes of dust in the above-mentioned realms were each to possess such mouths, such tongues, such voices, such phrases, and such wondrous meanings;

and suppose they were simultaneously to pose hundreds of thousands of difficult questions, each question distinct from the others—all at once, they would not even require a single cough from the Elder to resolve them. At that very moment—
The answer was given. Taking advantage of that moment, within that interval, he performed immeasurable and boundless, vast Buddha-works.

Each and every Buddha-work pervaded the entire Dharma-realm; that is to say, a single hair manifested spiritual transformations, and all Buddhas simultaneously preached the sutras, such that even after immeasurable eons, one could not reach their limit.
To proceed in this manner is acceptable for those who merely seek to stir up a bustling courtyard, but when viewed with the True Eye— [The text concludes here.]
Come! This is precisely the state where karmic consciousness is vast and empty, having no fundamental basis to rely upon. Within the gate of the Patriarchs, not even a single point is of use;
how much less so are these pedantic phrases and thorny sentences, or the flaunting of verbal acumen?

Not only do they bury the ancestral vehicle of the past, but they also break open the nostrils of the monks. Therefore it is said: "A thought tied to a hair’s breadth is the karmic cause for the three realms of suffering. A mere flicker—

Sentiments arise; ten thousand kalpas of bondage ensue. Holy names and common titles are all but empty sounds; extraordinary features and inferior forms are all illusory colors. If you seek them, will you not be burdened?
And when you grow weary of them, they again become a great affliction. Observe how the former sages issued such warnings:
they were like the weapons of a state, used only when there was no other choice. This is the fundamental matter.
Above, there is likewise no such news. Today, this mountain monk’s proclamation is much like speaking a dream while dreaming;
it is like gouging a sore on healthy flesh. When scrutinized, I deserve a blow of the staff. Is there anyone here now who can bring down that lethal hand?
If there is, you will be worthy of repaying unrequited kindness and assisting in the transformation of non-action. If not, then [it is as follows].
"By practicing this, one causes [delusions] to depart. He suddenly seized his staff and said, "Holding the Mo-he sword crosswise, I issue the full decree;

throughout the realm of Great Peace, I slay the foolish and stubborn. He struck the ground with the staff, gave a shout, and immediately descended from the seat. The prosperity of his Dharma was unsurpassed in his time;
his assembly numbered over two thousand, all of whom were eminent talents from every quarter. Even Zhang Gong Jiucheng, the Minister of the Board of Civil Office, followed him as a disciple.
He attained a clear and sudden realization. One day, as a result of discussing state affairs, he incurred trouble along with the Master.
In the fifth month of the *Xinyou* year of the Shaoxing era, he surrendered his monastic certificate and lived in seclusion in Hengyang.

There, he compiled the recorded sayings of former virtuous masters, interspersing them with his own comments and critiques, dividing them into three volumes titled *The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye*. After ten years, he moved to Mei Yang; five years later, Emperor Gaozong...

By the Emperor’s special grace, he was released and returned home. In the spring of the following year, he donned the *saṃghāṭī* robe once more; though invitations arrived from all quarters for him to occupy vacant seats, he generally did not accept them.

Later, he received an imperial decree to reside at Yuyang Monastery. After more than a year, an edict was issued appointing him to Mount Jing. As before, both monastics and laypeople looked up to him with admiration.
When Emperor Xiaozong was still the Prince of Puan, he dispatched an inner palace supervisor to enter the mountains to pay his respects to the Master.

The Master composed a verse as an offering. While residing at the imperial residence, he was again dispatched by the Inner Chamber Guest Officer to the mountain to provide offerings for five hundred arhats and to request the Master to preach the Dharma in order to pray for the longevity of the Emperor.
The Emperor personally inscribed the three characters "Miaoxi An" (Wondrous Joy Hermitage) and composed a eulogy to honor and send them.
He ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive..."
The principle is self-evident. He raises his whisk and asks, "Do you see it? He strikes the meditation seat and asks, "Do you hear it?
Hearing and seeing are distinct and clear; what is this? If you can grasp it here, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will both be fully repaid at once.
If not, Jingshan shall unravel the tangle for you. Again, he raises the whisk and says, "Look!"

Look! The World-Honored One Amitāyus, upon the tip of the whisk at Mount Jing, emits a great radiance that illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable, yet again unspeakable, Buddha-fields, turning the Great Wheel of Dharma therein.

They perform immeasurable, boundless, and vast Buddha-works. Within them, whether ordinary or noble, correct or deviant, grass or wood, sentient or insentient—whosoever encounters this light shall all attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
It is for this reason that the Buddhas attain it therein and become endowed with the knowledge of all modes; it is therein that the great Bodhisattvas attain it.

The accomplishment of the various *pāramitās*—this is attained here by the *pratyekabuddhas* and solitary awakeners (*viviktajñānas*). Emerging into worlds devoid of Buddhas, they manifest supernatural powers and radiance;
this is attained here by the assembly of *śrāvakas*, including the five hundred *arhats* who came at night to offer their invitation.

Attaining the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) and being endowed with the six supernormal knowledges (*ṣaḍabhijñā*)—this is attained here by devas and humans. Increasing the ten wholesome paths of action and practicing...
At this point, Rāhu attains it and eliminates his arrogance; the denizens of hell attain it and instantly leap over the ten stages (*bhūmi*);
hungry ghosts, animals, and all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and nine categories attain it here according to their respective faculties and natures.

Each received their respective enjoyments. The World-Honored One Amitāyus, having emitted great rays of light and completed all Buddha-works, then poured the waters of the four great oceans upon the crown of the head of the World-Honored One Maitreya, bestowing upon him the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
He shall act as the successor and perform great Buddha-works. The World-Honored One Amitāyus possesses such [qualities].
With such supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), such mastery, and such majestic spiritual authority, having arrived at this place—does anyone here know how to recognize kindness and repay it?
If there is such a person, come forth and meet with Jingshan; I shall bear witness for you. If there is none, listen to this verse:
"The entire Dharma-realm reaches the mouth of the person of realization; all that exists within the Dharma-realm is his tongue. Relying solely upon this mouth..."
I offer my tongue to you. May your sacred life be uninterrupted; may the fountain of your blessings flow for ten million years, as vast and unfailing as the surging ocean.

From within the lion’s den shall emerge the *sūmari* cub; from the Crimson Mountain cave, the phoenix shall surely appear. As auspicious omens, they shall pervade the nine realms, bringing joy to all plants, trees, insects, and creatures. I bow my head in reverence to this inconceivable marvel. Thus it is said: [The original Chinese text provided is a poetic prose fragment. A literal translation of the full passage is: "I offer my tongue. I pray that Your Majesty’s holy life be without end. For ten million years, may the source of your fortune flow forth; like the vast, surging sea, may it never be exhausted. Within the Lion’s Den, the *sūmari* (lion cub) is born;

the phoenix shall surely emerge from the Crimson Mountain cave. As auspicious portents, they spread throughout the nine directions; grasses, trees, insects, and animals all rejoice. I prostrate myself before this inconceivable event. [Note: The final character "喻" (*yù*) indicates that the preceding text is a metaphorical or illustrative verse.]
Like the myriad stars bowing to the bright moon, I now proclaim these wondrous verses. This is the true teaching within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). [Ascending the hall: The Patriarch said:
"When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault. When there is no fault, there are no dharmas; when there is no arising, there is no mind.

The capacity [of the mind] perishes along with the objects; the objects sink along with the capacity. Objects are objects because of the capacity; the capacity is the capacity because of the objects. Great and small...
The Patriarch, however, held the views of a Dharma Master. Jingshan is not like that: the eye cannot see itself;

a blade cannot cut itself. Eating food relieves hunger; drinking water quenches thirst. Linji and Deshan have needlessly become lost in confusion, wasting their spirit on the bestowing of blows and shouts.
Set aside the blows, cast away the shouts—how can you stop this fellow Meng? [He] ascended the hall and said:
He held up his staff, struck once, and gave a shout, saying: "Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout—today I shall take them up again for you.
How high is heaven? How vast is earth? Do not add further rags to the heap of refuse. Change your bones and wash out your entrails;
then, Jingshan steps back three paces and allows you all to deliberate. But tell me, what is it?"
"How shall one deliberate upon this? He threw down his staff, gave a shout, and said: "With rouge and powder, it is easy to become a beautiful woman;
without money, it is difficult to be a fine gentleman. Ascending the hall, he said: "On the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the first month, at Shuangjing, gongs are struck and drums are beaten.
If you wish to recognize the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, look at the village songs and communal dances. Ascending the hall again, he said: "It has rained for a long time..."
Clear skies. The heavens and earth are wide open and pure. As for the matters within the Gate of the Patriarchs, what need is there to present them further?

Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Chan Master Yuan Tongxiu, who addressed the assembly, saying: "Sitting in cold seclusion at Shaolin for nine years, one was nonetheless seen through by Shen Guang."
Now, jade and stone are difficult to distinguish; one can only wrap them in hemp and paper.

This one, that one, and yet another—if it were a person with clear eyes, what need would there be for further explanation? Today at Jing Mountain, I cannot help but continue the "dog's tail" after the "marten’s fur.
There is something here as well: the Old Barbarian fell into a trap of words for nine years; it is a pity he let it pass then, which led to this silence.
The followers of Zhao sit in meditation for years within the ghost cave—this one, that one, and yet another.

Although he has spoken with bitter and earnest admonitions, it is like the wind passing over the treetops. Upon ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat, he said: "Mañjuśrī dwelt in retreat in three places;
Master Zhi was no idle monk. Even Kāśyapa, wishing to exercise his rightful authority, could not avoid seeing ghosts before his very eyes."
Now tell me: what is the business at the gate of Jingshan today? After descending from his seat, everyone should perform three prostrations with the head touching the ground.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Is there? Is there? The Hermitage Master held up his fist. "Is this truly so, or not?
The Master immediately descended from his seat and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. Ascending the hall again, [the Master said]: "The mud ox beneath the water chews raw iron; Kāśyapa..."
Bhadrapāla bit his tongue; the Sea God, enraged, brandished a coral whip; Sumerudīparāja suffered pain that pierced to the marrow. Entering the hall, he said:

"It is just the Mid-Autumn Festival of the eighth month, and already it is the fifteenth of the ninth month. He struck the ground with his staff and said: "Only this does not migrate. Throwing down the staff, he said:
"The entire assembly has heard it with their ears and seen it with their eyes. Entering the hall, he said: "He breaks through the azure..."
A thousand-foot pine tree falls; the waters of the red dust are cut off in a single stream. Not knowing his original true face, one might think someone else has composed a poem for Deqiao.
He ascended the hall and said: "Last year, on the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month, there was such a message."
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month this year, there is no such news; yet there is such news. This is a matter concerning each of you;
Mount Jing does not participate in it. That there is no such news is a matter concerning Mount Jing; you all have no share in it.
Suppose someone were to ask Mount Jing, "I wonder what kind of news this is? He would suddenly pick up his staff and say:
Do not touch it; if you touch it, I shall break your donkey’s waist. (He throws down his staff and descends from the seat. On the first day of the year, he ascends the hall.
Holding up his staff, he makes the gesture of writing characters in the air and says: "On this auspicious morning, as one grasps the brush, all matters are auspicious.

May blessings be received in accordance with the season; may there be no occasion for celebration that is not appropriate. If one were to propagate this according to worldly truth, one would fall flat on the ground. Furthermore, regarding the Buddha...
While discussing the Dharma, his eyebrows and beard fell out. Zuo struck his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "Buying iron, one obtains true gold;
seeking rain, one receives auspicious snow. The five peaks are carved from jade; a thousand trees are laden with silver blossoms. The Dragon King sends down auspiciousness."
Samantabhadra presents his own ugliness and clumsiness. The secret gate of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time is today, all at once, completely leaked out.
Even so, there is one point here that is suspicious. Tell me, what is it that you doubt? I fear that after the sun rises, [it will be too late].
A momentary lapse. He ascends the hall, takes up his staff, and strikes it once. He calls to the assembly, saying, "Do you hear?
He then raises it and says, "The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara has arrived! He is here upon the tip of the staff at Mount Jing, speaking incessantly:
'All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they are the law of arising and ceasing. When arising and ceasing are extinguished, quiescent extinction manifests. He sets the staff down.
Mount Sumeru upon the palm of one’s hand; swinging on a swing within the eye of a needle.
Even if you were to see through it in such a manner, you would still be ten thousand eight thousand leagues away from the staff. But tell me, what is so extraordinary about the staff of Jingshan?
Throwing it down, he said: "It is not worth half a penny. Ascending the hall, he said: "Jingshan has not a single inch of land."

The Field. This summer, I have arranged for the community’s needs as circumstances required. Too weary to discourse on the Way, too indolent to talk of Chan; with my staff, I have brought everything to completion.
There is no need to stifle the mind or eliminate delusive thoughts; everyone simply eats their fill and then sleeps. As for dozing off, that is certainly not lacking.
"What if, as in a dream, someone comes to collect the price for rice? How would you deal with that? "Vaguely like a melody just barely worth hearing, it is again blown by the wind into another tune.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When inverted thoughts arise, birth and death continue; when inverted thoughts cease, birth and death are cut off.
Where birth and death are cut off, nirvana is empty. Where nirvana is empty, it is but a speck of dust in the eye. Nirvana..."
Since it is empty, what do you call "eye-impurity"? White clouds may briefly appear over the green peaks, but the bright moon cannot be made to descend from the azure sky.
Ascending the hall, he said: "First moon arises: the Iron-Wheel Emperor issues his decree throughout the realm. Second moon arises:
Fenggan rides a tiger into the bustling marketplace. Third moon arises: within the eye of a gnat, a giant turtle overturns the sea. Suddenly, he seized his staff.
He said, "Is there anyone who lives and dies together with me? Come forth and meet with the staff of Jingshan.
After a long silence, he said, "If one sees what is right and does not act upon it, how can they be called brave? He then threw down the staff. Ascending the hall, he said:
"When the mind arises, phenomena cease; when the nature manifests, emotions vanish. If you awaken here, how could it be difficult to subdue the strange? (Holding up his whisk, he said:)"
Look! Avalokiteśvara, Maitreya, Samantabhadra, and Mañjuśrī—all gather their heads together at the tip of the whisk of Mount Jing to spin their webs of sophistry.
If you let them loose, let their mouths grow weary and their tongues boil over; if you hold them fast, not even a single blow is required.
(With the whisk, he strikes the meditation seat. He descends from the seat. Entering the hall, he says: An ancient said, "Once one thing is understood, ten thousand matters are settled."
[The discourse] is finished. This morning is the first day of the ninth month. How do you all fare? [The Master] suddenly picks up his staff and says:
"You must not call it a 'staff. Just understand it well. Since you do not call it a staff, how do you fare?
He cast [the incense] down and said: "To miss by a hair's breadth is to lose by a thousand miles. On the anniversary of National Teacher Yuanwu’s death, the Master held up the incense and said:

"This venerable one was in his lifetime stubborn and upright, his spirit overwhelming all quarters. He displayed an overbearing, reckless boldness and employed a straightforwardness that transcended conventional boundaries.
He himself declared: 'I shall trade my wooden prayer beads for the eyes of everyone in the world. Yet he was not at all..."
It is known that an unfilial son will soon be bound with a rope through his nostrils.
Since the end of the rope is already in the hands of Jingshan, whether he is made to live or made to die depends entirely on Jingshan. Now tell me: how would you say it?
"What is the proof? he asked. He then burned incense and said, "This shall serve as the proof. A monk asked, "When Bodhidharma came from the West, what did he transmit?
The Master said, "One must not take everything as the view of a wild fox spirit. The monk asked, "What is the coarse entering the subtle?
The Master said, "A single pore within the ocean of fragrant waters. The monk asked, "What is the subtle entering the coarse? The Master said, "One..."
The Fragrant Water-Ocean within the Pores. [Question: "How is it before an ancient mirror has been polished? [Master: "Fire is not dependent on the sun to be hot.
[Question: "How is it after it has been polished? [Master: "Wind is not dependent on the moon to be cool. [Question:
"How is it at the time of being polished and at the time of not being polished? [Master: "Intersecting. [Question: "Who is the one who does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?"
“When I tell you that you must first swallow up the waters of the West River in a single gulp, then I will speak to you.
“What do you mean by this? The Master said, “Nailing it down with a nail and gluing it with glue. He asked, “If there is even one dharma, Vairocana falls into the state of an ordinary person;
if there are no ten thousand dharmas, Samantabhadra loses his realm. Apart from these two paths, I pray that the Master will speak quickly. The Master said, “A shell-shedding turtle flies away.”
[The Master] ascended to heaven. [A monk] asked: "When one bows high to Śākyamuni but does not bow to Maitreya, what is it like? The Master said: "To be wide awake within a dream. [The monk] asked:
"Does a person of great cultivation still fall under the sway of cause and effect? Baizhang of former times said: "He does not fall under cause and effect. [The monk asked:
"If so, why did he fall into the body of a wild fox? The Master said: "Whenever you meet someone, simply speak of it in this way. [The monk] said: "But as for that very point—"
Later, Baizhang said, "Dao does not obscure cause and effect. Why did he shed his wild fox body? The Master said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply speak thus.
[The monk] asked, "If someone were to ask Jingshan, 'Does a person of great cultivation still fall under the sway of cause and effect?
I wonder, what would you say to him? The Master said, "I would tell you: whenever you meet someone, simply speak thus."
[The Master] raised his staff and asked: "When the bright side comes, what then? The Master said: "The head is large, the tail is thin. [The monk] asked:
"When the dark side comes, what then? The Master said: "Wild horses neigh in the wind, their hooves clattering. [The monk] asked: "Tomorrow there is a meal at the Great Compassion Hall;
how about that? The Master said: "Xuefeng has already spoken. [The monk] asked: "The past mind cannot be apprehended. The present..."
"The present mind cannot be apprehended. When the future mind cannot be apprehended, what then? The Master said, "The words of a parent come from the parent’s own mouth.
[The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand how one should receive and uphold this. The Master said, "Simply receive and uphold it in this way; you will certainly not be deceived."
Question: "In our school there are no words or phrases; when in reality not a single dharma is given to anyone, what then? The Master said: "Five-flavored porridge for a weight-measuring hammer.
Question: "When both mind and Buddha are forgotten, what then? The Master said: "An old woman selling fans shielding her eyes from the sun with her hand."
Question: "The teachings speak of it at every speck of dust and in every world-system, without interruption. I wonder, what serves as the tongue for this?
The Master struck the right corner of the meditation seat once. The monk said: "The World-Honored One spoke of non-speaking; Kāśyapa heard of non-hearing.
The Master struck the left corner of the meditation seat once. The monk said: "I know that today’s command has not been issued in vain. The Master [nodded].
[The Master] said, "Discernment is very good at distinguishing between good and evil. In the master’s room, he asked a monk, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
How do you understand this? The monk said, "I understand. The master said, "Your understanding brings down the seven generations of ancestors in your household.
The monk then gave a shout. The master said, "Just now you said 'I understand,' and now you shout; what does this have to do with 'it is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing'?"
"What is it? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him out. The monk then requested further instruction on the dialogue concerning the realm of Jia Shan.

Before he had even finished speaking, the Master let out a shout. The monk stood dazed. The Master asked, "What were you asking? As the monk prepared to speak, the Master struck him repeatedly and shouted him out.
As soon as the Master saw a monk enter, he said, "It is not so; get out! The monk immediately left.
The Master said, "A man of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words. Then another monk entered. The Master again said, "It is not so;
get out! The monk, however, stepped forward. The Master said, "I told you it was not so; what more do you seek by coming closer? He then struck him out. Again—
A monk entered and said, "The two monks who were here just now did not understand the Master's meaning. The Master lowered his head and let out a single sigh;
the monk was at a loss. The Master struck him and said, "In fact, it is you who have understood my meaning.
He then asked the monk, "The other day I had a question for you, and you answered me the day before yesterday. Why are you nodding off now? The monk— [remained silent].
The Master said, "So it is, so it is. The monk asked, "What do you say? The Master said, "What? The monk said, "It is not so, it is not so.

The Master struck him twice with his staff, saying, "One blow strikes you for saying 'so'; one blow strikes you for saying 'not so'. He then raised his bamboo stick and asked the monk, "To call this a bamboo stick is to encounter it;
not to call it a bamboo stick is to turn away from it. You may not offer a word; you may not remain silent."
[The Master] was silent. "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk said, "I ask the Master to set down his bamboo staff, and then I will speak to you.
The Master set down the bamboo staff. The monk shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "Attendant, recognize this monk!"

Again, he raised the matter and questioned the monk. The monk said, "Are you afraid the turtle will escape from the jar? The Master stepped down from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Tell me quickly, who said that?
The monk said, "Truly, I did not dare deceive the Master. This was what Zen Master Zhuan-an instructed me to say.
The Master struck him several times with his staff and said, "Make this clear to all quarters! The Master then departed.
In his advanced years, he sought to retire from public life. In the spring of the *Xinsi* year, he received imperial permission to withdraw and reside at the Moonlight Hall (*Mingyuetang*).
In the first year of the *Longxing* era, one night a star fell to the west of the temple, its radiance brilliant and intense. Shortly thereafter, the Master manifested a slight ailment.

On the ninth day of the eighth month, when his disciples came to inquire after his health, the Master exhorted them to propagate the Way. He then said slowly, "I shall set out tomorrow. At the fifth watch of the night, he personally wrote his final testament.
He also sent a letter of farewell to the Layman Ziyuan. When his attendant monk Liaoxian requested a verse, he wrote it out in large characters:
"In life, it is just so; in death, it is just so. What difference does it make whether there is a verse or not? He then threw down his brush and passed away peacefully.
At dawn, a snake about a foot long with a white waist and head was found coiled upon the railing of the Dragon King Well.
The one dressed in monastic robes was, in fact, a manifestation of the Dragon King. The fourfold assembly wailed in grief, and when the Emperor heard of this, he sighed with deep regret.

He composed a eulogy for the Master’s portrait, which reads: "Arising and ceasing, yet not ceasing; eternally abiding, yet not abiding. Perfect enlightenment is empty and luminous, manifesting according to the objects it encounters.
Following the Prime Minister, successive officials arrived to present offerings. His disciples enshrined his entire body within the pagoda at Mingyue.

Beside the hall, he lived for seventy-five years in winter and fifty-eight in summer. By imperial decree, the Mingyue Hall was designated as Miaoxi Hermitage, and he was posthumously granted the title Pujue.
His stupa was named Baoguang. At the beginning of the Chunxi era, his complete recorded sayings in eighty fascicles were bestowed upon him.
This circulated within the Great Canon.
Chan Master Shao Long of Huqiu, Suzhou Prefecture, was a native of Hanshan in Hezhou. At the age of nine, he took leave of his family to rely upon Fohui Monastery.
More than six years later, he received the tonsure and full ordination. Another five years passed before he traveled to Hefei to pay his respects to Chan Master Xing of Changlu.

Having grasped the general outline [of the teachings], a transmission of Yuanwu’s words reached him. Upon reading them, the Master sighed and said, "It is like imagining the juice of fermented vinegar;

though it has not yet moistened my intestines or bathed my stomach, it nonetheless brings a sense of joy and exhilaration to the person. Thereupon, he followed Zantang at Baofeng, stayed as a guest at Huanglong, and questioned Sishin.
Subsequently, he visited Yuanwu. One day, during a private interview, Yuanwu asked, "At the moment of seeing the Seer, the Seer..."
"It is not seeing. Even seeing is already free from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. Raising his fist, he asked, "Do you see it?
The Master said, "I see. Wuzu said, "This is placing a head on top of a head. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization. Wuzu rebuked him, saying, "What have you seen?
The Master replied, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through. Wuzu approved him and subsequently appointed him to oversee the library. Someone asked Wuzu:

"Master Long, you are so gentle and yielding; what can you possibly accomplish? Wuzu replied, "He is but a dozing tiger. Later, he returned to his home district and resided at Kaisheng Temple west of the city.

During the disturbances of the Jianyan era, he built a thatched hut at the foot of Mount Tongfeng. The Prefectural Governor invited him to reside at Zhangjiao Temple, and subsequently he moved to Huqiu.
His Way became widely renowned. One day, ascending the hall, a monk asked: "What is the one phrase for opening the hall for the sake of the nation?"
"How would you say it? the Master asked. The monk replied, "First, I pray for the Emperor’s ten-thousand-year reign; second, I pray for the officials’ thousand-year prosperity.
The Master said, "As for the time before the Buddha was born, where did that one stroke fall?
The monk said, "In that case, I shall wave my hands and leave Chang'an. The Master said, "Do not misrepresent it when you meet people."
The monk said, "What can be done about what is right before one's eyes? The Master said, "One who understands the Dharma is afraid.
The monk said, "The official will not allow even a needle; how is it when one privately poses a question? The Master said, "Seizing the tiger’s head and grasping its tail.
The monk said, "As for the matter in between, how is it? The Master said, "A fellow bound by his own straw rope. The monk said, "Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on this long ago, continuing until—"
"Even now, one does not obtain the wondrous. The Master said, "How many times have you traveled the paths beneath the cliffs, yet failed to see the white-haired man?
He then continued, "O assembly, I originally had no mind to seek anything. Now this great treasure of the Dharma King has arrived spontaneously.
I dare ask you, sirs: how would you describe this great treasure of the Dharma King? Raising his whisk, he asked, "Do you see it?"
If one can discern this here, then the Buddhas of the three periods have used it to receive beings and benefit living creatures;
the patriarchs of successive generations have used it to transmit the true pulse; and the elder monks of the world have used it to reveal the orthodox eye at the crown of the head.

It pierces the dust and hits the mark; its glorious legacy endures for ten thousand ages. Pervading the realm and filling all space, the true wind does not fall; it is like the sky covering all universally. Like...

The earth universally upholds [this land], capable of repaying the unrepayable debt of grace and assisting in the transformation of non-action (*wuwei*). Its profound radiance is crystal clear throughout the ten voids;
the sun of Yao and the sun of the Buddha increase in brilliance together, while the Golden Wheel and the Dharma Wheel turn in tandem.

Bringing forth the ordinary and nurturing the sage, it takes the three realms as its home; benefiting oneself and others, it serves as the refuge for the four types of birth. It responds to conditions as they arise...

All things arise through no other cause than this. It is like a mirror set upon a stand: whatever is raised before it, there is nothing it does not reflect. The great manifests within the small; the small manifests within the great.
In its unfolding and rolling up, it establishes heaven and earth beyond the square realm; in its vertical and horizontal extension, it hangs the sun and moon within the domain.

Even such a proclamation still falls within the bounds of the present age. Have you not seen the Way of Changsha? "The Buddhas of the three periods, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, are entirely..."
Mahāprajñā: When the light has not yet been emitted, there is as yet no news of Buddhas or sentient beings.
Just as when the light has not yet been emitted, where do people find their understanding? Even if one were to attain awakening within this very state, one cannot avoid tripping over level ground.
Furthermore, regarding the phrase "establishing one's home and enjoying one's livelihood," how would you say it? When the smoke of war is swept away entirely.
Ten thousand regions celebrate the Great Peace. Again, [the Master] raised the case of King Aśoka questioning the Venerable Piṇḍola:
"I have heard that you, O Venerable One, personally saw the Buddha come. Is this so or not? The Venerable One raised his eyebrows with both hands, and after a long while, said: "Do you understand?"
The King said, “I do not understand. The Venerable One said, “The Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal;
I was also included among those invited. The Master said, “Pinṭuluo attained great capacity and manifested great function; he did not deceive us by claiming to have personally seen the Buddha.
Nevertheless, we owe it to King Aśoka that he let him off. Had he not let him off, he would have been struck until his eyebrows were lost. Let us set aside for now the matter of letting him off.”
The Venerable One raised his eyebrows. Again, how is it? Do you understand? A single mirror upon the dais is as bright as the sun;
throughout the eternal clear sky, there is no room for right or wrong. Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "What is the meaning of the ninety-day restriction of the feet?
The Master said: "When principle prevails, one follows it. The monk asked: "As for those whose six sense organs are incomplete, can they also observe this restriction? The Master—
[The Master] said, "It passes right through the nostrils. The monk said, "Today this student has encountered something great while coming out small.

The Master said, "A surrendered general is not executed. The monk said, "In that case, the Master is letting me go as I please. The Master said, "Letting prisoners stay only increases their cleverness.
He then said, "The season of bright red begins; the first days of summer have arrived. The eminent practitioners of the four seas have ceased shaking their golden staffs. His mind—
The monkey has suddenly come to rest; the horse of the mind ceases its march. His precepts are as pure as pearls in the vast ocean; his nature is as bright as the moon in the azure sky.
Not a speck of dust can stain him; the Indra’s net reflects light upon light. Transcending forms and extinguishing names, the true mechanism is revealed alone. At this very moment—

Regarding the *an-gu* (summer retreat), how do you speak this single phrase? Who would have known that the events of that year on Vulture Peak remain as vivid as ever, with a single thought turning the light back upon itself?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The doors and windows are flung wide open; ten thousand miles away, not a single cloud hangs.

The bright sun soars into the sky; looking around, a pure breeze fills the seats. The lake’s light is vast and boundless; the wild landscape is clear and luminous. The myriad phenomena of the universe are fully revealed within the ocean."
Seal! Thus one attains wondrous function in every instance and the true mechanism in every thing; mind and environment are as one, and not even a speck of dust can stand.
At this very moment, ten thousand functions cease, and the thousand sages have nothing to carry. One sits firmly atop the crown of Vairocana and pays no heed to Śākyamuni;
one regards the Śrāvakas as maidservants and calls the Bodhisattvas slaves. Deshan and Linji would find themselves staring with eyes wide open and mouths agape.
There are staffs and shouts; not even a single one is needed. But tell me: what if a person from among them should suddenly arrive?
"Meeting under the overturned canopy, we are old friends as before; why should it hinder him from coming to drink Zhaozhou’s tea? [The Master] invited the administrators to the hall. [He said:
"Closing the room at Mahākāśyapa’s cave, sealing the mouth at Vimalakīrti’s dwelling, facing the wall for nine years, crossing the night at Huangmei—these are all matters of testing and selection."
To come here is already to fall into calculation. Little do you realize that the sun does not wait for fire to be hot, and the moon does not wait for wind to be cool.
Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. To act without acting is non-action.

If you can understand it in this way, you will be able to expand the Dharma seat, support the monastic community, erect the banner of the Dharma together, and circulate the true lineage. I dare ask the assembly: according to the command, what is it?
"How do you say it in a single phrase? "In Jeta Grove, springtime abounds from ancient times to the present; every blossom is fully opened as a *campaka* flower. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The affairs of the world drift aimlessly, sinking and floating; I cherish the white clouds as the years deepen.

Looking up, everything is no longer ordinary grass or wood—how could one so stubbornly sever an arm to seek peace of mind? Although this is so, matters are never one-sided. [He] picked up [the whisk].
Holding up his staff, he said: "Bodhidharma has arrived! He is upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff, preaching the Dharma-door of settling the mind for all of you.
Do you believe it? If you can believe it, your mind will be at peace right now. If not, then wait."
When the ocean dries up, its bottom is finally seen; when a person dies, their mind is not known. Entering the hall: At Mahākāla’s Cave, the room was closed; at Vaiśālī, words were withheld.

These were all instances where the Principle was governed by the Spirit, such that the mouth remained silent because of it. How could one say they lacked eloquence? It is simply that there is eloquence which cannot be spoken.
Let loose the Iron Ox of Shanzhou; strike to death the Great Elephant of Jiazhou. Break through the Celestial Gate and overturn—
He overturns the axis of the earth. Look, look! He has smashed the skulls of everyone present. Is there anyone here who can recognize the sensation of pain?
After a long silence, he said: "Ten thousand mountains do not obstruct tonight’s moon; a single expanse of pure light shines all the more brightly. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
An ancient said: "The entire universe and the great earth are gathered up like a grain of millet and scattered before everyone.
Those who are like lacquer buckets do not understand; beat the drum and invite all to look! I wonder, what is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"In an acre of land, there are three snakes and nine rats. The monk said: "I do not yet understand your meaning; I beg you, Master, to grant me further instruction. The Master said: [Silence].
The mouth of the sea is difficult to express. The monk asked, "If the entire earth is as small as a grain of millet, then where do the myriad phenomena, humans, animals, grasses, and shrubs reside?
The Master said, "This question is not bad. The monk asked, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "One cannot die from being struck by a staff. He then said, "The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the borders."
A single phrase settles heaven and earth; a single sword brings peace to the world. Thus one sees the times are prosperous and the Way is flourishing, and the four seas are tranquil and clear.
Yet, within the gate of this monk, it is not so: the staff has swallowed up heaven and earth, leaving not even a hair’s breadth of leakage.
Where else could there be a single thing to serve as a condition or an opponent for all people? Do you understand?
[The Master] said, "Mò. After a long silence, he said, "Each of you, please return to the hall for tea. On the occasion of the *xià* (summer retreat) conclusion, he ascended the hall. A monk asked:
"A monk once asked Yunmen, 'What was the meaning of Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall? Yunmen replied, 'Niànqī (the seventh day). I do not know what the intent of the ancient was.
The Master said, "A single grain of elixir can transform iron into gold. The monk said, "Why does the student fail?"

He pinched the master’s nostrils. The Master said, "This clears the injustice done to Bodhidharma. He then said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to.
Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly; below, cut off your own self. From the beginning, there has been no facing or turning away; fundamentally, it is free from all nets and cages.
Stepping out the door, you bump into Subhūti—where not even an inch of grass grows for ten thousand miles. This is the long-beaked one."

Birds, do not say they will not perch upon fragrant trees; do not vainly speak of Chan or the Way. Moshetuo, even if your mind were hanging from the treetop, you could not avoid your body sinking to the bottom of the sea.

how do you speak it? "The green mountains and clear waters remain as they were of old; the bright moon and pure breeze are together [with us]."
One Family. Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the true source of the Great Way? The Master said, "Mud and water blended together.

Language. Where the wind cannot enter, one blends mud with water; where mud and water are blended, the wind cannot enter.

With a shout, wind and thunder manifest the Great Function. From the tip of the staff, the eyes are struck open;

having illuminated all phenomena, they are found to be entirely void. Stepping out the door, one bumps into Subhūti; pressed against the void, the whole body is revealed—a single expanse of empty stillness."
"Severance" refers to emotion. Ten thousand miles of clear light, the jade hare flies. Entering the hall: No dharma before the eyes; the myriad phenomena are dense and vivid.
The intent is right before one's eyes, yet it breaks forth so suddenly it is difficult to discern. It is not a dharma of the present moment; wherever you touch, you encounter him.
It is not something reached by the ears or eyes, yet it does not depart from seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing. Although this is so, you must still tread upon it.
Only then can you grasp the pivotal mechanism of the higher path. Thus it is said: "He does not stay when caged; he does not turn his head when called.
Buddhas and patriarchs have made no arrangements for him, and to this day he has no fixed abode. If this is so, there is no need to laboriously collect the mind;

the gate of the multi-storied pavilion opens, and without moving a single step, one reaches all hundred cities. [The Master] suddenly took up his staff, drew a line, and said: "When meeting death on the road..."
"Do not strike and kill the snake; take it home in a bottomless basket. Ascending the hall, he said: "Day after day the sun rises in the east;
day after day the sun sets in the west. Human life lies in a single breath; a hundred years pass in a fleeting instant. Suddenly one encounters Him, overturning the pit of birth and death.
He struck his staff and said: "Let loose the falcon from the vast heavens; it pierces through ten thousand layers of clouds in a single bound. *Chuan* (Recorded).
The Grand Secretary requested the Master to ascend the seat. A monk asked, "When all affairs have been brought to rest and not even a single sage carries anything with them, what then?
The Master said, "Not yet sufficient to behold the splendor. The monk asked, "Is there anything extraordinary? The Master said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak."
The monk said, "In that case, the Main Peak is high and the Foreground Peak is low. The Master said, "All things are completely cut off.
He then said, "The Buddha’s words take the mind as their essence; all is one. The gateless is the Dharma-gate; one is all.
You people here, with your staffs over your shoulders, stride across the world—have you yet trodden upon this gate? If you have..."
Abiding in this gate, every year is a good year; every month is a good month; every day is a good day; every moment is a good moment.

It is as bright as the radiant sun and as vast as the great void. The Buddhas of the three periods give birth to ordinary beings and nurture sages through this gate, bringing extensive benefit to all classes of beings.
The ancestral masters of successive generations have, through this gate, realized mind-to-mind accord and transmitted the True Dharma.
Continued: The Patriarchal Ancestor of the World revealed the Eye of the Human and Heavenly Eyes through this gate, upholding the path that transcends all.
Heaven and Earth take this gate as their covering and concealment; the sun and moon take this gate as their illumination and descent.
The four seasons take this gate as their cold and heat; kings take this gate to govern the world; and the hundred officials take this gate to fulfill their loyalty and service.

"This is the guest within the guest. The Master said, "You are a field-slave. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Meeting yet still coarse and rough.
[The monk] asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "The sword's radiance pierces the clouds of sorrow.
[The monk] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "Beating the bone and striking the marrow. The Gaozong era, the *shengwu* year of the Shaoxing reign, the tenth month.
At the beginning of the month, he manifested a slight illness. On the eighteenth day, the head seat Fachuán requested his final instructions. The Master said, "Exhaust this mind and intention;
support one another through the Way. Having spoken these words, he passed away. After the cremation, his eyes, teeth, and tongue remained uncorrupted.

The ground where the event occurred emitted light throughout the night, and those who obtained *śarīra* relics were beyond counting; they continued to appear for over a month without ceasing. Huangguan Luò Zhàocháng, Píng... [text ends]
One day, he asked his teacher about the Way. Upon returning from outside, he found that he alone had gained nothing. His aspiration for the Way was fervent and earnest;
while he was eating with a guest, as he was chewing, there seemed to be something in his mouth. When he spat it out, it was a *śarīra* (relic), about the size of a bean and the color of amber.

A person fond of such things took it away. He then prostrated himself again at the site of the cremation. Hearing a sound from within the incense casket, he opened it immediately and obtained what he had sought.
As before, his disciples enshrined his remains and divided them to be interred in pagodas at Mount Mao and West Flower. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Dawu.
Chan Master Foxing Fatai of Daming Mountain in Changsha Prefecture was a native of the Li clan of Hanzhou. A monk asked:

"When principle follows the transformations of phenomena, it encompasses all existence yet remains a single expanse of void and stillness. When phenomena follow the integration of principle, they equalize all differences and return entirely to [the source]."
"Ultimate Reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). What is the Dharma-realm of Principle (*li-fajie*)? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. "What is the Dharma-realm of Phenomena (*shi-fajie*)?

The Master said, "The myriad phenomena in their dense array. "What is the Dharma-realm of the Non-obstruction between Principle and Phenomena (*li-shi wuai fajie*)? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north.
"What is the Dharma-realm of the Non-obstruction between Phenomenon and Phenomenon (*shi-shi wuai fajie*)? The Master said, "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Pushing to the limit of the Real, the Real has no marks; exhausting the delusory, the delusory has no form.
When both Real and delusory are non-existent, the eyes are revealed in vast openness. Now that the eyes are revealed, what do you see? The bright sun melts the snow at the cragside;
the northern wind blows open the plum blossoms in mid-winter. Ascending the hall, he said: "When the precious sword is taken up, it is used immediately; how could there be any delay?"
Doubt! Plucking up the eyebrows and walking away—there is no further hesitation or evasion. At all times, it soars through the present and illuminates the past;

in every place, it cuts off all nets and cages. It does not strike against the sharp edge, nor does it look back into the mirror. Let us set aside for now the matter of its solitary transcendence beyond all things.
"When all ten thousand affairs have been exhausted, what then? After a long silence, he said, "The eighth month is autumn; where is there heat?
He ascended the hall and said, "Nirvana has no divergent paths; skillful means have many gates. He raised his staff and said, "Look, look!
This mountain monk’s staff swallows up the waters of the West River in a single draught. The carp of the Eastern Sea leaps up to the thirty-third heaven. The Emperor... [text ends].
Releasing his wrath, he struck Mount Sumeru with a single blow, shattering it to pieces. The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā joined her palms and praised him, saying:
"Behold the Dharma of the Dharma King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. He then struck the meditation seat with his staff and descended from the seat.

To ascend the hall [and preach] while having merely realized the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena does not yet accord with the ancestral style of the Buddhas. Likewise, to have merely embodied the totality of function and the totality of illumination...
This is not the essential subtlety of a monk; one must simply break through the sturdy barrier and recognize that uppermost aperture.

What is the uppermost aperture? "The spring chill is biting; it freezes the young to death. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Today is the middle of the first month. Everywhere the lanterns flicker and swirl;
throughout the city, silks and brocades are crowded together as people go back and forth, enjoying themselves. Text.
Shu rushed off into the midst of the crowd; Puxian sat upright in a high tower watching. Now tell me, where is Guanyin?
Thundering drums are beaten, shaking the heavens; flutes and songs are played, deafening the earth. Entering the hall [he said]:
"Vast and remote, encompassing the ten directions; level and expansive, beyond form and beyond appearance. The eyes wish to look, yet the pupils wither; the mouth wishes to speak, yet..."
The words fail; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have no skill at all. Linji and Deshan, however, do not hesitate to proclaim it:
"A tortoise swallows the iron ox of Shanzhou; a snake bites the Great Buddha of Jiaozhou. This startles the carp of the Eastern Sea until its belly remains distended even unto this day.
Hehe! [Ascending the hall to pray for rain: Fiery clouds scorch the field crops; the springs and sources have ceased their flow. Sāgara...
"Great Dragon King! I do not know where you are," he said, striking the meditation seat with his staff. "You are right here! Look!

Clouds rise from the southern mountain, and rain falls on the northern mountain. I, the old monk, shall further provide the sound of thunder to augment your majestic radiance and cause it to spread afar.
Then, raising his voice, he said: "Hōnō, hōnō! [He then] ascended the hall. Sometimes speaking is wrong; opening one's mouth—
"Sometimes it is so. Coarse words and subtle speech all return to the primary meaning. The bowl-chiming sound of Old Śākyamuni; the stench of excrement from Bodhidharma’s coming from the West.
Only the water-buffalo before the mountain emits rays of light from its body that illuminate heaven and earth.
He ascended the hall and said: "To have mindfulness or to lose mindfulness—there is nothing that is not liberation. What kind of talk is this? To establish the Dharma or to destroy it?"
All phenomena are called *nirvāṇa*. This is a matter of mutual penetration and intermingling. Wisdom and folly are both collectively termed *prajñā*.
The vast and open Buddha-nature—the dharmas accomplished by both Bodhisattvas and non-Buddhists—are all *bodhi*. Yet, there is still a slight discrepancy.
Nevertheless, even so, it is like Emperor Yang losing his camel. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, look at these very words."

This serves as my standard. Now that I am old, what thing could I possibly know?
I cast down the vajra-hammer and shatter the bones of a thousand sages; I hurl them onto the four-way crossroads and can no longer begrudge them.
I pass through this floating life as I please, taking south for north, calling a tortoise a turtle, and naming beans "grain. Let those with clear eyes laugh.
I have no set rules or guidelines.
This is Chan Master Cichan Jingyuan of Huguo Temple in Taizhou Prefecture, a native of the Zhang family from Nanxi in Yongjia.

At the age of eighteen, he received full ordination under Higan at Mount Ling. Later, he studied the Tiantai teachings; subsequently, he left them to visit Yuanwu at Zhongfu Mountain, where he heard [the Dharma].

The ink gathered from the earth was pitch black; in his later years, he further eliminated all traces of artifice. Wielding the vajra mallet, he shattered the den of delusion.

[The monk] asked, "As soon as one emerges, one becomes a human being. Furthermore, how is this so? The Master said, "Waves overturning the void atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.
[The monk] asked, "That which heaven cannot cover and earth cannot support—what thing is it? The Master said, "A holeless iron hammer.

[The monk] said, "The hosts of devas and all classes of living beings all receive the power of its grace. The Master said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. [The monk] asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods..."
The Buddha spoke of the "bottomless phrase. I beg the Master to speak it quickly. The Master said, "Blinking the eyebrows upward. Question: "To know before it is raised;
to see before it is spoken. What is the lineage of Miu and Yang? The Master said, "Pushed forward, they do not go ahead; restrained, they do not retreat.
[The student] said, "In years past, the site of Sanping was restored. On that day, Yuanwu held high the ancestral seal for the first time."
[The questioner] asked: "From the Master’s own tradition, what is the Linji school? The Master said: "To kill or to give life without batting an eye. [The questioner] said:

"In building and transforming, how can one avoid walking the 'Bird Path'? When returning to the source, the subtle wonder reveals the family style. [The questioner] asked: "What is the Caodong school? The Master said:
"Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know the dawn? [The questioner] said: "Drawing back the mirror before one's eyes, those who grasp it..."
[The monk] said, "It is rare indeed. What is the Yunmen school? The Master said, "The three eyes on the crown of the head shine throughout heaven and earth.
[The monk] asked, "It is said that 'the three realms are mind-only and the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. What is the Fayen school? The Master said, "The tips of arrows meet point-blank;
there is no yielding. [The monk] asked, "Is there still a path above this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the path above? The Master—
[The monk] said, "A pitch-black expanse. The Master shouted. The Master said, "For the sake of one grain of millet, they lose six months' worth of rations.
He ascended the hall [to teach]. "Before the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranāda, this group of fellows was off by seven or eight; after the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranāda..."
That former group of men fell two by two, three by three; yet now this present group of men sits and stands with solemn dignity.
Tell me, is this being off by seven or eight, or is it falling two by two, three by three? Can you still reach a definitive conclusion? Raising his whisk, he said:
Hūṃ hūṃ. The Bathing of the Buddha: Entering the Hall. When Old Śākyamuni was first born, he immediately made a spectacle;
pointing one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, he said, "In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. Yunmen said:
If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, just to bring peace to the world.
Yet there are still those who refuse to let it go, saying, "Only Yunmen could truly praise the Patriarch. But tell me, where is the place where he praises him?
Is it at the point where he strikes him dead with a blow? Be glad to know there is no connection. Today, Nan...
I can clearly see that we must let this matter pass. If we did not let it pass, every person throughout the entire world would have to beg for their lives.
Now, as there is no other recourse, let us join the assembly and offer each of them one ladleful at the Buddha Hall.
Why? Have you not heard it said: "It is better to violate a specific rule than to overstep a precedent"? Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The jackal howls, yet the lion roars; eyes wide open, mouth agape. The Southern Star moves, the Northern Dipper stumbles.
Great assembly, do you know where this falls? Crouching beneath the Diamond Stair, the divine tortoise runs through the fire.
Later, while residing at West Mountain, Master Lingfeng Gu was invited by Dragon Scholar Geng to ascend the seat at Jingguang Monastery. Lingfeng raised the example of Baiyun seeing [the Buddha]."
Yangqi instructed that the case of the "Tealing’s Verse on Awakening" be cited, requesting the Master to provide a critical evaluation. The Master said, "All you Zen adepts:
Yangqi laughs loudly; his eyes look toward the southeast, yet his intent lies in the northwest. Baiyun attained awakening, but he did not truly attend to the matter—he mistook the bell for a jar.
When scrutinized from beginning to end, even the old fellow Yangqi is all upon the rack."
"Follow the error with the error. If one were from Nanming, it would not be so. "I have a single bright pearl; take care not to let it slip past you at the very moment it is presented.

Although it is shown face-to-face, it must still be broken with a single blow of the hammer. Raising his whisk, he said: "Do you understand? When a chess game meets a worthy opponent, one's skill cannot be hidden;
when a poem reaches the point of being recited repeatedly, its craftsmanship finally reveals itself. On the day he manifested illness, he spoke thus.

He invited Xitang Ying’an Hua to serve as the head of the assembly (zuoyuan) and entrusted him with the affairs of the monastery. He gave instructions as was his custom. Suddenly, he clenched his fist and passed away.
Upon cremation, five-colored śarīra were obtained; his teeth, tongue, and right fist remained entirely intact.
He was enshrined in a stupa before Liúguǎn Dòu to the east of the temple. He was fifty-three years old.
Chan Master Xiansha Shibei of Fuzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya;
on the earth there is no Maitreya. Tell me, where is Maitreya? After a long silence, he said: "When walking at night, do not step on white;
it is either water or stone."
Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng in Suzhou Prefecture was a native of that region. He received ordination under Zhang of Ruipeng in Min.

Upon returning home, he visited Qionglong Yuan and suddenly attained realization; he then presented his insights to Yuan. Yuan said, "Although you have gained entry, you have not yet reached the proper place.
You must truly spur yourself on. Thereupon, he took leave and visited various seats of practice. Later, he attended Yuanwu, and just as he entered the inner quarters—*cái*... [text fragment]
Wu followed him to the door. Wuzhuo said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master struck a pillar once. Wuzhuo said, "Why do you not speak a single word to the point?
The Master said, "If the teacher shakes his head, the disciple wags his tail. Wuzhuo said, "Try wagging your tail for me."

The Master performed a somersault and exited. Wuzhuo laughed heartily; from this, he became renowned. Later, while residing [at the monastery], a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?
The Master said, "The Hegemon and the King reached the Wu River. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'?
The Master said, "Building the altar and enshrining the generals. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said, "Ten thousand..."
"The villages, mountains, and rivers have attained great peace. [The student] asked, "What is it that is not usurped by either the person or the environment?

The Master said, "When the dragon roars, the mist rises; when the tiger howls, the wind arises. [The student] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "You have missed it right before your face.
[The student] said, "Truly a master craftsman! The Master said, "A ghost deludes people in broad daylight. One day, he entered the city and walked among the monastics and laypeople.
Upon arriving at Shilang Lane, someone asked, "The lane is right here; I wonder where Shilang is?
The Master raised his arm and said, "Follow me."
Chan Master Zhengfa Jian of Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have no horns.

Without a hair’s breadth, without a speck of dust—like mountains, like peaks. Upon the point of a needle, the lion turns its body; within the hollow of a lotus root, the great garuḍa spreads its wings."
Suddenly and unexpectedly, he passed beyond Uttarakuru; the sun, moon, and stars all turned black at once.
Chan Master Anmin Huazang Miyin of Jiangning Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family of Jiading. Initially, he lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.

He became the one to whom the Chengdu scholastic community turned for guidance. At that time, Yuanwu was residing at Zhaojue Temple; the Master and Fengsheng were friends, so he went to visit him there.
Upon hearing Yuanwu’s *xiaocan* (informal evening discourse), he heard him cite the kōan concerning the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant.

Zhaozhou had commented on it, saying: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters themselves do not take shape, the traces of the brushstrokes are already manifest. Where is it that the traces are already manifest?"
The Master harbored doubts about this matter and went to visit Xiang. Upon entering the room, Wuzhuo asked him, "What sutra does the Preceptor lecture on? The Master replied, "The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
Wuzhuo said, "In the *Śūraṅgama*, there are the 'Investigation of the Mind in Seven Places' and the 'Discrimination of Seeing through Eight Returns. Ultimately, where does the mind reside?"

The Master frequently presented his interpretations of the meaning, but Huineng would not accept them. The Master requested further instruction, and Huineng directed him to manifest his realization in all situations.

Wu shouted, "The patterns have already been revealed! Upon hearing this, the Master attained a realization. Wu then applied his characteristic methods of the "tongs and hammer" to test him, but the Master was at a loss for what to do.
One day, the Master said to Wu, "Master, do not speak further; wait until I explain it myself. Wu consented.

The Master then cited various passages from the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra* and matched them to the practical applications of brandishing the whisk, raising the staff, shouting, and striking the meditation seat. Wu—

He laughed and said, "So you have been making your living here all along. He then pointed at him and said, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras that the wondrous nature is perfectly luminous and free from all names and forms?
At these words, the master was suddenly relieved and attained realization. He left Sichuan and resided at Jia Shan. While serving the master, he attended the night assembly.
When the master raised the kōan regarding the ancient sail that had not yet been hoisted, the master heard it but did not yet comprehend it. Thus...
He sought a definitive resolution. Huineng said, "Ask me. The Master recounted the previous conversation. Huineng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.

At this, the Master attained immediate realization without doubt and said, "The ancients said it was like a drop falling into a vast ravine; they did not realize that the great ocean can fall into a single drop.
Huineng laughed and said, "What can be done with this fellow? Not long after, he ordered him to share the seat [with the Master]. Later, he went to visit Master Foyin.
In light of this, Jian asked, "Foguo has a phrase that he never spoke carelessly for others; has he ever spoken it to you?
The Master said, "Shut that dog’s mouth! Jian raised his voice and said, "This is not the principle. The Master said, [silently].
"No one has stolen your salt and tea bag. What do you call it? Jue said, "If Foguo does not explain it for you, I shall explain it for you.
The Master said, "When you have doubts, O Monk, leave this monastery and go elsewhere to study. Jue laughed heartily.
Not long after, the Master began teaching the Dharma at Baoning, then moved to Huazang, and finally returned to his hometown to preside over Zhongfeng.
He ascended the hall and said: "The multitude sells flowers, while I alone sell pines; though their green hue is not as red as theirs, when calculated, they ultimately do not accord with the times.
Return, then, to the midst of the verdant mists! "How laughable that the ancients spoke thus! It was much like fleeing from a peak only to rush into a ravine. [He paused,] "To avoid..."
Drowning yourself or throwing yourself into fire—how can these compare to following one’s lot and seeking out even half a person at the edge of a cubit-and-eight-inch or a five-inch iron hammer?
Even so, Baoning would not accept even half a person. Why? "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few;
the poor resent that a single body is too many. On the winter solstice, he ascended the hall and cited Yuyuan Hao, saying: "Snow, snow, every flake is indistinguishable. He then descended.

When the twelfth month arrived, they continued as before without ceasing through the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh months of the following year.
"Let them freeze to death or starve to death," [the master thought], "so that they will stop their wild and confused talk.
The Master said, "This was not a curse, nor was it praise; it surpasses Linji and Deshan, yet it is not like Yunmen."
He resided at Arhat [Temple]. Someone asked, "Tell me, what was the intention of Yuyuan? After a long silence, he said, "If only the snow could melt away completely, spring would naturally arrive.
Later, he passed away at his home mountain. When his body was cremated, a great many *śarīra* relics remained.
Commoners dug the earth about a foot deep and all obtained them; these were especially radiant and pure. His heart and tongue also remained uncorrupted.
Chan Master Ché'ān Dàoyuán of Zhāojié in Chengdū Prefecture was the son of the Dèng family from Miān Prefecture.

After receiving full ordination (*upasampadā*), he traveled east to pay his respects to Dào at Dàbié. While contemplating the words "Vast emptiness, no sage," he suddenly burst into laughter and said, "Dànmó has been here all along!
Dào praised him. He subsequently went to study under Fójian and Foyǎn, and later relied upon Yuánwù at Jīnshān. Because...
He reported what he had seen to Baizhang Huaiwu. Huaiwu did not grant his approval. Huaiwu moved to Yunju, and the Master followed him.

Although he attained a degree of faith and understanding, he remained inwardly troubled, harboring doubts that the "substantial thing" had not yet been removed. It happened that Huaiwu asked the assembly of practitioners: "When birth and death arrive, how will you deal with it? A monk said:

Xiangtaizi laughed at Master Heshang. He then asked the Master, "How do you understand this? The Master replied, "The bandit has been utterly defeated. Wuzhuo said, "What would you say if someone were to ask you this?
As the Master was about to answer, Wuzhuo seized him with contempt and said, "The bandit has been utterly defeated!
At that moment, the Master attained complete realization. Wuzhuo struck him with his fist, and the Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Wuzhuo said, "What did you see that made you..."
It was thus. The Master said, "The poisonous hand has not yet been requited; it shall never be forgotten for kalpas. Wuzhuo returned to Zhaojue and appointed the Master to lead the assembly.
When Wuzhuo was about to pass away, he commanded the Master to succeed him on the seat.
Chan Master Ren of Zhentian Temple in the central district of Hangzhou Prefecture was a native of Luoyang. In his youth, he left the household life at Fengxian Monastery in Dongjing.
At the beginning of the Xuanhua era, he received official documentation for the tonsure ceremony at Qingjidian.

After receiving full ordination, he traveled between the Tripitaka Translation Institute and other locations, thoroughly investigating the sutras and śāstras; yet, he remained particularly unconvinced by the Chan school. At that time, Yuanwu resided there...

Tianning went to visit him. At that time, Wuzhuo was conducting the *入室* (entering the room) ceremony for the assembly. Upon seeing him, the Master [Tianning] felt deep reverence and submission; he stepped forward with vigor.
