Xinghua said, "When I meet someone, I do not come out; when I do come out, I am already acting for others. The Master asked, "And how about this? He replied, "A mistake.
[The Master] said, "Xinghua’s banner and spear stand upright; Sansheng’s liver and gall are laid bare together. The Master said, "He cannot lead you there.
[The Master] asked, "Right now, how would you act for others, Master? The Master said, "One blow, one mark. (Quoted from *Jǔxuán*).
The Story of the Three Kinds of Illnesses of the Monk Sha. The verse says: "Blind, deaf, mute—caught and defeated! What more need be asked?
Blind, deaf, mute.
This was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Yunju Hui.
Chan Master Wansong Huainan Dalian praised the image of Śākyamuni Emerging from the Mountains, saying: "His practice fulfilled and his merit perfected, he is reduced to the bone;
He cannot bear the emaciation, his hair matted and disheveled. His transgressions against heaven are now beyond counting; In the midst of this Vaiśya-like state, he offers a single confession."

Master Xian of Inan at Longming in Wenzhou Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Wan’nan Ben, ascended the hall for the assembly. He raised the example of Fayen saying, "If you recognize the bench..."
It is more than sufficient all around. Yunmen said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
The Master said, "Old man Fayan sits people to death; Great Master Yunmen runs people to death. Longming, however, is not like this.
Having recognized the bench—its four legs planted firmly on the ground—one sits when one wishes to sit and rises when one wishes to rise.

Entering the hall, he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman and offered this verse: The lady of ice and snow possesses a most extraordinary countenance; She constantly plays her jade flute for all to hear.
Within the melody lie boundless matters of sorrow; Only the lady herself is permitted to know them alone.
Chan Master Jiàn of Yìān at Dàméi in Chángshā Prefecture was a native of Huìkē. He ascended the hall and said: "The trees have fallen and the sky is bare;
the heavens are cold and the waters are frozen. Śākyamuni has nowhere to hide his body.

He tears down the eastern fence to patch the western wall, only to run into the Bodhisattva Abhaya, who requests instruction on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation. How truly strange! Yet he replies, 'The golden light...'"
Mingyun: After the formal session, he went for tea. He ascended the hall and said: "The Old Barbarian opened a single path;
how direct it is! It simply says: 'Rest and you are Bodhi. This intrinsically pure, luminous mind is not obtained from others. Later generations have failed to find its gate."
Rushing incessantly north and south, traveling back and forth east and west, throughout the years and to the end of time, there is no place of rest.
Can you all find rest? Enough! Enough! Ascending the hall, he raised an example: One day Huìtáng asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Nánxióng Prefecture. Huitang said, "What did you come out for? The monk said, "To visit venerable elders. Huitang said, "It would be better to go home."
[Huangbo] said, "I am fond of my hometown. [Huitang] asked, "I do not yet understand the Master’s intention in ordering me to return to my hometown.

Huitang said, "In my hometown, for three coins one can buy a piece of fish sauce as large as a palm. The Master said, "I would rather have my body shattered into fine dust than ever again blind the eyes of a monk.
Huitang was slightly inferior; some people would simply say, "It is difficult to forget what is familiar."
There was no common ground for conversation. He ascended the hall and raised the story of the King of Kaśmīra asking Venerable Siṃha about the "emptiness of the aggregates" (*skandha-śūnyatā*).
He spoke in verse: "When did the Venerable ever attain the emptiness of the aggregates? The King of Kaśmīra needlessly cut down the spring breeze himself.
After the rain, the peach blossoms scatter in profusion, Dyeing the flowing waters of the stream a crimson red."
Chan Master Xue’an Congjin of Tiantong in Ningbo Prefecture was the son of Zheng [family] from Nanxi in Yongjia.
He received the tonsure under Puan Zihu and went to visit Xinwen at Ruiyan. Xinwen brought up the "A Flake of Snow on a Red Furnace" story and questioned the Master.
As the Master was about to give an answer, he heard the single call [of the master] and suddenly realized the meaning.
He remained in attendance for three years, then went to Min Province, where he met Fozhi at Xichan Monastery. Fozhi asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Siming.
Fozhi asked, "Have you ever seen the Mad Bagu? The Master gave a shout. Fozhi struck him. The Master caught the staff and said, "Master, do not be so hasty. Fozhi said, "Blind fellow!"

Guo stood at the side. Xinwen was the head of the Jiangxin community. When the Master returned for a visit, he appointed him as the Rector (*karmadāna*). One day, Guo asked the Master, "In 'One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function act simultaneously,' what is 'one shout distinguishing guest and host'? The Master then gave a shout. Guo said, "As for this one shout, is it the guest or the host? The Master replied, "As a guest, it is always a guest; as a host, it is always a host. Guo said, "What about when it is neither guest nor host? The Master shouted again. Guo said, "This shout—what is it? Is it the guest or the host? The Master said, "As a guest, it is from beginning to end a guest; as a host, it is from beginning to end a host. Guo said, "How can there be both guest and host within a single shout? The Master said, "When the guest is present, the host is absent; when the host is present, the guest is absent. How could there be both guest and host within a single shout? Guo said, "If so, then there is no guest and no host. The Master said, "If you say there is no guest and no host, that itself is the guest and the host. Guo said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The guest and the host are like the two sides of a pair of scales. If you weigh them with a mind of duality, they will never balance. Only when you let go of all calculations and do not seek anything outside yourself will you see the guest and the host. Guo bowed deeply and departed. Later, he went to visit Master Xuedou. Xuedou asked, "Where have you come from? Guo replied, "From Master Baizhang. Xuedou asked, "What did he say to you? Guo recounted the preceding dialogue. Xuedou said, "Baizhang has already finished his work; why do you still ask for more? Guo said, "I do not understand. Xuedou said, "He has already given you a shout; why do you still ask for another? Guo said, "Please, Master, give me one. Xuedou shouted. Guo said, "This shout is the guest; where is the host? Xuedou said, "You have been a guest from the very beginning. Guo said, "I do not understand. Xuedou said, "If you do not understand, you must go back and serve Baizhang. Guo bowed deeply and departed. He returned to Baizhang and reported everything to the Master. The Master said, "Xuedou is a man of great capacity; you must go and study under him. Guo then went to Xuedou and became his attendant. One day, Xuedou asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Guo said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Xuedou said, "You have attained my marrow. Guo then composed a verse: "The cypress tree in the courtyard stands in the bright moonlight; / The clear wind blows through the autumn night, cold and deep. / If you ask me for the meaning of Bodhidharma’s coming from the West, / I point directly to the cypress tree in the courtyard. Xuedou said, "You have truly attained my marrow. Guo then took up residence at Mount Donglin. Later, when the Master [Baizhang] passed away, Guo returned to the temple to pay his respects. The assembly requested him to take charge of the monastery. Guo declined three times. Finally, he accepted. One day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The Great Way is not difficult; only avoid picking and choosing. If you pick and choose, you fall into the weeds of views. If you do not pick and choose, you are free from the weeds of views. Therefore, the ancients said: 'If you wish to know the Way, do not create difficulties for yourself. What is meant by 'not creating difficulties'? It is simply to stop the mind's wandering and cease the flow of thoughts. If you can do this, you will naturally accord with the Way. Do not seek outside; do not look within. Just let go of all things and rest in the state of non-action. This is called the 'Gateless Barrier. Thus he spoke. Guo lived at Donglin for many years, and his reputation spread throughout the land. His disciples numbered over a thousand. In the spring of the second year of the Tianxi era (1018), he suddenly announced to the assembly that he would pass away on the eighth day of the fourth month. On that day, he ascended the hall and said, "My life has reached its end; I am now going. He then sat upright and passed away. He was seventy-one years old. His dharma heirs included masters such as Foyan Qingyuan, Xuedou Chongxian, and others. His remains were enshrined in the Donglin Monastery. His posthumous title was "Great Master Wuxin" (No-Mind). His epitaph reads: "The Master’s name was Guo; his courtesy name was Zhenzhong. His ancestors were from Jiaozhi. His father, Guo, served as a district magistrate. The Master left home at the age of twenty-four and studied under Master Baizhang Huaihai. He later visited Xuedou Chongxian and attained enlightenment. He resided at Donglin for thirty years, guiding countless practitioners. His teaching was direct and unerring, and he was revered by all. This concludes the biography of Master Wuxin.
Zhongzhu heard this and said with a laugh, "You have once again suffered from visual distortion. The Master then presented a verse, saying: "One shout distinguishes guest and host;
Once more, my eyes are blurred. I flip a somersault backward; Trampling to death a dead shrimp. He first resided at Lingyan in Yizhen and later moved to Tiantong.
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Lingyan? The Master replied, "The Cold Spring of Deer-Run soaks [all things]."
Clear Moon. The deep harbor of Longdougang conceals white clouds. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, Mount Sumeru is placed in the nostrils. The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Looking up, one does not see the sky."
A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The whole body enters the wild weeds. The monk said, "A master! The Master said, "Withdraw. He ascended the hall and said:
"To turn over within the diamond circle is to strike the nostrils of Śakra. To let go at the edge of a precipice is to bring forth the eyes of Bodhidharma.
Though we have gone back and forth three times, the momentum is not yet exhausted. Once the pivot of the mechanism turns, its force cannot be checked."
Stop! To grasp a scorpion by its tail is to invite its sting; to stroke a tiger’s whiskers is to provoke its rage.

While the slave calls out "Bodhisattva," Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya is not yet born. The ancestral command of the Buddha-Dharma now rests entirely in the hands of this new celestial youth.
For now, he holds fast—how will he let go? After a long silence, he said: "A holeless iron hammer is hurled right at your face; it rises up, covering heaven and earth."
Clear Breeze. Ascending the hall, he said: "When the golden mallet is wielded, the Buddhas of the three periods dare not face it head-on.

When the Dharma-ordinance is put into practice, externalists and celestial demons all fold their hands in submission. Lofty and towering, there is originally nothing to grasp or look up to; pure and naked, there is no need for contrivance.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, do not harbor doubt. Good and evil, right and wrong—let them all be dropped at once. Thus he spoke.
Afterwards, mixing mud with water, he pulled the plow and guided the oxen, moving freely in all directions without any hindrance.
At such a time as this, tell me: how does one sing the "Song of Great Peace"? After a long silence, he said: "The iron boat lies across the ancient ford; the old family style is restored.
On the twenty-third day of the seventh month in the Gengshen year of the Qingyuan era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty, he requested a bath and changed his robes.

He wrote a verse on his robe, then cast aside his brush and entered nirvana. He was eighty-four years old and seventy years since his ordination. His entire body was interred to the right of the Xinwen Pagoda.
There is a verse of his that is considered among the very best of the ancient masters.
Chan Master Jingmeng Gu’an of Zhimen in Wenzhou Prefecture was a native of the Shao family in Pingyang, Wenzhou. From childhood, he delighted in hearing the sound of bells and sutra recitations.

At thirteen, he donned the black robes and studied the Tiantai teachings; however, finding that the study of names and characteristics was insufficient for realizing the Great Matter, he abandoned them.
He went to visit Fozhi at Yuyang Monastery. When the Master asked where he was from, the teacher replied, “Yongjia. The Master then asked, “Do you still recognize Yongjia?”

"Do you recognize the Great Master Yongjia? The Master was about to answer when the King shouted at him to leave. Thereupon, he remained dazed as if in a stupor, unaware of sleep or food for several months.
One day, hearing the sound of a bell, he suddenly attained enlightenment. He went up to the abbot’s quarters, and the King asked, "Do you still recognize the Great Master Yongjia?
The Master replied, "On this very day, I humbly wish the Preceptor ten thousand blessings in health and well-being. The King said, "As for the matter beyond [phenomena]..."
"How is it? The Master was about to respond when the King struck him with a hot staff and drove him out. On the following day, he went again to the Abbot’s quarters;

as soon as the King posed his question, the Master raised his voice and said, "This old man has failed today! With a single clap of his hands, he departed. Consequently, he returned to his hometown to visit his parents and saw Longxiang.
Longxiang asked: "Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. He who receives the words perishes; one who lingers in phrases..."
[The Master] said, "This is delusion. Try to convey a message at the point where words and explanations fail.
The Master drew a circle (○) with his left hand; Xiang struck it with his whisk from the left. The Master drew a circle (○) with his right hand; Xiang struck it with his whisk from the right.
The Master then drew another circle (○) in the center, presenting it by cradling it with both hands; Xiang drew two lines across it with his whisk. The Master bowed, rose, and stood. Xiang—
He laughed and said, "For thirty years I have been selecting cats; today I have found this one with a black head. He then returned to Deer Park (Mṛgadāva). Xiang named his hermitage after the valley.
Furthermore, he once visited Xian-ning Zhi. Initially, he went forth to reside at Zhi-men, and subsequently moved to Rui-yan. The Master was solitary and aloof, transcending the mundane;
though physically frail and unable to bear even the weight of his robes, he was stern, cold, and severe, such that one could not easily approach or fathom him.
The Chan Master Shanjie of Hantang at Tiger Hill in Suzhou Prefecture,

a dharma successor of Chan Master Tiantong Guan of the nineteenth generation after Great Mirror (Dajian), inscribed the following upon an image of Guanyin Carrying a Fish Basket: "Cloud-like tresses..."
With heavy makeup and forced smiles, she enters the dusty world for the sake of idle matters. She brings with her that which is truly alive, yet no one buys it;
they view it merely as dead merchandise for sale by the pound.
Chan Master Shunjing of Huazang Chuan’an cited the story of the Sixth Patriarch regarding the wind and the banner. His verse says: "It is neither the wind, nor is it the banner;
Where the white clouds end, one sees the green mountains. How pitiable are those countless men of heroic spirit;
With eyes wide open, they solemnly enter the gate of death."
Chan Master Wenwei Xiaoyan of Tiantai Yifu in Shaoxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: He cited Yunmen’s instruction to the assembly: "Everyone possesses a radiant light;
yet when one looks for it, it is dark and dim. What is this radiant light of yours? [Yunmen] answered on his own behalf:
"The kitchen and the main gate. He further said: "Better not to have such a thing at all. The Master said: "Everyone..."
All possess radiance; when looked upon, no dark gloom is seen. Kicking over the mountain gate and the kitchen storehouse— At this moment, light and darkness are naturally distinguished.
Chan Master Boyan Ning composed a verse on his tattered robe, which says: Torn and frayed through many years, Picked up as it comes and draped over one shoulder;
At midnight, returning from meditative concentration, I fold it together, And my entire body wins nothing but the clear blue sky.
Chan Master Jingshou Rujué of Mount Jingshan in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Tiantong Ying. He was a native of Wuzhou. Initially, he visited Chidun, who asked him:
"What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "A rotten winter melon. He then presented a verse: "What is the Buddha? A rotten winter melon.
When bitten, its frost penetrates the teeth. Though it has no root or stem, nor any hollow interior, It blooms once a year.
He also once composed a gāthā and presented it to Chidun, saying: "At Mount Zhong, I pushed against white blades with my bare body; How many times have I undergone this?"
He was buried alive. Since the time his person perished and his house fell into ruin, he has fully realized that there is no fixed position to arrange.
Later, on the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said: "A new year strikes a new drum, Universally bestowing the new rain of Dharma.
All things are entirely renewed, Each and every one conforming to the rules. The Great Being Samantabhadra rejoices; Seizing this moment, he opens the gate And lets forth the white elephant."

"O King! Throughout the entire earth, there is nowhere to be found. [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "What is this? Within a peach pit from a thousand years ago, it is still that very same kernel.
Small Retreat *Xichan* (General Discussion): In our school, the true command is fully exerted; it is like a violent wind and torrential rain, surging forward without obstruction.
It is like a spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning—once you try to pursue it, you cannot catch up. As soon as you form an intention, you lose the source; as soon as you lift your eyes—
It has already been missed; it is not a dharma of the present moment. Do not give rise to various thoughts.

Even if you were to cultivate the three types [of practice] in alternation, striving to attain realization within a fixed period—whether at the second or third head—no matter how many times you brace yourself or prop yourself up, you will only find yourself becoming more and more breathless. Little do you realize this.
Before the skull is even formed, the eye is already present; the first cry of birth is clear and decisive, putting everything to rest once and for all.

Nevertheless, those who have realized this through direct experience are not one in ten thousand, while those who misunderstand it are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The Verse on the Buddha’s Enlightenment says:
What was accomplished during six years on the Snowy Peaks? Striking out the eyes of the ghosts from long ago.
With shame covering his face and nowhere to turn, he has been terrified at the sight of the morning star until this very day.
Chan Master Demeng of Xuefeng on Mount Feng in Fujian Province composed a eulogy for the Mad Bagman, saying: Carrying a cloth bag upon his staff, he wanders through the red dust of the world.
How has he ever seen the true reality? His karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, lacking any foundation;
wishing to open his mouth to laugh at others.
Chan Master Gaoyuan Zuquan of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Qiji of Jinshan, cited the following:

When Jingqing was at Xuefeng on a communal work assignment, Xuefeng said, "Guishan said, 'When you see form, you see the mind. Is there any fault in this? Jingqing said, "Why did the ancients [say that]?"
"What matter? Feng said, "Even so, I wish to deliberate with you. Qing said, "If it is thus, it would be better for me to go and hoe the ground myself.
The Master said, "Xuefeng held the probing pole in his hand and carried the camouflage grass upon his person;
had it not been for Jingqing’s communal labor, things would have nearly come to ruin. [The Master] cited the Ninth Patriarch, Bodhidharmatrāta, who questioned the Eighth Patriarch:
"Buddhanandi: My parents are not my kin; who is my truest kin? The Buddhas are not my Way;
who is my truest Way? The verse says: "My parents are clearly not my kin; The Patriarch pours out his very heart and liver to others.
If you can directly and intimately realize this, The *udumbara* flower blooms as spring within the fire. Presented to Huang Hanling.
The Verse of Welcoming Guests says: The road winds around the crest of ten-thousand-fathom precipices; When travelers reach this place, they all give rise to sorrow.
Suddenly finding a place of rest, They roam at will across layered passes and mountains.
Chan Master Wumen Huikai of Huanglong was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wanshou at Wanshou Monastery. He was the son of the Liang family of Liangzhu in Hangzhou; his mother was of the Song clan.
He received his initial training from Tiantong Huihong and later studied under Yue-lin at Wanshou Monastery. Yue-lin instructed him to contemplate the koan: "The dog has no Buddha-nature."
Xinghua spent six years [studying] without finding any point of entry. He then resolved with a vow, saying: "If I do not cast off sleep, let my body rot away.
Whenever he reached a state of exhaustion, he would pace back and forth along the corridors; when drowsy, he would strike his head against a pillar.

One day, upon hearing the sound of the vegetarian drum, he attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "A clap of thunder in the blue sky and bright daylight— The eyes of all living beings on the great earth [are opened]."
Suddenly opened up. The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms all bowed their heads together; Mount Sumeru performed a three-stage dance. The next day, he entered the room.
When Yantong asked about his realization, Lin hurriedly said, "Where have you seen gods or ghosts? The Master gave a shout; Lin also shouted. The Master shouted again.

From then on, their spiritual resonance and functional application were perfectly harmonized. In the Wuyin year of the Jiading era of Emperor Ningzong, he emerged into the world at Baoguo Temple in Anji.
He subsequently moved to Longxing Tianning, Huanglong Cuiyan, Kaiyuan and Lingyan in Suzhou, Jiaoshan in Zhenjiang, and Baoning in Jinling.
In the *bingwu* year of the Chunyu era of Emperor Lizong (1256), he received an imperial decree to open the mountain at Huguo Renhuang Chan Monastery.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If a person recognizes their own mind, there is not an inch of earth in the great world. When the ancients spoke thus, Huanglong did not agree. He said:
"If a person recognizes their own mind, the great world is entirely earth. Ascending the hall, [he continued]: "Right and wrong, long and short—these are but winds at one's ear.
Do not seek out differences or similarities therein. If you wish to remain unmoved by the eight winds, let the ground of your mind be free."
"Equal to space. Old Man Cishou only knew how to hoist the sails with the current; he could not steer against the wind. Huanglong, however, was not like that.
"Both right and wrong have been cast off—realize it within right and wrong. Why is this so? Listen:
"How many times the black winds have tossed the great waves, yet never once has it been heard that the fishing boat capsized. [Ascending the hall: "Two-thirds of one's life..."
Too early. An ox in Huai Prefecture eats the grain; the single point of the numinous terrace has not been rubbed clean. A horse in Yi Prefecture suffers from bloating;
those who greedily pursue their lives in trivial toil seek out physicians throughout the world. When called, they do not turn their heads—what can be done?
To apply moxibustion to the left shoulder of a pig—if you can realize this, your study of the Way is complete. If it is otherwise, Elder Ma and all of you...
The man spoke thus, whereupon [the Master] planted his staff upright, descended from the seat, and ascended the hall. Zhaozhou said: "To those coming from the south, I unload for them;
to those coming from the north, I load up for them. This is much like worldly sentiments observing warmth and cold, and people's faces following the rise and fall of circumstances.
Cishou said: "To those coming from the south, I give them one smile; to those coming from the north, I give them another smile."
It seems much like joyful banter; there is a blade within the laughter. If it were Jiaoshan, however, it would be otherwise.
He would treat those coming from the south with equanimity, and he would treat those coming from the north with equanimity. He would neither be angry nor laugh.
There is neither low nor high. Why? Because in a world of pure peace, there is no need for weapons. The *Chāoyáng* verse says:

"When it is cold, one must urgently use that which is essential; seize the warmth to apply some needle and thread. Suddenly, when the twelfth month arrives, you will avoid having your feet flustered and hands in chaos.
The verse on facing the moon says: "Having first seen a mere glimmer of light, one seeks to resolve the final matter."

[The Master] said, "If it were a fist with no opening, I would not strike such a dull-witted fellow. Later in life, the Master grew weary of the mallet and whisk and lived in a hermitage by West Lake;
yet his students remained numerous. Emperor Lizong summoned him to Xuande Hall to preach the Dharma, whereupon he prayed for rain and achieved a miraculous response.
By imperial decree, he was granted a golden-embroidered dharma robe and the title "Fuyan" (Buddha-Eye).

Chan Master Shichuang Zhuyan Miaoyin of Changsha Prefecture was the son of the Wan family of Jinxian. He received his monastic training under Shaotan of Longtang and traveled widely to consult various masters.
He remained for the longest period at Longmen with Guangchidun Ying. Upon arriving at Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou, he went to pay his respects to Yue-lin.
During an entry into the inner chamber, Yue-lin asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "A rat gnaws."
He broke a lamp bowl. Lin nodded in agreement. He resided successively at several monasteries, later moving to Shishuang. While reading the sutras by moonlight, he composed this verse:
"The patterns and colors are revealed before the tongue has moved; The five thousand scrolls are completed all at once.

If one says they must wait for the moon to open the volume again, I dare guarantee that even in a donkey’s year, they will not have reached the end. In his later years, he built a hermitage called Zixia (Purple Mist). Prime Minister Zhao...
Kui resided in his private residence in the village of Yanju. He once invited a master to discuss the Way.

On the twenty-third day of the eighth month of the year Baimao of the Baoyu era of Emperor Lizong, he wrote a verse: "Sixty-nine years, all for one great dream; let us return home—take care, take care!
Having finished writing, he passed away peacefully. His stupa was erected at Zixia.
Chan Master Deshou of Nanshan Gufeng in Xinghua Prefecture was a native of the Chen family of Lianjiang, Fuzhou. He received the tonsure at Hanshan in Suzhou.
On ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase? Xuefeng remained silent for a long while.
The monk brought this up to Changsheng. Changsheng said, "This is the second phrase. Feng then instructed the monk to ask Changsheng, "What is the first phrase?
Changsheng said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said: "These two great elders handled the matter in such a way that one would shed tears of heart-wrenching pain.
As for the first phrase, they have not yet seen it even in their dreams. Suppose someone were to suddenly ask Yishan: [what would he say?]"
"What is the first phrase? [The Master] simply said to him: "The sword has long since been gone. Ascending the hall, Zhenjing said:
"The Ascetic’s Rock is shrouded in moss; Peak of Thrown Pens is entangled by *bìlì* vines. At Luohan Monastery, three novices are ordained each year;
at Guizong Monastery, one drinks tea after the formal meditation session concludes. The Master said: "Do you all wish to understand? Listen."
Take one verse: When the sky clears and the sun rises, rain falls and the ground becomes damp. I have spoken my heart’s content;
I only fear you will not believe it.
The twentieth generation under Dajian.

The Verse Composed by Chan Master Shigong Yu of Xuefeng in Fuzhou Prefecture, Successor of Chan Master Huazang Jing, in Venerating the Stupa of Xuefeng: "Entering Min Province, I was already over forty years old;
I bound my dwelling beneath the cliffs of Elephant Bone Peak. Who would say that this is after the era of Emperor Kaiping? In the spring fields, the mist..."

Yu Ji-li-chu. Chan Master Xiangjiang Mou of Tiantong, Ningbo Prefecture, was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Tiantong. He held the position for forty years; his appearance was withered and emaciated.

His governance of the assembly was solitary and stern, and his words were sharp and piercing. His voice was like a great bell. During the reign of Emperor Lizong, he received imperial favor three times.
Xixi addressed the assembly, saying: "A sunny spring day; the oriole sings. How most intimate! Who understands to listen?
When Chijue was presiding at Yujisi, he once sent a verse that contained the lines: "A thousand-fathom waterfall, its atmosphere fresh; a single roar before the cliff, all dust is cleared away.
As he was about to enter extinction, he looked toward his attendant monk and said: "A smile, turning over—Sun Face, Moon Face. Thereupon, he passed away.
He passed away while holding his brush.
Zen Master Kongyan You of Zhongzhu Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture, a dharma successor of Zen Master Jingshan Jue, once offered this instruction within his quarters: "Cast in pure gold."
Tie (Iron). The Real Man Donghai Yong once composed a verse that says: "A young lord in brocade robes, drunk at a peasant’s home, Slept soundly upon a wooden bed as the sun had not yet slanted.
Thirsty and parched, he called for water but found none; He thus traded his jade belt for a bowl of tea."
Chan Master Jingci Qianlai Shanqing of Hangzhou Prefecture was the son of the Peng family of Yanling.

Orphaned at the age of seven, he had no fixed abode and followed his maternal uncle’s example in studying Confucianism. He went to visit Huai Chu, who recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and asked, "Are you able to leave the household life?
The Master replied, "It is indeed my original vow. Huai Chu then ordained him, whereupon he received the full precepts and disciplined his person with great rigor.
Yan traveled extensively throughout various regions without attaining realization. Later, hearing that Jing-sou was presiding over Jingci Monastery, he went there to rely on him as a disciple.

One day, upon hearing the master cite the story of Dongshan’s "three pounds of flax," he suddenly awakened to its profound meaning. He subsequently took up the monastic leadership at Baoguan in Yixing, later moved to Tianning in Jiahe, and finally ascended the throne of Jingci.
He once composed the *Fuzong xianzheng lun* (Treatise on Supporting the School and Manifesting Orthodoxy), which Emperor Renzong read and...

The Emperor praised him and bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya* and the honorary title "Huiguang Puzhao Wencming Tongbian" (Wisdom Light Universally Shining, Civilized and Luminous Penetrating Eloquence).
When he retired from his duties, he built a residence called "Guixiu" (Retirement) and lived there in tranquil repose as if floating in emptiness.
He passed away on the third day of the eighth month of the Wuyin year of the Yuan Zhizheng era at the age of seventy-nine.
Chan Master Wuji of Baolin Temple in Jinhua Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyinquan, ascended the hall and spoke. He cited a verse by Miaoxi on the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra*:
"Abiding at all times, do not give rise to deluded thoughts; yet do not attempt to extinguish those deluded minds. Dwelling within the realm of deluded perceptions, do not apply further discernment."

[The monk] said, "I know. [The Master] said, "To not understand that which is beyond comprehension and to fail to discern the reality is like this: 'The lotus leaves are round and round, as round as mirrors;
the water chestnut angles are sharp and sharp, as sharp as awls. The wind blows the willow catkins like floating balls; the rain beats the pear blossoms and the butterflies fly. The Master said:
Miaoxi may be called the peach and plum blossoms; they together form a single family. Shuanglin is not so.
"Having been in Bingzhou for ten years, my heart longs for Xianyang day and night. Without cause, I have crossed the Sanggan River again; looking back toward Bingzhou, it is my true hometown.
[He] ascended the hall. "Reeds face the red of the smartweed; the trees have fallen, and the mountains reveal their bones. It is like..."
Yangzhou. It resembles the Kingdom of Yue. Holding up his staff, he strikes it once and says: "For you, I strike through the cave of the spirit;
the True Man of No Rank is stark naked."
Chan Master Chou-an Zong, of the Huguo Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Huanglong Kai, ascended the hall for a discourse. He cited Fenggan’s words to Hanshan and Shide:
"If you and I go to tour Mount Wutai, you will be of my same kind. Hanshan said, "You go to tour Mount Wutai..."
Tai asked, "What is it? Gan replied, "I am prostrating to Mañjuśrī. Shan said, "You are not of my kind. The Master said, "When Fenggan opens his mouth, it does not depend on his tongue;
when Hanshan and Shide are in the same pit, there is no difference in the soil. To examine this closely, two hunchbacks have run into each other;
from the beginning of the world, there has never been a straight man. He then ascended the hall and cited the story of Yue-lin Zhen.
Addressing the assembly, Lin said, "The mouth of the market bag is open; is there anyone who would buy? A monk said, "There is.
Lin said, "Neither cheap nor expensive—how will you buy it? The monk was speechless. Lin said, "I, this old monk, have lost the profit.
The Master said, "Yuelin set up this question-stem; it is truly extraordinary. Yet when confronted by someone saying the word 'there is,' he was immediately at a loss for where to hide."
In the west, they were covered; there was no time to hide them away. Today, Huguo opens the mouth of his sack.
Is there anyone who would buy it? After a long silence, he said: "Though we lean upon the same railing, we view the mountain colors differently."
Chan Master Huiyun Wuchuan of Hangzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Buddha after Buddha has expounded extensively, yet even great wisdom cannot know it.

Patriarch after Patriarch has transmitted it, yet ordinary sentiments cannot fathom it. Before heaven and after earth, through formation and destruction, it endures forever. Entering death and being born, coming and going, it remains unchanged.
To realize this [truth] is already to enter the realm of fragmentation; if you have not yet done so, listen to this mountain monk."
To provide a further annotation, he struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "Crying until the blood flows is of no avail;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring."
Chan Master Wujian Xialu of Huazang in Wenzhou Prefecture cited the story of Xinghua beating Kebin. His verse says:
Xinghua beat Kebin; The words were intimate, the speech was intimate. From the tip of the staff, like falling raindrops, He struck forth the Jade Qilin.

During the Chunyou era, the lay practitioner Yu of Hangzhou Prefecture, who had formerly been a cowherd, went to visit Wumen. Whenever he asked a question, Wumen would block him head-on, saying, "Not so!
Not so! Later, when Yu met Chou’an, he said, "What have you seen, Master, that you dare to distort right and wrong before this assembly of gods and humans?
Chou’an replied, "When I was with Wumen, there was no dharma to be attained, and no path."
It can be transmitted, yet there are only two characters. The scholar asked, "What are these two characters? The Hermit said, "Not so, not so.

At this, the scholar attained great enlightenment; he finally understood that the Gateless Gate has no place for human artifice. He once established the "Barrier of Is and Not-Is" to test what others had realized, saying:

"Directly pointing at the human mind, seeing one's nature and attaining Buddhahood—turning the light back to reflect within, it is utterly free from all obstruction. As soon as one attempts to conceive of it..."
As for measurement: white clouds ten thousand miles away. Encountering people, one evaluates them; meeting things, one critiques them with "purple and yellow" (i.e., praises and blames).

Valuing the ancient while disparaging the present, esteeming what is heard while degrading what is seen—let them indulge in their own conjectures and hesitations; they have not yet dreamed of the gate of right and wrong. How can they penetrate it? For now, look!
What is the primary meaning? To answer it, one must not break one's teeth; instead, one displays spiritual powers to cross the river in secret.
There is a portion of restless toil that does not approach the noble; bring forth your mind and I shall settle it for you. Great pain is soundless, piercing to the very bone with a chilling cold.
Picking leaves and seeking branches is not the mark of a master hand; the Western Heaven remains dark and vast as ever. Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell;
the swallow carries away the spring colors. When the cuckoo cries, snow fills the sky; ten thousand points of fallen red are the rain of longing. Where there is no Buddha, pass by in haste;
the Precious Hall of the Awakened King, one refuses to sit within. Six years of cultivation, then departing the mountains.
"Come! Only then will you believe that the axe-head is made of iron. Laywoman Shen Dao-po of Anji County asked, "How many phrases are there regarding the barrier of right and wrong?
The Master said, "There are four phrases. The laywoman asked, "How do you cite these four phrases? The Master said, "The first phrase..."

"It is" and "it is not"—this is unacceptable. This is the second phrase. "Neither 'is' nor 'is not'"—this is also unacceptable. This is the third phrase. "'Is' and 'is not'"—this is also unacceptable.
This is the fourth phrase. "Neither 'is' nor 'is not'"—this too is unacceptable. Only when one is free from these four phrases does one finally behold the natural radiance of the original ground.
[The Master] asked, "Have you been able to free yourself from them? The scholar replied, "I have not been able to free myself."
[The Master] said, "Every person has their own lot; how could I avoid what I cannot escape? The scholar said, "When a chicken is married off, it flies after the chicken;
when a dog is married off, it runs after the dog. [The Master] asked, "What is the scenery of the original ground? The scholar said, "The crescent moon shines upon how many islands?
How many people rejoice, and how many grieve? [The Master] said, "I am not asking about this scenery. The scholar said, "Then which scenery are you asking about?"
He said, "There is no basis for the marks of male or female. The scholar said, "Since there are no marks of male or female, what is the point of asking about right and wrong?
He said, "Is there something further beyond this, or not? The scholar said, "There is. He asked, "What is this thing further beyond?
The scholar said, "A horse-leech bites the leg of a heron; when you ascend to heaven, I shall ascend to heaven as well."
Chan Master Wanshan Xiu of the Nangshan lineage was Chan Master Zhengning Wanshan of Gushan in Fuzhou Prefecture, a native of the Li family of Taihu in Shuzhou.
At the age of seventeen, after both his parents had passed away, he went to Daoying at Shuangquan in Huangzhou to receive the tonsure; he subsequently received full ordination at Ezu.
In the Kaiyuan era, he first attended upon the Third Patriarch Huan’an Lian; next, he attended upon Zhongshan Chijue Chong and Changlu Nanshan Zhe, but found no resonance with them.
Later, he attended upon Wuming Xing at Shuangta. Wuming asked, “What was the intent behind Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall?
The Master replied, “There is a principle that is difficult to extend. Wuming struck him a blow across the chest with his fist, and the Master suddenly attained realization. He then said:
That which I have used throughout my life was shattered like crumbling walls or melting ice by that old fellow’s single punch.

Entering Min to pay respects at Gufeng, the Master raised the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature; the Teacher could not answer. After more than half a year, he finally attained the innermost depths and presented this verse:
"Zhaozhou says 'no'—the arrow does not miss its mark. Striking it, hitting it, one is fully alive and fully present."
"Kill! Feng said, "You have attained it, but you are not yet there. One day, Feng raised the story of Deshan seeing Longtan and asked, "Where is the place where Deshan reached his own ground?
The Master covered Feng’s mouth with his hand and said, "The pond does not see the dragon;
the dragon does not appear. His entire body is already within the Hall of the Empty King. Returning from a dream, he suddenly hears the dawn oriole singing; the spring wind has fallen away."
Tao Hua Pian. Feng said, "Only today do you know that the Great Sage of Sizhou does not appear in Yangzhou.

He then appointed him to serve as the incense attendant. When Feng moved to Xichan and Nanshan, the Master attended him in both places. After Feng passed away, he went to Deng Shigu and subsequently relied upon Xuefeng and Shuanglin, where he indeed served as the head of the board.
In the Ding-si year of the Baoyu era, he appeared in the world at Fuzhou.
Diaotai. Qian Wansui. After a long time, the Grand Tutor Chancellor Jia invited him to reside at Gushan. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "It has been only three days since entering the monastery;
I am busy attending to social obligations. Yet the lanterns and the pillar are deliberating closely and intimately.
But tell me, what are they deliberating about? He struck the meditation seat and said: "Last night, the blue sky was calm and the wind and waves stilled; a single bright orb [shone]."

The moon reflects upon Luojiang River. Ascending the hall: On the first day of the sixth month, summer is already mid-way. Lotus flowers bloom upon the water’s surface; lychee fruits reflect the mountain’s crimson hue.
The True Man of No Rank meets one everywhere. To hesitate is like facing ten thousand layers of clouds and mountains.
Gushan enters the monastery and ascends the hall. Holding up his staff, he says: "Lay down the adze for tending the mountain; pick up the Patriarch’s sacred [staff]."
[He] struck the staff once and said: "A single arrow pierces three passes; the sharp edge of the pivot is like a flash of lightning.

Meeting the source on both left and right, the full mechanism of killing and giving life reaches such a point that Dading Peak and Xiaoding Peak look up at the sky and rub their foreheads in admiration;
Baiyun Pavilion and Yongquan Pavilion nod their heads from within smiles. At this very moment, tell me: where does the merit reside? Relying on his staff, he said: "Carved."
The bow has been hung and the smoke of war has ceased; ten thousand nations come to court to celebrate the peace of the age. To the assembly:

where the myriad affairs of state do not reach, even the thousand sages knit their brows. When the true command is being exercised, who dares to attempt to fathom it? To understand it in such a way already falls into the second level of truth (the conventional).
It is much like hoping for plums to quench one's thirst—what joy is there in that? For the patch-robed monks, take this black bean...
Son, to change a person’s eyes, to pull tight the binding rope, and to pierce a person’s nostrils—this is not considered going beyond the ordinary.

But tell me, what principle do these patch-robed monks perceive? He strikes the meditation staff and says: "If one lacked such an eye for selecting a Buddha, how could the wind of the ancestral school have reached the present day?
He then cites Xuefeng, who addressed the assembly, saying: "This matter is not obtained from the lips; it is not..."
"It was obtained from the yellow scrolls; it was not obtained from the venerable elders of various quarters.

From where, then, could it have been obtained? You must speak with great care. He spoke in verse: "A single drop of true pearl, red as fermented wine; With earnest entreaty, he urged me two or three times.

When the Master of the East’s intent was finally exhausted, I swallowed the cup offered at the moment of departure as I mounted my horse. As his end approached, he gathered the members of the two orders and addressed them.
Leaving behind his final instructions, he took up his brush and wrote a verse, saying: "Eighty-four years are like a single dream;
when the dream breaks, all returns to emptiness—there is not the slightest thing remaining. He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Jie of Shuanglin in Jinhua Prefecture inscribed this on a portrait of Master Fu:
Neither Confucian, nor Daoist, nor yet Chan, His fabricated practice is truly pitiable. Leaving his single body neglected for three lifetimes, Until now, more than eight hundred years have passed.

Chan Master Zhonghe Zhang of Daqing Shou Temple in Shuntian Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Haixi Hai, instructed his disciples within his quarters by sometimes brandishing a wooden sword or holding a silken snake.
When Haiyun Jian came to inquire, he asked: "I have come without coming; how do you receive me?"
[The monk] saw [the master]. The Master said, "In Zen practice, you must practice truly; in awakening, you must awaken truly. Do not strike the firebrand in the wild.

[The monk] said, "Because the sparks flew out when I struck [the flint], I realized that my eyebrows are horizontal and my nose is straight. The Master said, "In this place of mine, it is different. [The monk] asked, "How can one express this conviction? The Master said:
"My teeth are but a single piece of bone; my ears are but two pieces of skin. Jujian said, "I thought there was something else. The Master said, "Wrong.
Jujian shouted, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated! The Master then desisted.

The next day, the Master raised the story of Linji’s two head monks shouting at the same time, leading up to the dialogue on "guest and host being distinct. He asked, "How do you understand such talk? Jujian—
[The Master] said: "Break the mirror of the Qin dynasty; sharpen the ancient awl. When the dragon soars beyond the clouds and mists, why need one further use needle or awl?

The teacher said: "You have grasped its mechanism, but you have not mastered its function. [The Master] simply and abruptly overturned the meditation seat. The teacher said: *Note: This passage describes a classic encounter dialogue (wenda) between a master and a student. The student's initial response is praised for its cleverness ("grasping the mechanism"), yet the teacher critiques it for lacking practical application ("not mastering the function"). The student's final action—overturning the seat—is a demonstration of spontaneous, functional realization.*
"The joy of the journey has not yet reached home. Jǐan gave him a slap and said, "A spirit for a thousand years in a wild fox den;
now that it has been seen through, it is not worth a penny. The Master struck him with a whisk and said, "You have attained only its function, not its essence.
Jǐan stepped forward and said, "The green mountains tower with cold hues; the moon shines upon a springtime stream. The Master said, "You have attained only..."
[Zhaozhou] could not grasp its essence. Xiangyan Jian said, "The flowing water moves east and west; the falling flowers have no preference for front or back.
The Master said, "Though you are skilled in the samādhi of eloquent speech, you simply fail to reach the point. Jian raised his fist and gave a single clap, causing the entire hall to shake.
The Master said, "So it is, so it is. Jian then shook out his sleeves and departed.
Chan Master Gelu Tan cited a monk’s question to Shixi: “What is the Buddha? Shixi replied, “A short man watching a play.
He offered this verse: Majestic is the sixteen-foot purple-gold countenance; In the arena of a hundred performances, there is transformation and penetration.
When the short man looks on, his eyebrows stand upright; The iron awl has no hole—it dances in the spring breeze.

Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhongzhu You of the twenty-first generation under Dajian (Daokai) of the Linji school.
Chan Master Xinyuan Wenyong of Zhijue on Mount Kai at Shimen, Jiaxing Prefecture, ascended the hall and said:

"The ultimate pivot of the upward path, the final secret—this was not transmitted by Buddhas or Patriarchs, and all sages have been left speechless. Is there anyone here who can turn themselves around and breathe freely?
Come forth and convey this news. A monk asked: "The opening of the mountain with a chisel-axe has existed since antiquity; what about the Master?"
"Now that the Shimen Pass has newly opened, I have come by way of this road; may I ask you a question? The Master said, "Bring me your official pass.
The man asked, "Who is the master of the pass? The Master replied, "The Mohe sword is held crosswise in my hand; I am specially skilled at beheading the dull and obstinate."

The monk hesitated to speak. The Master gave a shout. The monk bowed. The Master said, "You foolish, stubborn fellow! Then he said, "Before one's eyes, mountains and rivers fill the view, utterly free from a speck of dust;
the boundless oceans of lands surround themselves naturally. The pavilions of Vairocana appear layer upon layer—who beholds them?
Every door has a Sudhana. He struck his staff down and said, "The Stone Gate is opened; the true field of awakening is revealed. Come as you please from the south."
Small Assembly for Those Coming from the North. To raise the banner of the Dharma and establish the fundamental principle—this is clearly the Buddha’s command at Caoxi.
Great assembly, while raising the banner of the Dharma is certainly necessary, what is it that establishes the fundamental principle?
Is it the three turns and five turns, the raising of the fist, or the shout? Is it remaining silent upon the seat, or shaking the sleeves and departing? Is it speech?
Are you taking ancient texts to confirm your views on the present? Is it not the case that you have a head of ash and a face of dust, sitting long without lying down?

You must be most careful. If your true eye is not clear, you will fall entirely into partiality, error, and stagnation. Therefore it is said: "The supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) is prized by the world;
yet when encountered by such people as these, it turns instead into a poisonous drug. Under the gate of our Patriarchs, throughout the ten...
The ten directions of the world are this seamless iron wall; Bodhidharma did not recognize it.
The entire universe is this unperforated iron hammer; Kāśyapa did not know it. There is no place for you to deliberate, no place for you to take up.

Turning heaven and earth, shifting the Dipper and the stars, releasing both simultaneously and gathering both simultaneously, penetrating from top to bottom—do you understand? With a sweep of the dragon’s sleeve...
The entire manifestation is revealed. Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes are severed. A monk asked, "Ultimately, what is the fundamental principle of establishing [the teaching]?
The Master said, "I will tell you in a moment."
The layman Lü Ti-chuan, a successor of Chan Master Fengfan, was born to his mother, Lady Qin, who dreamed that the Abbot of Gong’an Ersheng, Fuyan You, came to their home.
When Lü reached the age of twenty, he went to study under Kōsan. One day, Kōsan asked him, "Have you ever seen Zhaozhou?"
The official shouted in a stern voice, "No! The mountain retreats. He would often say to others, "I am a person of the second birth.
The official once served as the Regional Commander-in-Chief for Jianghuai; he subsequently established Yongshou Temple in Jiading, Suzhou, to welcome monks from all quarters.
His compositions, including his responses to the *Shanju shi* (Poems on Dwelling in the Mountains) of Yongming and other verses, all transcended his contemporaries and surpassed the mundane.
When Daomou offered incense, he said: "Coming from the West, you did not fulfill the Emperor of Liang’s intent; departing for the West, you carried nothing but a single sandal.
If one speaks of wondrous function and spiritual powers, what true monk would even count you? After nine years facing the wall, you finally stepped forth to receive [the Dharma]."
One person was obtained, yet he too was without arms; his robes and alms bowl were passed down to Lu Neng. From this point on, the entanglements grew without end;
the transgressions fill the heavens, while not a drop of water remains in the source stream. Today marks the anniversary of the忌辰 (jichén) of seven hundred and eighty-six years ago.
Which descendant would not feel a pain that pierces to the very marrow of their bones? With a single incense seal in the burner and a single bowl of tea, one repays their kindness.
This is one who has betrayed their kindness. I wish to raise my fist to show it to them, yet pity that they have already lost their front teeth.
Master Huazang, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Tianran of Jinyizhiling on Mount Yangshan in Suzhou Prefecture, addressed the assembly: "The entrustment at Vulture Peak..."

Cutting through the undergrowth of entanglements; the single transmission of Shaoshi became a den of right and wrong for all quarters. To settle the mind and repent of offenses, one must break open the lacquer bucket so it may shine once more.

In the transmission of the Dharma and the handing down of the robe, lingering in worldly conduct is but a vain effort at haggling over price. In the lineage of Muzhou and Yangshan, everything is perfectly round without a seam;
standing like a wall, it is devoid of center or periphery. In the Linji school, the true eye is opened by the staff; one’s lifelong livelihood is revealed beneath the fist. In the Caoxi school...
Dongshan: "A brocade curtain embroidered with mandarin ducks is difficult for travelers to see. Yunmen: "The three phrases can be discerned; a single arrowhead pierces the vast void. Fayan:

Today, for the sake of you all, I shall resolve this public case. Look, look! [He raises his staff.]

He drew a line with his staff and said: "The waves of the four seas are stilled; the dragon sleeps soundly. The clouds of the nine heavens are clear; the crane flies high. He then cited the words of Sansheng:

With staff in hand, two people pull it along; cease looking at the thousand peaks soaring toward the clouds. Behold the Milky Way falling from the Nine Heavens.
[The Master] cites the story of Śāriputra entering the city and Candrottarā leaving the city, and offers this verse: Leaving the city and entering the marketplace, the two meet face to face;
who says that their paths of coming and going are different? Turning one's head to gaze upon the Terrace of Nirvāṇa, the nine provinces and the four seas are but one.

The Master said, "Do not interpret this as being about Zen. At these words, Yuan was suddenly awakened from his dream.

The Hall. Six years in the Snowy Mountains—a mistake. Suddenly beholding the morning star—a mistake. Rushing down the mountain—another mistake. A mistake, a mistake!
