"The Dharma has always been right before one's eyes; it is people themselves who distance themselves from it. He then spoke this verse: "Time and again we meet face-to-face, yet do not recognize each other.
How many times have our innate vital energies been exhausted! At midnight, suddenly forgetting the pointing finger at the moon, A single red orb bursts forth from the void.
He went to see Zhiyan. As soon as Yan saw him, he shouted, "Where have you seen gods or ghosts come from? The Master—
[Zhaozhou] said, "Today I have caught the thief. Yanguan asked, "Where are the stolen goods? The Master then gave a shout.
Yanguan said, "Neither opening the mouth nor closing the mouth is right; bring forth what lies beyond this. The Master said, "Clearly manifest throughout the entire world, nothing is concealed.
Yanguan picked up his bamboo staff, and the Master overturned the meditation seat. Yanguan said, "You dare to come here and pull at the tiger's whiskers! and he struck him repeatedly.

Three times he was summoned [to court], and by imperial decree was appointed as an attendant. In the *Xinwei* year of the Zhishun era, he emerged into the world at Wushi in Li, remaining there for sixteen years before moving to Shixi in Guangde.
On the day he ascended the hall to give his inaugural sermon, a monk asked: "Having distanced yourself from Wushi Ridge to come to Stone Creek Mountain, you reveal the path for humans and devas;
how does one penetrate the Patriarchs' barrier? The Master said: "A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick, which..."
[The monk] shattered a piece of blue lapis lazuli and said, "In that case, we do not recognize one another face-to-face; yet from a thousand miles away, our ways may be the same.

The Master said, "Layer upon layer are the mountain passes and roads. [The monk] said, "Bodhidharma came from the West not to establish written words, but to point directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one becomes a Buddha.
Since he did not establish written words, how is it that they have been transmitted down to the present day? The Master said, "The official seal does not permit even a needle to pass."
[The Master] personally provided carriages and horses [for the guest]. [The guest] said, "Directly pointing at the human mind. [The Master asked,] "Which mind do you point to?

The Master replied, "Opening the mouth is not a matter of the tongue. [The guest] said, "Seeing one's nature is attaining Buddhahood. [The Master asked,] "Where is this nature? The Master replied, "Thirty-six thousand acres of Lake Tai;
night after night, the moonlight shines upon the waves. [The guest] said, "I recall Master Fu Daoshi saying: 'Empty-handed, holding a hoe...'"
"Walking while riding a water buffalo; a person passes over a bridge. The bridge flows, yet the water does not flow. "What is the meaning of this?

The Master said, "Above all, do not let it slip past you right before your face. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then when there is spirit, one adds to that spirit; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
The Master said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are as far apart. [The monk] said, "Let us set this matter aside for now."

In the sutra it says: "The great wealthy elder is none other than the Tathāgata. Does this refer to [the realization] accumulated over many kalpas, or does it refer to the realization attained in this present life?
The Master said: "The stream is deep where the flowers fall far away; the mountain is high where the tree shadows stretch long. [A monk asked:
"Today the layman Zhixin is establishing a practice site at Shixi and has invited the Master to reside there. Are these two cases the same or different? The Master said:
"When the lion roars, the fragrant grasses turn green; where the elephant king walks, the hundred flowers turn red. A monk asked, "If it is thus, what karmic fruit is obtained?
The Master said, "Life after life one returns to the Buddha-ground; age after age one delights in the realms of humans and devas. He ascended the hall and said: "The Great Way has no form;
it is beyond names and transcends signs. There is no need for cultivation or realization; how could it involve verbal expression? The seventeen hundred patriarchs..."
Section. Look closely: this is merely relying on others to form interpretations, which obstructs the gate of self-awakening.

If you wish to sweep away this tangle and cut off all superficial discourse, you must, at the very moment the Old Man of Yellow Face was about to hold up the flower—and before the Kāñcana-dhūta had even smiled—immediately overturn the meditation seat and shout to disperse the assembly, thereby freeing yourself.
"Let the descendants of future generations exhaust all their wiles and stratagems. Today, this mountain monk will not point east or sketch west;
I shall directly deliver a message to you all. After a long silence, he said: "The heavens are high and the myriad forms are upright; the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them.
In the twelfth month of the Gengxu year of the Hongwu era, he manifested a slight illness. He wrote a verse, saying: "Birth is originally..."
Birth and extinction are fundamentally non-extinguishing. With a sudden letting go of the hand, he departed; under a bright moon across the sky, he cast down his brush and passed away.
His entire remains were enshrined in the Ciyun Pagoda Courtyard at Wushi. He was seventy years of age and fifty years since his ordination.
Chan Master Nichuan Zhishun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Tianbao Shu. He was a native of the Chen family of Ruian, Wenzhou.
His mother venerated an image of the Great Master Zhiyi with great devotion. One night, she dreamed of a monk with a halo around his head traveling upstream along the river.
He said, "I shall become your son. Upon waking, she conceived. When the child was born, his excellent qualities were already fully formed from past lives.
At the age of seven, he followed his uncle, the śramaṇa Huiguang, at Chongxing Temple. Upon reaching adulthood, he received full ordination and traversed the ocean of doctrinal meaning.

Suddenly, he abandoned it all and went to Min, where he sought to stay under the tutelage of Tianbao of Tieguan. Tieguan rebuked him, saying, "A man of stature does not [seek refuge] with one who is not great..."

The monastic communities were vying for preeminence; he thought, "Is this all there is? He withdrew his body and entered [the monastery]. When the Master arrived at the guest quarters (dan-guo) the following morning, he wept bitterly.
Hearing of this, Guankai ordered him to enter the hall for formal practice. From that point on, the Master stood firm like a wall ten thousand fathoms high, with no distinction between day and night.

After more than a month, while using the toilet, he saw a gourd vine in the garden; this triggered an immediate awakening, and he felt as though the great earth had suddenly become level and submerged. He ran to see Guankai, who said:
This was merely his first entry into the gate. As for that one phrase pointing beyond, it spans thousands and tens of thousands of miles—and yet another half-year passed.
One day, he suddenly spoke in a stern voice to Guanyou, saying, "Nanquan has broken through the barrier; I have seen it now. Guanyou asked, "It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing—what is it?
The Master replied, "The ground is paved with bricks; the roof is covered with tiles. Guanyou said, "Nanquan..."
"Quanyou, where are you now? The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla. Guankai said, "Wrong. The Master also said, "Wrong.

Guankai said, "Wrong, wrong. The Master bowed and withdrew. He was then appointed to manage the treasury keys; shortly thereafter, he was ordered to share the seat with the Master to preach the Dharma.

When Guanzu passed away, the Master succeeded him in leading the affairs of the monastery. Before long, he abandoned his post and crossed the Yangtze River into Huai province, where he paid homage at the stupas of various patriarchs.
Returning from Jianye to Zhejiang, he soon went back to Yongjia. He established Ba’en Monastery in Ruian and later moved to serve as the abbot of Jiangxin.
He further founded Guiyuan in Pingyang. The imperial court bestowed upon him the official plaque of the monastery, a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya*, and the title Fóxìng Yuán (Buddha-nature Yuan).
Chan Master Bian was invited by the Chancellor Yan Zhibuhua, who was stationed in Min, to reside at Dongchan Xuefeng Monastery.

At the beginning of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict summoned ten eminent monks of realized virtue to hold an assembly at Mount Zhongshan. The Master responded to this summons and ascended the seat to preach the Dharma;

the Emperor visited in person and bestowed upon him the utmost consolation and honor. Upon returning south, he was appointed as the abbot of Jingci Monastery. In the sixth year [of his tenure], he was again summoned to the capital.
Shortly thereafter, he manifested a slight illness. Having bathed and recited a verse, he passed away while seated.
Chan Master Lingjiu Bibeng Baogin of Wutai Mountain in Taiyuan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhen of Jin’yun; his secular surname was Shi, and he was from Yongshou in Qianzhou.
His son was named Yiming Zhou. His parents were devoted to the good. A śramaṇa bestowed upon them an image of Avalokiteśvara. Not long after, the Master was born;

at the time of his birth, a white light filled the room. When he was just six years old, his parents commanded him to leave the household life. After undergoing tonsure and receiving the precepts, he traveled extensively among the lecture halls, but suddenly sighed that this was not the path, and so he changed his robes.
He went to see Ruhai Zhen in Jin-yun, where he applied himself with diligence day and night. Once, by chance—
Carrying a basket and gathering vegetables, [Fengxue] suddenly sat down and remained motionless. After three periods had passed, he finally awoke. Zhen asked, "Did you enter meditative absorption?
The Master replied, "Yes. Zhen asked, "What did you see? The Master replied, "I have attained realization. Zhen asked, "How is it that you have realized this?
The Master held up the basket to show him. Zhen said, "It is not that. The Master set the basket on the ground and stood with his hands clasped in reverence. Zhen spoke again: "It is not..."

"It is so," [the Master] replied. The Teacher then gave a shout. Zhen lunged forward, seized him by the chest, and said, "Speak! Speak! The Teacher clenched his fist and struck him. Zhen said, "Not yet. This is merely a temporary cessation of worldly toil.
You must sever the path of the mind and penetrate the Patriarchal Barrier; only then will the Great Dharma be clarified.
From that time on, the Teacher did not let his side touch the mat for three years. One day, hearing the sound of wood being felled, he broke into a sweat as if pouring.
It rained. [Zhaozhou] then said, "The ancients said, 'There were eighteen great awakenings and countless small awakenings.

How could they have deceived me? Only today do I finally understand what occurred before birth. He went at once to see Xuanzhen. Xuanzhen did not grant him an audience. The Master overturned the meditation seat and left.
The following day he went to see Xuanzhen again. Xuanzhen drew a circle on the ground; the Master brushed it away with his sleeve. Xuanzhen—
Again, he drew a circle. The Master drew a single line within the circle and then wiped it away.
He drew another circle; the Master drew a cross within the circle and then wiped it away. He drew yet another as before;
the Master made a *svastika* at the corners of the cross and then wiped it away. The student laughed loudly and said, "Are there no one in the world who has realized the Way through study?"

He was able to clarify the great function of the spiritual capacity; how many others could there possibly be like him? He was subsequently granted a prediction of enlightenment and commanded to go to the region of Shuofang, where the Way would be widely propagated.
Previously, while in meditative concentration, the Master had seen a mountain of exquisite beauty, with multi-storied pavilions and magnificent halls shimmering in gold and green.
Bodhisattvas were practicing the Path therein, and one of them beckoned to the Master, saying, "This is Bimozha Rock. You..."
He practiced the Way therein; why have you so hastily forgotten it?

Later, while the Master was traveling to Mount Tai, he encountered a woman with disheveled hair, wearing tattered garments of five colors and walking barefoot at a slow pace, followed by a black mastiff. The Master asked where she was going, and she replied:
He entered the mountains. A master asked him, "For what purpose have you entered the mountains? He replied, "I do not enter for any purpose whatsoever. Having finished speaking, he vanished.
When his companions searched for him, they could not find him; they realized he was an emanation of Mañjuśrī. Consequently, the master established the Lingjiu Hermitage in the mountains.

He waited for those who would come from afar. Monastics and laypeople, hearing of his reputation, flocked to him; at times their number reached ten thousand. In the winter of the Wuzi year of the Zhi Zheng era, he was summoned to the inner court.
During a great snowfall, a crimson light emerged from the master’s chamber at night and pierced straight through to the heavens.

The Emperor was struck with wonder and bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya*. The following year, his prayers for rain were immediately answered, and by imperial decree he was granted the title "Great Chan Master Jizhao Yuanming."

The Master’s title was [inserted]. By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Haerin Temple. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he was summoned to the capital to reside at Tianjie Temple; his exposition of the Dharma pleased the Emperor.
In the *Xinhai* year, a Pujihui (Universal Salvation Assembly) was established on Mount Zhong, and the Master was commanded to preside over its proceedings.

He was granted *ipubo* (vegetarian) offerings, and the Emperor personally visited him, bestowing a poem written in his own calligraphy. In the sixth month of the *Renzi* year, he bathed, changed his robes, assembled the congregation to bid them farewell, and passed away. His younger brother...
The disciple requested a verse. The Master said, "Even the Tripitaka and the twelve divisions of the scriptures are but old paper;

what need is there for my words? He sat upright and then closed his eyes. His worldly age was sixty-five, and his monastic seniority was fifty-nine. Upon cremation, his relics were formed in five colors.
His teeth and gums were all intact.
Chan Master Wumen Sichong of Xiangyan in Ruzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Cihua Qiong. He was a native of Xiangshan. Initially, he studied under Dufeng, who instructed him to contemplate:

Regarding the saying, "This mind is not the Buddha, nor is it an object," Yunfeng, Yueshan, and five others—six people in total—established a covenant to investigate this matter together to its ultimate conclusion.
Subsequently, they went to see Wuneng Chao of Huaixi, who instructed them to take up the "Mu" (No) kōan for investigation.
One day, while with his fellow practitioners, he met the senior monk Jing. Jing asked, "In these six or seven years, what realization have you attained? The Master replied, "Every day..."
"Right now, there is not a single thing. Jing said, "Where does this whole string of yours come from? The Master was at a loss.
He then asked, "Ultimately, how should one realize this great matter? Jing said, "Have you not heard it said?
'If you wish to know the essential meaning, look south for the Big Dipper. Having said this, he departed. Pressed by these words, the Master was utterly unable to understand.
For seven days while walking and sitting, he happened to visit the bath attendant’s quarters.

His state of doubt remained unresolved, but after the time it takes to eat a meal, he suddenly realized that his chest felt light and clear, and all people and things before him vanished from view. He was truly covered in sweat all over his body.
Upon seeing Jing, Jing held up a fan and said, “Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master immediately replied, “It is clearly revealed when raised; how wonderful! The pure breeze pervades everywhere.”
It permeated his heart completely. "The message within this is not much; it simply results in one’s entire being coming forth in joy.
From then on, when he spoke words or composed verses, he encountered no obstruction whatsoever. Yet, when it came to the path that goes beyond, he still could not attain a sense of liberation.
Consequently, he entered Mount Xiangyan to spend the summer retreat and again visited Wufang Pu. Pu asked him: "All phenomena return to the One; to what does the One return?"
Deshan said, "The nose stands upright and the eyes stare sideways. Wumen replied, "That is something learned. Deshan said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree;
when the duck is cold, it enters the water. Wumen said, "I do not ask about that. What is your original face before your parents were born?
Deshan raised his fist and said, "Look! Wumen said, "A good thirty blows of the staff for this! Deshan shook out his sleeves and departed.
Just as it happened, Tieshan was returning from Goryeo to Shishuang when the Master went to visit him. Tieshan asked, "Where is your native place? The Master replied, "Ruzhou.
Tieshan asked, "What are the features of Fengxue’s countenance? The Master recounted his twenty years of diligent practice in its entirety.
Tieshan then seized his throat and asked, "What is 'Mu'? The Master said, "I recently came from Tanzhou."
[The Master] arrived. Having not received news from North Lake, Mount [Shan] said, "It is not yet so; speak further. The Master said, "When did you leave Goryeo, Preceptor?
Shan said, "It is not yet so; speak further. The Master gave a shout and, shaking his sleeves, departed. Shan said, "This brother is excellent in every way, yet he has one great illness:
he claims he has attained realization. Upon hearing this, the Master was moved with gratitude and re-entered the hall.
He dwelt in the mountains of Zhoushan for seventeen years before finally attaining liberation. He once addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dharma has no fixed form;

it becomes the ultimate principle when meeting with conditions. Grasping the Vajra sword, one swallows the thorny jujube fruit; one cuts off the tongues of the patch-robed monks and sits upon the crown of Vairocana’s head.
One takes a single blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body; one takes the sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a single blade of grass."
Directly let them be without a single thread of clothing. The moon is cold in the autumn sky; cold ashes flare into flame.
When one reaches this point, if you call it "Buddhadharma," you will enter hell as fast as an arrow shot. If you do not call it "Buddhadharma," you will enter hell as fast as an arrow shot.
O virtuous ones, how ultimately shall you understand this? Have you not seen what the Boatman said: "Where the body is hidden, there is no trace"? No trace...
Do not hide your body within the traces of the past. Even so, when viewed with the true eye, all these are merely idle accoutrements;
from the perspective of a patch-robed monk, they are of no concern at all.
Chan Master Jizhao Wujie Dao of Yuxing in Changzhou Prefecture was the son of the Zhao family of Wuxing.
At the time of his birth, a white light filled the room for three nights. During the Yuan army’s invasion of the south, his mother, Lady Ji, was captured by roaming soldiers.
When the Master grew up, he sought his mother while reciting the name of the Bodhisattva with such intensity that he searched everywhere for over ten years before finally finding her.
Thereupon, Hejian went together with [his companions] to pay homage at Putuo. At Mount Tie, he shaved his head under Qiong.
Next, he visited Xinyuan at Jigan at Daochang, and Wuyin at Jingci. While boating upon the lake, he heard the songs of fishermen and attained a sudden realization. He presented this to Yuan.
Yuan said, "There is no place for you to lodge here. The Master brushed off his robes and departed. He subsequently built a hermitage on the southern slope of Mount Bian.
After his mother passed away and he had completed her burial, one night a person dressed in white appeared in the air and said, "Your karmic affinity lies in Yixing. Thereupon, [he went there].
He obtained Mount Yufeng and established the Jizhao Chan Monastery; the local people unanimously revered him.

On the sixth day of the first month of the Ren-shen year of the Zhi-shun era, he passed away while sitting cross-legged without illness. He was sixty-five years of age and had thirty years of monastic seniority. His body was cremated.

The relics are innumerable. The pagoda was divided and enshrined in two hidden locations within the realm of tranquil illumination (*jìzhào*). The "Middle Hidden" site is located to the northeast of the town;
it was also founded by the Master himself.
This is the twenty-fourth generation after Dajian (Huineng).
Chan Master Wuyi Fuhuan Wuya Daoyong of Linggu Monastery in Jiangning was a native of the Wu family of Fushih in Xian’an, Quzhou.
His father dreamed that Mingguo arrived at his door before he was born. He entered the monastic order under Chan Master Jiefeng at Wushi Mountain. Jiefeng asked him: "What..."
Feng asked, "Where do you come from? The Master replied at once, "Empty space has no front or back. Feng pointed his finger at the bell and showed it to the Master.
The Master spontaneously composed a verse: "Rolled out from within the hundred-fold smelting furnace, Empty space originally never gathers dust.
Now it hangs upon the heads of men; When struck, its great sound pervades the nine realms. At that time he was only twelve years old, and Feng marveled greatly at him. He then...

He served as an attendant for tonsure, residing in the lower quarters. Through long-term devotion to his duties, all doubts and obstructions were completely resolved, and he attained unimpeded eloquence.

Master Feng certified his realization. During the Yongle era, he was commanded by imperial decree to reside at Linggu Monastery. At that time, the court was holding a great vegetarian feast (*dazhai*), and the officials overseeing the affairs were extremely strict.
When the Master appeared indifferent to these matters, those around him questioned him in astonishment. The Master replied, "Within myself, there is one great..."
The matter was extremely urgent; there was no leisure for anything else. He bathed, changed his robes, sat in the lotus position, and wrote a verse:
"Life and death drift on, severed from worldly ties; Blessed by grace, I enjoy eternal peace and prosperity. This time, casting off my hands, I return to the void;

The snow has cleared, the clouds have vanished, and the moon is full. Having set down his brush, he passed away. When the Emperor heard of this, he dispatched an eunuch to present offerings. His body was cremated, and the *śarīra* relics were distributed everywhere.
[The robe] was distributed. The seven assemblies marveled at this unprecedented event.
Hu Long Taichu of Wenzhou Prefecture, whose original name was Qiyuan, was a disciple of the Japanese imperial house, the Son of the Genji. His father was a high-ranking official.

At the age of nine, he was sent to Kenchō-ji Temple to enter the monastic life. At eighteen, he requested an imperial decree to travel south for study. After three years of traveling, he arrived at...
Fuzhou. At that time, in the second month of the Bingwu year of the Wu Yuanzhi era, [the Master] was presented at court as a tribute.

He was introduced to the Emperor, who was pleased. By imperial decree, he was granted an audience with Jitan Le. Le instructed him to travel extensively to visit various masters. Later, he visited Jiefeng. One day, Jiefeng ascended the hall and said:
"Snow covers the thousand mountains; why then is the solitary peak not white? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said, "The thunder rumbles, yet there are no drops of rain.
Feng said, "On the thatched hut is laid a roof of lapis lazuli tiles; within the stone chamber is hidden a bottle of agate.
The Master said, "A tiger has mounted upon a tiger of the South Mountain. Feng said, "A tiger gives birth to seven cubs; which one among them does not have a tail?"
The Master said, "The seventh one. Feng said, "I grant you thirty blows for that. Thereupon, he was permitted to enter the inner quarters.
Later, he took his leave and built a thatched hut on Mount Lu. He subsequently moved to Shilong, where he appeared in the world to widely save beings.
He then transferred to Sanfeng in Luoyang and later again to Hulong. He once set forth the "Three Critical Words": the first asked, "Why does the Śūnyatā-deva drag his feet upon level ground?"
"Muddy and dripping with water. Second: "The Golden-Winged Bird King splits the sea to seize and swallow dragons;
why then is he swallowed by a mud-skipper? Third: "The Buddhas of the three periods cannot speak of it; why then do the 'cat' and the 'white ox' recite the *Mahā*?
On the first day of the third month of the Dinghai year of the Yongle era, he gathered the assembly and spoke this verse: "In life, an iron mask; in death..."
Iron Mask: A single blow shatters a hundred fragments. By day he circumambulates Mount Sumeru; then he passes away while sitting. His stupa is enshrined at Nanyuan.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Xingtong of Western Sichuan, a successor to the Patriarchs at Potalaka in the South Sea,
of the Linji school under the seventeenth generation of Dajian.

Chan Master Miaoguang Hui’an of Jiaozhong, a native of Quanzhou and a descendant of the Li clan of Min, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Dahui Zonggao of Mount Jing. From childhood, he spoke little and seldom smiled;

yet whenever he heard Buddhist chants, he would rejoice. At the age of fifteen, he took the tonsure under Master Huìyuán of Youyán, yet he still delighted in reading a wide range of secular and religious texts. One day—
One day he left and crossed the mountain ridges to pay his respects to Yuanwu at Yunju. He subsequently studied under Huangbo Xiang and Gao’an Wu, with whom he attained resonance in both cases.
Due to the outbreak of bandits in Huai and Chu, he returned to visit Foxin. It happened that Dahui was residing in Guangzhou, so he went there to follow him.
Hui said, "Let us try to cite one or two instances of what you have attained while dwelling within the Buddha-mind.
The Master cited the public case of Puhua regarding the Buddha-mind’s ascent to the hall: "The Buddha-mind would not do so; when none come in this manner at all, how is it?"
[The Master] struck him across the spine, saying, "Let it be so that your body manifests throughout the entire world. Huì asked, "What is your intention?
The Master said, "I am unwilling to add a footnote at the end of this. Huì said, "This is precisely taking the illness as the Dharma. The Master responded with firm resolve.

Wuxin was dissatisfied with this. Hui said, "You simply try to grasp it through contemplation. The Master ultimately still did not believe this. After ten days had passed, he recalled Haiyin’s remark:
"The thunder is vast and loud, yet there are no raindrops at all. Only then did he feel free from obstruction; he hurried to inform Hui.
When Huì heard that Jǔdào saw off both Yánglǎ and Xuánshā as being "not yet thorough," he questioned him. After the Master had answered, Huì laughed and said:
"Although you have advanced one step, you have merely failed to find your place. It is like a man cutting down a tree:
if he strikes a single blow at the root, the life-force is severed. If you strike the branches instead, how could you sever the life-force? Now, throughout all quarters..."

"Those who discourse on Chan in such a vast and empty manner are for the most part like this; what benefit does it bring to the matter? Of the true lineage of Yangqi, there are only three or four people.
The Master departed in indignation. The following day, Huì asked him, "Do you still have doubts? The Master replied, "There is nothing to be doubted.
Huì said, "When the ancients met one another, even before a word was spoken, they already knew whether the other was genuine or false. Or when they heard his..."

[The Master] spoke, and [Yunmen] immediately discerned the depth of his understanding. "How is this principle? he asked. The Master was struck with awe and broke into a cold sweat, not knowing where to turn.
Yunmen ordered him to investigate the phrase "having words" and the phrase "having no words. One day, as Yunmen passed by Yunkuan’s hermitage, the Master accompanied him as an attendant.

He asked, "I have reached this point, yet I cannot attain thorough penetration. Where does my illness lie? Yunmen said, "Your illness is most chronic; even the physicians of the world would fold their hands in helplessness."
"Why is this? An ordinary person, once dead, cannot return to life. You are now alive and have not yet been willing to die.
To reach the ground of great peace and bliss, you must undergo one great death. The Master’s state of doubt grew even deeper. Later, he entered the inner quarters.
Huì asked: "The porridge has been eaten; the bowls have been washed. Cast off all medicinal taboos and bring forth a single phrase. The Master—

[The Master] said, "Torn asunder! Huì struck him with his staff and shouted with a thunderous roar, "And you speak of Chan again? At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. Huì beat the drum and addressed the assembly, saying:
"If one can grasp the hair of a tortoise, one laughs heartily; with a single blow, ten thousand layers of locks are opened.
What joy and fulfillment in life is found today! Who would say that a thousand miles have deceived me here? The Master also presented a verse, saying: "A single squeeze—"
When the thunder roars at the opportune moment, it startles the Mount Sumeru and causes the Northern Dipper to emerge from its storehouse.

The vast waves surge and flood the heavens; you grasp the nostrils but lose the mouth. Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Why act so foolishly?
When the tree falls and the vine withers, where do the phrases go? I know full well that all of you, in the end..."
"I sought its head and nose but could not find them. Why is this so? It is simply because it is too clear; this very clarity causes what is attained to be delayed. He ascended the hall and said:
"Dreams, illusions, and empty flowers—what need is there to grasp at them? Gain and loss, right and wrong—let them all go at once.
He cast down his whisk and said: "I, this mountain monk, have already let go today. As for you all, what will you do?"
He spoke again. The attendant took up the whisk. A monk asked, "Why was Mañjuśrī unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi?
The Master said, "I am tired today. The monk asked, "Why was Wǎngmíng able to emerge from it? The Master said:

This caused people to harbor doubts and attachments. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then the thousand peaks of Mount Hua are split open to reveal their splendor, and the Yellow River is released in its full, clear current.
The Teacher replied, "Feel free to speculate as you wish."
Chan Master Wanzhan Daoyan of Donglin in Jiuzhang Prefecture was the son of the Xianyu family of Tongchuan.
He had long studied under Yuanwu and attained a slight realization. When Yuanwu returned to Shu, he instructed Daoyan to rely upon Miaoxi, sending a letter to Miaoxi that said:
"Daoyan’s painting is already complete; he only lacks the dot in the eye. On another day, his succession of the lineage will be beyond measure. Miaoxi resided at...

Yunmen and Yangyu both served the Master; it was through questioning them morning and evening that he attained great enlightenment. Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma hall, he said:
"One leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven. One speck of dust rises, and the great earth is gathered up. When Niaoke blew on his cloth-hair, someone immediately attained awakening.
Why is it that students of today do not recognize their own selves? After a long silence, he said: "Do not err."
"Strange fellow, very well. He ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to know the mind of the Buddhas, simply recognize it within the thoughts and actions of sentient beings.
If you wish to know the eternally abiding, unfading nature, simply realize it within the shifting and changing of the myriad things. Do you recognize it yet?"
"If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Wheel.
He ascended the hall and said: "Where all people know, Liang-sui knows entirely; where Liang-sui knows, all people do not know. What is the place where Liang-sui knows? He then said:
"The cormorant speaks the language of the crane. He ascended the hall again and said: "In the bitter cold of mid-winter, there is no peace in the three realms. As for the wealthy..."
"How happy! The poor suffer from hunger and cold; they do not recognize the profound principle and mistakenly fixate on a flat tray.
Why is this? Placing the ox's head upon its tail; looking south for the Big Dipper. Entering the Hall: One drop of water, one drop of ice.
Heaven is cold, people are cold. The wind moves, the banner moves. Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking Śakra."
The nostrils. A sea carp from the Eastern Ocean receives a blow of the staff; the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
This is not something apart from what you all experience and utilize throughout the twelve periods of the day. Ascending the hall, he said: "The gateway of universal penetration is flung wide open.
If one enters through the gate, they are unworthy of conversation. One must enter the gateless gate before they can sit within the inner sanctum."
Therefore it is said: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already accomplished this gate; the Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter its perfect clarity;

those who practice and study in the future should rely upon this very Dharma. From the various sages of antiquity down to the present, there has fortunately existed such a vast and grand tradition of the Way.
Yet, how can it be that you are unable to carry on this lineage? Why do you so readily cast yourselves aside in self-contempt, acting like thieves and burglars breaking through walls?
"What a fine man! I venture to ask the great assembly: how does one enter the gate that has no gate? After a long silence, he said, "It is not only Avalokiteśvara;
I, too, have realized it from within. He then ascended the hall. "The Lantern Festival has already passed, and the fundraising masters are departing."
The group of six bhikṣus each followed their own kind; this assembly no longer has branches or leaves, but consists purely of those who are genuine.
It is well that such people of overweening pride should withdraw. A qilin does not constitute an auspicious omen, nor does a phoenix bring honor;

ears of wheat with two stalks and grain stalks with nine ears are entirely unnecessary. I only wish for peace and lack of affairs within the official sphere, so that I may dwell beneath the forest trees in meditative concentration.

The water buffalo lies full and at ease; the man with his shoulder-board slung rests in the setting sun. Content in pure poverty, they have enough gruel and enough rice. They move and rest according to the season;
the chopsticks do not jostle the rice basket, nor does the rat gnaw the steamer lid. Such is the livelihood of the mountain folk—simple yet enduring.
They pay no heed to the Goddess of Fortune, nor do they loathe the Lady of Darkness. A wise host accepts neither.
After a long silence, he said: "A gentleman loves wealth, but takes it by the proper way. Ascending the hall, he said: "Last year’s Cold Food Festival was after;
this year’s Cold Food Festival is before. Every day is a good day. This is not 'the biased within the central. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Long lingering in a guest house, with the setting sun upon my hometown. Three months of rain hang from the eaves; the waters have submerged the lotuses of both lakes. The cauldron leaks and burns..."
Lamp bowl. Wood smoke fills the hearth; all thoughts of north and south have been forgotten. Gazing afar, the plain stretches out endlessly. Entering the hall:
In a sandalwood grove there are no other trees; dense and deep, it is the dwelling place of the lion.
Thus, a sandalwood forest is surrounded by sandalwood; a thornbush forest is surrounded by thorns. One person is the master; two persons are companions. This is how it is accomplished.
Throughout ten trillion lands, whether among the scholars, farmers, artisans, or merchants, or even among yakṣas and rākṣasas, should they witness the practice of demonic deeds, let them say:
"How leisurely! How carefree! Let us pass our years in ease. A monk asked, "Regarding the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree, what is its essential meaning?
The Master said, "It cannot be sketched; it cannot be painted. The monk said, "Though Li Ling was a skilled hand, what could he do against being trapped by the barbarians? The Master said, "..."
“Where have you come from? [The Master asked. [The monk] asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “You are Yuangu.
The monk stepped forward and said, “Yes, yes. The Master said, “The trousers have no crotch; the pants have no opening. [The monk] asked, “What is the Buddha?
The Master said, “Master Zhigong. [The monk] said, “I am asking about the Buddha; why do you answer with Master Zhigong? The Master said, “Zhigong does not...”
At that time, the Master said, "What is the Dharma? The monk replied, "Yellow silk, young lady; the grandson’s pickle mortar. The Master asked, "What sutra passage is this?
The monk replied, "A most exquisite composition. The Master asked, "What is a monk? The monk replied, "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat.
The Master asked, "Why do you not speak directly? The monk replied, "Master Xuansha. The Master said, "The Three Jewels have already..."

Having received the Master’s instruction, [the monk] asked, "What is the matter regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage? The Master said, "Wang Qiao feigned immortality and attained it.
The monk laughed heartily, and the Master then tapped his teeth with his tongue.
Chan Master Lǎn’ān Dìngxū of Xīchán Monastery in Fúzhōu Prefecture was the son of the Lin family of that same prefecture. In his youth, he pursued the civil service examinations and achieved renown.
At the age of twenty-five, while reading the *Śāriputra-prakaraṇa* (Yìjiào jīng), he suddenly exclaimed, "How nearly have I been misled by the scholar’s cap!

He wished to leave the household life, but his mother opposed him on the grounds that the wedding ceremony was imminent. The Master then cut her off, saying: "The peach blossoms and apricot flowers—[all at once...]"
Entrusting it to the spring breeze—emerald bamboos and yellow flowers. From now on, let us be companions forever on the Way. Eventually, Yi Bao-shou took pleasure in becoming a bhikṣu;

with his single staff, he traveled through Lake and Xiang, visiting renowned masters everywhere. Upon returning to his hometown, he built a hermitage on the summit of Qiang Peak and did not descend the mountain for three years.
Fo-xin Cai entreated him to emerge and lead the assembly at Dachen. He once asked students: "If..."
"The mind is the causal condition for the Buddha. At that time, at Miaoxi Hermitage on Yangyu Island, the master’s friend Miguang sent a letter to him, saying:
"The Master's approach is distinct from those of other quarters; would you come for a brief visit? The Master did not reply.

Miguang used this as a pretext to invite the Master for a meal, and the Master went to attend. It happened that Miaoxi was entering the room when he raised the case of a monk asking Mazu, "What is..."
The Buddha. Zu said, "The mind itself is the Buddha. [The Master] offered a response. Miaoxi rebuked him, saying, "With such an understanding, do you dare to presume to be a teacher to others?

He then beat the drum for a public discourse, exposing the places where [the Master] had throughout his life held himself in high esteem and found strength, dismissing them as erroneous interpretations.
The Master’s tears fell upon his chin; he did not dare look up, silently reflecting: "That which I..."
He attained realization. Since he had been thus cast out, how could the intent not transmitted from the West have ended with this? He then assumed the etiquette of a disciple.
One day, Xì asked, "When there is no letting out from within and no letting in from without—just at such a time, what is it like?

As the Master was about to open his mouth, Xì took up his bamboo staff and struck him three times across the spine. At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment and cried out in a stern voice:
"Venerable Master, you have already had enough," said Xiyuan. He struck him once more. The Master prostrated himself. Xiyuan laughed and said, "Only today do I know that I have not deceived you.
He then sealed his realization with a verse: "The eye of Mahesvara stands erect upon the crown of the head;
The life-stealing talisman hangs askew from behind the elbow. Blind the eyes and cast off the talisman; Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall. Thus it was.
The sound vibrated through the groves. After his stay, he ascended the hall: "In the phrase there is the meaning; in the meaning there is the phrase. Mount Sumeru towers over the vast river.
When the phrase cuts away the meaning and the meaning cuts away the phrase, it is like a heroic man loosing a wild arrow.

Even if one were to face him with fangs like swords and a mouth like a blood-basin, merely displaying verbal sharpness and vainly flaunting one's spirit is of no avail. This is why Vimalakīrti remained silent; from the start, such talk has already fallen into verbosity.
Verse: Makka closed the gate and exposed his family’s disgrace;

as for the old fellow of Waguan and the Great Master Yantou, who on the peak of Qiangfeng grasped the wind and stirred the waves, playing with divine transformations—thirty blows are well-deserved beneath their heels.
But tell me, where does the fault lie? After a long silence, he said: "The mechanism was not made by Han Guang; do not take it into your breast."
One should remain equanimous. Upon reaching the festival, he ascends the hall. Before the twenty-fifth day, the masses of yin have subsided and the mud-dragons close their doors;
after the twenty-fifth day, the first yang returns and the iron trees bloom flowers.
Precisely on the twenty-fifth day, the intoxicated guests amidst the dust—whether riding donkeys or horses—move from street to street, offering mutual congratulations. Beyond the mundane world...
A man of leisure. With his patched robe covering his head, he sits in meditation by the hearth. The wind whistles; the rain whistles; all is cold and still.
Who cares about you, Master Zhang, Daoist Li, or Bodhidharma? Entering the hall: The Lazy Old Man is the laziest among the lazy;
he is too lazy to preach Zen. He values neither himself nor the sages of old. Furthermore, who cares about the earth? And—
Who cares about heaven? Beyond the mundane world, one is carefree and has nothing to do; even when the sun has risen three *gān* high, one still sleeps.
[The Master] ascended the hall and raised the case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the ancient saying? Zhaozhou said, "Listen closely, listen closely. The Master said:
Listen attentively; it is not that there is nothing to hear. One must strictly avoid mistaking the bell for a water jar. In the room, the Master asked a monk, "The myriad dharmas return to the One;
where does the One return? The monk said, "To the land of Silla. The Master said, "I am in Qingzhou, making a hempen shirt that weighs seven catties—what about that?
The monk said, "Today I have personally seen Zhaozhou. The Master said, "Seen in front, seen behind. The monk...
He then made a gesture of slashing his own forehead. The Master asked, "Where are you from, Senior Monk? He replied, "Jiangxi.
The Master said, "Why have you come here with such tattered and worn-out robes? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him out.
Chan Master Dongchan Meng’an Siyue of Fuzhou Prefecture was a native of Jiangzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "Walls, tiles, and rubble preach all dharmas;
moths, sheep, and ants manifest boundless bodies. When the place of seeing is clear and vigorous, one will surely penetrate through the midst of hearing.
Therefore, whenever Xuefeng saw a monk approach, he would roll out three wooden balls, like performing a variety play."

[The monk] acted as if he were similar [to the ancient masters]. Xuansha then made the gesture of chopping a wooden plaque. "You base fellows, you talk nonsense and bring it forward! Today, Puxian slanders the ancients;
even if a thousand Buddhas appear in the world, there shall be no repentance for this. If anyone here slanders Puxian, they will surely enter the Hell of the Plow that Tears Out the Tongue.
But tell me: who is it that does not slander? After a long silence, he said: "The heart does not betray others; the face..."

With an expression of shamelessness, he ascended the hall and said: "When Bodhidharma first arrived, everyone here knew the Sanskrit language; yet after he departed, those in the Western Heavens all came to understand the language of Tang.

If we discuss 'directly pointing at the human mind to see one's nature and become a Buddha,' it is much like a goral hanging from its horns—when the hounds search for the tracks, their single-mindedness goes astray and ten thousand words are useless. It can truly be said that when he came, others laughed."
I do not know how long it will be before I laugh at others after my departure. The Tang and Sanskrit languages have been personally entrusted [to you].

Since ancient times, those who provide vegetarian offerings for monks have feared the night tea. Entering the hall: At the beginning of the twelfth month, the year has passed; the Yellow River is already frozen solid.

Deep within, there are auspicious fish, leaping with lively vigor, unable to escape. Yet they cannot moisten one another with their dampness, nor can they soak one another with their froth. How shameful!
"O Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, when will the spring breeze arrive to melt the ice of the Yellow River, allowing the fish to transform into dragons and surge straight through the peach-blossom waves?
If you understand, then you understand; do not speak of such dreams before a fool. He then ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is the first part of the day? [To practice] giving away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges. The Master said, "Discern the field from its sprouts;
recognize a person by their words. The monk asked, "What is the middle part of the day? Again, [to practice] giving away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.

The Master said, "Striking it, bumping into it. The monk asked, "What is the latter part of the day? Also, [to practice] giving away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges... [The Master said: "The same as before."

He offered his entire body as an act of almsgiving. The Master said, "The text below is long; it shall be entrusted for another day. He spoke again: "One turning word is like the sky universally covering;
one turning word is like the earth universally supporting. One turning word is that the tongue simply does not leave the mouth. One turning word is: 'For now, rejoice that there is no connection.
Do you wish to understand? It is shameful; even the World-Honored One’s face would turn red. It is better to speak directly. Great indeed is Master Yue!"

[The Master] took his seat. His mouth was like a foundation stone. Today, while answering the questions of the monks and lecturing on the sutras, he unconsciously explained away all the footnotes at once.
Then he descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "I have silenced my own mouth;
you must speak. I have blocked your ears; take care not to miss it. Yesterday someone came from Tiantai, yet he says that the Great Sage of Sizhou is here."
In Hongzhou, one sits in meditation while selling goods at the crossroads. What is this? It is the broken-soled straw sandals and the peaked-brim bamboo hat.
At Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou, Chan Master Shoujing of Ciana ascends the hall; having finished offering incense, he takes his seat and the mallet is struck.

He said, "In this Dharma assembly, you dragon-like and elephant-like ones should contemplate the primary meaning. As he spoke these words, the Master let out a shout and asked, "Which meaning is this?
Those who had long studied under former masters already discerned the source of the inquiry; those among the later students who had doubts were not hindered from asking questions. A monk then asked:
Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the World-Honored One transmit? Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded, "Yes?
[Kāśyapa said,] "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "By all means, do not touch it.
[Ānanda] asked, "As for Kāśyapa saying, 'Throw down the bannerpole before the gate,' how is that? The Master said, "The stone ox lies across the ancient road."
The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Do you have this very message from the Buddha-sun? The Master said, "I have no such message.
The monk said, "But how can one deny that Dingguang beckoned from afar at Jindi, and Zhiyi nodded his head in secret at Jiangling?
The Master said, "Do not take the cypress by the courtyard and lightly compare it to the weeds by the roadside. The monk bowed; the Master then said, "Ding..."
Guangqin pointed his finger from afar; Zhe nodded his head in the dark at Jiangling. It is already ten thousand miles away amidst white clouds;
how can one bear to not know when to stop? Even if one were to stop right here, the resulting chaos would be no small matter.
"Is there anyone here who can discern this? If not, today the mountain monk has lost face. [He] ascended the hall and said:
"To discuss the profound and speak of the wondrous is to scatter excrement and urine; to wield the staff and shout is to use salt to quench thirst;
to establish host and guest is to split the patriarchal teachings like flowers. Even if one does none of these things, one is still sitting in a ghost cave. Reaching this point, the mountain monk..."
The drum for retreat has already been beaten. But tell me: when you people are usually filled with indignation in your hearts and stifled by frustration in your mouths, what should you do?
Do not let your idle learning and intellectual interpretations bury the mind of the Patriarchs. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you clarify only the self,"

If one does not awaken to what is before one's eyes, this person has eyes but no feet. If one only awakens to what is before one's eyes but does not clarify one's own self, this person has feet but no eyes.
Only when the eyes and feet support each other are they like the two wheels of a cart or the two wings of a bird.
When you arrive at this place of Xichan, it is precisely where you must be interrogated and then struck. Entering the hall for discourse: "The midsummer heat is scorching;
the wooden man’s sweat flows without ceasing. With last night’s rain, it has become cool. Do not say that this mountain monk does not speak.

[He] strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends from the seat. Entering the hall for discourse: "If you wish to correctly grasp the guiding thread, you must first let the great earth fall into ruin."
When coming to clash with the edge of the snow-blade, one cannot avoid exposing its sharp point.
At such a time, setting aside for a moment the question of whether Śākyamuni could not show his head, how do you all understand this: "Hiding one's body within the stirrup"?
Entering the hall, he said: "The Way is the constant Way; the mind is the constant mind. You people, having heard the mountain monk speak thus..."
"What do you say? he asked. [The monk] immediately said, "I understand. "The large month has thirty days; the small month has twenty-nine.
Above your head is heaven; beneath your feet is earth. In your ears you hear sounds; through your nose you breathe air.
But suppose the four great oceans were upon your head, a venomous snake pierced your eyes, and a toad entered your nostrils—then what would you do?"
Ascending the hall: Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra discuss principle and phenomena; Linji and Deshan employ the staff and the shout. Dongchan takes a single nap until daybreak;
he simply loves the wind blowing from a cool place. *Tu!* Ascending the hall: A skilled fighter does not look back for his head;
a skilled warrior will surely achieve merit. Once that merit is achieved, peace is brought about with ease. When peace is established, [all is resolved].
With a high pillow, there is no worry. Lay aside the three-foot sword; cease playing with the single bow. Return the horses to the south of Mount Hua; release the oxen into the wilds of Taolin.
The winds blow favorably and the rains fall in season; the fisherman sings and the woodcutter dances.

Even so, even the sovereigns Yao and Shun still possessed their transformative influence. How can they compare to the one for whom heaven and earth cannot be contained? Yao— *Note: The text appears to be an excerpt from a Zen discourse (likely by Master Dahui Zonggao), ending abruptly. The final character "堯" (Yao) likely serves as a signature or a thematic marker.*
Shun did not know his name; the whole family ignored matters of rise and fall. He simply loved to occupy the Lake Dongting with the clouds.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "When the mouth is closed, one speaks constantly; when the tongue is cut off, there is no interruption.
This lack of interruption is most marvelous and extraordinary. Yet, being so marvelous and extraordinary, why does it become a speck of dust in the eye? It is perfectly clear."

At that time, there is nothing to be understood. Even the realm of the profoundest mystery must be critiqued. Entering the hall: Upon the crown of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, there is a vast, sky-reaching great road.
If you have not yet penetrated the barrier of birth and death, how can you dare to take a step forward? Or, if you do not take a step forward, the great trichiliocosm is without obstruction.
A single phrase cuts off all verbal explanation; Nanda holds up an iron pillar. A monk asked: "Buddha after Buddha hands it down, Patriarch after Patriarch..."
The Patriarch transmitted it; I do not know what was transmitted. The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times. The monk asked, "Without employing a single blade, I request to meet the Master.
The Master said, "When encountering strength, I become weak. The monk asked, "Why do you bury your troops and engage in combat? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"Simply because you, Ācārya, have not applied even an inch of blade. [The student] asked, "I do not yet know: is there still something further above? The Master said, "There is.
[The student] asked, "What is this matter that is further above? The Master said, "A defeated general is not executed. He then asked, "Before the hall of the ancient Buddha..."
"Who arrives first? The Master said, "The blind old man from the village. [The monk] asked, "I do not understand how he proceeds.
The Master said, "Carrying his staff slung across his shoulder."
Chan Master Daosheng of Kaishan in Jianning Prefecture was the son of the You family of that same prefecture. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

Having lost his parents at an early age, he vowed to leave the household life in order to repay his filial debt to them. He first traveled to the capital and relied upon Yuanwu, yet he attained no realization.
Later, he followed Miaoxi to Quannan; when Miaoxi took charge of Mount Jing, the Master also accompanied him there. Not long after, Miaoxi sent the Master to Chang...
Sha. This was a letter sent by Tong Zhang Ziyuan. The Master said to himself, "I have practiced Chan for twenty years without reaching a point of entry.
If I undertake this journey, I will certainly fall into neglect. I intend not to go. His friend Zongyuan rebuked him, saying, "It is not that you cannot practice Chan while on the road.
Go! I shall go with you. Reluctantly, the Master set out. While on the way...
Weeping on the road, he said to Yuan, "I have spent my entire life practicing Chan, yet I have found nothing at all that brings me strength. Now, moreover, I am rushing along this path;

how can I attain resonance with the Way? Yuan told him, "You need only take whatever you have studied under various masters, whatever you have awakened to, and whatever Yuanwu and Miaoxi have explained for you—do not concern yourself with any of it. On the road, you may set them aside."
"As for this matter, I shall do everything for you; there are only five things I cannot do for you, which you must attend to yourself.
The Master asked, "What are these five things? Yuan said, "Clothing oneself, eating food, defecating, urinating, and carrying a corpse along the road.
At these words, the Master was suddenly liberated; unconsciously, he began to dance with his hands and feet. Yuan said, "You..."
"This time you may send a letter; it is appropriate for you to proceed. I shall return first. Yuan immediately returned to Mount Jing; the Master did not return for half a year.
Upon seeing him, Miaoxi said, "Son of Jianzhou, this is our parting. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he said:
"The mind of the Great Sage of the Land of Zhu was secretly transmitted from east to west. What is this mind that was secretly transmitted? Liang...
Jiurui said: "In the autumn of the eighth month, where is there heat? He ascended the hall and said: "A thousand fathoms of sheer cliff—where can the Buddhas of the three periods set foot?
This is so, yet it is far too unapproachable for human sentiment. Let us open a single thread of the path: throughout the ocean of lands in the ten directions."
To emit light and shake the earth—this is indeed so. But how can one avoid being like mud mixed with water?
You must know that where a single thread-way is penetrated, the wall stands ten thousand fathoms high; where the wall stands ten thousand fathoms high, a single thread-way is penetrated.

Held crosswise or used upside down, pressed straight or lifted sideways, like rolling thunder and rushing torrents, like collapsing cliffs and splitting stones—this is indeed so, yet it still falls within the gate of transformation. Here, the wall...
To stand at a height of a thousand *zhang*—no connection there. To penetrate a single thread of the Way—no connection there.
To be contrary to human sentiment, to mix mud with water—altogether no connection there. This very "no connection" is itself no connection. It is so; it is indeed so.
Furthermore, there is no principle of Buddha-dharma. If one can emerge from the four crossroads, one will surely stride alone across heaven and earth.
As for this phrase "striding alone," how would you say it? Do not take offense at my former haughtiness; he has already stepped upon the highest barrier.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: Last year there was a June fifteenth; this year there is also a June fifteenth.
The fifteenth day of the sixth month. Last year’s fifteenth day of the sixth month was less than this year’s fifteenth day of the sixth month.

This year’s fifteenth day of the sixth month is more than last year’s fifteenth day of the sixth month. Where there is excess, there is no need to subtract; where there is deficiency, there is no need to add.
Since there is neither addition nor subtraction, then at the place of excess one uses it extensively, and at the place of deficiency one uses it sparingly. Thus...
He gave a shout and said, "Is this much or is it little? After a long silence, he said, "Among those who possess this message, how many can truly know it?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Dongshan’s 'three pounds of flax' was weighed on a scale with no markings;
each pound came out exactly at one hundred and sixty-two coppers, not even a hair's breadth less. It is just like Zhaozhou."
"It is just like those inside the palace; it simply does not accord with being sawn apart by Dayu or weighed on a scale. Consequently, people are unable to comprehend it.
If you wish to comprehend it now, simply ask Yunmen about the 'dry shi-jue' (rotten wooden pestle). He then ascended the hall.
The phrase "having a sentence" and "lacking a sentence" is like a vine leaning against a tree. It knocks over the lanterns and shatters the pillars;
the Buddha Hall is in a frantic rush, and the Sangha Hall looks back. Look closely: what kind of furniture is this? *Duh!* It is fit only for beating rats. Ascending the hall:
You all have come up here from the Sangha Hall in such a manner; shortly, you shall go down from the head of the Dharma Hall in such a manner.
"Go! You have never taken a single step astray. Why, then, do you not understand? After a long silence, he said:
"It is precisely because it is so utterly clear that what is attained seems delayed."
Chan Master Fozhao Deguang of Yuwang Temple in Ningbo Prefecture was the son of the Peng family of Linjiang.

At the age when he resolved to study the Way, he took the tonsure under Master Ji of Guanghua Temple on Mount Dongshan in his native prefecture. One day, while entering the master’s room for instruction, Ji asked, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, and it is not an object—what is it?
The Master was at a loss and consequently harbored a deep doubt. He did not sleep the entire night; the following day...
He went to the Abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction, saying, "Yesterday, I was graced by the Master’s question:
'It is neither mind, nor Buddha, nor a thing. Ultimately, what is it? I hope the Master will compassionately point this out to me.
Ji-zhen gave a shout and said, "You little śrāmaṇera, do you want me to provide a commentary for you as well? He then took up his staff, struck him across the back, and drove him out.
At this, the Master attained a realization. Later, he visited Yue’an Guo, Ying’an Hua, and Baiyang Zhen, yet he never accepted their teachings as final.
When Dahui was presiding over Yuyang Monastery, the Master went to consult him. Dahui asked: "If you call it a 'bamboo stick,' you commit the fault of contact;

Face to face. The ears hear nothing; the eyes see nothing. Suffering and joy, opposition and compliance, are forged into a single whole.
Tell me, what is it? When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; carry it home in a bottomless basket. Entering the hall:

To awaken to the Way by hearing sounds is to fall into the second or third rank; to clarify the mind by seeing forms is to err by seven or eight. As for the single path of the living mechanism—still...
Along the way, let us consider this: who is the person who penetrates the diamond circle and swallows the thorn-bush fruit? "Donning the straw raincoat, standing askew beyond a thousand peaks;
leading water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders. In the *Chunxi* year *Pingshen*, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Lingyin Monastery.

"When Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains to practice the Way, he achieved it after six years. What was it that he achieved? The Master said: "I thought Your Majesty had forgotten. The Emperor [laughed].

The Emperor was pleased and bestowed upon him the title of Chan Master Fozhao. From then on, he was summoned for audiences at any time. He once stayed in the Neiguantang (Imperial Meditation Hall) for five nights before departing.
On the fifteenth day of the third month of the Guihai year of Jia Tai (1303), he composed a final letter, gathered the assembly to bid them farewell, and wrote in large characters:

At sixty years of monastic seniority (*śramaṇa-varṣa*), his entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Dong’an on Mount Mao. He was posthumously titled the Great Chan Master Puhui Zongjue.
The pagoda is named Yuanjian (Perfect Mirror).
Chan Master Zongyan of Huizang Dun’an in Changzhou Prefecture was the son of the Zheng family of Fuzhou.
While ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "If you recognize this, the work of a lifetime of study is finished. When the ancients spoke thus, [it was] Huizang.

Why? "When you reach the river, the land of Wu ends; beyond the bank, the mountains of Yue abound. On the first day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and said: "In the first nine and the second nine, when we meet, we do not take out our hands.

"Life! For the sake of all you people, I shall now act. He struck three punches right to the face and delivered a single palm-blow across the cheek.
A sharp-witted monk knows his own pain and itching; as for that turning-around phrase—how would you say it? "Go to the hall to drink tea. He ascended the hall and said:

With eyes popping out and a mouth open in laughter, this time it no longer clings to its old branch. This was the occasion when [Zhaozhou] shaved his head and received the precepts.

Birth: When white waves arise, cast out a single hook; let fish and turtles compete for it at their own head. Later, after taking his seat in the hall, he said:

Relying on this: “The moon in the empty expanse over the ten-thousand-year-old emerald pool—only after repeatedly searching for it will you finally know it.

Chan Master Danyuan Zunpu, the Great Enlightened One of Yufu Temple, was a native of Fuzhou.
In his youth, he studied the Way alongside Yuquan Yi under Yuanwu for several years. Later, he returned to his hometown and assisted Yi at Xiangyun Temple in Putian.

"To act for others, yet not to speak for oneself. You say: "Do these two old fellows have any way to manifest themselves?

"To give Xinghua his due credit—quickly speak! Quickly speak! When the Master hesitated, Huai struck him and said, "You must never forget this one blow.

"What is it? When a monk appeared, Muzhou would immediately say, "This is a ready-made case; I grant you thirty blows.
You say, "Do these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others or not? The monk said, "They do. Huaihai said, "Got it! As the monk hesitated, Huaihai gave a shout.
Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment. Huaihai joyfully granted him approval.
Chan Master Nanyuan Zuyuan of Nengren Monastery on Mount Yan in Wenzhou Prefecture was a native of the Lin clan of Min.

Initially, he visited Xuefeng Yu; subsequently, he relied upon Foxin Cai. With neither did he find deep resonance. Later, while relying upon Dahui at Yunmen Hermitage, he sat through the night and saw a monk trim a lamp.
