the single point of the numinous mind is not polished. Greedily pursuing days as they pass in trivial toil—when called back, it does not turn its head;
what can be done? This old fellow Xuedou is coarse and clumsy, blunt and uncouth; let us add thirty years to him!
"Even after many years, one has still not yet realized Chan. Nevertheless, though this is so, the land is vast and people are few;
let us try to provide a footnote to this. The three eyes of Maheśvara are blinded; north, south, east, and west—the paths are no longer distinguished.

Leaves fall from a thousand forests, but no one sweeps them up; alone at the pine gate, he stretches out his legs and sleeps. He ascended the hall and, citing the story of Zhaozhou’s "Go drink tea," the Master said:
Zhaozhou meets people and offers them tea; who knows that this matter arises from within the household? With a flip of the hand, he creates clouds and rain; with the wind, he scatters earth and sand.
This has led Dongshan, lacking in wisdom, to ask about the Buddha and yet answer, "Three catties of hemp.
To the assembly: A Persian from the South Sea holds a secret mantra; of its thousand words and ten thousand phrases, few know them. A spring breeze comes blowing in.
"Where? Three or four branches of peach blossoms have been blown down.

Chan Master Kaiyan Qian’s dharma heir, the practitioner Wu Shisan of Mount Xianzhou in Jianning Prefecture, frequently used his own realization to question various Zen masters, but none [could satisfy him].

He entered [the monastery] and, following Kai Shan, settled in a thatched hut nearby. Day after day he applied himself diligently to investigation. On the eighth night of the third month in the Gengshen year of the Xiangshu era, he attained a sudden and clear awakening.
He composed a verse and presented it to Kai Shan, saying: "Originally there was no seam or crack; upon being touched, it immediately shines forth.
Since this is a treasure worth a thousand pieces of gold, why need one use it to shoot at sparrows? Kai Shan replied: "When it snaps with a 'tsai' sound, it is truly..."
How joyful! Birth and death, ordinary and holy, are all leveled and submerged. Beneath Mount Xianzhou, a hearty laugh; the moon is old, the wind is high—the heart of ten thousand ages.
*Continued Lamp, Orthodox Lineage*, Volume Ten.
*Continued Lamps of the Orthodox Lineage*, Volume Eleven:
The Linji School, compiled by the Śramaṇa Xingtong of Xichu, a successor to the Patriarchs at Putuo in Nanhai.
Chan Master Zhishan Miaofeng of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Guang of Yuwang, the eighteenth generation descendant of Dajian.
He was a native of the Liu clan of Wuxing; his family had resided for generations in Pengcheng.
In previous generations, all [members of his clan] attained high-ranking official positions. The Master was born into a family of fine silks and satins; by nature, he was lofty and pure.

At the age of thirteen, he left home to receive instruction at the Qizheng Monastery in Deqing. Whenever he encountered a scripture or treatise, he immediately grasped its essential meaning. He then traveled to visit various masters throughout the land.
He visited Fozhao at Mount Mao and attained realization through the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner. Fozhao presented him with a verse, which said:

"Today I have joined you with a single thread; cutting through nails and severing iron, you shall raise up my school. Following this, he went to Wukang and built a hermitage at the foot of Miaogao Peak.
Ten years later, he shared the teaching seat at Nengren in Yanshan, entered the world at Huizhen in Taizhou, and subsequently moved to Hongfu.

He spent ten years in retirement at Gaotingsi on Mount Gaoting among the various monasteries of Wanshan. He subsequently took charge of Ruiyan in Mingzhou, Wanshou in Suzhou, and Huazang in Changzhou.
In his later years, he resided at Lingyin. Being in close proximity to the imperial palace, Lingyin was thronged by the constant traffic of carriages and horses;

yet the Master would shut his door, neither welcoming nor seeing anyone off. Even when high officials or nobles encountered him, he would exchange with them nothing more than a simple greeting of seasonal inquiry.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that does not enter the common flow? The Master said, "A tortoise drills through a wall.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase of wondrous essence being free from partiality? The Master said, "One donkey among a hundred horses.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase of blinking eyes and raising eyebrows? The Master said, "Flowers rain before the crag, and the rocks nod their heads. The monk asked, "What is the extraordinary?"
[The Master] said, "Under the *zhizui* flower is the *zhizui* official. A student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Thirty years hence. He ascended the hall and said:
"Responding to things and manifesting form is like the moon in the water; picked up with a casual hand, it is revealed all at once."
Striking the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk, he said, "This is the cauldron of boiling water and the furnace of burning coals.
Striking again on the right side, he said, "This is the sword-trees and the mountain of blades. "In front are Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta; behind are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra.
"As for this one stroke in the middle—do you know where it lands? He struck once more and said, "Vipaśyin Buddha."
"Apply your attention early; even until now, you have not attained the subtle.

He ascended the hall and, citing the occasion when Yunmen was working together with the community to carry firewood, Yunmen threw down a piece of wood and said, "The entire Tripitaka only speaks of this.

The Master said, "Great as Yunmen was, he saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's head. He ascended the hall again. [He spoke of] discussing the profound and explaining the subtle; matters were as follows...
Hemp. It adds sand to the eyes of people of this age. Having managed to squeeze in through sheer, bare-bones poverty, his way of life is one of reckless abandon.

Hanging up a goat’s head while selling dog meat; drinking the official wine and sleeping on the official streets. He laughs until his tattered straw sandals fall off at the base of the fence. Addressing the assembly:
Those who have long practiced as eminent gentlemen look upon the four seas with empty eyes; their nostrils point toward heaven. Even when they see, they see [nothing].
"Intimate. He speaks intimately; he acts intimately; he employs [the Way] intimately. It is simply that they have not yet recognized this old monk’s staff. Why?
Because although the mountain is nearly nine fathoms high, they do not advance even a single basketful of earth.
When the Master was about to pass away, he bathed his body, sat in the lotus posture, and wrote a verse, saying: "Coming is thus; going is thus."

Thus it was: coming and going were as one, like a clear breeze across ten thousand li. Having finished writing this, he passed away on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month of the year Yiwei of the Duanping era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty.
He was eighty-four years old by secular age and seventy-one by monastic seniority.
After cremation, countless śarīras were obtained and interred on the western ridge of Lingyin Temple.
Chan Master Jingci Beijian Jujian, courtesy name Jingsou, was a native of the Long family from Tongchuan. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

He received full ordination at Guangfu Monastery in his home district. Upon reading the records of Wan’an, he attained realization. Later, he studied under Fozhao; their spiritual faculties were in accord, and he followed him for fifteen years.
He subsequently emerged into the public sphere at Panyu Monastery in Tai, and later served as abbot at Ba’en and Guangxiao, where he greatly expanded the assembly.
Zhen Xishan served as a regional inspector (bù shǐzhě) of Jiangdong at that time. Because Donglin used his influence to urge him to accept the post, he refused;
instead, he retired to seclusion for ten years at Beijian on Mount Feilai, hence he was known as Beijian.

He was subsequently summoned to serve at Tiefo in Xi, Yifu in Chang, Xianqing and Biyun in Suzhou, Huiri in Su, and Daochang in Lake District. Later, by imperial decree, he was transferred to Jingci Temple.
Ascending the hall: "If you recognize the One, all matters are finished. A monk who has settled the matter does not recognize a single character.
Even if it were so, it would not yet be called the Full Manifestation. "Where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west. Ascending the hall:

Taking Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery, body and mind dwell in peace within the Wisdom of Equality. Drinking the official wine, sleeping on the official street—this is what it means to be truly at home.
When one is to be executed, they should be buried where they stand; originally there is no fixed position. Why use forceful arrangement?
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Elder Mi and Dongshan while they were sitting in a bakery. Elder Mi drew a circle on the ground and said to Dongshan, "Take this away.
Dongshan said, "Bring it here. Baoning Yong remarked, "Not only did these two elders fail to carry it off..."

[The monk] said, "It cannot be lifted. The Master said, "Even all the people in the entire world could not lift it. The Master continued, "Beijian dares to say that Baoning’s resources were exhausted and his strength spent.
He ascended the hall and said: "For twenty years Yunyan was at Yaoshan, clarifying only this matter. A clear pool does not permit the blue dragon to coil within.
For forty years Zhaozhou did not employ a distracted mind; except for the two times of rice gruel and meals, he had no other distractions."
The Mind-Abode. How could a rabbit ever leave its burrow? Ascending the hall, he raised this case: One day, Zihu entered the Sangha hall and cried out, "Thieves! Thieves!
Seeing a monk, he seized him and said, "The thief is right here! The monk said, "It is not I; it is someone else.
Zihu pushed him away and said, "It is indeed you, but you simply refuse to take responsibility for it. The Master said: "Zihu..."
To hold on too tightly is perilous; to let go too hastily is reckless. At Jingci, it is not so: "A thief in one's own house is difficult to guard against;

one's own wealth will surely be lost. [He] struck the meditation staff and said: "One may err in seizing, but one must not err in releasing. He ascended the hall and said: "The former Buddha Zhao said..."
"Striking with the head of the staff, one encounters a living monk; the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye increases in value. Bei Jian said, "It is not so.
Striking with the head of the staff, one encounters a living monk; the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye shatters like ice melting away. Now tell me, how does this compare to the former Foguo Zhao?
Whether they are the same or different, let us cite the story of the World-Honored One’s first birth. The verse says: With one cry of "wa-di-pien-ta-li," A great icchantika suddenly emerges.
He brings calamity to this land and the Western Heaven; Majestically washing away the earth, he leaves not even mud behind.

Next, let us cite the story of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* regarding the six faculties being resolved and the one ceasing. The verse says: The six functions are powerless and faith does not penetrate; the one...
At that time, he entrusted [his affairs] to the spring breeze. A single curl of incense smoke lingered idly through the clear day; though no birds came, the flowers bloomed red on their own.

In the spring of the *pingwu* year of the Chunyu era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty, he manifested illness. He requested a brush and wrote a verse, adding at the end of the paper the six characters: "April First, Take Care.
When the appointed day arrived, he requested a bath, after which he passed away while dozing. He was eighty-three years of age; his *laba*...
62. His entire body was interred beside the Chang Pagoda at Yuet Tong, in accordance with his final instructions.
His *Beijian ji* (Collected Works of Beijian) in nineteen fascicles circulates in the world.
Chan Master Zeweng Ruyan of Jingshan, Hangzhou Prefecture, was the son of the Zhou family of Taizhou. Once, while ascending the hall for formal discourse, he raised the following case:
A monk once asked Qianfeng, "The Buddhas of the ten directions all enter the single path to nirvana; I wonder, where does the beginning of that path lie?
Qianfeng drew a line with his staff and said, "It is right here. The monk then requested further instruction from Yunmen, who took up [the staff].
He raised his fan and said, "The fan leaps up to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, striking Śakra’s nostrils;
it strikes the carp of the Eastern Sea, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. Do you understand? The Master said, "The higher the song, the more abrupt the response."
I return this to the two elders. Even if it were the single path to nirvana for the Bhagavans of the ten directions, you have not yet stepped upon it.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Jiangshan calls this a 'staff'; you all also call this a 'staff.
Is there any distinction between them or not? Though we lean on the same railing, the mountain colors..."

A Different Perspective. He composed a eulogy for Vimalakīrti, saying: In Vaiśālī he manifested illness and displayed his feigned ignorance, adding to the suspicions that filled the bellies of the people of the age.
Had it not been for Mañjuśrī’s personal investigation and exposure, who would have known of these underlying maladies?
Chan Master Wujie Liaopai of Tiantong Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The fifteenth day of the third month; the full moon faces the door.
Although it pervades the earth and fills the heavens, not even a hair’s breadth is revealed. Facing this scene, who can speak of this mind?"
This makes one recall the words of Hanshan once again. Entering the hall, he said:
"In the twelve periods of the day, as you come and go, turn and pivot, bow and stoop, and exchange greetings, you cannot deceive Chong'en by even a single point.

Right now, as you sit and stand with solemn composure, guest and host intermingle, and you gaze into one another's faces, Chong'en likewise cannot deceive you by even a single point. Since this is so...
"Yet we do not deceive one another; why then do you create obstacles for yourselves? He gave a shout and said, "Blowing on the fire with the wind requires little effort.
He ascended the hall and said: "Last night I prepared a piece of Chan; when dawn broke, I had forgotten it all.
Now the drum is beaten and the assembly has gathered like clouds; facing this moment, I must improvise as the occasion demands. He then looked back toward his attendant.
The Master said: "Take note of this one point. When the Buddha ascended the hall for his *nirvāṇa*, Śākyamuni, from the past until this very day, has entered the Great Samādhi of Stillness.
It is truly laughable that the monasteries throughout the world have been 'sawing the boat to find the sword' for over two thousand years, never ceasing their petty efforts.
Today, Chong'en, without moving a muscle, twists the nose of Gautama; it is not that I seek to strike him..."
"Startled by the grass, he saw the snake. As long as everyone meets one another, you all should observe with great care;
do not let it pass you by. He then joined his palms and said, "I do not know, I do not know. [He then] ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha-dharma is in your daily activities;
it is in your putting on clothes and eating meals; it is in your speech and social exchanges; it is in your walking, standing, sitting..."
"Your place of rest is where you void excrement and urine. As soon as you attempt to deliberate with the mind, it is already not so.
*Tut!* To weep until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut through the remainder of spring. The inscription for the portrait of Master Yushan says:
"When my donkey stumbled on the bridge over the stream, I mistakenly took the crushed beans for pearls. My children do not understand how to hide [the truth]."
"Family disgrace. This causes the old, ancient adept Yangqi to fall over laughing.
Chan Master Xingkong Zhiguan of Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said:
A monk asked Yanguan, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? Yanguan said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher. The monk brought the pure water pitcher to him.
The official said, "Return it to its original place. The monk asked again, and the official replied, "The ancient Buddha passed away long ago.
The Master [Yunmen] said, "It is difficult to share patterns and colors with the blind; it is difficult to share sounds with the deaf.
Since this monk could not realize the pivot of the occasion, Yanquan’s efforts were in vain. Yunmen said, "No trace remains," yet he failed to support Yanquan's words.
Xuedou said: "Even if one were to point one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, how could one avoid [the consequences]?
Yet, even this cannot rescue Yanguan. With his whisk, he drew a line and said, "The preceding entanglements are all cut off at once.
Now tell me, what is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? He threw down the whisk and descended from the seat. On another occasion, he ascended the hall and cited Baoshou’s opening of the assembly.

One day, San-sheng brought forth a monk’s koan. The Master said, "The assembly has been discussing it, saying that San-sheng possesses the art of 'crossing the rushing current and passing through the blade,' creating waves upon level ground;
while Bao-shou employs the mechanism of 'swift flames passing through the wind.'"
Thundering a clap of lightning toward the void, the two elders each extended a hand to uphold the *Linji Zhengfayan Zang* (The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji).
To speak in such a manner—to claim to be a descendant of Linji—is to proceed with extreme caution. Dongchan said:
"How can a mosquito support a great pillar? How can a lotus fiber bind Mount Sumeru? If it were truly the *Linji Zhengfayan Zang*, [it would not be so].
It is definitively extinguished within the two people.
Chan Master Yixian (Puweng) of Shangfang in Huzhou Prefecture possessed a naturally extraordinary and transcendent character; his eloquence was vast and unimpeded.
He ascended the hall and, citing the case where a monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou replied, "No. He then offered this verse: Dog...
"The Son has no Buddha-nature"—this returns it to the Great Man. Though right and wrong enter his ears, he hangs a gourd upon the wall.

In praise of the image of Bodhidharma: "A single word once uttered is as hard to recall as a galloping horse; Fortunately, the Sovereign let him pass. At the heart of the Yangtze River, a reed is used for a rudder;
How can the crest of the waves compare to the peril of this question?"
Chan Master Kongcou Zongyin of Yuyang in Ningbo Prefecture was a native of Western Sichuan. He first resided at Chongxian Baoshou in Huzhou. A monk asked, "What is the original body?
The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Nailed down and glued shut.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Great Way is level and expansive; it is free from names and free from forms. Eradicate [all conceptualization]..."
To do so would lose the essential meaning; to establish [a fixed position] would deviate from the fundamental principle.

From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of old down to the masters of ancient and modern times, all those who manifested great capacity and displayed great function were merely closing off the void and locking away dreams—their transgressions fill the heavens. Yet, could even the Venerable Yin escape having his face torn open?
After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and said: "If one does not enter the startling waves, it is difficult to encounter the fish that satisfies one's heart."
Ascending the hall: "Two arise from one; do not cling even to that one. Upon the level ground, there are countless dead people.
When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault. Plunging in and out within a pit of excrement—solitary and towering!
The flower must bloom through the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. Ascending the hall: An iron child of Kunlun receives a blow; [he goes] to the South Sea.
The Persian dance did not cease. At midnight, he lost the sash around his waist. Old Uncle Wang of the eastern village fell over laughing.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Entering the hall, he raised the case: A monk asked Changsha, "What is the place where those of the highest caliber walk?
Changsha said, "Like the eyes of a dead man. [The monk] asked, "How is it when those of the highest caliber meet one another? Changsha said, "Like a dead..."
A human hand. The Master said: "The eyes of the dead, the hands of the dead; the golden crow flies, the jade hare runs.
Cutting directly to the root, it is grasped from either side. Old Zhang falls drunk, lying on the official street; it was originally Old Li drinking private wine."
Chan Master Tui Gu Yiyun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was the son of the Huang family of Minqing in Fuzhou.
In his youth, he studied Confucianism and received the tonsure under Shantang Chun. He traveled extensively to seek instruction, eventually reaching Wu, where he first visited Tie’an Yi.

Next, he studied under Fozhao at Lingyin Monastery, and later followed him when he moved to Yuyang Monastery. There he served as the First Seat for ten years before departing to reside at Xiangshan for five years.
He was transferred to Kuangxiao Temple in Taizhou, and subsequently moved to Ganlu in Zhenjiang, Wanshou at Tiger Hill in Pingjiang, and Changlu in Huainan.
Late in life, he was appointed to Yuyang. Later, he retired to Xiangshan, but by imperial decree was summoned to preside over Jingci Temple. A monk asked, "Regarding the path of Sansheng:
'Whenever I encounter a person, I manifest; yet when I manifest, I do not act for others. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The East Dipper."
He moved westward. This is called the Way of Xinghua. "When I meet people, I do not come out; when I come out, I am already acting for others.

Furthermore, what does this mean? The Master said: "The Southern Dipper turns north; it is ten thousand *li* to Yuzhou. Ascending the hall, he said: "A rushing torrent passes the blade; a swift flame exceeds the wind.

The 'cracking' and the 'pecking' occur simultaneously—ten thousand *li* to Yuzhou. Someone said: "It is like a person learning archery; through long practice, one becomes skillful. But they fail to realize that...
To hit the mark before even drawing the bowstring is already to have wandered into circuitous paths.

Setting aside for a moment Zhaozhou’s act of leaning on his staff upon arriving at Zhuyou, what was the meaning of Upāsaka Fu saying, “The holy arrow has been broken”? [The Master] gave a shout and said:
"If one does not sleep in the same bed, how can one know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt? Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Shoushan picking up a bamboo stick.
Zhaozhou said, "If you call it a bamboo whisk, you contradict it; if you do not call it a bamboo whisk, you turn your back on it. What do you all call it?
Xiangyan Sheng stepped forward, seized the bamboo whisk, snapped it in two, and threw the pieces down the steps.
He then asked, "What is this? Zhaozhou said, "Blind! Xiangyan immediately prostrated himself. The Master said, "The school of Linji has been swept away to the very ground."
He passed away on the fifth month of the Bingyin year of the Kaixi era of Emperor Ningzong of the Song dynasty. He was fifty-eight years old, with thirty-five years of monastic seniority.
His stupa was erected in the northwestern corner of the temple.

Chan Master Miaosong of Shaolin on Mount Jing in Hangzhou Prefecture was a native of Jianning. He ascended the hall and, citing a case, said: A monk asked Muzhou, "What are words for unfolding and displaying?
Muzhou replied, "Appointing to office according to one's talent. The monk asked, "What are words that do not unfold or display?
Muzhou replied, "I humbly pray you will continue to enjoy [the sacrifice]. The Master said: "Muzhou was an ancient Buddha who skillfully responded to the stimuli of those who came to him. Although...
"However, it is thus; I have only attained eighty percent. Someone asked, 'What are the words of exposition and manifestation?
I replied to him: 'If you ask ten, I answer a hundred—what difficulty is there in that? Then they asked, 'What are the words of non-exposition and non-manifestation?
I gave a shout and said: 'Do not let the cesspool boil over!'"
Chan Master Xiuyan Shouyi of Yuyang Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture ascended the hall and said: He cited Daowu, who remarked, "Exaltedness does not lie at the summit;
wealth does not lie at Fuyan; joy does not lie in heaven; suffering does not lie in hell.
Acquaintances fill the world, but how many can truly know one's heart? Miaoxi said: "Exaltedness lies at the summit; wealth lies at Fuyan; joy lies..."
Heaven is in paradise; suffering is in hell. Who knows that beneath the straw hat is none other than the person of old?

“Great assembly, it is not that these two elders lacked the ability to apply themselves according to the occasion. However, as for the gate of the patch-robed monks (*śramaṇa*), they have not even dreamed of it.
But tell me, how is it within the gate of the patch-robed monks? After a long silence, he said: “If one is not a true connoisseur, all talk of enduring the cold year will be in vain.”
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Guankui’s visit to Linji. As Guankui entered, Linji descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and held him fast.

Guankui said, "I understand, I understand. Linji then let go of him. The Master offered this verse: After the rain has dispersed and the clouds have cleared, Lofty peaks rise in their dozens. Leaning on the railing, gazing again and again.

"Looking back, with whom am I together? He ascended the hall and raised the following case: Yanhua asked Baoci, "What is the true nature of the Buddha? Baoci replied, "Who does not have it? Yanhua was not satisfied.

He then requested further instruction from Huguo, who said, "Who has it? The Master said: "To say 'who does not have it' and 'who has it' is to speak with the full power of one's total capacity (*quanji*).
Yet, to turn oneself around at such a word is nothing short of being unremarkable (*bu jiliu*). Even if you were to act before the words were even raised, it would still be so."
"Mistaking a winnowing basket for an ironing board. A-he-he! If a person can understand how to ride a donkey backward, they will not follow after others for the rest of their lives.
Master Guyun Quan of Yuyang in Ningbo Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "A monk asked Xuefeng: 'The ancient stream is cold...'"
"A monk asked, 'What is the state of the cold spring at the ancient ravine? Feng said, 'Staring with wide eyes, one cannot see the bottom.

The monk asked, 'And what of those who drink from it? Feng said, 'It does not enter through the mouth. The monk then asked Zhaozhou, 'What is the state of the cold spring at the ancient ravine? Zhaozhou said, 'Bitter. The monk asked, 'And what of those who drink from it?
Zhaozhou said, 'Death. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: 'One person follows the waves; the other cuts off the flow of all streams.'"
To bring it forth: in the end, there is a lack of understanding. Today, if someone asks, "What is the old stream and cold spring of Yuyang?
you should simply reply to them, "One must personally see Xuefeng. As for "How is it for one who drinks from it?", ask Zhaozhou.
There is a verse for sending off a monk returning to Fengshan: "The phoenix child beneath Mount Fenghuang— As soon as its patterns appear, its wings and feathers are complete."
Qi. An iron net covers the heavens, yet it cannot block his returning heart, which already rests upon the branches of the azure paulownia tree.
Zen Master Hai-men Shi Qi of Tiantong, Ningbo Prefecture, first resided at Ruiyan in Taizhou; by imperial decree, he was transferred to Tiantong.

Every morning when he rose, his novice attendants would carry incense boxes and follow him through each of the halls as they performed their rounds of offering incense. Upon completion, [the following occurred].
He returned to the abbot’s quarters and, facing the Buddha, made a dedication (*pariṇāmana*) saying: "The *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, one volume, has been recited above;
I dedicate the merit toward True Suchness (*tathatā*)," and so forth. He did this daily as his constant practice, yet the entire monastery never believed him. The Master then said to the assembly:
"Each of you, eighty-one people, take up one scroll of the scripture and listen to this old monk recite it. The assembly [did as instructed].
Following the instructions, the Master sat upon his seat and recited. Each of the eighty-one people heard what was being recited;

it matched exactly what each held in their hands, word for word and phrase for phrase, without the slightest discrepancy or omission. Only then was the assembly’s doubt dispelled, as they realized he was a Great Bodhisattva of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra reborn in this world.
When Chan Master Shigan Zhenghao returned to the lakeside, he composed a verse that says: "Birds do not startle into flight, and the waters do not flow;
The azure pool is vast and empty, coldly containing autumn. Upon the tip of the single strand, there is no fragrant bait; The wind rolls the reed flowers onto the fishing boat."
Chan Master Shu’ān Fanzōng of Yunju in Nankang Prefecture ascended the hall and spoke on the story of Baizhang and the Wild Fox.
He offered this verse: Baizhang’s wild fox, The stone maiden has no husband. Once a single tear falls, The vast ocean dries up. Ascending the hall for the Buddha-Bathing ceremony, he said:
"How joyful it is that today the Sole Honored One has descended. At Shu’ān, there is nothing to celebrate his birthday; we simply take this brief moment..."
Rosewater: Washing away the pure Dharma-body of lake and mountains.
Master Tiennuyin of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said: He cited Nanquan, who said, "I, Old Teacher Wang, have raised a water buffalo since I was young.
If I intend to let it loose to the east of the stream, it will inevitably eat the king's water and grass."
If you let it loose toward the west of the stream, it will still not escape consuming the water and grass belonging to the king. It would be better to accept things as they are, bit by bit;
yet even this is not seen. The verse says: It would be better to accept things as they are, bit by bit. To call this an ordinary matter is already a mistake.
Green grass by the stream reveals their horns; in the mist and rain of a single straw cloak, to whose house does it belong?
Master Huizheng of Yueku at Heshan in Huzhou Prefecture, a Dharma successor of Master Huayan, ascended the hall and spoke. He cited how Tiantai Shao first visited Master Fa...
Yan. When a monk asked Yan, "What is a single drop of water from the Cao source? Yan said, "It is a single drop of water from the Cao source.
Upon hearing this, Huichao attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse: A single drop of water from the Cao source— Even if you scold one another, it is still a ladleful of soup.
The quail and sparrow chirp uselessly in the air, While the noble steed has already galloped a thousand li.

Chan Master Xiaoweng Miaokan of Yuyang Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Quanzhen of Tiantong. He was the son of the Mao family of Cixi. He had a broad forehead and a flat crown, with a noble and refined bearing.
He received his initial instruction from Yan’an Qin and later relied upon Xian’an Guan at Mount Jinshan, where he studied under Songyuan.
He visited Mount Yue and Lingyin, but in neither case did he find resonance. At that time, Wuyong was residing at Tiantong. The Master went directly to his quarters.
Wuyong asked, "Are you a wandering monk (*xingjue seng*) or a mountain-roaming monk? The Master replied, "A wandering monk. Wuyong asked, "What is the business of a wandering monk?

The Master then struck him with his sitting cloth (*zuju*). Wuyong said, "This monk dares to come here to pull the tiger's whiskers! He then had the Master attend the meditation hall. Wuyong... one [day]... [continued].
Every day, he asked the Master about the saying, "The dog has no Buddha-nature. As the Master was about to open his mouth, [Zhaozhou] struck him across the face with a bamboo staff.
The Master immediately presented a verse, saying: "A great poison-drum, thundering through heaven and shaking the earth; turn your head and look back!"
"Corpses lie scattered for ten thousand *li*. He nodded in agreement. He immediately ordered his attendant Xiang to prepare; shortly thereafter, Bao'en invited the Master to share his seat.
Subsequently, he took up residence at Miaosheng, then moved to Jinwen, followed by Guangxiao and Baoyun in Tiantai. Next, he went to Xuefeng in Min.
Not long after, an imperial decree summoned him to reside at Lingyin, where he founded the Great Compassion Monastery. He later moved to Ruiyan and responded to the call at Jiangxin. Before long...

When the imperial decree for Jingci Monastery was issued, he requested leave to decline, but it was not granted. The following year, the Governor-General of Jinghu submitted a memorial ordering that monks and Daoists purchase purple robes and clerical titles (*shihao*), and that those holding such titles be permitted to serve as abbots.
The Master indignantly declared, "If this were so, then even those with a thousand pieces of gold could preside over the Dharma;
our Way would surely be in peril. He submitted a memorial to the imperial throne and addressed a letter to the court, and thus the proposal was finally abandoned.

He retired from office. By imperial decree, he was summoned to move to Tiantong, but he declined with all his might and returned east to Cuiyan. When the seat at Yuyang was vacant, another edict ordered him to take up the post;
the Master declined a second time, but it was not permitted. He then accepted the decree. He propagated the teachings of Dayue and followed the lineage of Miaoxi in a systematic and orderly manner.

Entering the hall for discourse, he said: "The timely rain has fallen; the mountains and rivers are as if washed clean. The hidden birds call from the lofty trees; the remaining petals drift upon the distant waters. It is indeed so.
Pitying those who are blind, deaf, mute, or speech-impaired, [the Master] notes that they do not recognize the true essence of the teachings of this Dharma-method.

He cites the story of Baoshou opening the hall where the Three Sages pushed out a monk; the verse says: "One person’s journey on the road is as vast as heaven; Another’s returning heart is as swift as a light arrow.
Though their respective paths differ, You must know they arrive at the Celestial Court on the same day. He then cites Fenyang’s recognition.

He attained the realization of the "Staff" (zhuzhangzi) and concluded his travels. He spoke in verse: "On level ground there is no cause for establishing the topic; A sky-shaking sound stirs the cold, raging waves.
Even if one were to recognize the staff, It would still be viewed as a letter's envelope.

At that time, a second official letter arrived from Tiantong. The Grand Councilor, Zhao Gong, again invited him to take charge of Jingci Monastery, but he declined them all. He then manifested illness.
He wrote a verse, saying: "The mirror of karma hangs high; seventy-two years have passed. With one blow, it is shattered; the Great Way is level and vast.
He set down his brush and passed away in serene stillness.
Chan Master Xiyi of Lingyin Stone Drum in Hangzhou Prefecture cites the dialogue regarding the meeting between Langye Huijue and Fahua.
His verse says: "Meeting in person is not as good as hearing the name; Hearing the name is not as good as meeting in person. There is not even two ounces of gold here;
The common folk buy three sheng of wine. He then cites Nanquan, who said: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, last night at the third watch, arose..."
The Buddha saw it as a violation of the Dharma; he gave each of them twenty blows of the staff and expelled them from the monastery.
Zhaozhou said, "Whom does the Master intend for the staff to strike? Baizhang said, "Tell me, where exactly did Old Wang commit a transgression? Zhaozhou bowed and withdrew.
The Verse says: The spring breeze blows down the emerald peach blossoms; A single petal flows past a hundred thousand homes.
Who is there at the painted tower where wine is bought? Inviting one another to come drink Zhaozhou’s tea. In response to Liangshan Yuan’s verses on the Ten Oxherding Pictures: 1. Seeking the Ox:
He simply busies himself seeking it outwardly, Unaware that beneath his feet the mud is already deep. How many times has he passed over the fragrant grasses?
In the slanting sun, one sings a new tune of Xinfeng in vain. Second, seeing the tracks: before the cliff of withered trees, divergent paths abound;
rolling within the grassy thickets, do you realize it is not so? If your heels follow others, you will inevitably stumble past him right at the head. Third, seeing the ox:
having recognized its form and identified its sound, Dai Song has since excelled in his painting of cattle. Through and through.
They appear entirely similar at first glance, yet upon closer inspection, they are not quite complete. Having attained the ox in four stages, hold fast to the rope’s end and do not let it go;
many faults have not yet been eliminated. Slowly lead it by the nose, for you must first cause it to turn its head and recognize its old home.
Five: Tending the Ox. I willingly entrust this body to the mountain forests, though at times I also tread the dust beneath horse hooves.
Never having harmed another’s crops, one travels back and forth in vain labor for those on one’s back.
Riding the ox home, he points to the front slope, saying, "This is home. Blowing his *tóngjiǎo* horn, he emerges from the mists; suddenly, it transforms into a melody of returning home.
Not everyone appreciates a true connoisseur, as was the case with Bo Ya. Having forgotten the ox while retaining the man, when there is no ox within the pen, one drives it out into the mountains.

With smoke-shrouded cloak and rain-hat, even idleness is a luxury. Singing while walking and playing music while seated, free from all constraints, one wins the freedom of a single body amidst heaven and earth.

The eight persons and the ox are both forgotten; the realm of sentient beings is already empty. How can the message within this be communicated? There is no one coming from behind and no one departing before.
I wonder who will rely upon to continue this school? Returning to the root and source for the ninth time, the numinous mechanism does not fall into the trap of existence or non-existence.
Seeing forms and hearing sounds, there is no need to be deaf. Last night the golden crow flew into the sea; at dawn—
Returning as before, the single wheel is red. Entering the marketplace with hands hanging down—this fellow has personally come from among the heterodox species;
clearly visible are the horse's jaw and the donkey's jowl. With one sweep of an iron staff as swift as the wind, ten thousand households and a thousand gates are all flung wide open.
Chan Master Liaozong of Xuefeng Mettang in Fuzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Vast emptiness, cold and ice-cold—such is the principle of pure vacuity;
ultimately it has no body. Why, then, are there so many mists and rains? Do you understand?
If you understand, you will receive the seven kinds of offerings from all of you; if you do not understand, even a drop of water will be difficult to digest."
Chan Master Yuchun Chu of Xuedou in Ningbo Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Though you investigate with every possible means, you do not see his face; at once, let it rest.
Wherever you encounter him, he is there—on the long rows of beds, eating porridge and rice, taking full satisfaction as his goal.
Now I ask you: how many times has a single grain of rice from the monastery passed through your hands? He then ascended the hall and said: "Chopping nails."

Cutting through iron. Deliberately eccentric. Leveling the high by descending to the low—a source of laughter for the patch-robed monks. When Huangjue reaches this point, there is no reason that can be fully articulated.
I wonder, how will you gentlemen explain this? Ascending the hall, he said: "The true eye of Mahesvara is radiant and blazing.
When one point is thoroughly penetrated, ten thousand functions respond all at once. Binding tigers and capturing dragons, it startles heaven and shakes the earth. Yet, it is simply ordinary."
"A single phrase. Again, how is it? "Do not bring right and wrong to judge me; this floating life’s contrivances have nothing to do with one another.
Chan Master Siduo of Panshan in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying:

"Climbing mountains and crossing waters rely entirely upon this person. He then threw down the staff and said: "It is easy to get along when we first meet; it is difficult to maintain harmony while living together."
Ascending the hall: "Silent and alert—this is a dead man with breath. Alert and silent—this is a useless block of stone.
Heh! To whom shall this cool breeze be entrusted?"

Chan Master Miaoji Congkuo of Yuyang Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuyang Puxian. He was the son of the Lin family of Changxi. From his youth, he was exceptionally intelligent and did not speak frivolously.
At the age of fifteen, he received the tonsure and became a monk. He studied under Focin Cai and Lan’an Xu, and later relied upon Dayuan Puxian. There was...
He obtained [the position] and served diligently for several years. Daoyuan took him under his care, regarding him as one of his own kindred.

Daode participated in the assembly at Miaoxi beneath Huigyan Peak and subsequently attended Daoyuan during his move to Yuyang Monastery. When Daoyuan succeeded to the seat at Jingshan, the Master presided over the First Seat.
Prime Minister Shen invited him to take up the abbacy at Mount Lu; it was there that Yixiang offered the incense for Dayuan. He was later transferred...

When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, he issued an imperial decree for the Śarīra reliquary stupa to proceed to the imperial capital and be enshrined within the Guantang Hall of the Forbidden City.
He summoned the Master to the Bilin Hall and asked, "From where did these śarīras manifest? The Master replied, "They manifested from Your Majesty’s sagely mind.
The Emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed upon the Master the title of Chan Master Miaozhi. The King of Japan also read the Master’s verses and sayings.
He claimed to have achieved personal enlightenment. He observed the rites of a disciple for the annual memorial services and even donated timber for the construction of a Śarīra Hall.
In his later years, the Master retired to Mount Wushan, where he established the Xiaoyue Hermitage as his final dwelling. In the *gengzi* year of the Chunxi era, he manifested a slight ailment;
after reciting a verse of gāthā, he passed away at the age of sixty-two, with forty-seven years of monastic seniority. His stūpa was enshrined within the private quarters of the hermitage.
A monk once raised the story of Zhaozhou seeing a novice attendant with a master for Master Ruruyuan (如如顏丙), a lay disciple in the lineage of Chan Master Xuefeng Yan.
When asked about it, the layman answered with a verse: "To grasp a single blade of thatch grass And call it the sixteen-foot golden body— If one understands this..."
Every single thing is the Way; the pupil in the eye is the person before you. Regarding the verse on the story of the Dog of Zihu:
"In my poor home there is nothing at all; I keep only a single dog. Even if a Buddha were to appear, he would still have to meet one bite."
The Nineteenth Generation under Great Mirror (Dajian):
Chan Master Qingyuan Yin’s Dharma Heir, Chan Master Zheng’an Zongguang of Jingju Monastery in Jixian Prefecture. A monk asked: "Not within, not without..."
"Not outside, nor in between. Tell me, where is it? The Master said, "When meeting people, do not speak of it mistakenly.
The monk asked, "Is there still a way to seek further instruction? The Master said, "Seeking cleverness leads to failure. The monk bowed. The Master said, "That is quite close.
He ascended the hall and said: "Father and son have inherited this mountain; the regulations of the monastic community are not many. The master..."
The guest’s countenance remained as it was before. He suddenly called to the assembly, "Tell me, after remaining as it was before, what then? A single stick of incense answers the Sacred Countenance.
He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "Do not cherish the sacred; 'sacred' is a provisional name. Do not loathe the mundane; 'mundane' is falsely established.
If you can simply exhaust the sentiments of sacred and mundane, then naturally both self and other will be forgotten. It is exactly like this."
At that time, who could have fully understood this? He held up his staff and said: "The stone woman pierces the needle; the mountain colors are exquisite.
The wooden man pulls the thread; the ocean clouds arise. Then he struck the ground once and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Wuming Huiweng of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture, a native of Fuzhou, was a successor of Chan Master Yong of Gushan. He ascended the hall and spoke, citing the following:

A monk from under the guidance of Master Jiashan went to Gaoting. As soon as he prostrated himself, Gaoting struck him. The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects; why does the Master strike me?"

He struck him. The monk bowed again. Ting struck him once more and drove him out. The monk returned and related this to Jia Shan. Jia Shan asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Jia Shan said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. Had you understood, Jia Shan’s mouth would have been closed for good.
Ying’an said, "For a time, Gao Ting could not restrain his impatience; yet, alas, he let go with his staff too hastily. If that monk had at that moment—"
"This fellow—let alone Gaoteng and Jia Shan; even if Bodhidharma himself were to appear, he would cut him into three pieces.
Why? Because when a family prospers, filial sons are born; when a state is powerful, it has strategic ministers. The Master said:
"Gaoteng and Jia Shan each employed their methods with perfect appropriateness, yet one among them was slightly off the mark. Mingguo speaks thus."

This is the tea pitcher from Gong County. In the Dingchou year of the Jiading era, the Master compiled the *Lian Deng Hui Yao* (Essentials of the Linked Lamps), which was transmitted throughout the monastic communities.

Chan Master Zangsou Shanzen of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou Prefecture was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyin Shanhui; he was the son of the Lü family of Nan’an, Quanzhou, and at the age of ten...
Third: He received the tonsure at Chongfu Monastery in Jun County. At sixteen, he traveled abroad and received full ordination in Hangzhou.

He visited Miaofeng at Lingyin Monastery, entered his room for instruction, and realized the essential meaning. Later, he emerged from seclusion to reside at Guangxiao Monastery in Li, then ascended to Chengtian.
Subsequently, he moved to Suxi Yuanjue in Anji, then to Xuefeng in Fu. Thereafter, by imperial decree, he was transferred to Yuyang and then to Jing Mountain.
"Regarding 'occupying the room': this refers to the place where one stands after having finished inquiring after the master's health and burning incense by the old monk’s side.
You fool, it is you who are at fault; do not come here to blame the old monk. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"The ancients said, 'The single word "knowledge' is the gate to all wonders. Yet others have said, 'The single word "knowledge" is the gate to all calamities.'"

One can enter through these two gates, but one must also be able to exit them. The Buddhas of the three periods have not been able to exit; the six generations of patriarchs have not been able to exit;
the old monks of the world have not been able to exit. Why? It is easy to transform iron into gold, but difficult to transform gold into iron.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The Great Earth is the body of purple-golden hue. Every day, you people..."
Opening his eyes, he beholds the very heart and liver of Śākyamuni; taking a step, he treads upon Śākyamuni’s nostrils.
To speak of existence or non-existence is deception; to speak of arising or ceasing is slander; to speak of the mind being the mind or not the mind is delusion.
Without deception, without slander, and without delusion: the spring breeze blows down the peach and plum blossoms; thin mist and sparse rain enshroud the green peaks.
Ascending the hall: Spring snow is cold, spring nights are short. The heart of the ancient Buddha is broken within the lamp bowl;
the Eye of the True Dharma is dry, a mere wick of paper. Shake up your spirit and simply keep looking, keep looking. The Big Dipper shifts west, the Southern Dipper turns east;
the Lantern Festival remains the fifteenth day of the first month. Ascending the hall: Lingyun attained awakening upon seeing peach blossoms. Xuansha said, "I dare say that old man..."
The elder brother had not yet penetrated it. When Xiangyan heard the sound of striking bamboo, he attained awakening. Yangshan said, "You have not yet understood the Patriarchs' Zen.
Among the practitioners of Zen, ten out of five or two will say, "In this school of mine, there is no path at all that can be approved.
Even so, they still do not know where Xuansha’s or Yangshan’s tongues fall. Do you wish to see these two great elders? Drunken me in the sky of falling blossoms. Borrow—
From the *Guǎnxián Lǐ*: A Small Sermon on New Year’s Eve. The Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked an old master, "What is it like when the year has ended and the age is exhausted?
The master replied, "It remains as before: 'Early spring is still cold. The Master said, "When the old master answered in such a way, I fear you all might forget.
If someone were to ask me today, 'What is it like when the year has ended and the age is exhausted? I would take up my staff and strike them immediately."
When the other asked, "Why did you strike me? he immediately replied, "Do you want me to tell you that it is still cold in the early spring?
He once inscribed his own portrait, saying: "In my Zen practice there has been no awakening; in my literacy there is but a limited measure.
My eyes are triangular like those of a sorrowful foreigner from Mount Yan; my face is wrinkled like Zhao Po’s when she takes a sip of vinegar. This one stroke stands far above all others."
I venture to say: "Rice is made from grain. He sent this verse to the monk Ren: "The silver threads in my temples cannot weave a cold-weather robe;
How can the characters I cook provide relief for hunger? I wish to bestow upon you the Dharma of peace and bliss, But being so busy, I have yet found no leisure.
He was born on the twelfth day of the tenth month of the Jiayin year of the Shaoxi era of Emperor Guangzong of the Song dynasty. He passed away during the Jingyan era.
The twenty-first day of the fifth month in the year Dingchou [1277]. At the age of eighty-three, his remains were interred in the South Pagoda Cloister.

Zen Master Dongsou Zhongying of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Most certainly do not seek it following others; there is no need to laboriously seek it within yourself.
Transverse and vertical, lively and agile—there is letting go and there is gathering in. What is this? A single leaf falls, and the heavens..."
Late autumn. He ascended the hall and said: "Deluded beings are caught in stillness and agitation; the enlightened have neither good nor evil.
This old man Qici from Fenghua County has a protruding belly and short legs. Tugging at his cloth bag through the crossroads, he is dazed and foolish, carefree and unconstrained.
How does he compare to Old Longya, who holds a broken wooden ladle in his hand? He ascended the hall and raised his whisk.
He drew a single line and said: "Fuxi revealed the secrets of heaven and earth; for those who do not yet understand, let them receive this message. He then added three dots and said:
"Gautama displayed the form of the circle and the *ī* [the three dots]; for those who do not yet understand, let them receive this message. How can one discern the meaning of these messages?
[The Master] did not speak of the Way. On the winter solstice, the festival of recording the clouds, he struck his whisk and ascended the hall.
He said: "Above, it is not in heaven; below, it is not on earth; in between, it is not in man. He gave a shout and said: "Tell me, where does this one shout fall?
If you can understand it, there is guest and there is host; there is illumination and there is function. If you cannot..."
[The Master] says, "Understood. After the formal session, he tours the hall and partakes of tea. He ascends the Dharma seat and strikes the drum;

the assembly gathers, hearing with one ear and seeing with one eye, transcending heaven and earth and surpassing past and present. Why is this so? On the fifth day of the fifth month is the Dragon Boat Festival. [He] ascends the Dharma seat.
The practitioner walks when it is time to walk; the sitter sits when it is time to sit. To the left or to the right—there is nothing acceptable and nothing unacceptable.
Thorns in the garden of ambrosia; honeyed fruit on the head of the *phellodendron* tree. Just so, yet not so; not so, yet just so.
A house of skilled merchants does not allow goods to stagnate.
Chan Master Youyun Zongmao of Longji Temple in Jishui, Jixian Prefecture, was the son of the Wang family of Luling. From childhood, he delighted in sitting in meditation.
At the age of twelve, he left home to become a monk under Haishi Cong of Baoshou Temple. At nineteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
At twenty-two, he went to Lingyin Temple to attend upon Miaofeng. On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa, as Miaofeng ascended the hall, he held up his staff and said:
"Śākyamuni is coming! Do you all see him? His subtle and wondrous pure Dharma-body is endowed with the thirty-two marks.
Having said this, he set down his staff and declared, "Seeing that you all do not understand, I am entering nirvana.
At these words, the Master attained sudden and complete enlightenment. He subsequently ascended Mount Foding on the eastern side of Jishui, where he found the old site of the mountain master Xiu.
Eating from the trees and drinking from the mountain streams, his shadow never left the mountains. He once sang of himself: "The mountain monk has his lot dwelling among the misty vines;
No rice, no money—let him worry about none of it. The water is like lapis lazuli, the mountains like jade; Before my eyes, there is more than enough."
Later, Houfeng sent his dharma robe, a bamboo staff, and a self-portrait he had inscribed himself to the Master, saying: "Upon the solitary peak of Miaofeng, the grass grows lush;
Transversely grasped is a bamboo staff, three feet of iron. Only Foding and Longji may know it; Father and son do not transmit the true secret.
The Master once posted a notice on his gate that read: "Apart from the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, which one is it?"
If you can speak for yourself, I will grant that you have personally seen Longji. If not, then remain outside the gate.
Xueyan once said to him, "How many people has the Master ever accepted? The Master replied, "I have never, from the beginning, forced an ox to eat grass.
At the end of the year, a monk asked, "When the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives..."
"What? the Master asked. "There is no one at the gate demanding payment. On the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month in the Dinghai year of the Zhizhi era (1297), he suddenly manifested illness.
He gathered the assembly and entrusted them with his final affairs. Tapping his fingers once, he said, "This alone is my parting word to the assembly.
At the second watch, the assembly requested a verse. The Master took up a brush and wrote: "A single lamp is within sight; there is nothing further to be said."
The great earth sank level, and the void split asunder. Having finished writing, he became still and silent. His worldly age was eighty, and his monastic seniority sixty-one.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on a mountain peak.
Chan Master Wuchu Daoguan of Yuyang Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jian of Jingci. He was a native of the Lu family of Hengxi in Ning County.

Having studied under Beijian at Jingci and received his transmission, he served as the master of literary correspondence. Later, he resided at Yuyang. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "One 'dong' (east), two 'dong' (winter). You..."
"Nǒng wǒ nǒng! (We two, we two! Laughing secretly in the dark, he utters empty words to one's face. Though this is but ordinary tea and rice, who knows there are worms within the grain?
Last night a fine wind blew, snapping down a pine tree before the gate. [He] ascends the hall and employs the "black bean" method to change people’s eyes—there are as many as the sands of the Ganges.
But as for those who can understand the story of the brazier, how many could there be? Nine times nine.
Nine. The Buddhas of the three periods do not know its existence; turning his body around, he kicks over the five Sumeru mountains. Why use the Dharma-body to hide the Northern Dipper?
To hide the Northern Dipper is to clearly flaunt one’s family disgrace to the outside world. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:

"The orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma, the very nostrils of the patch-robed monks, fills the void of space; there is nowhere to avoid it. How laughable are those deluded streams who, under the bright sun and clear sky, open [their eyes]..."
Turn your eyes away; you do nothing but nod off to sleep. Furthermore, there is that "Yellow-Faced Old Man" who, failing to distinguish good from evil, plunges into the mud and the water, yet says:
"At the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I did not obtain a single dharma, and he conferred upon me the prediction of enlightenment.
How is this any different from gouging a sore into healthy flesh or seeking a stem for a flower in the sky? Ultimately, how is it so? *Siri siri*. Since one accords with the world, [erect] a stupa.
In the western hermitage of the monastery was Chan Master Jiandao Guangwen of Jing Mountain, a successor of Chan Master Daoyan of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou Prefecture.
He was the son of Lin [family] of Houguan; his mother was Chen. His family had followed their ancestral occupation for generations.

He was a Confucian by birth. His paternal uncle had become a śramaṇa, named Zhilong, residing at Guangxiao Temple in Wānlíng. He went to rely upon him and received the tonsure and full ordination at the age of eighteen.
Initially, he studied under masters of various lineages for a very long time, including Tierniuyin, Shaoshi Muzhou, and Wujie Pai. Later, he visited Zhe’ung at Tiantong;
although his mind met the teaching like a needle meeting its eye, he knew within himself that he was not yet settled. Upon visiting Shuangjing again, he sat in meditation one night.

Between the eaves, he heard the striking of the gong three times; entering the hall, he tripped while dragging his sandals. It was as if waking suddenly from a dream. The following morning, he went to the master’s quarters.
The elder raised the story of Zhaozhou washing his alms bowl. Just as the Master was about to open his mouth, the elder abruptly stopped him, whereupon he attained immediate and total enlightenment.
In the Wuzi year of the Shaoding era, he left to reside at Xiaojingci in Siming. Subsequently, he served in succession as abbot at Xiangshan, Wanshou, and Xuefeng.

On the occasion of opening the furnace for the eight monastic seats at Wujingci, Lingyin, and Jingwu under the patronage of Duke Dou Yu, the Master ascended the hall and cited Zhaozhou’s instruction to the assembly:
"Thirty years ago, when I was in the South, there was a 'no-host-and-guest' koan at the head of my brazier that has remained until this very day, with no one raising it.
The Master said: "The myriad phenomena of the forest and the mountains, brightness and darkness, form and emptiness—day and night they are raised!"
Yang. Zhaozhou was an ancient Buddha; it was not that he did not know, but rather that his progress was too hurried. Entering the hall, [he said]: "The pupils in the eyes of Yangqi;
the marrow in the crown of Linji’s head. One is not it, two are not it. If you do not respond when pointed out, white clouds lie ten thousand miles away.
On the occasion of the Buddha’s path, he entered the hall and said: "Mistake, mistake! For six years, the grass rope bound you in vain. Clear, clear! Opening [the gate].
Having attained the Eye, one arrives at the Great Dawn of Heaven. The heavens and earth of past and present; the sun and moon of past and present;
the stars and constellations of past and present. [He] clapped his hands once and said: "The sword has long since departed; one must strictly avoid marking the boat. Ascending the hall, [he said]:

"Yunmen’s bestowing of three blows of the staff upon Dongshan was like feeding an infant with chewed food. Huangbo’s striking Linji with three blows of the staff was like pressing down a cow's head to make it eat grass."

Right now, not even a hair’s breadth is transgressed; there is a skillful means. After a long silence, he said: "The great matter cannot be handled for you; the small matters you must take upon yourself.

Dongshan said: "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Caoshan immediately attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse: "Thirty years ago, I saw the cypress tree in the courtyard; today I see it as before, without change. If you ask me what the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West is—this very thing is it. Dongshan heard of this and said: "Caoshan has truly seen me. Caoshan then went to see Yunyan again and asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Yunyan said: "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Caoshan was greatly enlightened. He then returned to Dongshan and said: "I have finally understood the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West. Dongshan asked: "How did you understand it? Caoshan said: "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Dongshan said: "You have finally seen me. Caoshan then bowed and departed. Dongshan called out to him: "Wait! Wait! Caoshan turned his head. Dongshan said: "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Caoshan immediately attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse: "Thirty years ago, I saw the cypress tree in the courtyard; today I see it as before, without change. If you ask me what the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West is—this very thing is it. Dongshan heard of this and said:
"Where have you gone? Cao said, "I have gone to the place of non-alteration. [The Master] asked, "In the place of non-alteration, how can there be going?
Cao said, "Going, too, is non-alteration. The Master said, "Clouds hide the seamless robe; birds roost on the sproutless branch."
Ascending the hall: The spring wind is like a blade; the spring rain is like ointment. Where it cannot be cut or tailored, the color of the peach blossoms grows ever more exquisite.
When Lingyun saw them once, he went away without doubt; Xie Lang danced his oars and presented his rudders.
Ascending the hall: Guizong slew the snake; Bimozha held up the pitchfork; Heshan beat the drum; Zhaozhou offered tea. Opening a shop at the crossroads of the street.
"Buying and selling for cash, with no credit. He ascended the hall and said: "For thirty years I have sought the sword-wielder;
how many times have the leaves fallen and the branches sprouted again? Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, until this very day, I have had no further doubts. The Master said:
Upon reflection, my spring dreams have nothing extraordinary; there is only Lingyun who speaks of them to others.

As for Xuansha’s saying, “Truly accurate, most truly accurate—I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate,” how would you explain this? If it were not for sleeping in the same bed, [how could one know?]

How could one know that what covers the bottom has been worn through? Entering the hall: Ten thousand *li* without a blade of grass; overhead it stretches endlessly. Stepping out the door is already grass;
beneath one's feet it stretches endlessly. Traveling by night, one simply covets the bright moon, unaware of the cold of crossing the water while still wrapped in one’s robes.

Chan Master Wén of Lóngxī, Suìchāng, Chùzhōu Prefecture, addressed the assembly: "Without marks and without form, it is fundamentally still and vast. The moment one lifts the eyes, it becomes remote and distant.

Sitting quietly upon the meditation cushion with nothing else to do— Outside the window, a single cry of "pó bǐng jiāo!"* *Note: "Pó bǐng jiāo" is the sound of a bird (the *bìngjiāo*) calling for its young.*
