Why does one who knows how to catch mice become a cat? "A field of a thousand years has eight hundred owners.
For the bathing of the Buddha, he ascends the hall; the pure *dharmakāya* sifts through dust and raises up clouds of earth.
The perfect *saṃbhogakāya* relies on wealth to deceive the poor. Among the thousands of millions of *nirmāṇakāyas*, which body is being bathed? Thank you.
Sanniang Chengyin ascends the hall: Above your head is heaven; beneath your feet is earth. The green mountains are green mountains; the white clouds are white clouds.
If you understand this, when there is a horse you ride the horse; when there is no horse, you walk on foot. If you do not understand...
"When traveling at night, do not step on white; it is either water or stone. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The handless man performs a fist; the tongueless man understands speech.
Suppose the handless man strikes the tongueless man; the tongueless man hurriedly says, 'Not necessary. After a long silence, he said:
'Just this "not necessary"—no monk in the world can leap out of it. [He] ascended the hall and said: "This..."

Everyone carries the jade of Mount Jing in their bosom; everyone harbors the pearl of the vast ocean in their breast. They all claim to turn the pivot and handle the mechanism of Buddhas and Patriarchs, and to grasp the very core of the monk’s reality.
They all say, "The eye at the crown of the head is upright; the talisman behind the elbow is efficacious.

Yet they do not realize that the numinous tortoise bearing the cosmic map brings about the very omen of its own destruction. What is this phrase that transcends the ordinary? "When the morning mist does not emerge, the market is closed."
The evening clouds travel a thousand li. Entering the hall: Huangbo’s staff in hand—this is gouging out flesh to create a sore.
Dayu’s fist under the ribs—this is eating salt to quench thirst. If it is swift, it is easy to change; if it has lasted long, it is difficult to remedy.

If one who selects the Buddha lacks such an eye, what is the use of pretending to understand for a thousand years? (He lets out a shout. Entering the hall: Cast away the bowl, the spoon, and the chopsticks.
"You must not eat. Close off your throat, lips, and mouth. You must not exhale. The physical body (rūpakāya) is at ease; the Dharma-body (dharmakāya) cannot but be at ease.
Are the Dharma-body and the physical body one or two? The flower must bloom throughout the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow.
[He] ascended the hall. Juezhì held up a single finger. Xuefeng rolled three wooden balls. Shigong...

The bow is drawn and the arrow is set. At Huating, there is but a short oar upon a solitary boat; at Fengshan, there is no dharma to be preached—yet this does not hinder one from cutting off all paths.

Within Hangzhou, however, there is a certain excellence. Wherein lies this excellence? There are four or five hundred lanes of willows and flowers, and two or three thousand towers of pipes and strings.
[He] ascends the hall: "When the Great Matter is not yet clarified, it is as if one has lost one's parents. The Great Matter...
The matter is already clear. It is like mourning for one’s parents. You say: "Is there a stripping away? Is there no stripping away?
At the place where I usually see guests off, I recall the moment of parting from my own home. Entering the hall: hearing sound to awaken to the Way—this blocks your ears;
seeing form to clarify the mind—this replaces your eyes. Sitting upright upon the meditation cushion, threading a needle’s eye. A gust of west wind.
"Come. Two or three fallen leaves. In the year Jia-shen of the Zhi Zheng era, he moved to Benjue Temple in Hezhou.
In Ding-hai, the Imperial Preceptor bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Furi Puzhao Hui bian. This perfectly coincided with the words of the divine monk from former days.

Later, retiring from Guangxiao Temple, he returned to Tianning. Ascending the hall, he said: "It is easy to swallow the mountains, rivers, and the great earth within a single hair; however, [the mountains and rivers...]"
It would be difficult for the great earth to swallow up a single hair; yet it is neither difficult nor easy.
I spread my tattered mat and sleep by day, imagining that even in the Tuṣita Heaven above, there is no such thing as this sun scorching one’s back.

I have built the West Studio as a plan for my final years and styled myself the "Old Man of the West Studio. In the ninth month of autumn in the year Wushen of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict was issued to the Great [Monks] of Jiangnan...

More than ten Buddhist monks were assembled at Mount Jiang to establish a great Dharma assembly. The Emperor commanded the Master to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma; the Emperor was greatly pleased.

In the spring of the Jihou year, he again summoned the Master to preach the Dharma and bestowed a vegetarian feast below Wenlou Hall, where he personally received his inquiries. Upon the Master’s departure, the Emperor saw him off.

Silver was issued from the Inner Treasury to bestow as a gift. In the autumn of the gengxu year, the Emperor, considering the states and manifestations of ghosts and spirits to be profound, subtle, and difficult to fathom, intended to summon and interrogate those among the monks who were extensively learned in the Tripitaka.
The Master, along with Mengtang E and Xingzhong Ren, responded to the imperial decree and arrived at the capital.
They were lodged at Dajianjiesi Temple. The Master drew upon the sutras and cited the treatises to compose a work intended for presentation; however, he suddenly manifested signs of his passing.
He fell ill. Four days later, he bathed, changed his robes, and sought out a brush to write a verse, saying: "The true nature is perfectly luminous; fundamentally, there is neither birth nor death.
A wooden horse neighs at night; the sun rises in the west. Having finished writing, he said to Mengtang, "I am going. Mengtang replied:
"Where are you going? the Master replied, "I am going to the West. Daotang asked, "If there is a Buddha in the West, is there no Buddha in the East?
The Master then let out a thunderous shout and passed away. This was on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month of the Xinhai year.

When the Emperor heard of this, he lamented for a long time. At that time, cremation was prohibited; however, because of the Master, a special dispensation was granted to follow the precedent of *jiaowei* (cremation). After the fire had subsided, several teeth and the tongue remained.

The jewel did not decay; his śarīra were of five colors, interspersed among the remaining skeletal remains. His disciple, Wénshèng, reverently took the bones and all that remained undecayed back to the stupa in the Western Chamber.
He calculated his worldly lifespan to be seventy-five years and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇera-vaṣa) to be sixty-three.
Chan Master Yuguan Zhiji of Mount Jing in Hangzhou Prefecture was styled Yizhong and took the alternative name Xilu. He was the son of the Gu family of Wuxian County in Suzhou.
Having left home at a young age at Haiyun Monastery on Qionglong Mountain, he received full ordination and listened to the Dharma Master Xianshou lecture on the *Dharmadhātuvibhāga*.
Before the lecture had even reached its conclusion, he suddenly laughed and said: "The single true Dharmadhātu is perfectly identical to the great void; it is only when one engages with..."
These words would merely constitute superfluous dharma. Even if one were to obtain a rain of jeweled flowers from heaven, what benefit would that bring me?

He then went to visit Xiaoyin at Jianye. Xiaoyin’s literary talent and moral virtue moved the entire age. When the Master slightly revealed his own literary brilliance, they were able to extend their mutual acquaintance.
A man from Youyu rebuked him, saying: "With such talent as yours, do you not think of shouldering the True Dharma?"
"Shall I simply remain a slave to the literary world? The Master’s tongue was silenced and he could not answer. He returned to Haeyun, his mind stifled with distress;
for over a month, he did not close his eyes even for a moment. Suddenly one day, seeing autumn leaves falling in the courtyard, he attained sudden enlightenment.

He traveled to the Double Path (Shuangjing) to pay his respects to Jizhao and present what he had realized. Jizhao approved him. In the Renwu year of the Zhizheng era, he took charge of Longjiao in Changguo;
subsequently, he led Puci. In Wuxu, he was transferred to Jingci, and later presided over Mount Jing.
A monk asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? The Master said, "The Stone Gandang at the crossroads. As the monk hesitated—
He asked again. The Master said, "There is still a second ladle of foul water remaining. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest?
The Master said, "You head toward Xiangxiang; I head toward Qin. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest?
The Master said, "Constantly on the road, yet never leaving home. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "Constantly at home, yet..."

While on the way, [a monk] asked, "What is the master within the master? The Master said, "Holding Mohe Yan crosswise, I issue the full command; throughout the peaceful realm, I strike down the foolish and stubborn.
The monk asked, "I have already received the Master's instruction regarding guest and host. As for the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zongcheng*), what is it like?

The Master said, "A leap year once every three years; the ninth day of the ninth month is the Double Ninth Festival. [Another monk] asked, "Sentient beings are hindered by their own understanding. What about the Bodhisattva?"

[The monk] asked, "What about when one has not yet left behind discursive thought? How does the *upādhyāya* [act]? The Master said, "The weather is cold and the days are short; two people share one bowl.
[The monk] asked, "Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya is not yet born. At this very moment, to whom is the Buddha-dharma entrusted?
The Master said, "I, the old monk, beat the drum of retreat. [The monk] said, "With no Śākyamuni before and no Maitreya after, is there still anyone capable of studying the Way?"
[The monk] said, "There is not. The Master said, "The wind does not come; the tree does not move. [The monk] asked, "How far apart are the Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan?
The Master raised his hand and said, "When opened, it becomes a palm; when clenched, it becomes a fist. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "A mad dog chasing a clod of earth.
[The monk] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "The moonlight is white with the clouds; the sound of the pines carries..."
[Luohan] Han asked, "The mind of the Great Immortal of India was secretly transmitted from east to west. What is this mind that was secretly transmitted?

The Master said, "In the ninth month, yellow leaves flutter down like gold. [Luohan] Han said, "Master, do not point to external objects to show people. The Master said: *Note: This is a translation of the encounter dialogue (wenda) between Master Luohan Han and his teacher, Master Guishan Lingyou.*

“An old monk’s transgression. A question was asked: “If the mere intention to act is already a deviation, and the stirring of a thought is already a departure from the truth, then if one neither intends nor moves, is there still any fault?
The Master said: “There is. The questioner asked: “Ultimately, what then is it? The Master said: “Do not recognize your own pure *dharmakāya* (intrinsic nature).
A question was asked: “What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Master said: “A straw sandal with its heel-cord cut off. The questioner asked: “How about this?”
"This is the master of the Dharma-body. The Master said, "The peaked eaves and the scholar's hat. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "It is a ready-made commodity;
what is there you do not understand? As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. A monk asked, "The Ultimate Way is not difficult;
it only dislikes discrimination. When there is no discrimination, how is it? The Master said, "When meeting rice, eat rice; when meeting tea, drink tea. The monk bowed.
He prostrated. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "How is it when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water?

The Master said, "When it is cold, heaven and earth are cold throughout. [The monk] asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the water? The Master said, "When it is hot, heaven and earth are hot throughout.
[The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A lake before the gate. [A monk] asked, "As for the mind..."
"The Buddha and sentient beings—these three are without distinction. "Is there still something definitive about this? The Master said, "Definitive.
[The student] asked, "It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing. What is it? The Master said, "I do not know.

[The student] asked, "The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories. Why then are there thousands of millions of transformation bodies? The Master held up his whisk and said, "Tell me."
"What body-number is this? The monk prepared to offer a reply, but the Master gave a shout. He asked, "The new year begins its reign; all things are renewed.
What is the Buddha-dharma of the New Year? The Master said, "Incense and flowers every day; lamps every night."
[The Master] said: "Leaning quietly upon the meditation cushion, there is nothing else; the long day passes in vast stillness, a thanksgiving for the Great Peace.
The Master said: "Only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it. A question was asked: "What is the original body, Vairocana? The Master said:

"It is not separate from that which you, the disciple, are asking about. [The questioner] asked: "How does one maintain this? The Master said: "Since he has no wound of his own, do not injure him. A question was asked: "Without arising..."
"How is it at the moment of a single thought? The Master said, "A practitioner should be thus. [The monk] said, "If so, then I shall act in accordance with this.
The Master said, "You are a man who lives in vain and dies in vain. [The monk] asked, "How does one phrase embody the three mysteries? The Master said:
"Riding an iron boat atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak. [The monk] asked, "What is 'one mystery containing three essentials'?
The Master said, "The pupils in the eyes blow wood-whistles and shout. He asked, "What is the style of your house, Master?
The Master said, "I have blown down the one pine tree in front of the gate. [The monk] said, "I did not ask about this wind. The Master said, "What wind did you ask about? [The monk] said—

Regarding the family tradition, the Master said: "In my place, great merit does not warrant reward. A questioner asked: "How was it before Ox-head saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "A poisonous tiger hides in the deep mountains.
[The questioner] asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "A swarm of snakes is exposed in the shallow grass. [The questioner] asked:
"How is it both when he has seen him and when he has not? The Master said: "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night."
Question: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is; yet the cat and the white ox do know that there is.
I wonder, what is it that they know? The Master said: "A nun is originally made of woman. Question: "When a Śrāvaka perceives nature, it is like seeing the moon at night;
when a Bodhisattva perceives nature, it is like seeing the sun by day. How would you say, Master, it is for you to perceive nature? The Master said: "Yellow..."
“The Yellow River has nine bends. Its waters originate from Kunlun. It is said: ‘Directly pointing to the human mind, seeing one’s nature and attaining Buddhahood.
Is this actually so, or not? The Master said, “Ask the Great Master Bodhidharma. The monk hesitated. The Master said, “A hawk flies over Silla.”
Question: "What will it be like when Bodhidharma has not yet arrived? The Master said, "The eyes are above the nose. Question: "What will it be like after he has arrived?
The Master said, "The feet are below the belly. Question: "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "The soles of the feet are as large as the palms of the hands.
Question: "What is the matter of a patch-robed monk’s traveling on foot? The Master said, "Tie your straw sandals tight. Question: "If..."
"What is 'first illumination, then function'? The Master said, "Holding up the unperforated flute of Shaolin, I casually blow forth the joy of ten thousand years.
"What is 'first function, then illumination'? The Master said, "The carved bow has already hung; the smoke of war has ceased.
Ten thousand miles away, songs of praise celebrate Great Peace. "What is 'illumination and function simultaneous'? The Master said, "Where the clay ox bellows..."
The celestial pivot turns; when the wooden horse neighs, the terrestrial axis shakes. [A monk] asked, "What is meant by 'illumination and function do not occur at the same time'?
The Master said, "It is like grasping a golden whip and asking a traveler returning home: 'In the deep of night, who walks with you along the Imperial Street? He ascended the hall and said:

"At the beginning of the month of the winter solstice, sell the quilt and buy an ox. At the end of the month of the winter solstice, sell the ox and buy a quilt. There are thirty-six hundred days in a year."
There are six days [in the year]. By means of the intercalary month, the four seasons are fixed and the year is completed; it must not be shifted by so much as a single hair's breadth.
If you buy at the eastern end at a high price and sell at the western end at a low price, after thirty years, where will you have your worn-out straw sandals to put on? [Thus he] ascended the hall.
It was the third month; the season had reached Qingming. It was neither cold nor warm, half-shaded and half-sunny. Fallen blossoms and crying birds—one note after another.
Suddenly, he took up his staff and said: "I have pierced through the nostrils of those who understand emptiness and blinded the eyes of Bodhidharma."

Treading through worn-out straw sandals, walking barefoot; the fine mountain still stands at its highest peak. On the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, he ascended the hall and raised the following case:
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan said, "The ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou said:
“Must one still rely on purposeful movement? Nanquan said, “To intend to move is already to deviate. Baizhang said, “If one does not intend, how can one know this is the Way?
Nanquan said, “The Way belongs neither to knowing nor to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded perception; not-knowing is indeterminate ignorance.
If you truly penetrate the Way that is free from doubt, it is as vast and open as great emptiness—how could one forcibly impose right and wrong? Baizhang said, “Wanglaoshi! (Master Wang!)

Your transgressions fill the heavens. You have casually and utterly shattered the Unsurpassed Great Way attained by Śākyamuni Buddha through six years of myriad hardships and bitter toil in the Snowy Mountains; you deserve twenty blows of the staff.
Setting aside for a moment the fact that Zhaozhou’s eye-sight at that time pierced through the four worlds, is there anyone among the assembly today who can [save you]?
The World-Honored One has already pulled up the root of *timira*. If there were none, then the profound teachings would not have been for the sake of others to prolong ignorance.
Being an unworthy descendant of these bequeathed teachings, I cannot help but extend a hand. [He] took up his staff, descended from the seat, and struck everyone present at once to disperse them.

Entering the hall, he held up the staff and said: "It startles the minds of those on the Ten Stages; the followers of the Two Vehicles cannot fathom it. He struck the ground once with the staff and said:
The son inherits his father’s trade; how many people has he deceived? Relying on his staff, he descends from the seat and ascends the hall.
Zhaozhou said, “Go wash your bowl,” and that monk suddenly realized his home. Niaoke blew up some cloth hair, and the attendant immediately grasped the meaning.
A-he-he! La-la-li! Old barbarian Bodhidharma knocked out my front teeth. Up!
The Hall. The World-Honored One’s samādhi was not known by Kāśyapa; Kāśyapa’s samādhi was not known by Ānanda; Ānanda’s samādhi was not known by Śāṇakavāsin;
the Universal Compassion Samādhi was not known by the others; and the various people’s samādhis were each unknown to one another. Thus it is said:
"It is like the waters in a river, rushing and flowing together in competition; each does not know the other."
"Know this. All dharmas are likewise. He let out a shout and said, "I thought there would be some talk like this!
He ascended the hall and raised the following case: Xuefeng asked Deshan, "How do the sages of the past instruct people?
Deshan replied, "In my school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to anyone. From this, Xuefeng attained realization. Later, a monk asked Xuefeng...
Feng said, "When the Master saw Deshan, what did he obtain that he then retired?
Feng said, "At that time, I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed. Dongshan Yan said, "Today Baiyun speaks for those who have not yet penetrated it:
there were two people coming from Dongjing. When asked where they came from, they said they came from Suzhou. When asked about them—"
"How are things in Suzhou? He replied, "Everything is as usual. Although this is so, he could not deceive Baiyun. Why?
It was simply because their dialects were different. After all, what is it? "The water chestnuts of Suzhou and the white lotus roots of Shaoyang. The Master said: [This is the answer].

Old Dongshan may indeed be said to excel at using metaphors; his words are not pressing or urgent. Nevertheless, even so, he speaks only of matters on the periphery of the shadows of Deshan and Xuefeng.
As for those who share the same brow and tread the same path, who drive side by side and race neck and neck—[he has not yet reached them].

I did not dare grant him permission. Why? Because the customs of Min and Shu are the same; there is a worm within his belly. When the Buddha was about to enter *nirvāṇa*, he ascended the hall and said:
"The lake’s light glistens; it is even better in fine weather. The mountain colors are hazy; they are also marvelous in the rain. The body of the pure *dharmadhātu* neither appears nor disappears.
There is no need for sorrow or resentment toward this fragrant season. He then ascended the hall and, citing Dongshan Liangjie, addressed the assembly, saying: "The Patriarch..."

It is said that there is no attachment; the Buddhas look upon it and see nothing. This is the compassionate heart of an old woman from all sides, providing for you a single thread of passage. The Master said:
"If one were to cause tears to fall frequently, even the vast ocean would surely dry up. He ascended the hall and said: "Today is once again the first day of the eighth month."
Ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags stand solemn in autumn colors; an ox, trailing dark crows, passes through a distant village. Where shall Sudhana seek Maitreya?
A certain person, falsely accusing the Master of a crime, went to the provincial commissioner. Dissatisfied with the facts, the official fabricated a charge against him.

The Master ultimately did not dispute the matter and showed no sign of resentment whatsoever. After more than a year, the provincial administration and the censorate vindicated the Master’s innocence and issued a formal decree requesting his reinstatement.

Residing at Mount Jing, he took up the ceremonial document upon entering the monastery and said: "The life-force of the Buddhas of the past and the administrative regulations of the Buddhas of the future are all contained herein.
It is as solemn as driving six horses with a frayed rope; it is as precarious as drawing a heavy hook with a single strand of hair.
Had it not been for the Great Chancellor who personally took hold of it and bore the full burden upon his shoulders, where else would there be this day? Do you people still..."
Do you understand thoroughly? A cart is not pushed sideways; there is no principle for a crooked judgment. The Imperial Preceptor was granted the title "Chan Master Mingbian Zhengzong Guanghui.
In the Gui-chou year of the Hongwu era, ten śramaṇas of great virtue were summoned by imperial decree to assemble at the Great Tianjie Monastery; the Master was at their head.
Due to illness, he did not attend the imperial audience, and was granted leave to return to Qionglung. In the ninth month of the Wu-wu year, he took up his brush and wrote this verse:
He passed away. At his cremation, the flames were of five colors and a fragrant aroma pervaded the air. His teeth, jawbone, and prayer beads remained unharmed;

his remaining bones were a deep azure, like blue lapis lazuli, with *śarīra* relics interspersed throughout. He was interred in a stupa to the west of his residence, and his fingernails and hair were further distributed.
He returned to Mount Gui and was buried to the right of the Wudengcai Pagoda. His age at death was sixty-eight; his years since ordination were fifty-one.
Chan Master Zhiren of the Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou Prefecture styled himself the "Dweller in Serenity" (Danjuzi) and also the "Elder of Joyful Tranquility" (Xiyisou).
He was the son of the Wu family of Poyang; his father, Zhonghua, served as a Professor of Literature (Guangwen) at Jiangzhou. When the Master was five years old, he was sent to follow...
In the province, Master Jinmok Chunsu received his training at Bogeunsa Temple. He received the full precepts at the age of seven; his insight and discernment were exceptionally brilliant.
At that time, Jikong of Xizhou was summoned by Emperor Yingzong and stayed at Bogeunsa. Upon seeing the Master, Jikong marveled at him and instructed him in the Vinaya.

He then directed him to visit Yuansou. When Yuansou looked at the Master, he laughed heartily. The Master was at a loss for what to do and consequently failed to perform the ritual prostrations on the *niśīdana* (seating mat). Yuansou—
He scolded him, saying, "Go to the hall for practice. The next day, the old man asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Poyang.
The old man said, "How deep is Poyang Lake? How wide is it? The Master spread his hands and made a gesture of measuring.

The old man said, "No, no. The Master said, "Shut that stinking mouth! Thereupon, he was appointed to serve as the Head of the Secretariat. The old man once said to others, "The Secretary Ren is a tiger."
He was a successor to the lineage of the Later Qishui Zhide and Chongbao of Yuezhou Yunzheng.
He once resided at Wanshou on Mount Huqiu in Wu. While in his room, he took up a wooden pillow and asked a monk, "What is this?
The monk replied, "I know that the Master’s compassionate heart is most earnest. The Master threw the pillow to the ground; as the monk hesitated, the Master shouted and sent him out.
Addressing the assembly: This illusory body is approaching its end; I shall follow my heart’s desire. I will practice walking meditation beneath the pines and sleep upon the rocks.

Take care, you dragon-elephant assembly of Beishan! When will the discourse from the Putong era ever reach its conclusion? Ascending the hall: Layer upon layer, the distant mountains are green; far and wide, the river waters are verdant.
All day long at Xiaowu Pavilion, leaning against the railing, I can never look enough. Suddenly, he called to his attendant: "Put this away."
[He brandishes] the whisk and then descends from his seat. Entering the hall, he says: "The nature of Chan is birthless; it is free from the conceptualization of Chan as birth.
The nature of Chan is non-abiding; it is free from the stillness of Chan as abiding. On the Five Terrace Mountain, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a 'dog-urine sky.
At the top of the flagpole, *zhuanzi* seeds are being fried; three monkeys toss coins at night. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, the Emperor [regarding] ghosts and spirits...
He consulted his master regarding these matters. The master composed a letter in accordance with the Buddha’s intent and sent it in reply. The Emperor was greatly pleased.

On the day of Gui-chou, Wei Guan of Puzi became the Magistrate of Suzhou and sent three successive letters inviting the Master to restore the Wanshou Monastery. After the messenger returned three times, the Master finally accepted.
In his later years, he spent his leisure in a hermitage among the pine forests. On the full moon of the third month in the *Renxu* year of the Hongwu era, he manifested illness.
On the nineteenth day, his fellow practitioner Ruyu went to inquire after him, saying, "Master, you are departing. Your disciples are gathered here; why not grant us a final word?"
"Is this your final instruction? The Master replied, "The Buddhas of the ten directions all enter the single path to Nirvana.
[The disciple] said, "I have been in close fellowship with you for fifty years; after this parting, I shall go directly to the Pure Land to meet you.

The Master raised his voice and said, "The entire great trichiliocosm is this very Pure Land; where would we not meet? After a long silence, he asked for a brush and wrote a verse, then passed away peacefully.
He passed away. His secular age was seventy-four; his years of monastic seniority (*saṃgharātra*) were sixty-seven.
*Xùdēng zhèngtǒng*, Scroll Thirteen;
*Xùdēng zhèngtǒng*, Scroll Fourteen.
Compiled by the Chan monk Xingtong of Western Sichuan, a successor to the Patriarchs at Potalaka in the South Sea,
of the Linji school under the twenty-first generation of Dajian.
Chan Master Fuyuan Fobao of Mount Jing in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Zhongfeng Mendi. He was the son of Fang of Ninghai in Taizhou; his mother’s surname was Zhang.

He left the household life at Hangzhou’s Liangzhu Temple to seek merit and blessings. At that time, Shi Hu Mei was the abbot of Jingci Temple; the Master followed him there to have his head shaved and received full ordination.
He then went to visit Yuansou of Mount Jing. Yuansou asked, “Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, “Jingci. Yuansou asked, “What brings you here?
The Master said, “I have long admired your reputation for the Way, so I have come specifically to pay my respects. Yuansou said, “When Zhaozhou met Nanquan, he acted as follows…”
"How is it? the Master said, "My head touches the heavens and my feet tread upon the earth. The old man asked, "What is it like after seeing [this]?
The Master said, "When hungry, I eat; when weary, I sleep. The old man said, "Where did you learn such empty talk?
The Master said, "Today I have personally seen the Master. The old man nodded in approval. He entered the world at Lushan in Cixi, and subsequently moved to Dongshan in Yuezhou. (4)
Regarding Zhimen: At the beginning of the Hongwu era, a śramaṇa of eminent conduct was summoned by imperial decree. The Master traveled to the capital and was lodged at Tianjie Monastery.

He entered the inner court several times, and his responses were to the Emperor's satisfaction. After remaining there for three years, he was granted a return to Zhimen. Later, he presided over Mount Jing twice.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To raise one, you must not raise two. To let one pass is to fall into the second.
When the ancients spoke thus, they were truly like those who embrace their own plunder while crying out for injustice. Dongshan, however, was not so: "To raise one, you must not raise two.
To let one pass is to fall into the seventh. At this point, you must further realize that there is a path leading upward; only then will it suffice.
"What is the path that leads upward? After a long silence, he said: "Do not linger over the green grass on the cold cliffs; sitting amidst the white clouds, the essence of the school is not subtle.
He ascended the hall and said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven; when a single speck of dust rises, the great earth is gathered up.
Who says that Northern Uttarakuru is not Southern Jambudvīpa? One needlessly rides the ox while still searching for the ox. Up.

"Speech is slander; silence is deception. Is there anyone who does not involve themselves in either? He struck the meditation seat and said, "It would have been better to let the prisoner go, lest it foster further intellectualizing.
He ascended the hall and said: "All day long I wear clothes, yet never a single thread has ever caught upon me.
All day long I eat rice, yet never a single grain has ever bitten my tongue. It is like the earth supporting a mountain, unaware of the mountain’s towering height."
It is like a stone containing jade; one does not know the jade to be flawless. Do not seek the Buddha, do not seek the Dharma, and do not seek the Sangha. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Sometimes riding upon the bright moon, I pass through the vast ocean by chance. One day, as his illness became critical, an attendant requested a verse.
The Master rebuked him, saying: "My worldly lifespan still has three years remaining. Subsequently, this proved to be exactly so. When [the time came], and...
On the day of his passing, he suddenly clapped his hands and said, "A-he-he! O great assembly, look at this! Then he became silent.
His secular age was eighty-four, and his years as a monk were sixty-four. His entire body was interred on the right ridge of Jizhao (Silent Illumination).
Chan Master Xingyuan Huirang of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was styled Huanyin. He was the son of the Xiang family of Huangyan, Taizhou.
He left home to become a monk under Lushan at Baoguan Temple in Leqing. He first studied under Zhuyuan Dao at Zhituo Mountain and subsequently traveled to Mount Jing, where he visited Yuansou.
Yuansou asked, "Do you come from the eastern ridge? Do you come from the western ridge? The Master pointed to the ground beneath his feet.
Caoshuai said, "This was bought for three copper coins. The old man said, "That is not it; speak further.
The Master said, "I am just like this; I do not know what you, the Master, would say. The old man said, "Since you have come from afar, I shall let you off with thirty blows.

At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He went forth into the world at Wufeng in Yingzhou, later moving to Jinge. In the *Renzi* year of the Hongwu era, he was summoned to the imperial court.
The following is a brief account of the eminent monk [Zhaojue]. He established a dharma assembly on Mount Zhongshan, and both Jitan Le and our Master participated in it.

Jitan was granted an imperial decree to reside at Tianjie Monastery, while the Master served as the First Seat (Diyizuo), where he upheld the essential principles and maintained the standard for leading the monastic community. The following year, the Master was appointed to lead Jinshan.

In the year Wu-wu, he ascended to Lingyin Monastery. On the day of the Buddha’s Bathing Festival, he ascended the hall and, citing the story of Yaoshan, spoke of how he had followed Nun Zun during the Buddha-bathing ceremony.
The Buddha’s Successor (Yaoshan) asked, "You have only been able to bathe this one; can you also bathe that one? Xuanzhu said, "Bring that one here.
Yaoshan then desisted. The Master said: "This one and that one—each and every one has been bathed from the very beginning.
Yaoshan’s coarse cotton robe is in vain for deliberation; look closely and it becomes a mere fallacy. It becomes a fallacy, turning [into delusion]."

[He] spoke erroneously. Striking the meditation seat, he said: "The spring in Wulin has already faded; the terraces and pavilions are now filled with lush green shade. On the occasion of the Buddha’s birthday, he ascended the hall and said:
"As soon as the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, took seven steps, and looked around in the four directions, saying:
'In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. This truly constitutes the marks of a Great Man; it is not the behavior of a mere infant."
Xihu laughed. Yunmen said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him once with my staff and fed him to a dog, so as to bring peace to the world.
If you wish to be of the lineage of the Old Barbarian [the Buddha], you must act exactly like this.
Fachang said, "A fine staff! But it was far too late. Before he had even left Tuṣita Heaven, one ought to have given him a blow upon the heels; how could he have reached this day? Although...
"Yet it is so. It is much like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled. One thinks, 'The beard is red,' only to find there is another with a red beard.
This old fellow with the yellow face puts on a clever show at the very end; he truly acts as if no one else exists.

Although Yunmen and Fachang acted with courage when they saw what was right, alas, it is like marking the boat after the sword has gone. [Yunmen] drew a line with his staff and said: 'Do you understand?'"
A handful of willow threads cannot be gathered; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade. Entering the hall: Today is the first day of the intercalary fifth month;
as before, the sun rises from the eastern side. Every patch-robed monk understands the secret melody; whether chanting short or long, all remains in harmony with the rhythm.
The plum rains have cleared and the tree shadows grow dense; wandering leisurely beneath the forest, what is there to gain or lose? The Unpositioned One.
The Real Man, this bare lump of flesh, casually topples over Vimalakīrti. On the day of the Buddha’s Nirvāṇa, he ascended the hall and said:
"Nirvāṇa and birth-and-death are equally like flowers in the sky; 'Buddha' and 'sentient beings' are both superfluous words. When you people arrive here, what do you do?
After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and said: "One merely sees falling petals carried away by the water, unaware of where they flow out."
Spring within the Cave. The Buddha’s Birthday: Ascending the Hall. Xiangyan said: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is truly poverty.
Last year’s poverty still allowed for a place to set one’s staff; this year’s poverty, there is not even a staff.

If someone among the assembly were to come forward and say, "Venerable Sir, you have made a mistake," [Xiangyan would reply]: "Today is the eighth day of the fourth month; it is the Buddha’s birthday."
One day, [a monk] asked, "How do you handle this public case? The mountain monk simply replied to him, "The duties of the abbot are many," and then descended from his seat.
He then performed the tea offering for the cremation of Master Bifeng. Picked up from Mount Wutai, he was truly no ordinary seed.
The people of Kansai have no brains, yet they possess a spiritual root. Only this single cup of clear tea can wash away the feverish afflictions of sentient beings.
It is just like Zequan throwing down his tea basket and Yangshan shaking the tea tree—what exactly do they clarify?
Then, extending the cup, he said: "Tread over the sea of birth and death; topple the city of nirvana. [In] the room.

None among the assembly could reach a realization. Before long, the Master fell victim to slander and was arrested. Some urged him to leave early.

He made his own arrangements; the Master paid him no heed. With a serene countenance, he went to the authorities. Before the interrogation had even begun, he recited a verse beneath the corridor and passed away while sitting upright.
This was the twenty-third day of the sixth month in the Bingyin year of the Hongwu era. He was sixty-nine years old and had spent fifty-eight summer retreats.

Chan Master Wuan Benwu of Shangzhu Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was a native of Huangyan. He received the tonsure at Fushan of Jingci Monastery and served as a *gangwei* (administrative official) under Jizhao at Zhongzhu Monastery.
He had a maternal uncle who was a venerable elder of the Confucian academies (*jiaoxiang*), who urged him to change his religious affiliation.
Consequently, he went to see Zantang Cheng at Yanfu Monastery, where he studied the scriptural divisions with great diligence. Jizhao regretted his departure and composed [a verse for him].
He sent him a verse, saying: "Entering Chan from the Teachings has occurred in both ancient and modern times; Entering the Teachings from Chan has never existed in either ancient or modern times.
Though the gates of the one mind and three contemplations differ, The moon remains solitary as it fills the thousand rivers.

Later, when he appeared in the world to propagate the teachings, having already become the successor of Zhan Tang, he nevertheless burned a single incense offering to Jizhao, not allowing their difference in outward station to create a duality in his heart. —Jizhao.

At the time of his passing into *nirvāṇa*, the Master was residing at Yanqing in Siming. Zhaoguang specially left him a letter, entrusting him with the diligent propagation of the essential teachings of the two houses of Dajian Huineng (Dasu) and Shaolin.

Suddenly, the spring warmth returns. I think back to the day my nostrils were lost; what trace of that breath remains even now?
A celestial wind blows from the north as the year draws to a close; like a flash of lightning, one seeks its mark in the void. Later, at the time of his passing, he was free of ailment;
sitting upright, he shed his mortal coil atop Baiyun Terrace.
Chan Master Kaigen Yuzhong Shanru of Suzhou Prefecture was a native of Wujiang. He ascended the hall and said:

He requested them, and the numinous images rose majestically, floating side by side; as he attempted to lift and carry them, they suddenly boarded the boat.

In a world of peace and clarity, there is no need for deceptive words. He showed a verse to a monk from the Grass Hut: The Nation...

He once resided at Zhízhǐ Ān in Fēngmén, and people therefore called him "Master Zhízhǐ. As he approached the end of his life, he summoned his sons to bid them farewell; he remained serene and composed.

Chan Master Tianjing Yuanjing of Lingyin Puyin, Hangzhou Prefecture, was the son of the Ni family of Kuaiji.
His physical appearance was imposing and grand, and his temperament was broad and serene. He did not recognize worldly traps and snares as being anything at all. Initially, he followed Xueting Li.
He shaved his head and received full ordination from Zhaokong Ru. He further studied the *zhiguan* (cessation and contemplation) of the Tiantai and Huayan traditions under Tian'an Ji.
Possessing far-reaching aspirations, he visited Wujian at Mount Huading and subsequently traveled to Mount Yujing, where he called upon Shishi.

Shishi directed him to investigate with Yuansou in the Budong Xuan (Immovable Studio). Upon entering the door, Yuansou let out a thunderous shout; the Master was so startled that he broke into a profuse sweat.

When his bonds were exhausted and he was liberated, he immediately prostrated himself three times and withdrew. The Elder appointed him to the office of attendant; shortly thereafter, he took charge of the secretariat.

In the *bingshen* year of the Zhizheng era, he emerged from seclusion at Changqing in his native village and subsequently ascended to Tianyi. In the *renzi* year of the Hongwu era, an imperial decree summoned renowned monastics throughout the realm to assemble at Mount Zhongfu (Zhongshan).
The Master responded to the summons and entered the inner palace; there he conversed with ease on the Way, after which he was granted a meal and retired. *Bing...*
Chen succeeded him on the seat at Lingyin. He ascended the hall and said: "Sound is not sound; this is the samādhi of Avalokiteśvara.
Form is not form; this is the Dharma-gate of Mañjuśrī. Where sound and form are unimpeded, this is the realm of Samantabhadra. Holding up his staff and drawing a line with it, he said:
"The Great Peng bird spreads its wings over the Ten Islands; by the basket, the swallows and sparrows chirp in vain. He then ascended the hall and said: "This very mind is Buddha."
In Jia Prefecture, an ox eats grain; it is neither mind nor Buddha. In Yi Prefecture, a horse’s belly swells; it is not mind and not Buddha.
One searches the world for a physician to apply moxibustion upon the left shoulder of a pig. After a long while, he says: "To cry until the blood flows is of no avail."
"It would be better to keep my mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. Before ten days had passed, he was beset by false accusations and demoted to Shaanxi.
Upon arriving at Baoying, he said to his attendants, "My retribution-body is quite different from usual; it seems my end is near. That night, he stayed at Ningguo Temple.
As for the abbot, who had been vacant for some time, he was an old acquaintance of the Master and they greeted each other with great joy.

The Master said, "I have found a place for my remains to be entrusted. That night, they conversed and partook of food and drink as usual. At dawn the following day, he suddenly joined his palms, sat upright, and passed away peacefully.
This was the nineteenth day of the first month in the fifth year of the Hongwu era (1378). His Dharma-grandson, Fanyi, took the remains with him...

Upon returning, he found the śarīra relics nestled within his bones like a cluster of pearls. On the day of the Buddha’s bathing ceremony, a pit was dug beside the ancestral mound, and they were interred there.
He was sixty-seven years of age and fifty-five years of *dharma-luò* (seniority).

Chan Master Husheng Diyuanqi of Taizhou Prefecture was a native of Linhai. While he was still a lay scholar, he paid his respects to his paternal uncle, the Venerable Jian, at Baozang Temple in his hometown.

He happened to read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, and upon reaching the passage that states, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all objects manifested within the wondrously luminous mind," he set down the scroll and reflected deeply for a long time. Suddenly, he attained a clear realization.
He petitioned his parents for permission to leave the household life and took Jizhao as his teacher.
He donned the robes of a dhūta practitioner and became increasingly diligent over time. Later, he withdrew from public life to reside in the Eastern Hall for seven years.
He authored several works, including the *Dapuhuanhai*, the *Fayuntonglue*, the *Zuitan*, the *Woushuo*, and the *Rushishenghua*, totaling several volumes. Furthermore, he composed...
*Fu-zu-da-tong-fu* (The Great Synthesis of Buddhas and Patriarchs). At the end of his life, he was forty-three years old.
Chan Master Chuzhun of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou sent this verse for Attendant Zhong:
"When Niaoke blew up the cloth-hair, The attendant attained enlightenment on the spot. A pair of unperforated iron hammers— He flaunts the arts of the ghost family."

Consider this: if one is a truly sharp and gifted master, possessing a natural and innate bearing that expands the local scenery of the original ground and reveals the core essence of the patch-robed monk—then they can encompass the great thousandfold world within the tip of a hair and contain Mount Sumeru inside a mustard seed.
They walk directly upon the crown of Vairocana’s head; even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot block their path.
Chan Master Zhongyou Zuanchan of Tianning Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture was a native of the Chen family of Yinqian County.

He received the tonsure and precepts under Fozhi Kuang and attained the essential meaning of the Dharma while studying with Jizhao at Mount Jing. He emerged from seclusion at Lushan, subsequently moved to Xiangshan, and was later promoted to the Tianning Monastery of the prefecture.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha. It is not the mind; it is not the Buddha."
On the Five Terraces Mountain, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a dog-urine sky. At the tip of the flagpole, *zhuanzi* seeds are being fried;
three monkeys toss coins at night. Entering the hall: If we discuss the First Phrase, the Buddhas of the three periods cannot speak it;
the Six Patriarchs cannot speak it; the old monks of the world cannot speak it. I, this mountain monk—
"One cannot speak it. The great assembly cannot speak it. [The Master] picked up his staff and said, "Can this staff speak?
Even if it could speak, that would still be the second phrase. On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, head and tail are golden lotuses.
After the fifteenth day, white oxen and tabby cats run about in packs. On the very fifteenth day itself—" [He paused. "Lóu! (a shout).
The fire on the upper terrace illuminates the fire below; carriages and horses pass back and forth as people look at people. Good. But tell me, assembly, in what way is it good?
It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude. [He then descended from his seat.]

Chan Master Wuan of Jiangxin was the dharma heir of [blank] Chan Master Zhipu of Ba'en in □□ Prefecture. He was the son of the Long family of Guiyang. After taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said:
"In the sixth month, the traveler’s mouth spews smoke; all this toil is but for the sake of profit and fame. How can it compare to being without intention beneath the forest trees?"
Guest: One night, having awakened while still wearing my robes, I slept until dawn. Striking the meditation seat, he said: "Ganming does not begrudge his verbal karma; I shall explain it for you.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month, Old Man Yanma will demand from you the payment for your meals. He then ascended the hall to teach.

The spring colors are deep, the spring days are bright and warm. In the gardens and groves, the wild flowers are red. In the past, when Lingyun saw them once, he broke through both form and emptiness.
Now all of you see them as well; why do you not awaken? If you do not awaken, your eyes will be ensnared by forms.
Jigfuzi said: "To teach people wrongly is to resent the wind at the fifth watch.
Master Da Chan of Yunju Xiaoyin in Nankang Prefecture sat upright in his quarters all day long, appearing as serene and detached as ever.
When the remaining hair and beard were shaved off, the attendant plucked out the roots as they grew; everyone scrambled to preserve them. As soon as they grew back, śarīra relics were produced.

He once showed a verse to the Zen practitioner Xin, which said: "Faith is the source of the Way and the mother of merit; like a medicine that has proven effective, it need not be taken in great quantity."
If there is someone who can directly accept and uphold [this truth], what can even the Buddhas and Patriarchs do to them?

This is from the lineage of Chan Master Xī of Jìngshān, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Xiàoyǐn Dàyǐn of Dàlóngxiáng Jíqìng Temple in Jiāngníng Prefecture; he was of the Chén clan of Yìmén in Jiǔjiāng.
He was the son of [the clan name] family. He received the tonsure at Suilü Monastery in the prefecture. From his youth, he was exceptionally clear-headed and outstanding among his peers.

Initially, he visited Yishan Wan; subsequently, he was sent to Baizhang to attend Huiji. Upon first seeing him, Huiji held him in high esteem and appointed him as head of the secretariat (chamberlain). One day, he asked:
"When Huanglong had already attained the essential meaning from Letan, why did his spirit wither and his sweat fall when he saw Ciming? Where did his fault lie?"
"Where is it? the Master replied in a defiant tone: "In a peach pit a thousand years old—what 'kernel' from the past do you seek?

Later, while standing in attendance in the meditation hall, Xuedou Jue raised the story of the wild fox and questioned him: "If one does not fall into cause and effect, one falls into the body of a wild fox;
if one does not obscure cause and effect, one sheds the body of a wild fox. Tell me, where does the point of benefit or harm lie? As Xuedou was about to answer, Jue struck him.

Suddenly, he let out a thunderous shout, and the Master’s doubts were instantly dissolved like ice melting away. Because his fellow practitioners pressed him with difficult questions, the Master replied with a verse:
"Baizhang’s wild fox; the wild fox, Baizhang. Buried in a single pit—humbly praying you will partake.

Later, he appeared in the world at Wuhui on Lake Dongting, and subsequently moved to Baoquang Zhongzhu in Hangzhou. In the gengwu year of the Zhishun era, the Emperor Wen, while still residing in his former palace...
For the purpose of establishing Dàlóng Xiángjíqìng Temple, he selected a man of eminent virtue to serve as its founding patriarch (*kāishān*). The Master was the first to be chosen for this role.

He was granted the title "Great Chan Master Guǎngzhì Quánwù" (Extensive Wisdom and Complete Enlightenment). Furthermore, he was summoned by imperial decree to the capital and received an audience at the Kuízhāng Pavilion, where he was granted a seat and questioned regarding the essentials of the Dharma.
When Emperor Shùn ascended the throne, the Master’s treatment became even more honored. Later, seeking retirement due to old age and illness, he was granted a gracious imperial edict.
"Not permitted," [the Emperor] decreed, "entrust him to the Outer Office for protection and veneration, so that he may dwell in peace until the end of his days. Ascending the hall, the Master said:
"In the Land of Ultimate Bliss, the waterbirds and forest trees all recite the Buddha’s name. In the Heaven of Satisfaction, the trees touch one another, expounding upon suffering and emptiness.
Holding up his whisk, he said: 'This mountain monk’s whisk has pierced through the nostrils of you all. Where, then, will you breathe out your breath? "
Heh! Entering the new temple for the ascending of the hall: The primary truth (paramārtha-satya) is as bright as the radiant sun and as vast as the great void.

The myriad phenomena are dense and manifold, yet not a single speck of dust can be established. If one were to explain the present by citing the past, it would be nothing more than generating branches outside the joints;

"Resting thus, is there anyone who can stir up the mutual resonance [of the Dharma]? (The questions and answers are not recorded. Thereupon he said:
'Śākyamuni Buddha relinquished the Golden Wheel to ascend the rank of Buddhahood; the present Emperor, from the rank of Buddhahood, governs the Golden Wheel.'"
They gather the ocean of three thousand worlds within a single seal and fully embody eighty thousand dharma-gates upon a single hair-tip,
like the Bodhisattvas in the assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra who have attained the liberation door of the inexhaustible treasury of merit within a single vessel.

Various delicious foods and drinks were produced. Furthermore, while in the midst of the assembly, they looked up into the sky and rained down various precious jewels, satisfying all according to the inclinations of sentient beings.
Thereafter, those who obtained these jewels all realized the Dharma-gates.

Those who partake of its flavor shall all realize the wondrous Way; there is not a single speck of dust that does not fully embody the Buddha-work, and not a single dharma that does not perfectly fulfill the True Teaching.
Thus, as we now construct this jeweled monastery and propagate the gift of Dharma, the music of the devas resounds.
Without being struck, the drums resound of themselves; the *brahma* chants and hymns are spontaneously performed.

Bodhisattvas from the ten directions all assemble at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), and the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, join together in celebration and praise. Is there anyone who, without passing through the illusory city, ascends directly to the precious destination?

He then struck his whisk and said: "The four seas have already returned to the imperial transformation; the times are clear, so let us cease singing the Song of Great Peace. He ascended the hall and said:
"To gaze at the clouds from the summit of a solitary peak is to bury one's own spiritual brilliance.
To mix mud and water at the crossroads of the street is, for now, to value the circulation of the True Eye. Holding up his staff, he said: "Śākyamuni has already passed away; Maitreya..."

When he picks them up, they are pierced through in every direction; at every turn, the boundless wondrous body manifests. When he lets them go, they mirror the earth and illuminate the heavens;
everywhere, the ocean of jewel-kings is revealed. What need is there to say that "streams and mountains differ, while clouds and moon are the same"?
The ultimate transformation is non-action; its merit is not presided over by a sovereign. It is a vast, singular realm of the ancient sovereign’s wind.
Again, Master Zhigong raised the matter, sending someone to deliver a message to Sida, saying: "Why do you not descend the mountain to transform sentient beings?

What is the point of looking only toward the clouds and the Milky Way? Sida replied: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp. Where else could there be [any more]?"
"Sentient beings can be saved. The Master said: "When Sita was pressed by Zhigong, he was driven straight back three thousand paces.

When ascending the hall for the two orders of monks, one attains the 'first place' of mind-emptiness. Why choose an official when one can choose a Buddha? To shoulder the responsibility of the monastic community."

To serve the multitude as if serving oneself; to repay the nation by selecting people for the sake of the Dharma. Appointing according to their capacities is like a musical performance of nine movements, where every advance and retreat of the musicians accords with the measure.
It is just like a single shout that distinguishes guest and host, where illumination and function operate simultaneously.
How do you all discern this? He lets out a shout and says: "The nine-tenthousand-li Peng bird has just spread its wings; the three..."
The thousand-year-old crane soars away. Entering the hall, he said: "Words are not sounds; forms are not objects. What is the reason for this attachment?
To sleep amidst sound and form, to sit and lie down amidst sound and form—this is already somewhat better.

Therefore it is said: 'This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; there are no further sounds or forms to present to you. If one understands within this, there is nothing at all; the essence..."
"What does it matter whether they are divided or not? He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "Where do the yellow leaves come from as the water flows?

An ox with crows perched upon it passes through a distant village. He struck the ground with his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall for discourse, he cited Huanglong Nan’s words from his inner chamber:
"How is my hand like a Buddha’s hand? How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? Every person has their own karmic affinity (*jātisambandha*)."
