At that moment, the sound of a wooden board was heard. The Master struck the desk and descended from his seat. He addressed the assembly: "The dragon listens with its horns;
the ant listens with its body; humans listen with their ears; the Great Being Samantabhadra listens with his mind. [He then] took up his staff.
Zhàng said, "Who permitted this? Last night a north wind arose, and from afar I heard the sound of it striking the window.
The Master had served Qīngzhōng at Wǔyún. One day, Zhōng entered the attendants' quarters and said, "Attendant Shàn, do not sit idly here."
The Master said, "How would I dare? Zhong said, "Are you not dozing off? The Master made a gesture of lying down.
Zhong struck him. The Master then shouted. Zhong said, "So there is someone here! The Master then bowed.

That evening, Zhong spoke to the Master again, saying, "The National Teacher called his attendant three times, and the attendant responded three times. Wherein did the attendant fail? The Master stepped forward.
[Zhao] said, "From beginning to end, you are a master. Zhong asked, "Is there anyone who can clear the injustice of the ancients?
The Master said, "There is. "Who is it that clears the injustice? The Master covered his ears and departed. He went to visit Master Poshan at Jincheng.
Shanhui asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master replied, "Gao Feng. Shanhui asked, "How has Gao Feng been lately? The Master lowered one foot.

Mount [Shishuang] said, "What about the Senior Monk? The Master said, "I do not know. Mount Shishuang dragged his staff back toward the abbot's quarters; the Master shook out his sleeves and departed.
A monk came from Mount Muzhou, and the Master asked, "How has it been at Mount Muzhou lately? The monk replied, "It has been quite formidable. The Master said, "..."
"Wherein lies the point of greater or lesser importance? [The monk] said, "It is simply because your compassionate heart is too earnest. The Master asked, "Do you know what is happening right here?
[The monk] said, "I beg the Master to grant me an instruction. The Master struck him and said, "It is even more important!
The Master continued, "If you understand it in this way, then even I am a blind man," and he struck him again. He then asked a monk, "Why did the Venerable Guishan [hold his nose]?"
[The monk’s nose] was missing half of it. The monk pointed to the Master’s nose and said, “It looks exactly like that.
The Master said, “If you call this thing ‘this,’ you will enter hell as fast as an arrow. The monk asked, “Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, “Dongting Lake has no lid.

Later, when the monk brought up the story of Linji’s two hall heads shouting at each other simultaneously, before the story was even finished, the Master let out a shout. The monk [responded with a shout].
As he was about to deliberate [on the matter], the Master picked up his staff, pushed him out, and let out a shout.
Chan Master Zhufeng Huanmin of Zhiping in Zhongzhou was the son of the Xu family of Fengling. From birth, he was outstanding;
his intelligence and wisdom surpassed those of others. At the age of ten, he shaved his head under the two masters Foxi and Yebun, and [studied] with Wanfeng Shan...

The Chan Master [Zhaozhou] and [Shangxian] were both śrāmaṇeras serving under Qingzhong. At that time, among Qingzhong’s assembly, the two śrāmaṇeras Shan and Min were renowned for their sharp wit and eloquence, their fame shaking the age.
Although the Master was young, he remained silent and spoke little; those who discerned him knew he would surely become a vessel of great capacity.
Previously, it had been rumored that Master Shan was skilled in composing gāthās. One day, as Qingzhong entered the hall, he encountered Shan gathered around a fire.
Next, he was instructed to compose a verse. [The Master] said: "Red light flashes and flickers; purple flames swirl and coil. It can melt snow, and it also makes the golden lotus shine.

Zhong struck him once with his palm and returned to the abbot’s quarters. He then pointed to the lamp and commanded the Master to compose another verse. The Master said: "The light is like a flash of lightning;
it penetrates the void. As for the lamp to come—whether it be copper or iron. At that time, the Venerable Sanmu saw this.
Zheng said, "Is it copper? Is it iron? The Master said, "Waves arise within the fire. Zhong was struck by this and asked, "What is your name?
The Master said, "Huanmin (Illusory Acuity). Zhong said, "Before 'illusory acuity'... The Master said, "The blue sky beyond the bottom of the sea. Zhong said, "..."
After Huanshun had spoken, the Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is eternally inexhaustible. Zhong asked, "Where is this seen? The Master said, "It is at Anqi beneath Lingfeng Mountain.
Muzhe asked, "What about after Anqi has understood? The Master said, "The void and the great earth.
Muzhe asked, "Where do they fall? The Master stamped his foot. Muzhe said, "If you have feet to stamp, what do you stamp with if you have no feet? The Master—
[Zhao] said, "Master, do not be so earnest. Yunzhong laughed heartily. Zhao again asked about Shanshan. Shanshan said, "Refining true gold within the fire.
Yunzhong said, "Why does the assembly not look at the dialogue between these two śrāmaṇeras? Later, while the Master was reading the scriptures, Yunzhong said:
"Is it that one constantly sees such sutras within the eye? Is this it, or is there something else? The Master said, "The Abbot must understand it exactly like this.
Zhong said, "Set aside the paper and ink and bring it forth. The Master said, "There is not even a little wind from the east. Zhong said, "This young novice.
After the Master returned from Wuyun, Zhong said, "I have heard that you are used to hitting people. The Master [remained silent].
[Zhaozhou] said, "Venerable Master, be careful. Yunmen Zhong said, "What are you wearing on your feet as you walk?
The Master said, "Sandals. Zhong said, "Has the fierce tooth yet grown? The Master lifted his foot. Zhong said, "Which one? The Master said, "Why do you ask such a question?
Zhong said, "San Kong said you should strike him; he intends to bring you here for punishment. The Master said, "I have already spoken with him."
[The Master] understood. Zhong asked, "How do you explain this? The Master said, "Steal one and lose nine. Zhong said, "I shall assist you; you have come from afar.
Shan said, "Tongzhen, you should act as a novice and serve Zhong. The Master served Zhong for twenty-one years.

When Zhong passed away, the assembly requested that Zhiping succeed him on the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "Since I entered this community, I have possessed nothing but the head of a furnace."
A single line of iron spine; a single unchanging mind. As for the Way of Chan and the Buddha-dharma, there is not the slightest thing lingering in his chest or filling his belly.
Today, because the elder monk has turned the helm, he has been brought before this assembly of gods and men without cause.
Those who look with open eyes and listen with attentive ears—what, after all, will he say?
"What is this? [The Master] said, intending to transmit the past and initiate the future. After a long silence, he said: "Willow branches reflect a thousand springs of lushness;

flowers drifting from the trees carry the fragrance of ten thousand ages. Upon entering the stupa and returning to the hall for the lecture, he said: "With each passing season, everything becomes ever new.
The plum blossoms open and the golden petals display their exquisite forms; yet these very elements encompass the four seasons entirely—neither changing nor shifting."
"What is this principle that is unchanging and immutable? Is it that the jeweled stupa is renewed yet remains fundamentally unmoving, such that you might call it 'unchanging and immutable'?
No, that is an error. Is it that the śarīra radiates its brilliance, such that the eyes perceive its blue and white?"
"Can it be called 'unchanging and unalterable'? "Wrong. "Are you not the Elder Xin? Shaking your lips and wagging your tongue, you are merely weaving a web of complications again.
The Dharma and friendship among the fourfold assembly remain as they were; the aspiration for the Way is ever-present. Can it be called 'unchanging and unalterable'? "Wrong.
If you can understand these three 'wrongs,' you will be worthy of repaying the profound kindness of this old man and may complete his legacy."

If you have not yet understood this matter—if it is still not so—you will once again bring disgrace upon the lineage. [The Master] suddenly raises his fist and says: "Four fours, three threes, seven eights, eight eights.

On the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, during the retreat for the recitation of the precepts, he ascended the hall and asked: "The sagely brilliance governs the realm, and all nations are at peace;
the Way unites sovereign and subject, and the rivers are clear while the seas are calm. At such a time as this, what would you do, O Monk?"
"How so? The Master said, "Habitually handling the spirit-snake, its power is majestic through ten thousand layers.

[The monk] asked, "As for the civil and military officials, scholars, and the fourfold assembly of this province who have invited the Master to open the field and select the Buddha—tell me, by what means do they benefit their practice of the *dānapāramitā* (giving)?
The Master said, "Vividly seizing the living horse, its majestic spirit soars a thousand miles. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then may [the Master's] life be as long as—"
The mountain’s blessings are like the sea; its lineage continues like the spreading vines of a gourd. As the assembly of court officials gathered in solemn splendor, they departed.

The Master said, "Profoundly correct! Even more profoundly correct! He was asked about the Heart-Seal of Juyun and the fundamental principles of Linji: "What is the first phrase of Linji? The Master replied:
"Three before, three after, three after. [The student asked: "What about the second phrase? The Master said: "Seven do not form, eight do not join.
[The student asked: "What about the third phrase? The Master said: "Pouring tea, three dates. [The student] said: "In this way, not only do all monks have cause for celebration;

the civil and military threads of governance are all graced with honor. The Master said: "Be glad that you have met great fortune through a small exit. [The student] asked: "The ultimate Way is truly..."

The Vehicle. Originally there are no words or explanations; yet, to respond to capacities and engage with beings, one must rely on vigorous exhortation. Setting aside the question of the True Vehicle of the Ultimate Way, how do you respond to capacities and engage with beings?
The Master said, "At Caoxi, the road exists and all people arrive. [The monk] said, "Right now, the cold plum blossoms by the ridge have newly put forth their beauty;
the auspicious snow upon the mountain peaks vies with them for their fragrance and loveliness. I wonder, is this the wondrous function of spiritual power?"
"It is naturally so. The Master said, "Whose faith is it that has come here specifically? [The monk] replied, "In this way, from now on, the Dharma will be propagated in peace;
the true wind shall be borne by a thousand states and ten thousand nations. The Master said, "Today I have met a fellow practitioner.
He then took up his staff, struck it once, and said, "Thus, thus! How many times have I gazed upon the riverbank? The yellow plum blossoms..."
It blooms amidst the falling snow. Not so, not so. The tender willows sway their golden threads;
one must simply respond to the season. Try looking at Old Śākyamuni: that single point of the morning star—how marvelous!

Throughout the three Han dynasties, whether through parables or metaphors, through teachings or doctrines, even down to taming lame donkeys and healing blind horses, it was nothing more than responding to the occasion. Now look further back through the successive generations.
The Master says: What is meant by being "solemn, ancient, meticulous, concise, clear, and intimate"?
To turn one's body into another species, to finally grasp the fly-whisk handle and speak empty words—this is nothing more than responding to the demands of the times.

As for the civil and military officials, scholars, and the fourfold assembly of Dharma protectors present here, who have requested that this mountain monk open the furnace to select the Buddha and establish one hundred and twenty periods of training, thereby causing others...
People mark out boundaries by drawing lines on the ground; they are further commanded to don the five-strip, seven-strip, and twenty-five-strip robes.
First refuge, second refuge, third refuge. The path leads from level ground through peril; the person moves busily within stillness. This Way accords with the proper season.
It was not the proper time. After a long silence, he again struck the ground with his staff and said: "Originally a guest upon the banks of the Xiao River, going west, east, south, and north.
He then cited the case where King Prasenajit asked the World-Honored One: "Within the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), is there still conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya)?
If one says there is, then wisdom should not be one; if one says there is not, then wisdom should not be two."
"As for the meaning of 'one' and 'two,' what is that meaning? The Buddha said, "Great King, in the past, during the time of Dragon Light Buddha (Nāgaprabhāsa), you once asked about this meaning.
Now I have nothing to say, and you have nothing to hear. This absence of saying and hearing is called the meaning of one and the meaning of two.
Observe how King Prasenajit intended to pass through the successive stages of examination; the World-Honored One immediately covered his name over.
The Golden Pitcher. If among this assembly today there were one to ask about the primary truth (*paramārtha-satya*), this mountain monk would simply clap his hands and laugh "he-he.
Why is that? Since the time he first performed the *santai* dance, every clap has been nothing but song.
Chan Master Domyeon Deunghyeon of Tongsan in Chungju was the son of the Xia family of Fuling. In his youth, he followed Master Yingyuan;
he first attended Wansong for many years. When Wansong passed away, Qingzhong Ying invited him to White Rock Temple, and the Master went there to pay his respects.
One day, while standing in attendance with the assembly, Qingzhong brought up the story of "remaining silent for a long time" to test the assembly. The Master said, "It is very much like a house..."
Inside the marketplace, [Zhaozhou] was selling Yangzhou [silk]. Yunmen said, "Do not say that there is nothing to it. Zhaozhou said, "The Master is also being groundless.
Yunmen struck him. Zhaozhou shouted. Zhaozhou said, "In the future, do not let the old monk down. Yunmen bowed and withdrew.

He again attended Qingzhong at Wuyun. One day, having recovered from an illness, he presented a verse, saying: "Changing heads and faces through many lifetimes, Today, for no reason, my eyes have opened wide.
Entrusted to this skin-bag before one’s very eyes— What harm is there in being born in the belly of a horse or the womb of a donkey?
Zhong asked, "Which eye is it that you have opened? The Master held up his fist. Zhong said, "Put it down."
[The Master] entered. As soon as the Master had set down [his staff], Zhong said, "Where is it now? The Master replied, "Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Jincheng Temple.
Zhong said, "I grant you thirty blows! The Master said, "Take care," and departed. Zhong was presiding over the seat at Nan Cheng and appointed the Master as the Chief Administrative Officer (Jansi).
One day, the Master entered the Abbot's quarters; Zhong held up his whisk, and the Master gave a shout. Zhong said, "Because..."
"Very well! he shouted. The Master said, "I have no choice; affairs at the monastery are very numerous. Zhong then gave his seal of approval and departed to reside at Tongshan.
He ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said: "The vast waves surge and billow; white crests of foam reach the heavens.

Amidst the coral groves, the golden-haired lion is ensnared; within the realm of no-outflow, the bright moon hangs suspended. If you can accept this face-to-face, you have already missed it. Do you know?"
"Mò! The new year’s calendar has already been issued; there is no need to sing the song of 'Great Peace' again. He struck his staff once and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Tianyuan Tiri Denghui of Kuizhou was the son of the Li family of the commandery. He studied under Qingzhong at Tai... [text fragment ends]
Píng was one day hearing Zhōng raise the koan of Xiangyan striking the bamboo. Upon these words, the Master attained realization.
He then let out a "cup" sound and said, "So it was all along; how many 'brainless' heroes there have been! Zhōng asked, "What are you saying?
The Master held up his fist. Zhōng said, "What is that? Before Zhōng’s very eyes, the Master struck the ground three times, shook his sleeves, and departed.
After emerging from his quarters, he ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is clearly manifest and fully present.
How could it depend on my ascending the hall to scatter sand and dust as a teaching? I only wish that you all would truly practice; then there will naturally come a time when you gain entry."
"Is there anyone present right now who truly practices? Come forth and meet with this mountain monk.
A monk asked, "The various masters each give different answers regarding the fundamental principle of Jibei; what do you say, Master? The Master said, "I am not playing that drum or flute.
The monk pressed, "Since you are a patriarchal master, why act like this? The Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the first..."
[The Master] said: "A single phrase. [The student] asked: "How is it when the eyebrows of empty space drag upon the ground? The Master said: "The horns at the bottom of the sea touch the heavens.
[The student] asked: "How is it the second phrase? The Master said: "Kunlun rides an elephant as he runs. [The student] asked:
"What is the Vajra King’s Precious Sword? The Master said: "Nata carries the scent of blood. [The student] asked: "What is the Lion Crouching on the Ground? The Master said: "A fox..."
"Traces are cut off and footprints vanish. What is the 'probing pole' and the 'shadow-grass'? The Master said, "Do not view them as two different things.
"What is 'one shout that does not function as one shout'? The Master said, "A diamond rubbing the back of a clay figure.
"What is the 'host within the guest'? The Master said, "A black chicken flying over a stone. "What is the 'guest within the host'? The Master said, "The wind blows through the pines."
Yunqing asked, "What is the Lord within the Lord? The Master said, "The stone in the empty valley nods its head.

Another monk asked, "Are Linji’s guest and host the same as or different from Dongshan’s fundamental principle? The Master said, "A troop of monkeys tossing coins at night. "What is 'the partial within the central'?
The Master said, "Green mountains lying amidst white clouds. "What is 'the central within the partial'? The Master said, "Snow."
The mountain tortoise runs away. What is "coming from the center"? The Master said: "The moon shifts across the bottom of the water.

What is "arriving at the convergence"? The Master said: "Cold plum blossoms bloom at night upon the *yuanyang* tree. What is "reaching the convergence"? The Master said: [The tortoise] has gone over the ridge.
"The hundred plants have already been sown; it is the spring of old. "What is the Sovereign? The Master said: "The Imperial Axis opens the celestial mandate. "What is the Minister? The Master said:

"Generals and Ministers value loyalty and integrity. "How is it that the Sovereign turns toward the Minister? The Master said: "One does not go out to welcome the Sovereign beyond the borders. "How is it that the Minister serves the Sovereign? The Master said:
"With a sincere heart, one serves only to repay the state. "What is the relationship between Sovereign and Minister? The Master said: [The text here is incomplete in the source.]
The Way was in harmony. The Master said, "The enlightened and the good rejoice in their opening; wind and clouds gather. He asked, "What is it like when the Prince is born?
The Master said, "The nine dragons have just spouted water; his nobility is natural. He asked, "What is it like when the Prince is born at court? The Master said:
Purple Palaces resounded with shouts of "Long Live the Emperor," as he stood upright and brought about Great Peace. "What is the 'Prince Born from the End'?
The Master said, "The noble lineage and the worthy talent are each different. "What is the 'Prince Born of Transformation'? The Master said, "If decayed grass had no mind."
"Where is the glow of the firefly? What is it to be a Prince Born Within? The Master said, "One does not see the strange plum in bloom;
yet one still suspects the fragrance of the Imperial Garden. The monk stepped forward again. The Master shouted, "You rice-bag!
You are like a water crow catching fish—swallowing it whole and spitting it out whole. When have you ever gained even a bit of utility from it? Now, the essential tenets of the Five Houses are not...

This is merely what people have recorded from instructional manuals; it is nothing more than the vain display of empty fame. You must know that these words and phrases are the excellent prescriptions for curing illness.

What is precious is personal realization and awakening. When a teacher provides an answer, they are administering medicine according to the specific ailment—what is called "the physician not clinging to a fixed formula, but applying it as appropriate.
How could this be a rigid, dead-set approach, like a snake's head, that causes people to fall into pits and ditches? To stand [in such a way]...

The staff-bearer said: "The three phrases and four shouts; guest and host, the partial and the correct; the five ranks of ruler and minister, and the five ranks of prince—all these are within this mountain monk’s reach.
Can you swallow them all down in a single gulp? A hound like Han Lu need not chase after clods of earth; a lion is accustomed to biting men.
He struck the ground once with his staff and descended from the seat.
Master Yuanchen Deng of Wuyang was a native of this very district. Once, while presiding over the assembly, he raised the following case:

A monk asked Nanyue, "When a mirror is used to cast an image, once the image has been formed, where does the light go? Nanyue replied, "Where was your physical appearance when you were a young boy, Venerable Sir?
The monk said, "But once the image is formed, why does it no longer reflect? Nanyue replied: [The text ends here.]
Although it does not reflect, one cannot deceive it in the slightest. The verse says: The new moon is like a hook, suspended on a single thread;
Where the white clouds are thin, the sky is revealed within. Looking at it, one might suspect its cold radiance is faint; Who knows that herein lies a perfect mirror?
Master Tianfeng Deng of Nanchan was the son of the Lei family of Zhongzhou. He addressed the assembly, citing the case of Nanyue:
When Mazu was propagating the Dharma in Jiangxi, Nanyue dispatched a monk to investigate him. He instructed him, saying: "When he ascends the hall, simply ask him, 'What is it?
and remember the words he speaks in response. The monk went to Mazu exactly as instructed and asked, "What is it? Mazu—
He said, "Since the period of chaos thirty years ago, there has been no shortage of salt and sauce. The monk returned and related this to Shouyue, who approved of it.

His verse says: "To know one's son, none equals the father; In practicing benevolence, do not yield to the teacher. Having cast aside spears and laid down armor, From a thousand miles away, he secretly sets his trap."

Chan Master Xingche Dengfa ascended the hall and said: He cited the case of Qingyuan’s initial visit to the Sixth Patriarch, where he first asked, "What should one apply oneself to in order to avoid falling into stages?
The Patriarch replied, "What have you been doing? Qingyuan said, "I do not even engage in the 'Noble Truths.
The Patriarch asked, "In what stage would you then fall? Qingyuan said, "If I do not even engage in the 'Noble Truths,' what stage could there be? [The Master then gave] a verse:
It is said: Moss grows upon the golden hall in a springtime beyond the kalpas; as the night deepens and all is still, the moonlight shines bright. Beyond the realm of Vairocana, there is no news;
how could it concern the meritorious deeds of the Terrace of Qilin in this present age?
Chan Master Tianning Deng’s Praise of the Image of Bodhidharma: Facing the Emperor, he spoke of the profound mystery—there was not a single word.
For nine years he sat coldly; the stone was worn away. After he personally divided the skin and marrow equally, which man among us would not be a true hero?
Master Qingzhong Dengxiang addressed the assembly. He cited the kōan concerning the monk from Yungai Temple who begged for tiles. His verse says:
When he first begged for tiles from the official, A single question was answered by the monk from Yungai. This public case is now brought forth once more;
It does not hinder the golden bricks being spread across the ground.
Chan Master Dachen Dengji ascended the hall and, citing the circumstances of the Third Patriarch’s repentance for transgressions, spoke this verse:

"Already unable to endure as wind and ailment entwine his body, For what reason does he repent his transgressions to investigate the root source? Because he knows the nature of transgression is fundamentally empty, The autumn waters leave no trace and the moon is bright and clear."
Huībáidēng, the Chan Master Guì, cited the story of the wind and the banner. His verse says: The crux of delusion and enlightenment is truly not the same.

In the evening shadows of the corridors, the banner flutters in the wind. If the two monks had understood this message, They would have toppled Changgan Temple and caused it to transform into a dragon.
Chan Master Sishui cited the Great Master Sengcan, the Third Patriarch:

after receiving the Dharma from the Second Patriarch, he concealed himself in profound seclusion and dwelt in no fixed location for more than ten years, such that no one knew of him. At that time, the Fourth Patriarch, Daoxin, was a śrāmaṇera.
Lizang asked, “I pray that the Master will, out of compassion, grant me the Dharma-gate of liberation. The Patriarch said, “Who has bound you? He replied, “No one has bound me.

The Patriarch said, “Why then do you seek liberation? At these words, Xinxing attained great enlightenment. He spoke this verse: The patriarch asked, "Who has bound you? He replied, "No one has bound me. The patriarch said, "Then why do you seek liberation? At these words, he attained great enlightenment. He spoke this verse:
For many years it has remained unobserved by anyone; for the sake of the Dharma, it was deeply concealed, its very essence cold.
Who would have thought that a novice monk, devoid of all restraint, would recklessly propagate these words far and wide?
Chan Master Tianchang was the son of the Ran family of Nanbin. Having long served under Qingzhong, he was dedicated to the cultivation of Pure Land practices.

Qingzhong entrusted him with a verse, which said: "The roots and sprouts are extraordinary and utterly unlike anything else; They belong neither to the West nor to the East. When the season arrives, their fragrance remains as it is;
The Buddha’s birth is a single essence within being and non-being. The Master presented his own verse, saying: "The Buddha’s birth is a single essence; there is no 'that'..."
There is no such thing. One discerns the field from its sprouts; one recognizes a person through their speech. To act with excellence is to be benevolent; thus one may understand ritual propriety.
Chan Master Miao-de Niren-jian raised the story of the Sixth Patriarch’s “Originally there is not a single thing,” and offered this verse:

“Originally there is nothing to invite dust and grime; The rice is ripe, the work accomplished, yet alone he begs for the sifting. Robe and bowl were passed on after the third watch of night; One [verse]...”
The five-petaled flower blooms even to this day.
Gongbu Xiong Ruxue, the layman Yueya, was a native of Fengcheng in Yuzhang.

During the reign of Emperor Huizong, when the silver and bronze statues within the imperial palace were being destroyed, he was suddenly moved by the circumstances. The Emperor attained realization and ordered the Master to enter Sichuan to procure copper and lead.
At that time, Qingzhong resided at Pingdu, where his Dharma assembly was profoundly influential. The Duke visited him there. Previously, Zhong had dreamed of a man prostrating before his curtain;
a monk beside him said, "A disciple of the Master has arrived. Indeed, early the next morning, the visitor arrived. Zhong presented him with the koan of Dongshan’s "Walking on Water.
Within less than a year, he attained realization and offered a verse on the Essential Teachings of Linji, which begins: "A thunderclap..."

The wind dances upon the whetstone in a clear sky; entering the mountain gate, one walks into a lantern. When asked about the essential principle of Linji, [the Master] replied, "Today my tooth aches;
I cannot speak with you. Zhong said, "Touch! Touch! Touch! Furthermore, he offered a verse on the essential principle of Caodong:
"Latent movement and secret function, continuous and uninterrupted; The style of Caodong is profound beyond the profound. A mechanism upon the tongue weaves out brocade; The eyes..."
The former [masters] composed these chapters on non-self; the ancients have now fallen into the hands of the present. Today’s heat is like yesterday’s sky.
If you wish to understand the true countenance of the two masters, you must simply wipe away the five circles. On the anniversary of Elder Juyun’s passing, I offer incense:
the flowing water ever preserves the pulse of past and present; the high mountain never severs the clouds of coming and going. Green and lush is the cliff.
The fragrance of cassia flowers wafts afar; year after year, the autumn wind leaves traces of rain and dew. Today is the anniversary of the passing of my late Master.
I, his Dharma descendant, have come from ten thousand miles away with hopes of meeting him. I offer incense and pay reverence at the stupa;
having no material offerings, I take up this smile, which was his lifelong habit, as a token of my respect. A-he-he! But tell me, what is it that he laughs at? Zhong asked: "One ball, three sons."

"What is the meaning? the Master asked. The layman replied, "He is the Great Teacher of the Three Realms and the Compassionate Father of the Four Modes of Birth. The Master asked, "Why does he not preach the Dharma?

The layman replied, "He has been preaching the Dharma for a long time; it is simply that you, Reverend, have not heard it. The Master said, "If I were to hear it, it would not be the true preaching of the Dharma.

A monk standing nearby said, "The Layman has finished preaching the Dharma. The layman pointed to a chestnut burr. Yunzhong then said to the monk, "You have needlessly brought disaster upon yourself."
The man laughed heartily. Zhong nodded his head in agreement. "For the celebration of Juyun’s birthday, the previous month’s memorial day was just passing away;
how then does today’s birthday come to be? Though burned by fire, he does not die—the adamantine eye deceives all quarters, leaving them all buried alive.
Heh! If I were not his descendant, I would have cursed him until his bones were worn away. For Xizhou.

[The monk] said, "A woman gave birth to seven sons; six did not meet with a true知音 (yin-zhi, 'one who knows the sound'). Even this one alone is not worth keeping," and he threw it into the water.

"Furthermore, how about this? The Master said, "Do not show off so much. [The monk] said, "At that time, Yan-tou unconsciously stuck out his tongue. What was his intention? The Master said, "If there is joy, rejoice together. He asked another monk:
A questioner asked Yunmen, "What is the pure Dharma-body? Yunmen replied, "Flowers and medicinal herbs on the railing.
The Master [Dongshan] said, "Shen-sha [the sand demon] baring his eyes. Question: "If it is this very thing, one buries oneself; if it is not this very thing, how can one avoid burying oneself?"

"To fail the former sages and depart from these two paths—to dwell in such a place where mud and water are mixed—please, Master, speak the Way. The Master said, "A jade chopstick propping open a tiger’s mouth.
[The student] said, "One word spoken is as heavy as gold and stone; ten thousand matters cast off are as light as a goose feather. The Master said, "..."
"Do not deceive this old monk. A question was asked: "Everyone fears the heat, yet I love the length of summer days.

The fragrant breeze comes from the south, and within the halls and pavilions a subtle coolness arises. At that moment, how is it? The Master said: "They cast down their spears and strip off their armor.
On the anniversary of his own death, Huqiu offered incense and said: "Throughout my life I have had no luck; I have run straight into this witless old monk who has exhausted every artifice."
The two cannot be reconciled. From this point on, lay down the weapons of war; wear clothes and eat food according to your lot.
For twenty years you have sat upon a wooden platform, hanging up the head of a sheep while selling dog meat—what evidence do you have for this?
Nevertheless, on the day incense is burned once a year, it leaves people of all ages with ever-deepening resentment. The Master was able to forge [his disciples] within the meditation hall.
He refined those who were venerable and mature; thus, the world spoke of him and Daoyi as "the two gates of ambrosia" dwelling together. He once admonished his disciples, saying:
"For a monk to wear straw sandals and reside in a monastery—how could this be anything less than a viper clinging to its den?

On the thirteenth day of the sixth month in the year of Guiwei during the Longxing era of Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty, he passed away suddenly. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Miaoyan Xianjie of Tiantong in Ningbo Prefecture was the dharma heir of Chan Master Tian Tonghua, the eighteenth-generation successor of Dajian.
He was born into the Zheng family of Fuzhou; his mother dreamed of Mount Lu.
The old monk was born into a household and was precocious from his youth. He left home to become a monk and did not shrink from traveling great distances to visit various masters.
Later, he went to see Ying’an at Mingguo. Ying’an was solitary and stern, difficult to approach, and the master was repeatedly rebuked by him.

One day, during a private interview, Ying’an asked, “What is the True Dharma Eye? The master immediately replied, “A broken sand pot. Ying’an nodded his head in approval. More than a year later, the master took his leave and returned home.

[The Master] went to visit his parents. As he was seeing him off at the hermitage, [Zhaozhou] gave him a verse, saying: "The phrase for penetrating the Great Awakening, Directly opens up the crown of the head.

We have followed one another for four years now; In our mutual inquiry, not a trace remains. Though you have not yet been entrusted with the bowl and robe, Your spirit and bearing swallow the heavens and earth.
Yet you take the Eye of the True Dharma And call it a broken sand-pot. On this journey to visit your kin, Be careful not to simply follow along. I have a final word..."
The latter phrase: "I await your return; you must follow this essential path. Later, he went to Wugu on the road to the world beyond, and subsequently moved to Huazang at Jiangshan in Xiangfu.

Before long, by imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Jingshan, and later moved to Lingyin. In his later years, he lived at Taibai. A monk asked, "What is it like when empty space itself is extinguished?
The Master said, "The offense shall not be doubly punished. He ascended the hall and said: "Niutou expounds horizontally and vertically."
They do not know that there is a pivotal mechanism for ascending. There are certain types of lacquer buckets who cannot distinguish east from west or north from south;
they immediately ask, "What is the pivotal mechanism for ascending? How is this any different from wetting one's bed while wide awake?
Huazang has a turning phrase that lies neither in ascending nor descending; even the Thousand-Handed Great Compassionate One could not find it by groping about. The rain is cold and relentless.
He was out drying his laundry. Today there was a communal labor service (*pǔqǐng*), and he gave alms to the great assembly. After a long while, he said: "Master Bodhidharma had no front teeth.

He ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One spoke what was not spoken; he twisted the crooked to make it straight. Kāśyapa heard what was not heard; he looked into the void and offered a plea.
Mazu’s 'This very mind is Buddha' is like hanging up a goat's head while selling dog meat. Zhaozhou’s examination of the hermitage master—"
Buying high and selling low for not even a single coin’s worth. Take for instance Mañjuśrī, the teacher of the seven Buddhas—why was he unable to bring the woman out of her samādhi?
The river sky and lunar halo, the fish dividing their offspring; the oak leaves blown by the wind, the deer nourishing its antlers.
Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation staff and said, "When deluded, one is deluded regarding this very thing. He struck it again and said, "When awakened, one awakens to this very thing.
Even if you were to forget both delusion and awakening, you would still be adding more rags to a heap of refuse.

Is there anyone who can utter a single phrase from the state where the total function is uniquely liberated—where the east surges up and the west sinks down? If you cannot speak it, [it is like] a flower...
He departed for his own dwelling. Throwing down his staff, he said, "Thirty years hence. He then ascended the hall and cited Jinfeng’s instruction to the assembly:
"Twenty years ago, this old monk possessed a grandmotherly heart; twenty years hence, I shall have no grandmotherly heart."

At that time, a monk asked, "What is it like to have the 'motherly heart' before twenty years had passed? Feng said, "If you ask about the ordinary, I answer about the ordinary; if you ask about the holy, I answer about the holy.
The monk asked, "What is it like after twenty years when there is no more motherly heart? Feng said, "If you ask about the ordinary, I do not answer about the ordinary;
if you ask about the holy, I do not answer about the holy. The Master said, "Had Wugu seen this at the time, he would have simply given a cold laugh."
"Two sounds. If this old fellow were suddenly to have a flash of realization, he would naturally not fall into the conceptual traps of ordinary or sage.
Entering the hall, the Master raised the story of the old woman burning the hermitage. He said: "This old woman’s inner chamber is deep and secure, impenetrable as a watertight seal.
Yet she leans toward scattering flowers upon withered wood and kindling flames within cold ashes. This monk stands solitary and remote, accustomed to entering the great flood."
Tao! He casually sits and cuts off the surging tide; in the end, his body is not wet by even a drop of water.
If one examines this closely, there is no doubt that these two men are bound in shackles and chains; yet as for the Buddha-dharma, they have not even dreamed of it.
Where does Wugu’s such upholding ultimately lead? After a long silence, he said: "A single tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered in."
Mist blends with smoke as it rests upon the jade balustrade. Entering the hall for the discourse: A different melody when the strings are moved;

leaves fall and one knows autumn. To raise one and clarify the three; the eyes discerning the weight of a grain. Like a king wielding a sword, killing or giving life according to the occasion—this is still the ripples of windless waves.
As for the single path beyond, where the thousand sages walk hand-in-hand, they would surely be cast into the hells. Right at this moment...
At such a time, what should one do? In Jiangnan and Liangzhe, it is cold in spring and hot in autumn. [The Master] ascended the hall and said:
"To call the entire universe and the great earth 'one phrase' is to carry a cangue and wear shackles. Not to call it 'one phrase' is for the karmic consciousness to be vast and murky.
When both ends are completely transcended—pure, naked, and bare, with nothing to grasp—this is the school of Bodhidharma."
It sweeps away all traces until nothing remains. This is why Yunmen said: "Throughout the entire universe and the great earth, there is not even a hair’s breadth of fault;
yet this is still a 'turning phrase. To see not a single dharma is merely half the teaching. You must further know that there is a time for the 'total presentation.'"

Whether Great Yunmen or Small Yunmen, the sword has long since departed; to now mark the boat is merely to follow after it. Later, he entered nirvana and was interred in a stupa on the central peak of the monastery.
Chan Master Bai Zhuo Shandeng of Guangxiao Monastery in Quzhou Prefecture was the son of the Min family of Wujiang, Huizhou. A monk asked:

"When the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, saying: 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am the most honored. What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "One person may pass on a falsehood, but ten thousand people pass on a truth. The student said, "When there is spirit, one adds to that spirit;
where there is no elegance, there is still elegance. The Master said, "Even praise cannot fully capture it—praise, indeed, cannot reach it. The student said, "..."
It is just as Yunmen said: "At that time, I saw him; I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, so as to ensure peace throughout the world.
Ultimately, what kind of eyes do you possess? The Master said: "Realize it from behind the head.
Ascending the hall, he said: "By day there is bustling clamor; at night there is profound stillness. One walks along the long corridors, step by step, lacking nothing. Not...
Recognize the master of consciousness; his entire body enters the wild weeds. He encounters Master Fu, who greets the Elder Vimalakīrti as he lies ill in the city of Vaiśālī.
How many know the dawn of heaven? If one is a person of transcendent capacity, they do not seek it there.
Why is this so? He lets out a shout and says: "Running downhill, one does not stop; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter."
Nan Shuji was a native of Fuzhou. Having long relied upon Ying’an, he attained sudden and complete enlightenment through the koan, "The dog has no Buddha-nature.
He composed a verse which says: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; Rāhu’s star enters its destiny. It is not that it kills people;
Rather, it is certain to be killed by others. Ying’an praised him for his carefree liberation. At the end of the Shaoxing era, he passed away at Guizong.

The Layman Li Hao, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, whose courtesy name was De-yuan and style name Zheng-xin, read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in his youth and felt as though he were returning to a familiar home.
He went to Mingguo Temple to seek formal instruction; when entering the inner chamber, Ying’an struck him on the chest and asked, "After you die, Minister, where will you go?
Startled, the layman broke into a cold sweat. Ying’an shouted at him to leave. The layman withdrew to practice meditation, and within less than ten days, he ascended directly to the inner sanctum.
He sent this verse to his fellow practitioner Yan Kangchao: "The gate has a shop for Sun Bin; the home retains the wife of Gan Zhi.
Sleeping at night and rising early— Who awakens, and who is deluded? There is one who sells rouge, Who has also long been a disciple of Ying’an."
He was quite self-confident. A scholar presented him with a verse, saying: "Without smearing red powder, he is naturally elegant;
Often, practitioners of Chan stop here. Having passed through the snares of past and present, He returns here to receive a blow from my fist."
The lay practitioner Yan Kangchao, a Professor at Changxing in Huzhou Prefecture, once sought the Way from Xuedang at Jianfu Monastery.
It was only upon meeting Ying’an that he first attained the essential meaning. He once composed a verse which says: "Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature;

I say the dog does have Buddha-nature. Suddenly, beneath these words, I knew my own home; From this point on, I no longer believe Zhaozhou’s mouth. He then composed the *Jingzhuan* (Essential Verses).
The spirit shakes itself free. Following behind others, there is no skillful hand; riding a cow while searching for a cow is enough to make people laugh to death.
Only now do I realize that all my former efforts were mistaken.
The nineteenth generation under Dajian (Mazu).

Chan Master Songyuan Chongyue of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tiantong Jie. He was a native of the Wu family of Longquan in Chuzhou. From his youth, he was outstanding and extraordinary.
At the age of twenty-three, he left home. First, he visited Master Miaoguang of Lingshi; subsequently, he went to see Dahui Zonggao at [Jingshan].
At Jingshan, Huisheng entered the hall and praised Yungan of Jiangshan for his direct and swift way of guiding people. Upon hearing this, the Master set out before dawn.
Once he arrived, he sought instruction from him morning and evening. One day, Yungan asked, "The World-Honored One had a secret word;
Kāśyapa did not conceal it. What do you say to this? The Master replied, "I leave the Master at a loss. Yungan let out a sharp shout, and the Master immediately prostrated himself.
An was greatly delighted. He spoke a verse to encourage [the master] to shave his head. In the Jia-shen year of the Longxing era, he received full ordination at Bailian Monastery in Lin’an.
He traveled extensively to consult various great masters, yet few met with his approval. Thereupon, he entered Min Province and visited Muguan Yong.
When Yong raised the koan regarding the "phrase with no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree" to question him, the Master replied, "Torn asunder. Yong said, "Langye said it is good..."
"A pile of rotten firewood," [Yunmen] said. The Master [Xuedou] remarked, "Adding a point to an arrow. Yong said, "Observing your words, I cannot surpass you, Elder;
yet it is as if you have not yet reached the mark. In the future, when the fly-whisk handle is in your hands, you will be unable to guide others, nor will you be able to test them."
The Master said: "For one who acts for others, it is indeed difficult to cause an ordinary person of common ground to leap directly into the city of the sages.
But for one who examines people, if they strike before someone's very face, even before the person has opened their mouth, he already knows their very marrow.

What difficulty is there in this? Yong raised his hand and said: "I have told you clearly: 'Opening the mouth is not a matter of the tongue. You shall know this for yourself later. [He passed away] after more than... years.
In his later years, Nanjian met Mian Shanren at Xishan in Quzhou. Whenever he asked a question, Mian would simply smile.
The Master was so intent on reaching the ultimate realization that he forgot to sleep or eat. He followed Mian wherever he moved—to Jiangshan Huazang and later to Jingshan.
Once, during a period of private instruction (*nishu*), Mian asked a monk, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. The Master was standing by his side.
He attained a sudden and great enlightenment, whereupon he said, "Only today have I finally understood Master Mukan’s saying: 'The opening of the mouth does not depend on the tongue.
From then on, his eloquence and discernment became unrestrained. When Miyun moved to Lingyin, the Master was appointed to share the teaching seat.
He subsequently entered the world at Chengzhao in Pingjiang, then moved to Guangxiao in Jiangyin, to Yeyu in Wuyue, to Jianfu in Raozhou, and to Xiangshan in Mingzhou.
Shan. At Huqiu on Pingjiang, in the Ding-si year of the Qingyuan era, he was appointed by imperial decree to the position at Lingyin. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In general, to uphold and establish the lineage of our school, one must possess the true eye atop the head and the efficacious talisman suspended from the elbow.
For instance, when Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk; Baoshou struck him immediately. Sansheng said, 'To act as a teacher in this manner is to blind people.'"
"The people of the entire city of Zhènzhōu have lost their eyes. Bǎoshòu threw down his staff and returned directly to his quarters.
These two venerable masters, in their casual jostling and pressing one another, revealed the very marrow of Línjì’s mind.
Yet they did not realize that life and death were entirely in the hands of this monk. Is there anyone who can discern this? In years past, seeking fire, he obtained it along with the smoke; now—
Carrying the spring from the well at dawn and returning with the moon at dusk. On the first day of the year, he addressed the assembly:
"The new year begins and all things are manifest. Sometimes I let go; sometimes I cut it off completely. Without sparing even my two eyebrows, I shift the sitting mat along with the person upon it.
Buddhist Dharma and worldly dharma are, in their entirety, a single piece. Since they are both Buddhist Dharma and worldly dharma, how can they become one? Simply prepare yourself to be willing."
Mind—truly it shall not deceive you. Addressing the assembly: The ancients said, "When lifted up, heaven turns and earth revolves;
when set down, the grass bows and the wind blows. I, Yeshan, am not like this: "When lifted up, heaven and earth grow dark; when set down, tiles and stones emit light.
If suddenly there is one or half a person who, in a flash, pierces the eye atop their head, then the Dharma of Bodhidharma—
The Master, before the assembly had yet become quiet, addressed the group. He raised the public case of Linji’s “weed-whisk” and cited Xuedou’s comment:
“Linji’s letting go was too precarious; his gathering back was too swift.
The Master took up his staff and said, “Linji acted according to the mandate, yet he did not realize he was failing Huangbo. Xuedou carried this burden with all his might, yet he saw only one side.”
Now tell me: where does the essential point of Jianfu lie? [The Master] threw down his staff and addressed the assembly, citing Fenyang:
"If you recognize this staff, the business of traveling on pilgrimage is finished. The Master said: "Although Fenyang has opened his mouth to reveal his very heart, [the matter is not yet settled]."
Alas, how regrettable that it falls into the secondary category! [The Master] suddenly brandished his staff and said, "This cannot be called a 'staff.
You lacquer buckets! Go and study! [He ascended the hall for the discourse. He cited Baoning Yong’s ascent to the hall: "The Great Square has no exterior; the Great Circle has no interior.
With neither interior nor exterior, holy ones and commoners gather universally. Pottery shards and rubble emit light; Mount Sumeru is pulverized. The infinite Dharma..."
"Gate! Hundred thousand samādhis! [The Master] held up his staff and said, "Understand them all right here. *Sulu sulu, sili sili*.
The Master said, "Great as Baoning was, his karmic consciousness was vast and boundless; he could not even save his own boat. Break the scoop! He addressed the assembly:
"Why do clear-eyed monks lose their nostrils? There is a thief, yet no stolen goods. [A circle with a dot inside. Later.
Having resided at Lingyin for six years, he later retired to the Eastern Hermitage.

On the eve of his passing, he composed a handwritten letter bidding farewell to various officials and nobles, and also left a letter to his Dharma heirs, Miaoyun Muzhou and Fushan Kaixian, entrusting them with the preciousness of the Great Dharma. He further wrote a verse, which says:
Coming, there is no place from which he comes; departing, there is no place to which he goes. With a sudden turn at the profound pivot, even Buddhas and Patriarchs are at a loss.
He sat cross-legged in stillness, truly on the fourth day of the eighth month of the Ji-si year of the Jiading era. He reached the age of seventy-one and had spent forty summers in retreat.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the slopes of Beifeng Peak.

Chan Master Wop’an Zu’an of Wolong in Kuizhou Prefecture was a native of the Wang family of Guang’an. Having heard that the elder master Wen Yuan was residing at Zhaojue, he went there to seek instruction.
Their words were in accord, and he was ordered to serve as the successor to Yuanwu’s incense and offerings. One day, while passing before the abbot’s quarters...

[Zhao] Guo asked, "Is there anyone at the head of the hermitage? The Master said, "There is no one. Zhao struck him once in the chest with his fist and said, "What about you? At that moment, the Master suddenly attained realization.

He left the mountain valley and went to De Shan to receive the tonsure; shortly thereafter, he received full ordination. He traveled extensively, visiting various masters throughout the land, until he arrived at Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou.
There, during a snowy night while sitting in meditation, he thought to himself, "I have been traveling for several years, yet I have not attained peace and stability. He was deeply distressed.
He was in a state of persistent frustration. Suddenly, hearing the bell toll, he hurried to the rear gallery.
Raising his head, he saw the two characters "Zhao Tang" (Illuminating Hall), and his doubts were instantly dispelled. Shortly thereafter, he visited Shuian Yi at Shuanglin.
Shuian said, "Setting aside for a moment the Elder Siṃha being beheaded by Kāśmīra, tell me: why did the bearded man of India have no beard? The Master replied, "Not Shuanglin."
He did not raise this story. Shuizhuang said, "A master Chan guest. The Master said, "My heart owes nothing to others, and my face shows no shame.
Shuizhuang then pushed him away with his hand. The Master said, "I have seen through you. When Shuizhuang retired from his post, he went to visit Miman at Wugu.
Miman appointed him as the guest prefect. One day, in the abbot’s quarters, Miman raised the koan: "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving..."

Regarding the "Fluttering Banner" story: Master [Fengxue] attained a great awakening. The following day, Yun'an encountered him before the quarters and said to him, "You must not employ any clever stratagems;
try to reveal some sign of your realization. Master responded immediately, saying, "There is a guest in the Abbot's quarters.
Yun'an laughed heartily. When Yun'an moved to Jiangshan, the Master attended him as a disciple, serving him intimately for five years before taking his leave.

He returned to Shu. As he was departing, An sent him off with a verse: "Coming ten thousand li southward through the rugged mountains, The rushing torrent crosses the blade and knocks at the Mysterious Gate.
The *zhī* on the crown of the head blinds the Vajra eye; Going and staying are as identical as a pearl rolling on a platter.

When the Master reached Kuimen, the Minister Yang Fu invited him to take charge of Wolong Monastery. Before long, however, he abandoned the post and traveled again to the region of Wu, where he headed the assembly.
He resided at Jingshan Lingyin; later, he stayed at Jianfu in Changzhou, Lingyan in Zhenzhou, Xiufeng and Qionglong in Suzhou, and Zifu in Huzhou.
Finally, at the invitation of Zhang Qi (courtesy name: Yuezhai), he became the founding abbot of Guangshou Huiyun.

In all, he sat upon the site of enlightenment six times. [The following is] the discourse for ascending the hall: "When Yangqi first settled here, the walls of the house were sparse; the entire bed was strewn with snow-white pearls.
Shrinking my neck, I sighed in secret, suddenly remembering how the ancients dwelt beneath the trees.

Yangqi competes in excellence, not in inferiority; Xiufeng competes in inferiority, not in excellence. When Xiufeng first settled here, there was no distinction between kin and stranger; everyone harbored [this same realization]."
The Pearl of the Canghu Lake: One cannot look enough at the lakes and mountains that fill one's eyes;

Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his servants. Entering the hall, he said: "Master Miyuan said: 'If asked about matters of winter, the capital produces great yellow [myrobalan]. For the sake of a single grain of rice...'"

[The old saying goes: "One loses six months' worth of provisions. Xiu Peak, however, was not like this. When someone asked about the matter of winter's arrival, he replied: "In the capital, they produce great yellow [myrrh];
one seeks but a single grain of rice, yet gains a hundred years' worth of provisions. Or perhaps an administrator might say, "Venerable sir, Venerable sir!
Do not speak of a hundred years' provisions; even half a year’s provisions would be more than enough. To such a person, he simply says: "Just prepare a heart of resolve."
"I will certainly not deceive you. He ascended the hall and said: "Citing Dongshan’s words: 'What is Chan? The Jambu tree is on the southern shore of the sea.
Near, it is not separate from the square inch of the heart; far, it is one hundred and eight thousand miles. Ultimately, what is it? Chan, Chan."
The Master said: "Even the vaulting heavens have their way of being. What is Chan? The Jambu tree stands on the edge of the Southern Sea;

it supports the heavens and props up the earth, propping up the earth and supporting the heavens. It cannot be described through clever words; it requires only mind-to-mind transmission. Ultimately, how is it?"
"Zen, Zen. Ascending the hall, he said: "It is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. This mountain monk cannot restrain his impatience;
for your sakes, I shall provide a way to cast it all aside. He took up his staff, struck once, and said: "The flowing water silently wears away the rocks by the stream;
I urge you to abandon the difficulty of right and wrong. Ascending the hall again, he said: "Before the fifteenth day, it is as clear as a mirror..."
After five days, it was as black as lacquer. It was precisely the fifteenth day. Furthermore, what was it like? The oriole moves to the lofty trees, speaking repeatedly;
the butterflies cling to the fragrant clusters, flying in pairs. He presented a verse to the Abbot, saying: "Even seeing is detached from seeing; this is not true seeing.
When the eight returns are exhausted, there is nothing left to return to. Leaves fall from the autumn sky, and the mountain’s bones are exposed; I know not who—"
Shi Lao knew that the Master, Gautama, was about to enter parinirvāṇa and had composed a letter by hand to bid farewell to his friends and associates.

He further wrote a verse, saying: "The final word has already caused me deep distress; to set it down before others would be a thousand and ten thousand errors. Having finished writing, he sat upright and passed away.
This was the ninth day of the sixth month in the year of Xingwei of the Jiading era. At that time, he was residing at Mount Jing as a guest, having left instructions to scatter his bones.
In the forest, Zhuchi Shiqiao collected his remains and erected a stupa on a separate peak to the right of the existing one.
His age was seventy-six and his dharma years forty-nine.
Chan Master Caoyuan Daosheng of Jianfu Temple in Raozhou Prefecture was a native of Nanjian. He sat on the seat at Yunju and subsequently appeared in the world [as an abbot].
[He] bestowed upon him the wondrous fruit [of realization]. Moving to Guifeng, he ascended the hall and said: "The two words 'Buddha-dharma' are known by everyone.

Yet how can one allow such lethal poisons as wolf-tongue and arsenic to enter the mouth? Even if you were to penetrate beyond the time before Aishan (Vītarāga), you would still be wandering outside of madness.
This mountain monk has already been dragging through mud and water; what shall you all do? He let out a shout. Ascending the hall again, he said: "Now..."
The morning of the fifteenth day of the eighth month; the sky was half-sunny and half-rainy. How many travelers outside the gates failed to behold the full moon directly before their doors?
This is both laughable and lamentable. How can they compare to the team of ancient Buddhas at the West Lake temple, who, having finished their meditation session, returned to the hall to drink tea?
Ascending the hall [he said]: "The spring breeze fans eastward and westward; the spring rain is neither sunny nor rainy."

Pale greens and deep reds spread out like brocade; the warbling of orioles and the chatter of swallows play together like the music of flutes and harps. Each and every thing reveals the wondrous gate of universal penetration (*yuantong*);

at every turn flows the treasury of the true Dharma eye (*zhengfayan zang*). If you attempt to direct your mind toward it or settle upon it, you remain as before amidst ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains.
Only by knowing where to return directly can you see its seven holes and eight apertures. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended. He then ascended the hall for the formal discourse.

Snow and rain fall in profusion; water drips from the eaves. How excellent is Avalokiteśvara! Yet he cannot leap out from within the grass. How truly a grievance! A tortoise at the bottom of the water drills through an iron wall.
*Duḥ!* Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The moon gives birth to one": it topples over the silver mountains and iron walls. "The moon gives birth to two":
the Earth-Dweller (*Tu-sù*) rides an ox through the bustling market. "The moon gives birth to three": deep and secluded above the house.
The birds warble their songs; this is neither a tangled web of sophistry nor a profound discourse on ultimate truth.

At such a moment, how do you express the phrase where guest and host intersect? "A single hand hangs down from a precipice ten thousand fathoms high; amidst a thicket of myriad flowers, the udumbara blooms.
[He] ascended the hall: "At the break of dawn, the third month’s morning; the green peaks of South Mountain pierce the clouds."
Xiao said, "There is no need to seek the meaning of the Westany further. Outside the gate, the oriole sings its melodious song.
He clapped his knee once and said, "Good brother! Then he recited a verse on Lingyun’s stone: Clouds come and clouds go, yet they have no intention; Clouds come and clouds go, yet they have no mind.

Chan Master Tianmu Wenli, also known as Meister Mie'ung of Tiantong in Ningbo Prefecture, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Lingyin Yue. He was the son of the Ruan family of Lin’an, Hangzhou. His family resided at the foot of Mount Tianmu;

He subsequently moved to Nengren Temple in Wenzhou. Before long, he retired to Xiqiu in Qiantang. Zhao Jiezhai visited him incognito; after conversing with the Master all day, he departed.

Mount Shishuang said, "One avoids [it] within the boiling cauldrons and the burning furnaces. [The Master] asked, "But as for being within the boiling cauldrons and the burning furnaces, how does one avoid it?
Shishuang said, "The various sufferings cannot reach him. The Master composed a verse, saying: "Blind the three eyes at the crown of the head;
Roam freely within the boiling cauldrons and burning furnaces. If you say the various sufferings cannot reach him, When has this ever truly been so?"

Dazhu Huaihai was attending to his duties when he constantly performed prostrations in this manner. Nanquan Puyuan said, "What is the use of performing prostrations? Dazhu struck him. Puyuan said, "You are too crude.

"One can expound hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings. [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, struck once, and said:

The portrait of the Patriarch says: "Seeking the mind, there is nowhere to find it; one merely deceives oneself. Willingly enduring the cold of snow waist-deep, Rising after three prostrations, one stands in place.

The Layman Lu You, styled Wuguang and nicknamed Fangong, was a native of Shanyin.

He attained it. Shidian nodded in silent understanding and presented this verse: "Many times I have driven my carriage into the imperial capital, Meeting people one after another, their eyes both equally green.
Only today do I see the distinctiveness of our School; To speak of 'existence' or 'non-existence,' you must listen with your own eyes."
Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan of Mount Jing in Hangzhou Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wolong Xian. He was the son of the Yong clan from Zizhong in Shu.

At the age of nine, he left home to become a monk under Daoqin at Mount Yinping. In the Jiayin year of the Shaohui era, he received full ordination. The following year, he traveled to Chengdu and sat [in meditation].
In the summer, Master Xia Zhengfa requested instruction on the method of *zazen* from Yao, a senior disciple of Xiatang.
Yao asked, "What is Chan? Who is it that sits? The Master then investigated this day and night. One day, while using the toilet, he attained realization.
The following year, he went to see Fozhao at Yuyang Monastery. Fozhao asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Jianzhou. Fozhao said, "Have you brought your sword with you?"
"Are you coming? The Master let out a shout as soon as the voice fell. Zhao laughed and said, "This black-headed fellow is acting recklessly. After some time, he went again to Lingyin.
At that time, Pō'ān was serving as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò). They visited Shísǔn Ān together.

A practitioner from the monastery requested instruction on the koan regarding the "monkey that cannot be caught. Pō'ān said, "Why bother to catch it? It is like wind blowing across water; it flows naturally."
However, a pattern was formed. As the Master attended by his side, he attained realization. Before long, Pō’ān went to sweep the pagoda at Tiāntóng; the Master accompanied him.
He further invited Shìxī Yuè to travel together to Tái and Yàn. Upon reaching Ruìyán Yúnniáo, they requested the Master to occupy the seat of division (*fēnzà*).

That night, he dreamed of a person in magnificent robes and cap who presented him with a handful of thatch grass. The following day, a special messenger arrived from Qīngliáng in Míngzhōu to extend an invitation, which the Master accepted.
He entered the monastery and beheld the so-called temple guardian deity, whose surname was Mao and whose attire was no different from that seen in his dream.
The deity ascended the hall to expound the Dharma, and he offered a single incense stick to Po’an. After three years, he moved to Mount Jiao; the following year, he moved to Xuedou.

Another three years passed, and by imperial decree, he was transferred to Yuhuang Temple. Three more years later, he took charge of Shaolin on Mount Song. Subsequently, he was appointed to Jing Mountain. The following year, the temple was destroyed by fire.
The Master remained unmoving in countenance, his mind fixed upon the meaning of the scriptures. In the tenth month of that winter, an imperial decree was issued summoning him into the inner court.

The Emperor, presiding over the Xuzheng Hall, received him in audience. The Master’s responses were detailed and lucid; the Emperor bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe and further commanded him to proceed to the Ciming Hall to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma.
The Emperor listened from behind a lowered curtain and conferred upon him the title of Chan Master Fojian. Three years later, the temple was completed.
After six years, it was again destroyed by fire. Yet, with assistance arriving like clouds, within a few years it was restored to its former appearance.
A monk asked, "Zhaozhou said, 'Thirty years ago, while traveling in the south, there was at my hearth a saying concerning the absence of host and guest;
even until now, no one has brought it up. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "His tongue drags on the ground. The monk said: [The Master replied: "It is so."
"How, ultimately, is there the saying of 'no host and guest'? The Master said, "Words fill the world.
[The student] asked, "As for Xuansha hearing this and saying, 'This old fellow’s feet have not yet touched the ground,' what about that? The Master said, "Bury them all in one pit.
[The student] said, "It can truly be called 'a hot brick striking a frozen base,' or 'red-eyed, bumping into a firebrand.'"
The Master struck once with his staff and ascended the hall, saying: "Under the gate of Wuping, there is nothing at all.
The meditation seat is cramped; the offerings in the hall are sparse. What one treads upon beneath one's feet are broken bricks and shattered shards;
what one encounters before one’s face is Wang Gela and Li Mahu. To dwell in such poverty as this is truly to bring shame upon the Old Barbarian."
After a long silence, he said: "Even though it is so, let us clarify it further. He ascended the hall and said: "The summer retreat is now complete; there is nothing left undone.
Thus, I have taken up my alms bowl from Suizhou and my ceramic bowl from Qiongzhou. He ascended the hall again and said: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon; at Caoxi they spoke of the moon.

He addressed the assembly: "If one were to discuss this matter, it is truly simple and direct. Alas, how is it that you all create difficulties for yourselves?"
This creates an obstacle for oneself. Thus, whenever I see people on the eastern or western corridors bowing and inquiring after my well-being, I simply lower my head in response;
there is truly nothing else to it. It is simply that I wish everyone to recognize that this old monk is a native of Longqing Prefecture in Xichuan.
If you can recognize me, I shall speak some local dialect with you. Please listen.
A few words of local dialect. For now, let us not ask whether you recognize the Elder;
rather, each of you should know your own native place. Do you know it? Mingzhou has six counties; Fenghua has eight districts.

In the autumn of the Wushen year of the Chunyou era, I built a dwelling by the Moonlight Pond and inscribed its name "Retiring from Plowing. I requested retirement from the court on the first day of the third month of the Jiyou year.

Chan Master Shitian Faxun of Lingyin, Hangzhou Prefecture, was the son of the Peng family of Meishan. From birth, he was exceptionally intelligent and quick-witted.
At the age of sixteen, he left home at Fabao Monastery on Shilong Mountain in Danling. At twenty-two, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
Traveling to Shichuang, he paid homage at the stupa of Lei Qian and composed a verse, saying: "A single thought of compassionate countenance is fundamentally never separated;
why need one suddenly act so perversely? To level the high and accommodate the low, his compassionate heart is urgent—how could it fail to vex Master Lei?"
He was busy at night. Consequently, the Master’s fame grew great. Hearing that the reputation of Pò’ān at Qiónglóng was eminent, he went to rely upon him.

red-eyed one bumps into a firebrand. Pò’ān marveled at this. Thereupon, the Master resolved to remain in reliance [upon him] and stayed with Wú...
He trained under Zhunri, who sharpened him through rigorous mutual challenge; after a long time, he took his leave to engage in universal study (*biancan*).
Lingyin’s Yue and Jingci’s Chonghuazang Yan both praised him highly. Later, he emerged into the world at Gaoping in Suzhou, and subsequently moved to Hanshan.

Yin. Ascending the hall, he said: "One is direct; two is circuitous. If a patch-robed monk understands this, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences.

Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Mount Jing in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jianfu Sheng. He was the son of Xun of the Changjiang clan in Wuxin.
Having failed in his attempts at the imperial examination for the jinshi degree, he subsequently received monastic ordination at Miaoyin Monastery in Zizhou and traveled to lecture halls in Chengdu.
He studied the sutras and śāstras. In the *Renzi* year of the Shaoxi era, he left the Gorges to visit Songyuan Yue at Jianfu Monastery;

however, due to the famine that year, he did not succeed in doing so. He then encountered Caoyuan Sheng, who had been installed as abbot at Miaoguo. The Master went to see him, and upon hearing the words of his entrance into the gate, he attained realization.

He joined the assembly hall and was appointed to attend to the incense. Day and night, the Master did not spare him a single "old fist" or painful blow. At this point, all the views and knowledge he had held throughout his life were utterly severed.

The Story of the Sand Basin. The verse says: When the young son of a nobleman from the Five Tombs was in his prime, He galloped on spring breezes with a horse in high spirits.

Lei asked, "I, an old monk, do not know either. He ascended the hall and said: "The earth is great, the water is great, the fire is great, and the wind is great.
If for a single moment there is no doubt, the earth cannot obstruct you. If for a single moment there is no attachment, the water cannot drown you.
If for a single moment there is no anger, the fire cannot burn you. If for a single moment there is no joy, the wind cannot blow you away. To be thus is to be without dependence."
"O practitioners of the Way, the Buddha arises from non-reliance. If one awakens to non-reliance, even Buddhahood is unattainable.

One day, as he sat upon his meditation cushion, suddenly before him everything opened up like the earth collapsing. At that moment, there was pure nakedness; it was silent and still, yet buoyant and pervasive—whether moving or still.
It has been more than half a month since the signs of non-arising appeared. From that time on, I have sat in meditative absorption for ten years, with a persistent obstruction in my breast.
Ordinarily, when entering the room and encountering the raising of the "Principal Host" (zhǔzōngzhǔ) dialogue, I could immediately leap up with a bound.

However, if one were to command the raising of the "monk’s nostrils" or the "fang-teeth of the Buddhas and Patriarchs," there would be no place at all to apply the teeth of one's mouth. Later, while traveling with Zhong Shiliang across Mount Tianmu, I raised my eyes and beheld ancient cypresses.
Upon touching the realms previously attained, they all fall away at once; the "obstructing thing" that has been pressing against the chest finally bursts apart.
From this point on, one no longer doubts birth, no longer doubts death, no longer doubts the Buddhas, and no longer doubts the Patriarchs.

One thoroughly perceives the place where the Elder of Jing Mountain stands firm. Later, he appeared in the world at Longxing Temple in Tan, and subsequently moved to Daolin Temple in Xiangxi. There he resided.
At Furi in Zizhou, Husheng in Taizhou, and Guangxiao in Huzhou—beginning in the Jisi year of the Xianchun era—he first took the seat at Yangshan.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The single melody of Shaolin was transmitted through five generations until it reached the Sixth Patriarch; in deep mountains and cold waters, it produced the pure tones of antiquity.
Passing from Nanyue through nine generations to Ciming, the singing was lofty and the resonance steep, playing a tune that transcends all hearing."
The "rarefied sound" (xīshēng)—that is, the Buddha-dharma—was once flourishing in Jiangxi and Hunan, so vast and so profound that it defies all naming.
Yet who would have thought that over the course of three hundred years, the land has become desolate and the people sparse; the Way has changed with the times.
The *huángzhōng* and *dàlǚ* notes are silent and no longer played, and even the sounds of Zheng and Wei have ceased to be heard. Reverend Qin certainly possesses no great talent.
As for this place—having been on the other side of Zhejiang, it was blown by a gust of karma-wind into the city of Tanzhou.
Having no choice but to change its tune and alter its melody, it shall now be re-performed at the crossroads. But tell me, what is the rhythm? Striking the whisk, he said:
"Wan Nian Huan" (Ten Thousand Years of Joy). He then cited Zhaozhou, who said: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha..."
"A golden Buddha does not cross fire; a clay Buddha does not cross water; the true Buddha sits within.

The Master said, "To reveal the true body of the Tathāgata and to elucidate the supreme lineage of our school—Zhaozhou was indeed a masterful hand. However, he was simply not right to needlessly create such complications.
My view at Xinglong Temple is otherwise: a golden Buddha crosses the furnace; a wooden Buddha crosses the fire; a clay Buddha..."

"Crossing the waters—this is the true Buddha. One must strictly avoid falling into idle talk. Suddenly, a man came forward and said, "If you act like this, you are merely creating artificial complications.
[The Master] struck his knee once and said, "I thought there was no one to witness this.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To see it once is to see it; once attained, it is attained forever. He extended his hands and said, "With both hands opened wide, let everyone look! Ultimately, it is clear."
What is this clarity? Within and without the city of Tanzhou, there are eighteen city gates.

By day, thousands upon thousands and tens of millions of people pass back and forth, coming and going at will toward the east, west, south, or north. As the Head Seat and the Rector ascend the hall: "The eyes of the human and celestial realms;
the governing principles of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Though they differ in a thousand ways and ten thousand variations, they are all unified by a single thread. How do you see it?"
He was able to discipline his subordinates, yet he did not prevail in the battle of the Dharma. Nanquan slew a cat. He ascended the hall and said:
"In the spring morning, the burn scars are green; the cuckoo calls everywhere, urging the plowing.

Although this matter is most clear, one must simply not look with the eyes nor listen with the ears. Why? As soon as there is a single thread of thought, there is already a single thread of thought. Above.
The Hall. The stone gate is steep and perilous; the Jade Gorge flows with murmuring currents. If you have not yet reached this place, it is natural to harbor doubts.

This is the great divine mantra; this is the great illuminating mantra; this is the unsurpassed mantra. Do you all see the "Yellow-Faced Old Man" [the Buddha]?

With his staff, he struck them all at once and dispersed them. Ascending the hall, he said: "The cuckoo cries until its blood drenches the flower branches; In such haste, it bitterly urges one to return home.
