The phrase that encompasses heaven and earth; the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current; the phrase that cuts off all streams.

from antiquity until today—when this mountain monk arrives here, he truly finds no way to insert his hands. Do you all believe that you yourselves are Yangshan?

Suddenly, the bright sun appears in the sky; heaven cannot cover it, nor can earth support it. At this very moment, it is like...

[Ascending the hall: A fragrant breeze comes from the south; within the halls and pavilions, a subtle coolness arises. This is the manifestation of all Buddhas.
This point—take care not to misjudge it. Even if one attains realization before words or takes responsibility beyond phrases, Yangshan dares say it is still "not yet.
Why? "Tender bamboo strikes the wind, sounding like emerald birds; lotus leaves toss in the rain, drenching the mandarin ducks.
[Ascending the hall: "The waters of the sea cannot be measured with a peck; empty space cannot be gauged with a ruler; a pure ground cannot be strewn with sand. [He breaks off. "Rotten..."

At the Great Xiangguo Monastery in the Eastern Capital, there is a banana tree; when the wind blows and the rain beats upon it, it looks just like a tattered *kāṣāya*.
Ascending the hall [he said]: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. A white egret descends to the field—a thousand dots of snow. Yellow...
The oriole perches upon the tree with a single branch; three thousand miles away, he sells his cotton robe.
Coming from no great distance, why does he set down his mud-platter and laugh heartily? "Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on this long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Zen! The trees above call out in clamor; the Way says the wind blows vast before the gate. In the cold of the earth, one reflects..."
This measure is truly laughable. Tell me, what is there to laugh at? "Casually picking up a pear from Zhengzhou, yet upon closer inspection, it turns out to be a jujube from Qingzhou.
Entering the hall, he said: "This matter is fundamentally manifest; though you seek it, it cannot be seen.
A flawless white jade is originally without blemish, yet polishing it instead creates a flaw. To grasp it as a substantial reality is like lightning flashing in the void. Regarding it as...
Trifling! A red thread is added beneath your feet. Take care, you who study the Way; look well at the expedient means. How so?
You must quickly turn your eyes to look at the immortal; do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand. A monk asked, “What is Deshan’s staff?
The Master said, “It pierces through your skull. The monk asked, “What is Linji’s shout? The Master said, “Return!”
"Did you hear that? [The Master] asked. "What is the Tiantai (Miaoyun) school? The Master said, "A father is kind; a son is filial.
He asked, "What is the Linji school? The Master said, "So swift that a clap of thunder leaves no time to cover one's ears. He asked, "What is the Caodong school? The Master said:

"At the third watch, there is no need for a night-bright curtain. [The student] asked, "What is the Yunmen school? The Master said, "The body is exposed to the golden wind. [The student] asked, "What is the Fayen school?
The Master said, "The mountains are naturally green and the trees are naturally lush. [The student] asked, "I have received your instructions on the five houses of the lineage;
as for the ultimate vehicle of the patriarchs, what is it like? The Master said, "The head touches the heavens and the feet tread upon the earth. The Master [continued].

Compassionate toward the fact that the fundamental tenets had lost their support, he provided guidance through *tiqi* (raising the topic) and *nian-song* (verse commentaries), and inspired others through the dynamic interplay of *kiao* (striking) and *chang* (singing).

His realization of the ultimate truth transcended all schools, and for a time, the monastic tradition was revitalized by his influence. Emperor Shizu of the Yuan dynasty bestowed gifts and honored him with ritual respect.

In the Dinghai year of the Zhizhi era, he sent a bamboo rattle and a fly-whisk, along with the "Green Water and Blue Mountains" as a formal transmission of the Dharma, to Gao Feng Yuanmiao, accompanied by a verse of praise.
It was said: "The Great Master Shangda has already passed away; Xueyan knows the proper rites. His empty fame fills the heavens and earth.
He entrusted [the lineage] to Attendant Yuanyao. At over seventy years of age, he manifested his passing.

Dharma heir of Chan Master Fanzhi of Mount Jing, the twenty-first generation under Dajian of the Linji school.
Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was the son of the Xu family of Huangyan, Taizhou. His mother was Liu. She conceived him after dreaming of the moon.
At the age of eighteen, he received the tonsure at Guangci Monastery in Yongjia. Initially, he went to Ruiyan to see Guyuan Dao;

there, upon hearing the kōan regarding "three pounds of hemp," he became filled with doubt. He traveled extensively to consult various masters of the different quarters. One day, while at Yunju, he encountered...
While reading the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra* in his mountain hall, he reached the passage stating that mosquitoes, insects, and ants have no speech yet are able to perform their tasks.
He attained a sudden realization and remarked, "Zhaozhou’s ‘Cypress Tree’ koan is truly direct and to the point; yet it has not been explained to others.
Shortly thereafter, he visited Wuzhun at Xuedou. Wuzhun asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tiantai. Wuzhun said, "Have you passed over the Stone Bridge?"
"Is it a wooden bridge? The Master said, "I have already broken it with a single step. From then on, people called him Duanqiao (Bridge-Breaker).
One day, Zhun asked why a dog has karmic consciousness and instructed the Master to provide a response. After thirty turns of speech, none were in accord.
The Master asked, "Is there no expedient means? Zhun showed him a verse by Zhenjing. The Master stood up straight and silent for a long while, and then he heard [the truth].

Upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, sweat poured from his entire body; thereupon, he was suddenly liberated and free of doubt. Zhuan invited him to occupy the seat at Yuwang and Shuangjing, where the Master shared the dais with him.
He subsequently presided over Qiyuan, moved to Ruiyan and Guoqing, and later took charge of Jingci. Ascending the hall, he said:

"In the mountains of Jing there is jade, yet the one who obtains it does not remain in the mountains of Jing. In the waters of Chi there is a pearl, yet the one who picks it up does not remain in the waters of Chi."
A patch-robed monk possesses the True Person of No-Rank. For one who has realized this, coming and going do not occur through the face-gate.
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, holds it crosswise, and says, "Do you understand? A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou.

[He] ascends the hall and cites how Ciming kept a basin of water in his room, with a sword placed upon the basin and a pair of straw sandals set beside the sword. Whenever a monk arrived, [he would point them out].
He then pointed. This is the causal occasion for the saying, "As soon as he hesitated, [the Master] struck him. The verse says: "Amidst a thicket of a hundred flowers, the whip flashes by;
How much brilliance and elegance there is! The unexamined scholar peeks with a sidelong glance; With a heart full of helplessness, what can he do about his old sorrows?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Deshan lowered his head; Jiaoshan nodded his head; Jueyi held up one finger; Xuansha struck and broke it."
[He points to] his toes. Holding up his staff, he says: "All of this does not go beyond the tip of this mountain monk’s staff.
How do you see this? He strikes the ground with the staff and says: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven. Ascending the hall, he cites Daguan Ying, who said:
"The Seven Buddhas are the subjects of nature; the myriad dharmas are the slaves of the mind. But tell me, where is the master? [Daguan] then gave a shout himself.
The seven Buddhas and those below them emerge from beneath their heads. Again, they respond in unison, saying, "Each shall attend to his own duties.
The Master says, "To call the seven Buddhas 'slaves of nature' and to point to the myriad dharmas as 'servants of the mind'—Daguan claims for himself a path of transcendence.

Yet, when he himself shouts and himself responds, these are merely matters concerning slaves and servants; when has the true Master ever been seen even in a dream? If you, the great assembly, wish to see the Master—"
"Is it so? he asked. With his whisk, he made a single sweep and said, "A spring breeze stirs at dawn; throughout the gardens, a hundred kinds of flowers bloom.
As he was about to pass away, he entered the room with the assembly. Afterward, he wrote a letter bidding farewell to the various mountains and the Duke of Wei.
When the Duke sent medicine as a gift, he would not accept it. He then sent a messenger to ask the Master, "The Master was born in Tiantai; why then do you die here?"
Jingci asked, and the Master replied, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. Thereupon, he passed away in a state of profound stillness.
His secular age was sixty-one, and his monastic seniority was forty-four. He was interred in [the location of] the stupa.
Chan Master Liao-hui of Xiyuan in Tiantong, Ningbo Prefecture, was the son of the Luo family of Pengzhou.

While still a young boy with hanging tufts of hair, he would always delight in building Buddhist stupas and images while playing with other children. One day, Zudeng arrived at his home from Mount Yuzhang; the Master faced him with palms joined in reverence.

Recognizing the karmic affinity between teacher and disciple from past lives, his parents allowed him to leave the household life. Zudeng then instructed him in the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi* (Banzhou Sanmei).

Fei felt that this was not his true aspiration and took leave to go to Chengdu, where he visited Zhaoguan Zhao at Zhaojue Temple. Zhao recognized his potential and commissioned him to travel south for inquiry.
He subsequently went to Jing Mountain to study under Zhejiang Weng Yan. Hearing that Gao Yuanquan was a man of straightforward character, he went to visit him;
it happened that Yuanquan was about to depart for Ruiyan on Mount Tai, so the Master accompanied him there. One day, Yuanquan asked: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth..."
"Is it existence? Is it non-existence? As the Master was about to open his mouth, Yuan immediately shouted at him. He then presented a verse to Yuan, to which Yuan replied, "There is no connection.
One day, the Master happened to write down some words he had spoken to the assembly regarding the white poplar tree.

Upon reading them, Yuan laughed and said, "You may be quite capable of writing characters and composing phrases, but what can you do about there being no connection? The Master was filled with indignation. Yuan said, "Your karmic affinity does not lie here."
"You may go to Xuedou to see Master Zhun. Following these instructions, the Master went to pay his respects and explained his background.
Zhun rebuked him, saying, "Go back to sleep! Subsequently, he appointed him as an attendant who did not handle administrative affairs.

One day, Zhun said to the Master, "The place you have not yet seen through lies right at the tip of your nose; the place where you cannot express it does not leave your lips. If you seek it, [you will find] a thousand..."

[The distance was] ten thousand *li*. Master Kang raised his voice and said, "I thought there would be much more. Zhun succeeded to the position of Abbot at Yungwang Monastery. The Master attended him during his travels and fully mastered his essential teachings.

When Zhun moved to Mount Jing, the Master served as the Second Seat. Zhao Guanwen, the Prefectural Governor of Suzhou and titled Jiezhai, recommended the Master to open the Dharma seat at Foding Monastery.
Subsequently, he moved to Nengren Monastery in Yongjia and Donglin Monastery in Jiangzhou. Later, he arrived at Tian... [text ends].
The Master [Tong] ascended the hall following the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "The Yellow-Faced Gautama was a fierce general of Central India.
He took compassion as his bow and arrows, and wisdom as his halberds and spears. Leading a million heroic troops, his valor was irresistible;
deploying over three hundred battle arrays, his momentum was invincible. In this manner, for forty-nine years, he performed..."
Although more than five thousand scrolls of military treatises had circulated among the world, not a single word had ever been leaked.
Consequently, as he was at enmity and in opposition with the demonic armies of birth and death, he constructed a great city on the banks of the Bahudā River and inscribed its name as Nirvāṇa.
Within that city, he first used his body of purple-polished gold to reward all the soldiers, commanding them to gaze upon it in veneration.
He took as much as he needed. After repeatedly comforting and exhorting him, he further distributed eight *hu* and four *dou* of pearls. His intention was no other than this:

he surely wished to universally bestow these upon all sentient beings throughout the great earth, so that they might break through the prison-barriers of birth and death, travel together upon the living path that reaches the heavens, and finally arrive at the field of great peace and security and great liberation. He has not yet fulfilled his ambition, nor has he yet presented his merit. Since this mountain monk knows that his strength is exhausted and his stratagems spent, I cannot help but draw my sword to assist him.
Striking once with his staff, he said: "The waves of the four seas are stilled; the dragon sleeps in peace."
The clouds are clear in the nine heavens as the crane flies high. Elder Fuyong ascends the hall. He cites the case of Master Fuyong Xun visiting Master Shixing.
When Shixing ascended the hall, he held up his staff with his right hand, pointed it toward the left, and said:
"If it were not for my elder brother, Fuyong, this story would be very difficult to fully comprehend. He then offered this verse: Exhausting all the spirit of an old man, Cups and plates...
Extraordinarily new: Who would have known that the wine of a village tavern is difficult to persuade a person from the Jade Tower to drink?
Once, when Nanquan arrived at Lestam, he saw Chang sitting facing the wall. Nanquan then patted Chang on the back. Chang asked, "Who is it? Nanquan replied, "Puyuan. Chang asked, "How so?"
Quan said, "It is quite ordinary. Chang said, "Why do you make such a fuss over this matter? He then spoke in verse: "The wall is piled high as he leads his guest past;
He asks who it is, and then asks further, 'How is it? To say it is ordinary already constitutes a great deal of fuss; If one examines my own affairs, they are even more numerous.
When he was staying with Miaofeng at Lingyin, he once inscribed these words upon the murals of the two corridors: "Fortunately..."
The ten directions have no walls; who would paint the void with five colors? In the eyes of Sudhana, cataracts have grown, yet layer after layer is peeled away.
In his later years, he retired to Huanzhi Hermitage. When he was about to pass away, having instructed his attendants, he asked, "What time is it now?
They replied, "It is the second watch. Thereupon, he relaxed his body and passed away. This was during the Jingding era of Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty.
The day was the eleventh of the third month in the *wuxu* year. His age was sixty-five; his monastic seniority (*xià*) was forty-seven.
Chan Master Ning, who retired from farming at Lingyin in Hangzhou Prefecture, first resided at Chongsheng in Jiaxing.

Chan Master Bieshan Zuozhi of Tiantong, Tianbo Prefecture, was a native of the Yang family in Shunqing, Sichuan. At the age of fourteen, he received full ordination.
Initially, while listening to a monk reciting the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he heard the passage about entering the Maitreya Tower and it closing again behind him; he was then suddenly as if in a dream.
Upon awakening, he immediately attained the verse concerning the karmic conditions of Lingyun seeing peach blossoms, which contains the lines: "Among ten thousand greens, a single red dot;
how many rejoice, and how many grieve? He then visited and consulted various masters of the Linji lineage, including Zeweng Yan, Wujie Pai, Gaoyuan Quan, Chun'an Jing, and Miaofeng Shan.
Finally, he met Wuzhun at Xuedou; Wuzhun recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma.

He treated him with ever-increasing severity; at times, staff blows and shouts were delivered together, not sparing him a single word. Whenever the Master attempted to respond, he was suddenly silenced and unable to utter a sound.
Through this, his reliance on intellectual understanding was completely lost. After some time, he spoke up and said, "All the skills I have cultivated throughout my life are but dead methods.
Only now, meeting this old man, do I begin to travel the path of life. Subsequently, Zhuan was transferred to Mount Jing, where he appointed the Master [to succeed him].

He shared his seat [with others]. In the *jiǎxī* year of the Song dynasty (*wùxū*), he went forth to reside at Tiānwáng Monastery on Mount Dōngtíng. In the *bǐngchén* year of the *bǎoyòu* era, Tiāntóng Monastery was destroyed by fire.

County Governor Wú Gōng Qián memorialized the Emperor regarding the Master’s spiritual conduct. Upon receiving the imperial decree, the Master arrived carrying only a single bag and a single bowl; he bound together bundles of reeds to dwell in.
The city of Níng had not seen rain for a long time, but when the Master prayed for it, it fell immediately. Consequently, the people flocked to him, and within less than three [years]...

Chan Master Xuesou Hishou Shaotan of Ningbo Prefecture was a native of Western Sichuan. Having appeared in the world at Fulong, he ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "As for the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, what is it like? The Master said, "Drops drip from the eaves; clearly and distinctly. He then said:

Chan Master Jieqing of Longyuan at Daochang Monastery in Huzhou Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuyang Zhao. He was a native of the Wang family of Changxi, Fuzhou, and received the full precepts.

Chan Master Zhuyuan Miaodao of Jianyan in Kunshan, Suzhou Prefecture, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuwang Hong of the twenty-second generation after Dajian.

In both instances, he became a dragon. [The monk] said, "One may truly say: 'When the dragon meets the water, his spirit increases; when the tiger encounters mountain terrain, its fierce majesty grows.
" The Master said, "In a place where no one is, I shall rub my forehead in expectation of you. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Nailing with nails and gluing with glue.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Ants do not eat iron. [The monk] asked, "If..."
“What is ‘the biased within the central’? The Master said, “The grass fills the Dharma Hall. “What is ‘the central within the biased’?
The Master said, “Moss seals the ancient hall. “What is ‘coming from the central’? The Master said, “A monkey wearing a ceremonial cap.
“What is ‘arriving at the simultaneous’? The Master said, “The sun rises and the moon sets. “What is ‘reaching the simultaneous’? The Master said:
He halted his carriage by cutting across the stream and said, "The Five Ranks of Ruler and Subject have received your instruction; how is it with the affairs beyond the Night-Bright Curtain?
The Master replied, "Failing to return home at dawn, one waits for the sun to rise at dusk. Ascending the hall, he said:

"If I speak of the Buddha-dharma to provide for the assembly, you will inevitably lose your hair and beard. If I speak of worldly dharmas to provide for the assembly, entering hell is as easy as turning over one's hand."
An arrow shot. Departing from these two paths, what exactly do you say? A three-inch tongue has no place to use;
a pair of empty hands cannot form a fist. Small Assembly (Xiaocan). A monk asked Lingyun, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Lingyun said, "Facing the execution block, planting a crabapple tree at the bottom of a well. The monk said, "I do not understand. Lingyun said, "Now..."
"The peaches and plums of this year are precious; one fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold. Dahui said, "This koan has gone from ancient times until now without anyone bringing it forth.
I, this mountain monk, will not begrudge my verbal karma and shall further annotate it for you all: 'At the edge of the chopping block, at the edge of the chopping block;
planting crabapples at the bottom of the well. This year the peaches and plums are precious; one fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold. The Master said, "Dahui..."
The assembly. As for Lingyun’s response, it is a monk’s dialogue. Now tell me:

is this the same as Linji’s three times asking about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma at Huangbo and receiving sixty blows of the staff each time, or is it different? If you say they are the same, there is no such thing as a commonality in the Dharma.
If you say they are different, how could the Buddha-dharma have two distinct forms? I always admire Dahui’s saying: "In my place, oysters..."
Heshan, open your mouth and you see the heart, liver, and five viscera; this very thing is it. Nevertheless, he was still just a dung-collector in the great capital city.
A small instruction: An ancient said, "During the ninety days of the summer retreat, the feet are restrained, yet the fish swim through the net."
In the third month of the summer retreat, birds enter their cages; when life and death are exhausted, silkworms form cocoons.
How can one penetrate these three layers? [He] strikes the meditation staff and says: "When the mountain is nearly nine fathoms high, one does not add even a single basketful of earth.
Kaiyuan entered the temple for a small-scale sermon (*xiao-can*). He raised the case of Xuefeng asking Deshan: "By what Dharma do all the sages of the past instruct people? Deshan—
He said: "In my school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to anyone.
Later, a monk asked Xuefeng, "When you saw Deshan, Master, what did you obtain that you then ceased [seeking]? Xuefeng replied, "At that time, I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed.
Wuzu commented: "Now, for those who have not yet penetrated this, let me tell you: two men came from the Eastern Capital."
The Master asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Suzhou. The Master then asked, "How are things in Suzhou?
He said, "Everything is as usual. "Even so," the Master said, "you cannot deceive this mountain monk. Why? It is simply because our dialects differ. But in the end, what is it like there?
"Suzhou pears and Shaobu lotus roots," he replied. The Master said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. [It is] one's own self."
Coming down the stream, they are no different from rubble; Old Dongshan relies on a mold to cast his bricks.

Little do they realize that these two great elders are precisely those whose hearts are wounded by overeating. Nevertheless, since you have come from the Eastern Capital, why do you speak the dialect of Suzhou?

Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Once, while eating sweetmeats during a winter night, Dongshan asked the Head Seat Tai, "There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth, black as lacquer;
it is always present within activity, yet it cannot be contained within activity. Where does its fault lie?
Tai replied, "Its fault lies in being within activity. Dongshan then called for his attendant to clear away the table of sweetmeats.
The Master said: "Regarding these words, throughout the various quarters today, whenever winter nights arrive, they are never failed to be brought up for commentary and explanation.
Yet, regarding the main text itself, not a single phrase has ever been spoken. Some say: 'Dongshan saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's handle;
why does he suppress and distort people? Others say: 'The Head Seat Tai [did not understand]...'"
He obtained some fruit to eat, yet for the time being, no one throughout the entire world may eat it; those who benefit people are few, while those who ruin them are many.
Little do they realize that Dongshan possesses the skillful means of "partiality and correctness" (*bianzheng huihu*) which avoids transgression.
Even if the Head Seat Tai had said, "It does not reside within active function," one still could not have eaten his fruit. After a long silence, he said: "Water."
Where do the flowing yellow leaves come from? A cow with a flock of crows passes through another village.

New Year’s Eve Small Assembly: Tonight, the year ends, the month ends, and the day ends. Worldly affairs drift on and on; when will they ever end? Tomorrow, the year is new, the month is new, and the day is new.

Amidst a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations, we see them renewed once more. Therefore it is said: "When exhausted, there is change; when changed, there is penetration. (The Master) hung [the robe].
With a hook spanning the four seas, one catches only the fierce dragon. As for the three thousand majestic deportments and eighty thousand subtle practices, you all certainly do not know them.

If you could achieve harmony between sound and resonance, each maintaining the ancestral fields and gardens, and knowing that rice is made from grain, you would avoid extinguishing our school at the hands of blind donkeys.
(He strikes the meditation staff. "From of old, no one has recognized the sweating horses; only..."
One must re-examine the merit that covers the ages. When Yongfu entered the monastery for a small-scale sermon (*xiao can*), he said:

"In the bustling marketplace of red dust, at the crossroads of the street, at the tips of the hundred grasses, and atop the solitary peak—if you deliberate upon this as 'Buddha-dharma,' you will enter hell like an arrow shot.
Only when the myriad functions have ceased and the thousand sages are no longer carried about, where sound precedes sound and form follows form—then one may examine it."

To point this out is precisely the delusion before a skull. Even if one were to smash the skull, strip away the brain-casing, kick over Mount Sumeru, and trample the great ocean—if one could discern the truth beneath one's heels even then, it would still be a matter of falling into the seventh or eighth stage.
Only those of universal penetration and extraordinary stature, who have established their own livelihood, will ultimately never abide within another’s nest.

To the assembly gathered here in this cave: I hope you will examine this well. This mountain monk has traveled two thousand li through mountains and rivers and across land and water to come here to join with you.

It is for no other purpose than to hold a small assembly (*xiao can*) at the reconstruction of the Hall of Rest on the Winter Solstice. Opening wide the doors and windows, we restore the scale of former days.
Who is it that stands before the hall? One who cuts off the tracks of both sages and ordinary people; even the blue-eyed barbarian monk [Bodhidharma] would be at a loss.
Tsk! Even Śākyamuni and Maitreya are still his slaves. The lanterns and the pillars knit their brows;
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra serve as his errand boys. It cannot be drawn and cannot be painted. When it falls, it is not something other than itself. A cluster of flowers, a cluster of brocade.
Transverse and vertical are not of the mundane world; seize it and go. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—tread upon them and they provoke anger.

The body of the Dharma King is fully revealed. From antiquity until now, those who speak of the mysterious and the wondrous, yet fail to distinguish between the monastic and the lay, are as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.
As for those who, whether engaging with principle or phenomena, possess a transformative and unconventional mastery—how many such people can there be? A clever man has no fixed dwelling place.
"Knowing such matters as these, one simply lets them rest. But tell me: what is the matter that is known? Cold comes and heat goes; when yin reaches its limit, yang is born.
The jade tree in the courtyard blooms early; it is even better than 'walking on water at East Mountain. He planted his staff and gave a shout.
Ascending the hall, he cited the Night Retreat of Yewang Monastery, which said: "Shaoshi has no gate or door; how can one attain it?"
“Pass through! It is late at night; stand with patience and listen to my words from east to west. The Master addressed the assembly: “There is the provisional, there is the real;
there is illumination, and there is function. Yet you must not understand it in such a way. Take care! This was the small *chan* (meditation) discourse for the eve of the year.
Of the three hundred and sixty days of the year, tonight is finally the end. As for all of you, regarding your own...

Regarding matters within one's own domain, one must also know that there is a time when the ultimate point is reached. If you have not yet reached that ultimate point, you must press forward with resolute discernment.
Have you not seen how, among the seventy-odd practitioners who attended Dàsuí as spiritual friends, only one or two truly possessed the great eye?
And what does it mean to possess the great eye? Wǔzǔ went to the sea to seek it out.
Dozens of venerable elders, upon arriving at the assembly of Fushan Yuanjian, found themselves truly unable to open their mouths.
Later, when they reached Baiyun, they bit through a single iron sour dumpling and only then attained the fullness of a hundred flavors. He then said:
"Flowers bloom on the cockscomb, charming in early autumn; who can dye its purple silk head? Sometimes the wind stirs and they lean against one another repeatedly, as if..."

They fought incessantly before the steps. He gave a shout and said: "If the cultivation of the mind does not reach the ground of no-mind, ten thousand kinds and a thousand variations will follow the flowing water.
Baoning entered the monastery for a small assembly (*xiao-can*). Sitting grandly upon the dais, he encompassed a hundred layers and a thousand folds.
With a single phrase fully raised, it spanned heaven and enclosed the earth. The Buddha-eye cannot see it; even the ocean-mouth is difficult to proclaim. Ancient and modern are not the same.

The path is unfathomable to both the ordinary and the sage. It has reached the point where the qilin manifests its auspiciousness, the phoenix arrives in its majestic form, the mountain colors present their blessings, and the smoke of human dwellings gathers in profusion.
Yet, alas, Master Baogong of the Liang dynasty missed the mark regarding Bodhidharma.

Although he was called the Great Being Avalokiteśvara who transmitted the Buddha’s mind-seal, in the end, he did not recognize this very message. Do you all still lack a sudden awakening? (He plants his staff.)
Zhàng said: "If you do not sleep on the same bed, how can you know when the lining of the quilt has worn through?
In a small-scale instruction (*xiao can*), he raised the example of Sīxīn showing the assembly: "A high-ranking traveler must reach the place where one person resides;
he must reach the place where half a person resides; he must personally reach the place where no person resides. The Master [concluded].

It is said: "Such talk is like black rock honey; it is sweet from edge to center. Nevertheless: "Were it not for the wild geese returning at night, how could one see the autumn at the mouth of the sea?
The Small Lecture on New Year’s Eve: "Tonight, as the year ends, how has it ever truly ended? Tomorrow, as the year begins, it does not actually come.
Thirty-six hundred breaths turn like a wheel; how many times have the tides gone out and returned? This is the turning of the pivot of the spiritual mechanism.
At the turning point, even a flash of lightning leaves one bewildered; when the Great Function manifests before one, who can discern its true mark?

Eradicating the dust of emotional attachments before they arise, one forgets the ultimate principle through verbal explanations. Everyone’s nostrils reach toward the heavens, each settling into their own home and finding joy in their work.
When Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra give rise to views of Buddha and Dharma, they are banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains. Even the lanterns and the pillars suddenly manifest the Golden [Egg].
Gangyanzi laughed heartily. "Three pounds of flax, a dry piece of dung.
If you all attempt to deliberate upon this as if it were the Buddha-dharma, you will enter hell as fast as a shot arrow. Here, words and thoughts are cut off; the sphere of mental activity ceases.
All things are leveled in a single state of evenness, merging into total extinction. At such a time, what is it like? After a long silence, he said: "Last night, the east wind has melted away..."
Remnants of snow; withered tree branches are blooming once more. Regarding the small *śamaya* (summer retreat) *praśna*: tomorrow the summer retreat begins and you will arrive.
If you simply spend your days in idle indolence, by the time the drum is beaten and you ascend the hall, you will truly be unable to find a way out of your thoughts.
When all of you crowd together and come forward, you cannot help but mistake south for north. Before the Seven Buddhas, there was never such a thing as this news.

Since the time of the Seven Buddhas, although there have been such reports of this message, none were ultimately able to fully awaken to the unsurpassed Bodhi of the Tathāgata, nor were they able to enter the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment (*pariniṣpanna-bodhi*) to dwell peacefully in body and mind within the Wisdom of Equality (*samatājñāna*).

Consequently, for ninety days, these people concerned themselves solely with their mouths and bodies rather than with spiritual cultivation; turning their backs on awakening and joining with the dust of the senses, they merely wasted their time in vain.
Regarding "The Years and Months," the Fifth Patriarch said: "Master Bodhidharma came with his feet following their own path and spoke with his mouth following its own flow.
Later generations, however, turned this into mere calculation. Through such calculations, they imagine that heaven becomes clear and earth becomes peaceful.
Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nose of Śakra, the Lord of Devas; a carp from the Eastern Sea receives a blow, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. (Chu)
"A rooster is not a phoenix from Mount Dan; it loves to cry out atop the wutong tree. He once gave this instruction: "There is still more beyond this.
To reveal the lion’s claws and fangs, there is a further deliberation within; yet one cannot avoid brandishing a sword at the gate.
As for this sharp, spiritual blade—dare anyone even attempt to gauge it? The Master’s verbal prowess was steep and soaring, his discernment and insight were extraordinary. He responded...
After [the master] An, this teacher was perhaps the foremost person. He once compiled the *Zongmen Tongyao* (Essentials of the Lineage School). He passed away at Baoning Monastery.
Chan Master Tianyi Dujiang Jue'en of Shaoxing Prefecture was the son of the Gu family of Cixi.

He received the tonsure under Yunmen Guangxiao and followed Ming at Yanqing Monastery, where he studied the *Sijiaoyi* (Ceremonial for the Four Teachings). Within seven days, he was able to master it; Ming marveled at his extraordinary talent.

He went to visit Yuwang and Henxuan, with whom he attained karmic resonance within their chambers and received their seal of approval. His virtue and deeds became manifest day by day, such that at one time all the worthy scholars and gentlemen delighted in associating with him.
He took up residence at T'ien-p'ing in Su-chou, later moving to K'ai-yüan, then to Pao-fu in Ming-chou, and finally to T'ien-i in Yüeh-chou.
One day, while the assembly was standing in attendance within his chamber, he suddenly leaned on his staff and spoke.
He said, "This old monk leans against his staff amidst the hollows; he clearly depicts Subhūti. Looking left and right, he asked, "Do you understand?
After a long silence, he cast down his staff, leaned back against his meditation cushion, and passed away.
Chan Master Dongyu Dehai of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jingci Gong. He was a native of the Chen family in Linhai, Taizhou.
At the age of fourteen, he left home to become a monk under the Sichuanese monk Anshi. He went to visit Chan Master Gong at Shilin in Chengtian Monastery. Shilin asked, "What is..."
"You yourself! The Master hesitated. Lin pushed him out. The Master harbored doubts. One day, while entering the room for instruction, Lin asked, "The entire earth is the true body of the Vajra;
where would you place yourself, Upādhyāya? The Master was about to respond when Lin struck him. From that moment, he attained thorough realization.
When Lin moved to Jingci Temple, he appointed the Master to serve as his attendant. One day, in the room, Lin raised the story of the National Teacher calling his attendant three times.
[The Master] said, "It is not that you have lost the cat; it is certainly that you have lost the dog. Lin asked, "Is this betraying me, or is it not betraying me?
The Master said, "Deceiving others while deceiving yourself. Lin struck him with his bamboo staff and said, "He who will carry on our lineage is Hai.
In the Gengyin year of the Zhiyuan era, he took up residence at Hanyan on Mount Tiantai. In the Yisi year of the Dade era, he moved...
At Hanshan in Gusu, during the Jida cycle year of Jiyou (1309), he moved again to Dongchan in Kunshan. In the Xinhai year (1311), he was granted a gold-embroidered dharma robe by imperial decree.
In the Gui-chou year of Huangqing (1313), he moved once more to Zhongzhu. In the Yimao year of Yanyou (1315), an edict appointed him as the abbot of Jingci.
Upon reaching the mountain gate, he said: "The Pure Gate of Compassion; a single lake of autumn water. To enter or not to enter—tigers bite tigers, snakes [bite snakes]."
[He] swallowed the turtle’s nose. In his room, he gave a "hanging word," saying: "One holds a sharp sword in hand; why does the monkey not die?
One bites through the iron sour paste; why are there hungry people on the road? Fish take water as their life; why do they die within the water?
None of those present could answer in accord with the truth. He once composed a verse on the occasion of Guizong’s raising of a finger, which says: "Profoundly deep..."

It is bottomless; towering high, it is beyond reach. The more one contemplates it, the further away it becomes; the more one seeks it, the more difficult it is to find. In the year Yichou of the Taiding era, he moved again to Lingyin Monastery.
In the ninth month of Dingmao, he manifested a slight illness. Having summoned his disciples and finished his final instructions, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.

His secular age was seventy-two, and his monastic seniority was fifty-eight. The Emperor had previously bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Mingzong Huiren. [This concludes the record of] the stupa.
At the foot of the mountain behind King Aśoka’s Stūpa, there was the Chan Master Tianning Zhuyun Jingtan of Jiaxing Prefecture, a native of the Yan clan of Putian. He had long relied upon Shilin.
Later, he resided at Zhiping in Wuyi, Beichen in Suzhou, and Tianning in Huzhou. Upon ascending the hall, he said:
"The golden crow rises in the east; the jade hare sinks in the west. Clever monks search here and there. Suddenly, they smash through the void;
eons of time are but this very moment. He struck his staff and descended from the seat. A monk asked: "The Three Worthies have not yet attained it; the Ten Sages find it difficult..."
“I understand. What is the essence of this school? The Master said, “A holeless flute and felt clappers.
He asked, “Who is it that knows this? The Master said, “How could a deaf person hear it? He said, “I know that the Master is accustomed to such a device. The Master said, “A hawk flies over Silla.
He asked, “What is the mind of nirvana? The Master said, “Mount Sumeru. He asked, “What is the mind of deviation? The Master said, “The same as before.”
A separate verse of wisdom. The Master said: "The four great oceans.
In Suzhou Prefecture, Chan Master Shouyong of East Mountain at Tiger Hill sent a monk away with this verse: "Movement and stillness are nothing other than the one Great Chan;
Why need one further penetrate that which existed before birth? The ancestral garden is a thousand miles away, yet now you return; On land, there is the path of your journey."
There is a boat upon the water. [The Master] cites the story of Zhang Yuezhai’s entry into the Way. The verse says: A single strike of the bell penetrates the faculty of hearing;
The ocean of three thousand worlds is simultaneously darkened. The thief departs from the side of the bare flesh-ball; Tomorrow, it remains as before, never leaving the gate.
Chan Master Xianji Yun of Tiger Hill in Suzhou, a successor of Chan Master Yu of Mount Jing, had long relied upon Master Xutang at Mount Jing.
While serving as the First Seat, one day Baoye Yuan requested instruction from Xutang regarding the final words of Deshan, saying: "If one says they exist..."
How could Deshan not have understood? Yet, if one were to say he did not understand, Yantou further remarked that Deshan had not yet realized it.
[Xuedou] requests the Master’s compassionate instruction. The Hall Master said, "I do not understand; you should go ask the Head Seat.

Yuan went to the Master, who happened to be returning from a mountain excursion. He called for water to wash his feet; Yuan hurriedly brought the water forward and then threw himself down to massage the Master’s limbs. Because of this—
He brought up the previous conversation to question him. The Master then scooped up some water and splashed it on him, saying, "What is that final phrase?
Yuan did not understand and went back up to see the Hall Master. The Hall Master asked, "How did the Head Seat explain it to you? Yuan recounted the previous conversation.
The Hall Master said, "Na-na! I tell you, he has realized it. Thereupon, Yuan was relieved and understood the meaning.

He then cited the karmic connection concerning Xinghua’s response to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang regarding the price of the treasure of the Central Plains, and offered this verse: "The King’s treasure is naturally difficult to price;
How could Xinghua ever dare to borrow it for inspection? Since heaven and earth have no partiality in their covering and bearing, To this day it remains preserved as a stabilizing force."
Zhongyuan. Lu Xun asked Nanquan, "In my home, there is a large stone that has served as both a seat and a bed.
May I have it carved into a Buddha? Nanquan said, "Yes. Xun said, "Is it not also possible that one may not?
Nanquan said, "It depends on the conditions. Verse: Sitting and reclining through many springs, Half covered in moss, half shrouded in clouds. No...
Seamless and without joints, it is difficult to grasp; one holds their very liver and entrails and speaks them to others.
Chan Master Baoye Miaoyuan of Dingshui in Shaoxing Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Mount Xiangshan. He received full ordination and traveled to observe various masters.
When he encountered monks who pursued external things and neglected the Way, anxiety appeared on his face. Xu Tang refused to let him descend from the hall;

Qian, becoming enraged, imprisoned him to humiliate him. The Master served him with the utmost reverence; whenever he had doubts, he would immediately ask for clarification, and as soon as he asked, they were resolved.
After a long time, he attained a state of vast clarity. One day, Xu Tang said, "Yuan, you have now reached the Great Peace. When Tang passed away...

He took charge of Mount Jing and appointed the Master to lead the assembly. Later, he went forth to preside over Jianyan in Pingjiang, then moved to Shuilu at Quanzhou, and subsequently transferred to Dingshui.
There, he recounted the story of the World-Honored One and the Five-Supernatural-Power Immortal, composing a verse which said: "As for that one supernatural power—ask me!"
"The mouth is the gate of calamity. Causes invite their corresponding fruits. The Great Dharma King of Shame and Compassion. "The *bing*, *ding*, *li*, and *ren* trigrams do not belong to Fire.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Zhang Chu visiting Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Scholar, what is your noble surname? He replied, "My surname is Zhang and my name is Chu.
Shishuang said, "In this place, even cleverness cannot be found; from where have you come? At these words, Zhang Chu attained great realization.
A discourse on awakening. The verse says: Advancing forward, there is a precipice three thousand *zhang* high; Retreating backward, there are cliffs ten thousand *chong* deep.
Take heed, Old Man Zhang [Shi*chu] of Tiantang! The seamless iron hammer dances in the spring breeze. Later he resided at Yunjing. He passed away in the *Xinsi* year of the Zhizhi era (1341).
His stupa was enshrined at Yunjing. He was seventy-five years of age at his death.
Chan Master Nan-sou Mao, a successor of Chan Master Yue of Mount Jing-shan, cited the story of the ferrywoman at Yan-tou who threw her child overboard. He offered this verse:
"The impoverished ghost-child by the ferry at E-zhu, His entire capacity was mistaken at the moment he struck the boat’s side. How much better it would have been to offer another turn of phrase!"
The Discourse: Saving the Seventh Son of Baba. Citing the story of Jia Shan’s meeting with Chuanzi, he offers this verse:
"Formless and flawless, he immediately turned his spear back; It was all because he lightly trusted the Zen monk Zhi.
Had he not reached the banks of Huating, Even an iron boat-paddle could have done nothing for you. Citing the story of Layman Pang falling while crossing a bridge and being supported by Lingxiao.
The Verse says: Filial piety is a treasury; disobedience is a blemish before others that cannot be concealed. Those who are one's close kin in this life were enemies in past lives.
Dharma Successor of Chan Master Dushou of Jing Mountain.
Chan Master Jingfu of Huya Rock at Mount Jingshan in Hangzhou Prefecture was a native of Huai’an.

During the Zhizheng era of the Yuan dynasty, he was summoned to the imperial presence and presented a verse to the Emperor. Its summary reads: “All Tathāgatas of the past dwell securely within the secret treasury;

all Buddhas of the present in the ten directions have realized the Way and turned the wheel of Dharma; all sentient beings are the World-Honored Ones of the future—this is due to deluded conceptualization.”
Attached to views, bound by fetters, afflictions, hindrances, and entanglements, they wander in delusion through the bodies of the six realms and suffer the miseries of the three miserable paths.
They think only of the Buddhas of the past and present, yet fail to revere the Honored Ones of the future; thus they harbor enmity toward the Buddhas.

Some even cook, slaughter, and kill, failing to realize that the characteristics of sentient beings are entirely the body of *dharmatā*. In the past, there was the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging, who prostrated to all and said: "I do not..."

"I slight you; you shall all become Buddhas. If you can keep in mind that both yourself and others are equally future Buddhas, your blessings and lifespan will increase in this life, and in birth after birth, you shall be born in the Buddha-lands.
Upon hearing this, Emperor Shenzong was greatly delighted and asked the Master, "Has there ever been a sovereign from above who observed the precept against killing?
The Master replied, "One day, Emperor Renzong of the Song dynasty said to his ministers: 'Last night I was very hungry and thought of roasting a wildcat.'"

The sheep were spared; out of concern for future generations, this was subsequently established as a permanent custom. Rather than endure a temporary hunger, he could not bear to initiate an endless slaughter.
The ministers all cried out "Ten-thousand-year Reign! The Emperor praised and accepted his advice, immediately receiving the precepts from the Imperial Preceptor.
Chan Master Tiantong Zhuxi Tan of Ningbo Prefecture asked a monk, "From where have you come? The monk replied, "Jinge (Golden Goose).
The Master asked, "How high is Jinge Mountain? The monk said, "Its summit cannot be seen. The Master rebuked him. One day, he ascended the seat.
Regarding the public case of the World-Honored One holding up a flower:
the monk attained realization upon hearing these words. *Xùdēng zhèngtǒng*, Scroll Twenty-Two;
*Xùdēng zhèngtǒng*, Scroll Twenty-Three.
Compiled by the Chan monk Xingtong of Western Sichuan, a successor to the Patriarchs at Potalaka in the South Sea,
of the twenty-second generation under Dajian of the Linji School.
Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanmiao of West Tianmu Mountain in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Yangshan Qin. He was the son of Xu of Wujiang.

His mother dreamed that a monk boarded her boat to stay the night and she subsequently conceived. As soon as he left his swaddling clothes, he delighted in sitting in the lotus posture. At the age of fifteen, he entered the monastery at Jia...
He entered the monastic order at Hemin Temple. At sixteen, he shaved his head; at seventeen, he received full ordination.

At twenty-two, he first visited Duanqiao Lun. Lun instructed him to investigate the saying: "From where does life come? To where does death go? Thereupon, he did not let his side touch the mat [even for a moment].
Having forgotten both mouth and body, Xueyan went to visit the Master at Beijian carrying incense. As soon as he offered his greetings, he was struck out and the door was closed in his face.

On the fifteenth day of the first month in the second year of the Dade era (the *guimao* year), he passed away. He was sixty-four years of age and had twenty-six years of seniority as a monk.
