The monk asked, "The meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West has been pointed out by you, Master; what is the matter of its transmission here in the Eastern Land? The Master said, "The green pines atop the ridge remain magnificent for a thousand ages."
The flowing water by the mountain stream is pure for ten thousand years. [The student] asked: "What is the realm of White Water? The Master said:
"A single expanse of fallow fields stretches across the four wilds; three thatched huts stand grandly amidst the mountains. [The student] asked: "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said:
"Beside the head of the White Tiger is the Temple of the Son of Heaven; at the Black Dragon Pond is the foundation of the Sovereign King.

If one asks, 'What is it like when both the human realm and the environment are forgotten? the Master said: 'Su Wu did not know the intention of the green ram; the Seventh Lord always lamented the white crow’s return.
The monk bowed, and the Master struck the table once."
Chan Master Dahuì Juéhuá of Chongfú Temple in Jāngníng Prefecture was the son of the Liu family from Wéiyáng. Initially, he attained a realization upon meeting Hǎizhōu;
subsequently, he studied under Bǎoyuè at Fánchāng and received formal certification. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said:
Beyond the limit of majestic sound, it is simply this very thing. Even now, right before one’s eyes, it is also simply this very thing.
If you call it a whisk, you blind the eyes of humans and devas; if you do not call it a whisk, you likewise blind the eyes of humans and devas.
"Great assembly, ultimately what is this called? If you can see it directly, then you will know that Kāśyapa’s smile was the receiving of the Tathāgata’s transmission of the lamp;
and that the Second Patriarch’s search for his mind was fit to continue the orthodox pulse of the ancestral lineage.
[He] suddenly held up his whisk and said, "Do you see it? After a long silence, he said, "Not even a thousand sages can recognize it. He struck the whisk and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Deshan Cuifeng of Mount Funiu in Henan Prefecture was a native of the Xia region in Guanzhong. From childhood, he was simple and unadorned.
At the age of thirty, he first left the household life and became a disciple of Hai of Niu’ou in Yunnan. After Hai passed away, the Master began his travels to visit various teachers.
Yet that "obstructing lump" in his chest remained painfully unresolved. Consequently, he followed Gufeng to attend upon Baoyuetan.

Baoyue said, "Your heart is indeed far-reaching, yet you lack one final, thorough penetration to the very marrow. Once you have passed through this and come back to life from death, then when you speak and breathe before others, you will finally find your footing.
Otherwise, there will be no connection at all. Upon hearing this, the Master entered [the path].
He practiced austerities at Mount Funiu for six years before finally attaining great enlightenment. This incense offering for his emergence into the world was presented on behalf of Master Tan.
Later, while staying at Jixiang Monastery in the capital, the assembly grew so large that the imperial court became enraged by slanderous reports.
The Master relinquished the community and returned to Mount Funiu, where the congregation flourished even more. He preached the Dharma for thirty years. One day, he said to the assembly: "Return."
"Come back! Come back! I am a man of the north; my wish is to return to the place where my ancestors first settled.

He then returned to the capital and resided at Juyeon-sa. Not long after, he passed away at the age of eighty-one. His disciples enshrined his entire body and buried it behind the general cemetery of the temple.

There is a eulogy for the portrait of the Master which says: "When there is wind, there is clarity; when there is moonlight, there is brightness. How admirable is Chwaeong! Like jade, he vibrates; like metal, he rings."

Zen Master Dufeng Jishan of Tiantong in Hangzhou Prefecture was a successor of Zen Master Cheng of Daokang. He was the son of the Wu family of Fengyang and was born while his father was serving as an official in Leiyang, Guangdong.
At the age of seventeen, he left the household life. Initially, he met Yuanming, who instructed him with the "Mu" (無) koan.
The Master was immediately able to understand this. He brought up the case of Chen Ming. Ming said, "For twenty years I have been contemplating the word 'Mu,' like a mosquito on an iron ox.
As soon as you began to practice the work, you already possessed so many intellectual views. He spoke again:
"I observe that although your faculties differ from mine, you must by no means be deceived by others into becoming an elder; this would mislead you regarding your great matter.

Having received these instructions, the Master vowed that for the rest of his life he would take awakening as his goal. In the *Renxu* year of the *Zhengtong* era, he entered Sichuan to study under Wuji.

When Wuji was summoned to the capital, the Master subsequently closed his retreat chamber. Within the chamber, he did not provide bedding, but placed only a small stool. Whenever he felt weary or heavy...

He left his seat. One day, upon hearing the sound of a bell, he attained realization and spoke this verse: Profoundly still and silent, utterly free from action; Touched upon, it roars like thunder without cause.
With one sound that shakes the earth, all news and traces vanish; The skull shatters and the dream returns.
At that time, it happened that [his teacher] had passed away, so he followed Yuexi. Yuexi said, "The Buddha-dharma is not fresh fish; one fears it will rot.
Day after day, Yuexi struck east and west, secretly setting up examinations. One day, while attending Yuexi as they sat together in the garden, [Dayuan] spoke.
Xixi asked, "What *huatou* have you been contemplating lately? The Master replied, "The word 'Mu' (No). Xixi asked, "What is 'Mu'?
The Master said, "Looking at it now, it is like the Diamond King’s Precious Sword. Xixi asked, "What is the Diamond King’s Precious Sword?
The Master said, "Its cold radiance blazes forth, illuminating the past and soaring through the present. Xixi said, "Give me back the sword!"
The Master said, "If you intend to move, you will strike against his sharp edge. Xixi asked, "What about when one stands with the sword held crosswise before the hall?
The Master said, "I would kill even a Buddha; I would kill even a Patriarch. Xixi said, "What about when this old monk comes? The Master said, "I will not spare him either."
Xixi asked, "What is it like after killing? The Master said, "For now, let us rejoice that all under heaven is at peace. Xixi asked, "Ultimately, what is the meaning of the word 'wu'?
The Master said, "The stolen goods are clearly identified. Xixi said, "Setting aside the thief for a moment, give me back my stolen goods."
The Master said, "Six times six is thirty-six. Xuefeng said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master said, "The night is short and sleep is insufficient;
the day is long and hunger is more than enough. Xuefeng said, "When an ox passes through a window frame, its head, horns, and four hooves have all passed through;
why is it that the tail cannot pass? The Master said, "There is not a single dharma to confront the mind; in a flash, one's entire being is revealed in the open field. Xuefeng...
[The Master] asked, "Where do you currently establish yourself and find your livelihood? The teacher replied, "Where would it not be fitting to be honored?

Later, he took his leave of Master Xi and traveled to Zhejiang, where he shut himself in retreat at Wanfeng Hermitage on Mount Tianmu. Master Yuexi also received an imperial decree granting him permission to return to Daga in Jinling.
He sent a letter summoning the teacher to confer his final instructions. At that time, the teacher was away on business; as Yuexi approached the end of his life, he issued the command.
He presented him with a robe and a whisk. The Master resided on the mountain for over forty years.
During the Tianfeng era, he constructed the Three Pagodas at West Lake, as well as the Chaoming Temple at Mount Tiantu, the Baolian Temple at Mount Wushan, and the Ganglu Temple at South Mountain.
At the beginning of the Chenghua era, he closed his quarters at Shiwu. Later, he resided at Zhentian on Mount Ciyun. A monk asked: "What is the Master?"

Regarding the family style [of our lineage], the Master said: "The tide is swift in the river ahead, so the fish find it difficult to move; the peaks are high on the ridge behind, so the birds find it hard to perch.
A monk requested further instruction, saying: "Master Gaoping said: 'The mud ox beneath the sea bites the moon as it runs; the stone tiger before the cliff cradles its cubs as it sleeps.'"
An iron snake drills into the diamond eye; Kunlun rides an elephant while a heron leads it.
Within these four lines, there is one line that can kill and can bring to life, can let go and can seize. If a person can discern which it is, their lifelong study of the Way will be complete.
“I do not yet know which one it is,” [the student] said. The Master replied, “Wait until you have attained awakening, and I shall tell you. [The student] said, “I do not understand. The Master—
He said: "I do not see the Way. You have a staff; I give you a staff. You have no staff;
I take it away from you. To the assembly: "The precious sword is fully brandished in daily life; with high swings and broad sweeps, one is willing to be at ease.
When withdrawn, souls and gallbladders lose their courage before the wind; when extended, skulls lie scattered across the ground. Ten thousand deaths."
He utterly disregards the myriad living beings; with a single spear and a single horse, he achieves his purpose. Zhaozhou’s very life-force is clearly revealed here:
though blood-stained blades pierce the heavens, their edges remain hidden. With his whisk, he makes a sweeping gesture and says: "The void is vast and transparent, without a trace of news."
Ten thousand li of cloudless sky, the Milky Way azure; pressed so hard that Mount Sumeru enters a lotus fiber. Maitreya and Śākyamuni both cry out in protest:

"Riding an iron horse backward, chasing the western wind; startling the clay ox to emerge from the sea. O virtuous ones, if you understand this as something extraordinary, you betray your own spiritual nature;
if you do not understand it as something extraordinary, you are like one clutching stolen goods while crying out for injustice. But how will you proceed?
He understood it. After a long silence, he said: "To store the entire world within the world—only then does one see the horned sheep hanging from the treetops.
In the *Ren-yin* year of the *Chenghua* era, he passed away at Tianzhen; his stupa was built on the mountain where he resided.
Chan Master Pujie Guyue Jingcheng of Mount Wutai in Taiyuan Prefecture was the son of the Zhang family of Xihe.
He first studied under Yuexi, who instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (No) koan of Zhaozhou. After three days, he attained realization, which surprised Yuexi.
He subsequently entered Sichuan, where he lived in seclusion on Mount Feixue for three years. One day, after setting out to prepare a meal, he returned to find that the rice had already turned moldy.

Because he had sat on the ground for a long time, his feet were afflicted by cold and dampness, and he was unable to rise. Someone carried him to the rear mountains where he rested; only then did he recover.
One day, while sitting on a wooden platform, he heard the sound of firecrackers and attained a sudden, great awakening.

From that moment on, throughout all times, his realization was transparently brilliant and wondrous. He went to visit Guangfu to present what he had attained. Guangfu asked, "A person who has died a great death must come back to life."
"What is it like at such a time? The Master said, "The eyebrows span across the eyes; the nostrils are large and the head hangs down.

[The student] said, "When the great earth has sunk flat and empty space has been pulverized, where do you establish yourself and find your life? The Master said, "The clouds vanish and the mountain crags are revealed."
The sun rose over the sea, and the heavens were clear. In the fourth year of the Mingshun era, the Dingchou year, he returned to Qingliang.

The local ruler invited him to the inner palace to inquire about the Way and honored him with great respect. By imperial decree, a temple was established in Huayan Valley, titled Pujie, and the Master was appointed as its abbot.
There is a verse on dwelling in the mountains that says: Content with poverty beneath the forest trees, my thoughts wander at ease; On my bamboo couch, I sleep soundly with a stone for a pillow.
My life beyond the ordinary is sufficient as it is; It is all because there is nothing sought within my breast. I dwell by the side of red cliffs and green waters.

Utterly devoid of honor or disgrace, of leisure or busyness; this old monk does not understand the principle of returning to the source. Let the mountains remain green and the leaves turn yellow as they will.
He passed away while seated at his home mountain.
The Dharma-transmission verse of Chan Master Ning Yifeng of Dagang in Jiangning Prefecture says: "From patriarch to patriarch, there is no dharma to transmit;
Each person possesses it inherently from the beginning. You have realized the dharma that is not bestowed; In every dharma, there is neither before nor after."
Chan Master Lintian Fuzhan of Zhi Lin Monastery in Pengxi, Tongchuan Prefecture, entered the Way through diligent toil and received a prediction from Yuexi.

When he opened his hall to propagate the teachings, he became a great refuge for Chan students throughout Chu and Shu. At the age of seventy-seven, at the time of his passing, there was a verse that read:
"Riding an iron horse backward, roaring into the western wind; bright moon and clear breeze are one and the same. This was his parting word.
This is a verse from the *Shi* (Worldly). There exists a work titled *Tianyuan Lu* (Record of the Celestial Abyss) in two fascicles that is currently in circulation.
*Xudeng Zhengtong*, Fascicle 28; *Xudeng Zhengtong*, Fascicle 29.
Compiled by the Chan monk Xingtong of Western Sichuan, a successor to the Patriarchs at Potalaka in the South Sea,
of the Linji lineage under the twenty-eighth generation of Dajian.
Chan Master Baowen Hongyin of Tangcheng was a successor of Chan Master Ruixian of Xichan.
He was the son of the Zhang family of Tangcheng in Guyu. He paid his respects to Xuefeng and underwent a period of training for many years;
however, because Xuefeng had passed away, he had not yet received formal certification (inka). He traveled far to consult Chushan, arriving just as King Ding was passing away. Three...

Upon the completion of the *tan* mourning period, Master Shan was invited to ascend the seat. The Master stepped forward and asked: "The thunderous voice shakes the earth; the field for selecting Buddhas has opened.

The assembly at Vulture Peak remains solemnly as if it had not yet dispersed. I wonder, how may the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace be repaid? Shan replied: "The vast imperial wind purifies the six realms;
the brilliant Buddha-sun illuminates the three thousand worlds. The Master said: "I have heard the words of praise and blessing from the Master."
The Master said, "The meaning! What was the intent behind the flower and the smile? Shanshan said, "Before such a prompt, words find no place for the tongue;
only the *dhūta*’s single smile is permitted to be passed down. The Master said, "The jade plum pierces through the snow; the crimson leaves wither in the frost.

It is precisely the anniversary of the imperial house’s removal of mourning, yet it is also the day the Imperial Chariot departed on its celestial journey. I wonder where the golden countenance of the late Sovereign now resides?"

The Mountain Master held up his whisk and said, "Upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk, one attains perfect enlightenment, emits great radiance, and turns the wheel of Dharma together with the Tathāgata.
Do you see it? The Master said, "If so, then the entire world is free from concealment.
The Mountain Master said, "Yet, even with eyes, there is nothing to be seen. The Master said, "Precisely at that place where nothing is seen, there is no separation."
“Even a hair’s breadth,” Shanshan said. “That is not yet wondrous. The Master asked, “I wonder, what then is wondrous?
Shanshan said, “When both extremes have been wiped away, only then does one see the person prior to the kalpas. The Master said, “Thanks to you, Master, my adamantine eye has been pointed out;

from death to rebirth, I shall no longer doubt. Shanshan said, “Excellent, this monk! A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net; your words manifest the fundamental principle—you do not disgrace the West.”

As a successor of the Chan lineage, you must further maintain this realization; by no means deceive yourself. The Master said, "Heaven and humans bear witness; I thank the Master for his seal of approval.

Xingkong Wujie heard that the Venerable Master once composed a song on the Manifestation of the School (*Xianzong ge*), which says: "To realize this school, there is neither past nor present; it presses..."

Breaking through empty space, one repairs it oneself; amidst the heap of sounds and forms lies the field of wondrous enlightenment. Sending forth and withdrawing without obstruction—wondrous within the essence!
At midnight, a wooden man gazes into a mirror; the Persian on the southern bank chews cold ice.
Amidst function, there is mystery: a stone woman blows a flute atop a green tree; Zhaozhou’s gourd hangs from the east.
The Wall. Within the village, the King grows old; at night he burns paper money. The most profound within the profound, the most wondrous within the wondrous.

Amidst a jeweled net, bright pearls contend. One must pierce a single aperture within the darkness. The Sound of the Ocean Tide speaks with fervent intensity. A lute made of lion sinew plays the "White Snow" melody.

The green mountains on both banks smile and nod their heads. This ancient tune of a hundred years is turned into something new. (This was heard from Tiansi; it was mistakenly listed here [by Touzi Qi]).
Chan Master Xiantong Dawei Jinglun of Mount Wutai in Taiyuan Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Gudeng Huijing. He was the son of the Kang family from Yunnan.
He was born in the Dingwei year of the Xuande era. During the Zhengtong era, he received the tonsure under Master Tai of Wuji. When Gudeng resided at Fushan, the Master...
He went to call upon him, and within the room their spiritual resonance was established. Later, while residing at Xiantong, he ascended the hall and said:
"A holeless iron hammer is hurled right at your face; a black-lacquered Kunlun sits blocking the path. Is there anyone who can strike through it and grasp it?
Come forth and speak! A monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Tai? The Master said, "It is neither sunny weather nor raining."
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "Ten thousand bodhisattvas within the Vajra Cave.
[The monk] asked, "I do not know what Dharma you usually preach. The Master said, "A clear breeze blows through the secluded pines; the closer one listens, the better the sound.
[The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "This year the rains are timely; the farmers' spring wheat will flourish. [The monk] asked.
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Wait until the Immortal Mountain has turned its body, and I shall tell you.
He then continued: "To take arsenic and treat it as clarified butter—has such ever occurred? To scatter pearls like shards of tile—who would not do so?
To climb a tree with eyes wide open is to needlessly lose one's entire body; to dream of ascending to Tuṣita Heaven is merely to expose one's family disgrace."

Without stirring a thought, he transformed the demonesses entirely into vessels for the jewel of Bodhi; without exerting physical effort, he pointed to the Sahā world and made it the Pure Land of Abhirati.
The deep waters of Changshui recede as mountains accumulate, while the ice of Langye Jue melts away.
With a step of faith, he trampled the lapis lazuli pit; casually, he smashed the coral branches.

Entering the hall, San-sheng let out a thunderous shout, scattering sand within the Eye of the True Dharma. Nan-ch’uan brandished his white blade aloft, sweeping away the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas.
Why bother with the probing pole? It is not in the hands of others. From south of Hsiang to north of Tan, the model of the pagoda is held in its entirety.
Come! Spring returns upon branches that have never sprouted; a single snowflake flies amidst a mass of fierce flames.
Possessing such a strategy, one may truly be called a man of realization. In whose well-bottom is there no sky? Everywhere within the waves, there is the moon. Entering the hall, he said:

"The three greatnesses—essence, characteristic, and function—are simultaneously manifested; every particle of dust is encompassed. The five cycles of cause, effect, and wisdom are suddenly realized; all phenomena are perfectly interfused."
A hundred cities of misty waters do not exceed a single hair’s breadth; ten millennia of past and present do not shift one’s immediate thought.

When the red lotus blooms, one smells the fragrance of the water; touching it, one strikes the half-nose of a tiny gnat. Where the green mountains seem low, one sees the vastness of the sky; unfolding it, one reveals the single filament-brow of a gaunt mosquito.
A hundred rivers compete to flow, yet the substance of water does not move; ten thousand apertures cry out together, yet wind is fundamentally...
Self-quiescence. The golden lion need not laboriously crouch upon the ground; the water-buffalo accepts its share as it happens. A single movement fills the eyes;

the home-mountain remains as ever, under the blue sky and bright sun. Addressing the assembly on the Winter Solstice: The five peaks are heaped with jade and snow; the thousand pines have branches of pearl and jade.
All the springs, rocks, mists, and clouds of Mount Tai, the soaring pavilions and surging halls—these are all but a single hair of Mañjuśrī.
The true light of the eye of wisdom—this is you all, who constantly dwell within it while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.
Do you still realize that you have never once touched so much as a single hair on its brow?

If you can see it in this way, then you will gather the great trichiliocosm into the tip of a hair and expand the sands of Ganges into the Dharma-realm. If this is not yet so, take care not to seek answers here and there.
I cast lots for you all and report this in truth: this morning is the winter solstice, and the first yang has arisen. Take care. [He] addressed the assembly:
"Mountains high and seas vast; the moon bright and the wind clear; pines verdant and rocks weathered; summer heat and winter cold—all these are distinct and vivid, each appearing clearly before us.
But tell me, within the sphere of a patch-robed monk, what can be accomplished?"
"Is there anyone who has attained the Way? Come forward and speak! If there is no one, I, the old monk, shall speak for myself.
He took up his staff and descended from the seat. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Master Yuanzuo said, 'There is a most extraordinary matter to relate to you all.
If I try to explain it, I am hindered by the very act of explaining; if I do not explain it, I am hindered by the very act of not explaining. How great indeed was Master Yuanzuo!"
"It is much like the mythical tortoise dragging its tail; once a word has fallen upon people's ears, how can it be hidden? I, this old monk, also have a most extraordinary kōan.
I shall present it straightforwardly to the Great Assembly, so that those who merely lean against the door or hang by the eaves may each stand as firm as a cliff rising ten thousand fathoms.
He then descended from his seat and addressed the assembly: "In my place, I do not speak of the East..."
Village Elder Li Dala is too frugal; he does not speak of West Village Wang Er’s sister being too extravagant.
He knows nothing of calling a horned animal a rabbit, nor of adding legs to a snake or painting a dragon. At dawn there is a bowl of white congee; in the afternoon, a cup of clear tea.
Who cares for his old, rotten vines that bloom out of season? With hands outstretched, he says: "You all..."
"O people! What dry wood chips do you seek by coming here? He sang this while dwelling in the mountains: "In my unoccupied mountain cottage, the door remains shut;
On the earthen steps, spring rains have grown green moss. I thought this heart was known to no one— Then a solitary bird’s cry came from somewhere.
Later, he passed away at his native mountain.

Chan Master Wuliang Cang of Baiyun, a successor of Chan Master Zhen of Foji, addressed the assembly at Chuzhou Prefecture: "During the two periods of six hours each day, follow the *huatou* while walking;
follow the *huatou* while standing; follow the *huatou* while sitting; follow the *huatou* while lying down. Let your mind be like a grain of *liliji* (a thorny seed)."
It is like a tuft of wild grass. It cannot be swallowed up by any personhood, ignorance, the five desires, or the three poisons.
Whether acting or remaining still, one’s entire body is a single mass of doubt. Doubting and doubting until the end, one remains dully and steadfastly throughout the day.
Upon hearing a sound or seeing a form, you may take it for granted that a "clunk" will occur. Nevertheless, you must strictly avoid calling a bell a jar. *He!* (A shout).
One shout.

Chan Master Yonggang Zongruan of Ningbo Prefecture, a Dharma heir of Chan Master He’an Zhong, addressed the assembly: "In general, when practicing the work of cultivation, one must simply give rise to the Great..."
Regarding the state of doubt: do not lose right mindfulness. A thousand doubts and ten thousand doubts are but a single doubt.

As soon as there is an interruption, one falls into emptiness. Seeing how you all practice, if you have not yet achieved "one piece" within half a month or a month, how could you avoid being distracted?
If true doubt truly manifests before you, unshakable by any agitation, you will naturally have no fear of confusion. Furthermore...
You must not give rise to even a single thought of joy. As soon as there is the slightest divergent thought, strike it down into two pieces.
Merely maintain a state of fierce, relentless intensity, remaining like a dead man all day long. When you reach such a stage, [you will succeed].
"Even if the turtle escapes from the jar. [The Master said: "Venerable assembly, what if you suddenly catch the turtle inside the jar?
You must by all means avoid mistaking the servant for the master.
This is the twenty-ninth generation under Dajian (Mazu).

Chan Master Baofeng Mingxuan of Gaoping, in the Prefecture of Jiangning, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Cizong of Jinling. He was the son of the Fan family of Wujiang. By trade, he was a carpenter.

Once, while constructing a pagoda courtyard for Haizhou, his foot was injured. Seeking wine, Haizhou said, "It is fortunate that you have only injured your foot; had your head been cut off, even though..."
"Qian Cheng, can you eat this? The Master felt ashamed and subsequently requested ordination as a monk. One day, while he was carrying firewood after tending the fire, Zhuanzhou asked, "What is that?
The Master replied, "It is firewood. Zhuanzhou said, "If it is firewood, take it away and burn it. The Master harbored a doubt and could not sleep all night.
Suddenly, his eyebrows were singed by the fire, and his face appeared as if shaved with a blade. When he looked in a mirror, he attained great enlightenment and rushed toward [the Master].
When [Zhao]zhou saw the boat, he raised his staff. The Master snatched the staff away and said, "This six-foot pole has not been used for a long time;
today it must be raised once more. Zhaozhou laughed heartily. The Master presented him with a verse that contained the line, "A knife hidden within a smile—look closely.
Zhaozhou said, "By this very verse, you may succeed to my school," and he then entrusted the verse to him. [The Master was one of] the lion cubs of Linji.
Regarding the phrase "Your son": Later, he resided at Gao Feng Temple in Jinling. Tian Qi said came to visit him.
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? Qi replied, "From Beijing. The Master said, "Are you still just in Beijing, or do you go elsewhere? Qi said, "I am carefree wherever I am."
The Master asked, "Have you ever been to Sichuan? He replied, "I have. The Master said, "How is the landscape of Sichuan compared to here?
He replied, "Though the mountains and rivers differ, the clouds and moon are the same. The Master raised his fist and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in Sichuan?
He replied, "No. The Master said, "Why is it that there is not? He replied, "It is not my realm. The Master asked, "What is your [realm]?"
[The guest] said, "As for this realm, even the Buddhas cannot know it; who would dare to force a name upon it? The Master said, "Are you not, then, attached to emptiness?

He replied, "My original auspiciousness will never consist of making a living inside a ghost cave. The Master said, "Among the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths in the Western Heaven, you are the foremost.
[The guest] suddenly shook his whisk and departed. The Master was pleased, considering him a true seedling capable of carrying on the lineage. It was worthy.

He upheld the Way and subsequently wrote a verse to entrust it to him, saying: "The staff and shouts of Mount Ji are as thunderous in their wrath; killing and giving life are applied according to the occasion with intimate hand and eye.
Holy interpretations and vulgar sentiments are both cut off at once; a fresh branch of the *dharma-puṣpa* is brought forth.
The Master passed away on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month in the *Xinmao* year of the Chenghua era. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the left of Dongming Temple.
Chan Master Zhiying of Yunxi and Bifeng on Mount Lu in Jiuzhang Prefecture was, in his youth and vigor, painfully illiterate.
In his later years, he composed verses extemporaneously, which were frequently praised by many. He entrusted a verse to his disciple Zhisu, saying:

"Having seen through the true face of one’s birth-mother, One should especially strive to guard and protect one's innate nature. When the claws and fangs have been fully developed on a majestic day, A single roar—"
The sound startled the hundred beasts.

Jūn Peak, the Venerable Master Tong, had a Dharma heir named the Elder Qīngxiáng of Jūn Peak in Shàowǔ Prefecture, who had long relied upon Dàchǎn. One day, he suddenly attained realization and presented a verse.
It is said: "The nature of phenomena is empty and unimpeded; it is the impartial observation of self-mastery. To sever the mechanism of both extremes is called transcending the three realms.
This is what is expounded as such.
Chan Master Zhengfa Xueguang of Sishan Prefecture was of the Zhao clan. Having traveled extensively throughout various regions, he spent the summer retreat at Lingfeng.
Upon hearing the case of Venerable Yan’yang’s question to Master Zhaozhou being cited, he attained realization. He related this to Jizhao, who said:
"In the state of non-effort, one must apply effort precisely. Do not mistake a mere fragment of light and shadow, lest it mislead your entire life.
He then spent the winter at Jingde Temple. One day, while in meditative concentration, he heard the sound of a mountain waterfall;

this triggered his realization, and he thoroughly penetrated every kōan concerning the patriarchs and Buddhas of the past. He then went to visit Jie Kong and recounted everything from the beginning. Jie Kong said, "I have not seen..."

Regarding the Way, do not say that being "mindless" constitutes the Way; even mindlessness still leaves one separated from it by a further barrier. Once the Way is realized, one simply enters the chamber of rest.
From that time on, the Master was utterly devoid of mental preoccupations. He harbored doubts and could not reach a resolution.

One day, seeing the line from a poem by Hanshan, "My heart is like the autumn moon," his lingering obstructions were suddenly released. Later, he lived as a hermit in a mountain retreat. At the end of his life, he wrote a verse and passed away.
Chan Master Tiancai Ying of Jingshan, Hangzhou Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Tanning Xuan, addressed the assembly:

"The Elder Master Mo Tang stirred up waves upon level ground and struck wooden wedges out of empty space. Having been struck by its poisonous breath, he has now returned and says he has personally seen it."
"Baoyue, you do not know how many people's eyes you have blinded. Tsk! You have gone and opened your mouth to chatter.

Chan Master Jin Baofang of Tianmu, in Hangzhou Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Ning of Dagang, spoke this verse of dharma transmission: "The true nature is fundamentally without nature; the true..."
The Dharma is fundamentally without dharma. Having thoroughly realized the nature of non-dharma, where would there be anything not fully penetrated?
Chan Master Lanmu Zhanjue of Yuan Tong Monastery in Jingzhou Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Xingkong; he was born into the Zhang family of Qujiang in Chang'an.
From childhood, he aspired to the joy of *dhyāna*. He received the tonsure under Master Xiùshān of Lántián and vowed to investigate and clarify the nature of birth and death.
Day and night he applied himself with diligence until even sleep and food were neglected. One day, he attained a realization and went to see Master Xìngkōng to seek definitive resolution.

Subsequently, he received the master’s seal of approval and certification. In the *Bingxū* year of the Chénghuà era, he inaugurated the Dharma at Yuántōng. Entering the hall, he said: "In this field for selecting the Buddha, the weeds grow three feet deep."
In the Hall of the Empty King, waves surge a thousand fathoms high. Within Perfect Penetration there is a single phrase that cannot be disgorged whole;
if it is disgorged, it is no longer whole. If anyone can examine this and discern it, I grant him the possession of a single eye.

Chan Master Huanji Xueting of Zhaokong Temple in Hangzhou Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Xiuhui of Jingci Temple. He was the son of the Gui family of Renhe. In the *guisi* year of the Chenghua era, he went to Xianlin to visit Master Xiuhui;

upon their first meeting, they reached a profound accord. Thereafter, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he arrived at the passage concerning the manifestation [of the universe] on the tip of a single hair.
The King of Jewels Temple harbored doubts. Later, he went to Qianming Temple in Jiangyin and beheld the Wanfo Ge (Ten Thousand Buddhas Pavilion), its golden and azure splendor towering majestically.

Suddenly, he attained a realization. On the eve of the New Year in the Wushen year of the Hongzhi era, hearing the sound of the bell, he followed his former steps and suddenly perceived them as crumbling like a collapsing wall.
He composed a verse, saying: "The resonant circle is not heard by the mind; the great trichiliocosm is illuminated as one. Having brushed past the gate of the ultimate, further..."

He did not harbor any notions of profound mystery. In the year Yimao (1235), during a period of rest, he accepted the invitation from Jingci Temple. The Master again attended upon him and subsequently received his seal of approval (*inka*).
At the age of forty, he began teaching at Zhaokong Temple. He ascended the hall and said: "The mind is not the environment; the environment is entirely the mind.

Since they do not meet anywhere, how could it turn its back on you? Therefore, the mind does not exist as a mind of its own; when the neighboring rooster crows at dawn, Avalokiteśvara is revealed within the dew."
"Not from one's own realm. When the flowers bloom upon the trees in the courtyard, casting light and shadows, all within the dust are but guests who have come of their own accord.
The host within the hall must call them awake. After a long pause, he said: "Be careful not to nod off. He then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The great bell has a mouth but no tongue; struck once, its sound is heard throughout the four seas. It presses the scales until the head and horns of the brocade fish are revealed—wait and watch!"
On level ground, he rolled up the clouds and winds. Holding up a rock, he showed it to the assembly, saying, "The intent of my teaching is like a 'poisoned drum.
When struck once, everyone who hears it, whether far or near, perishes. At that time, there was a monk named Xiao Yan who asked, "What is the poisoned drum?
Yan Tou pressed his hand against his knee, leaned his body forward, and said, "Han Xin at the imperial court. Yan was speechless. The verse says: The black staff stirs the waters.

The waters of the four oceans cause shrimp, crabs, fish, and dragons to lose their courage and souls. Advancing or retreating, they encounter the waves and suffer "dotted foreheads" (defeat). How much more so when leaping about, only to hear the thunder crash down. Xuefeng raised this point for the assembly: "Beside the rice basket, countless people die of hunger; within the ocean waters, countless people die of thirst. Yunmen followed up with the saying: "His entire body is rice; his entire body is water. A verse on this: The four seas are vast and deep; Fish and dragons lose their wits. Advancing or retreating, they meet the waves; Leaping about, they face the crashing thunder. Countless die of hunger by the rice basket; Countless die of thirst within the sea. When Yunmen says, "His whole body is rice, his whole body is water," Who can fathom this? The Great Way is not far—just look at your own face. If you wish to see it clearly, Do not seek it elsewhere. It is right here before your eyes. If you do not understand, You will surely fall into the pit of doubt. If you understand, You will immediately attain liberation. This is the place where the Buddhas and Patriarchs dwell. This is the place where all sentient beings abide. If you can see it thus, You will be free from birth and death. If you cannot see it thus, You will wander in the three realms.

Therefore, I urge you to examine yourself. Do not wait until the end of your life. If you do not act now, You will regret it later. This is the true teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not let it pass in vain. If you can realize it in this very moment, You will transcend the world. If you do not realize it in this very moment, You will remain bound by karma. Thus, I exhort you all: Examine yourselves with diligence. Do not rely on others. Only then will you truly know your own mind. Only then will you truly see your own nature. This is the ultimate meaning of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. This is the essential point of the transmission of the lamp.

If you can grasp it, you are a Buddha. If you cannot grasp it, you are a ghost. Do not be deluded. Do not be confused. This is the true path of liberation. Do not seek it outside of yourself. It is right here, within your own heart. If you can see it thus, You will be free from all suffering. If you cannot see it thus, You will continue to suffer in saṃsāra. Therefore, I urge you all: Examine yourselves with diligence. Do not waste this precious human life. Only then will you attain the fruit of Buddhahood. Only then will you fulfill your original vow. This is the final instruction of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not let it go to waste. If you can practice it, you will be liberated. If you do not practice it, you will remain bound. Thus ends the verse.
It is said: "The pear-flower wine at the small shop is fragrant; how many have tasted it as the cowherd points it out?

Let him drip it drop by drop without touching his lips, yet he already lies with his whole body in the land of wine. This refers to when Nanquan saw Deng Yinfeng approaching and pointed to a water pitcher, saying:
"The pitcher is an object. You must not touch the object. Bring me some water. Yinfeng then took the pitcher.
He poured water before the spring, and the spring ceased its flow. The verse says: "Petals fall one by one, chased by the eastern wind;
The springtime light lies in disarray, the ground covered in red. Even if one were to gather them all up before them, A lingering fragrance still remains beyond the eastern wall.
Case: A monk asked Xuansha, "What is the student's own self? Xuansha said, "What would you do with your own self? The verse on this dialogue:

It is said: "In my whole life, I have never dreamed of the Southland; it is truly vexing that people come to speak of the *zhègū* [partridge]. Though I wear brocade, I cannot yet return to my native land;
I seek the Imperial Capital within a mere village of three households. Citing the initial words of Dongshan:

"When speech does not unfold the matter, and words do not meet the occasion, those who rely on the words perish; those who linger in the phrases are deluded. The verse says: "The white jade, though polished thrice, finds its flaws difficult to conceal."
A single moment of silence is like a sealed tongue; a slight movement and one is already lost from home. Ten thousand acres of autumn light, where heaven and water blend in azure;
a single sound of a fisherman’s flute, drifting through the reeds. I also once composed a poem on the oriole, which says: "Full of emotion, I naturally cherish the spring light;
It flies into the gardens, that realm of brocade and embroidery. Remembering how it startled me from my dream at the small window, The courtyard is filled with crimson blossoms."
Plum blossoms wear the slanting sun.
The Dharma heir of Chan Master Baofeng Xuan,
the thirtieth generation descendant of Great Mirror (Dajian).
Chan Master Tianqi Benrui of Jingmen Prefecture in Anlu was a native of Zhongling in Nanchang. His father was Jiangtang and his mother was surnamed Xu.
At the age of twenty-two, he left the household and traveled far to Jingmen to seek ordination under Master Wushuo. Wushuo assigned him the koan:
"All phenomena return to the One; where does the One return? Later, he met the Head Seat Quan of Gaoyou and went with him to Xiangyang.
Yang. On the way, he happened to hear a woman calling for her pig. Xuanquan said, "Mother calls 'na-na' from within the wall;
do you monks on the road understand? Once these pivotal locks are broken through, mother remains as she was, still the grandmother."
The Master was startled and broke into a cold sweat. One day, when his illness became severe, the Chan practitioner Huiming urged him [to rest].

without relying on a boat or oars, how can it be found? Third: The entire earth is a pit of fire;
it has all been burned away, leaving only a single strand of eyebrow hair. I wonder who is able to see this? [This occurred] while he was in the vegetable garden.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master pointed to some vegetables and said, "Yellow gourd, eggplant.
The monk did not attain realization. Later, descending the mountain, he met an elder. The elder asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Peak Tip.

The elder asked, "Regarding 'Great Rest,' what words or phrases were spoken? The monk recounted the previous dialogue. The elder joined his palms and said, "Truly great compassion! *Jiajing* [Era] year.
On the eighth day of the eleventh month in the year of Renyin, he gathered the assembly and wrote this verse:
"Holding the three periods of time as my staff, The ten directions are originally my old kashaya robe. The clay ox and stone tiger know the news; Treading through empty space, I have arrived home."
He set down his writing brush, sat upright, and passed away.

Master Yang’an Guangxin of Ehu in Guangxin Prefecture was a dharma successor of Master Ding of Mount Hua. His courtesy name was Wuita (No Other). He was the son of the Zheng family of Shangrao. Once, by chance—

While passing through a gathering of relatives, he discussed the meaning of the four modes of birth (*catur-yoni*) with a traveler. Thereupon, he attained a thorough understanding of the great principle of the equality of self and others.
In the *Yihai* year of the Wanli era (1615), he received the tonsure and precepts at Taiping Temple in Luoyang. Returning south, he spent the winter retreat (*laba*) at Mount Jiao.

Hearing the sound of a boat being pushed through the river, he experienced a moment of awakening and composed a verse, saying: "The night is still, the river vast and empty; The boat is being pushed, the sound of [mouth] + [mouth] + [mouth]. I know not what..."

Wherever he went, one side of his pack was lighter. Next, while traveling, he encountered the story of Mount Hua regarding "a segment of karmic affinity that is not contained within the six [sense bases].

Having doubts, he applied himself with fierce intensity for seven days until his body and mind were suddenly liberated. Upon returning to his hometown, he resided at the Central Terrace of Mount Ling.
On New Year’s Eve, seeing a wildfire in Minshan, he attained great enlightenment. He once painted a large circle on a wall and wrote: "Within..."
When writing, do not allow it to become blackened; when writing on the exterior, do not let it damage the white.

If you can apply your annotations both within and outside the circle, I grant you permission to study the Way without doubt. Later, he moved to Ehu. In the year Jihai, he presided over the primary seat using the *Wu yi* (Non-differentiation) as his text.
The corridors of his quarters were never locked, as he wished to verify those who would come. Beside the lock, he had written a verse that said:
"The lock has been handed down since ancient times; I rely on you to open it with the key of wisdom. If you lack the method for opening the lock, Then even if we meet, there is no need to come.
A monk asked, "I have often heard of 'clarifying the mind and seeing the nature. I wonder, how does one see the nature? The Master replied, "Today I am busy with guests."
"I just now told you I was busy. When the guest had left, the monk continued with his previous question. The Master said, "Did you see me just now when I was dealing with the guest?
The monk replied, "I saw you. The Master said, "I told you I was busy; why are you still standing here? A monk asked, "What is it like when the void is shattered?
The Master raised his hand, signaled for him to step back, and said, "Get out! Get out! The monk ran away. The Master said, "What a pity! *Gui*.
While preaching the Dharma at Dongshan Dongyan in Jianyang, on the first day of the third month in the *dingmao* year of the Tianqi era, he manifested slight illness.
On the twenty-eighth day, at the hour of *chou*, he summoned the assembly and spoke this verse: "For over eighty years within a dream-like illusion, The iron ox has plowed through the great void.
As I depart, I entrust you with this one phrase: At midnight, the golden sun bears the crimson glow. [Verse]
He sat upright until his passing. His age was eighty-one; his years since ordination were fifty-three. His stupa is at Mount Tangmao.
Chan Master Tianzhen Daojue of Mount Doufeng in Jianning Prefecture was a descendant of the Zhang family of Jian’an in that same province. While contemplating the ten thousand...
When the phrase "The Dharma returns to the One; where does the One return? was spoken, Hua had an awakening. He composed a verse, saying: "One hand claps, one hand drums;
The person of no station performs a dance beyond the ordinary. From the mouth, a melody-less song is sung; The three thousand Buddhas share the same mother.
When he went to see Gu Yin, Gu Yin praised him and immediately entrusted him with the Great Matter.
Chan Master Wú'ài Mínglǐ of Fúniú Mountain in the Henan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Dàfāng Kuān. He was the son of Héshì of Fénzhōu.

Having visited Chan Master Sōngzhú Dàfāng, he participated in the seven-day intensive retreat (*qītiān*) with the assembly. There, he uttered the phrase: "A single sound shatters the void, revealing alone the King of Dharmas. Later, together with...
Dayuan Yue’an entered Zhongnan. One day, while at the hermitage, the master brought up the koan of High Peak’s “silver mountains and iron walls.

The teacher attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse, saying: "Upon one awakening, the mind is empty and doubt vanishes; picking it up and letting it go, one is naturally carefree," and so forth.
He went to visit Dafang. Dafang said, "I shall not ask about the seven-day intensive practice at Funiu; what is your understanding of the hermitage at Zhongnan?
The Master replied, "At Funiu, the seven-day practice is like a lump of mud or a clod of earth; at the Zhongnan hermitage, it radiates great light.
Dafang roared with a shout of awe and asked, "Where is that light right now? The Master stepped forward and gave him a slap. Dafang laughed heartily.
It is said: "So it is, so it is.
This is the lineage of Zen Master Longquan Cong, the thirty-second generation descendant of Dajian."
Chan Master Debao of Xianguo and Yuexin Xiaoyan of Shuntian Prefecture was the son of the Wu family of Jintai.

He was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month in the *Ren-shen* year of the Zhengde era. When he reached the age of twenty and was listening to lectures on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, upon reaching the "Ten Grounds" chapter, his body and mind suddenly became vast and empty.
He sighed, saying, "For a thousand ages, all is but one single illusion and dream. Thereupon, he resolved to leave the household life and followed Guanghui.
He was able to shave his head. The following year, he received full ordination (*upasampadā*). Although he possessed deep faith and knew [the truth], he refused to rest content with that alone.
He visited various masters, including Dachu, Yuezhou, Guchun, and Guzhi. Later, he went to Guanziling to attend upon Wumen. Wumen asked him about the Ten Sages and Three Worthies.

[The student replied,] "I have already fully realized sage-wisdom; why then do you say the Way does not clarify this principle? Wumen then raised his voice sharply and said, "The Ten Sages and Three..."
“Virtuous one, you already know this. What is the meaning of this? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master uttered several words in succession, yet none were in accord with the truth.
Thereupon, he became despondent, abandoning both sleep and food. One day, carrying a basket, he went to a stream to wash vegetables. Suddenly, a leaf fell into the water and spun around;

though he tried to catch it, he could not hold it. At that moment, he attained realization. Carrying his basket, he returned home with great joy. As he reached the eaves of the hall, he heard [the Master’s voice].
The questioner asked, “What is it? The Master said, “A basket of vegetables. Wumen asked, “Why not say something else? The Master said, “Please ask me another question, Reverend.
That evening, during the private interview, Wumen brought up Xuansha’s story about daring to guarantee that his elder brother had not yet reached full realization. The Master said:
A thief entered an empty room and heard [the Master’s voice] saying, "This public case must not be handled with haste. The Master let out a shout and, shaking his sleeves, departed immediately.
Shortly thereafter, he went again to visit various elders such as Jie’an, Guyan, and Dajue, all of whom held him in high esteem.

He visited Wuwen again, whereupon he was granted a prophetic transmission (*vyākaraṇa*). After spending more than a year in close attendance, he took his leave and traveled through the regions of Xiang and Han.
Later, he arrived at Jinling, residing in places such as Jinghai, Niushou, and Gaosuo for several years, before returning to his hometown to dwell at Yuantong.
He subsequently moved to the various monasteries of Nan Temple, Luyuan, Ciguang, and Shanguo. On the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall. Dahui said:
"Today is once again the fifth day of the fifth month. The great ghosts clap their hands and the little ghosts dance. Suddenly they run straight into the Tao Fu deity;
with both hands they beat their breasts, crying out in grievous suffering. "Old man Dahui," [the Master] said, "is very much lacking a prohibitive remedy. Toward the green..."
Under the bright sun of heaven, some see gods and see ghosts; Xianyan, however, is not like this. This very day is the fifth of the fifth month.
Clouds follow the dragon, and wind follows the tiger. This mountain monk wishes to gamble with all the great sages present here.
Let us take a wager at random from the tips of the hundred grasses: what is sweet is sweet, and what is bitter is bitter. [He raises his staff and says: Suddenly, it breaks forth!
There is one thing that transcends all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past. You people here before me possess it in every way;
why then is this one thing alone lacking? Suppose there were someone who, seeing this meaning, acted with courage and stepped forward indignantly, saying:
"Preceptor, do not force the noble into the lowly! As for this one thing, I dare say that everyone possesses it."
"Not lacking even a hair's breadth. He then threw down his staff and said, "You truly do not know; why not add the point to the point, or pile more earth upon the mound?
Ascending the hall, he said: "A man of spirit may indeed harbor a will to charge toward the heavens, yet it is better to let it fall from the very start.
Even if one were to completely wither the skull to death, one must still cause the dead eye to open wide. Ascending the hall again, he said:
Nanyue once dispatched a monk to investigate Mazu, instructing him: "When he ascends the hall, go forth and ask him, 'What is it?
Observe what words or phrases he utters and remember them to bring back. The monk went there exactly as instructed.
Mazu said, "Since the time of the chaotic upheaval, for thirty years, salt and sauce have never been lacking. The monk returned and reported this to Nanyue.
Yue deeply approved of this. The Master said, "The Great Master Mazu spent thirty years with salt and soy sauce;
only then was he able to gather disciples and preach the Dharma. Here in my place, for thirty years I have never seen so much as a pinch of salt or soy sauce.
What kind of bowl are you all looking for here? With his staff, he drove them all away at once. Entering the hall, he said: "A single arrow right at the gate."
The visitor observed the Master’s expedient means and prepared to ask how it was. [The Master] pierced through the surface of his skull. The monk entered for an interview and asked:
"From the time of the ancient masters of the thousand and seven hundred, I have today strung them all together on a single thread and presented them to you, O Honored One;
I humbly request your judgment. At that moment, a dog suddenly barked outside the gate. The Master abruptly looked at his attendant and said, "Look! What kind of guest is this?"
"Come," the Master said. The attendant went out to pose a question for the monk, who was at a loss. The Master asked, "What was it you were just asking, Senior?
As the monk prepared to repeat his words, the Master struck him with a continuous blow of his staff and drove him out. One day, two nuns came to visit. After bowing, they stood to the left and right.
The Master said, "Women entering meditative absorption before the Tathāgata; having money but not knowing how to spend it; the old woman of Mount Tai."
"Go straight ahead! Even if you understand how to use it, you will still have no money. "How can these two types of 'old woman Chan' be made perfect?
The nun moved from the left to the right; the other moved from the right to the left. They faced each other with palms joined and each let out a single sigh.
The Master said, "In this way, you not only understand old woman Chan, but you also know how to drum up the steam of rice gruel. The nun— [ceased speaking].
[The monk] said, "Master, you had better save your eyebrows. The Master said, "Let us set aside the matter of this mountain monk’s eyebrows for a moment.
When Zhou Jin-gang was buying oil-cakes as a snack, he had them right at his mouth when an old woman snatched them away.
When Liu Tie-mo invited Shitou Xiqian to attend a great assembly banquet at Mount Tai, Shitou did not go. These are all instances of the same occasion; tell me, why is that?"

Their ways of accepting and rejecting were different. Two nuns paid their respects and said, "Had we not come to pay our respects to the Master, how could we have seen the great functioning of the ancient sages' spiritual powers?
The Master said, "Excellent! Thirty blows for each of you. Unfortunately, my staff is not here at the moment;
let us return to the tea hall to drink some tea. A monk asked, "What is the Samādhi of Universal Vision of Mañjuśrī? The Master—

[The monk] asked, "What is the eye of a dead man? The Master said, "The ear of a dead man. [The monk] asked, "What is the Samādhi of Universal Hearing of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said, "The mouth of a dead man.
[The monk] asked, "What is the single phrase that exhausts the ultimate meaning? The Master said, "The mouth of a dead man. A monk requested instruction on the saying:
"If one is treated with contempt in this life, it is because of the karmic offenses of a previous life, for which one should fall into the evil realms. The Master said, "You have..."

"Have you doubts? he asked. The monk replied, "I have doubts. The Master said, "If you have doubts, you will be held in contempt by others; if you have no doubts, you should fall into the evil realms.
The monk hesitated. The Master asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Bring forth that which you do not understand and let me see it.
He replied, "I do not understand. What am I supposed to bring forth? The Master said, "Your own karmic offenses. With that, [the monk] was suddenly enlightened.
"It is extinguished. The monk bowed in thanks and departed. [The Master] asked, "Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river. To which of the 'turns' (ji) do these fall?
The Master said, "They both fall into the second turn. [The monk] asked, "What is the first turn?
The Master said, "Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what did they obtain? The Master said, "It is evident."
"In the end, what have you attained? A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "Willow shadows stretch across the pond as fish climb trees; locust-tree shade covers the earth as horses mount branches.

The monk said, "If that is so, then form and shadow are divided, and right and wrong reveal themselves naturally. The Master said, "You have never yet eaten your fill of the rice of Luling; you merely grasp at your meditation cushions in vain."

[The monk] was recognized as a celestial being. A monk came to inquire: "I have heard that the appearance of all Buddhas in the world is for the sake of the one great cause and condition (*ekamahākaruṇāhetu*).
What is this great cause and condition? The Master said: "Dressing and eating; defecating and urinating. The monk did not accept this; he did not prostrate and departed.
The Master called him back and showed him a verse, saying: "The Buddhas appear in the world / Solely for the sake of the Great Cause and Condition."
Defecating and urinating together; eating when hungry and sleeping when tired. Such urgent matters before one’s eyes, yet people only wish to ascend to heaven.
Discussing the profound and speaking of the wondrous, they incur sin and must pay fines. The monk, feeling abashed, paid his respects and departed. Two officials were touring the mountains;
as they entered the gate, they recited: "Lush pines and tall bamboos. Looking back, they saw the master and asked: "How is it?"
"This is the style of our family of practitioners," the Master said. "Magnificent pines and tall bamboos," [the visitor] remarked. "What is the significance of this? the Master asked.
"It is not enough for me alone to behold it; I have left it here for guests to come and see. There was a scholar who, having read the Master’s verses on the Pure Land, asked:
"When the Buddha preached this sutra, the Buddhas of the six directions extended their broad and long tongues as witnesses. Now, when you, Master, speak these verses—"
"Who has testified to this? The Master said, "The layman’s tongue is not short either. He asked again, "What is inconceivable merit?
The Master said, "A person in the street ahead calls for his dog; a person in the alley behind scolds his cat. He asked again, "Venerable Teacher, how old are you this year?
The Master said, "As for years, I have not seen a bit of meat. Why else would I be so withered and thin? A monk asked, "..."
Entering the Dharma-realm in every place, seeing Vairocana in every thought-moment. "What is Vairocana? The Master said: "One need not defecate on clean ground.
[The Master] cited Zhaozhou’s question to Touzi: "When a person who has undergone the great death returns to life, what then?
Touzi said: "Night travel is not permitted; one must arrive at dawn. The verse says: "The thirty-six constituents are all reduced to ashes, leaving behind only..."
A pair of withered eyes placed in the middle of the nine-fold thoroughfare after the deep night;

where there is no light, they create light. Taking up the public case of the World-Honored One holding up the flower, the verse says: The wondrous accord between teacher and disciple is like a mustard seed meeting a needle; how could it not be found anywhere, as vast as the sea?
Having once cast one's eye into the flash of a stone-light, one finally knows that the Buddhas and Patriarchs have no mind to transmit. Taking up the Sūtra:

Inscription on the Character "Mi" (Eight). The verse says: Before black and white were yet distinguished, one had already fallen into partiality; how could one bear to deliberate further or waste effort in drilling and research?
The sages and worthies of India and this land—whose nostrils reach toward heaven—are all pierced through.
To the Abbot: Carrying a hoe everywhere, you expend your efforts; three or two coins are quite enough for a plan. When you have cleared away the fields and lands of others, your own...
The fields are entirely overgrown with weeds. To the monks: The profound subtleties within the Dharma are cataracts before the eyes; the wondrous mechanism beyond is dust upon the realm.
When the hoops on the black lacquer bucket break, one is a free person within the land of Great Peace. Sitting in stillness amidst cold crags, this malady is difficult to cure;
how could a man of spirit ever be willing to deceive himself? A single step to turn back is not far at all—only then does one truly believe in the dust.
The Dharma-realm is vast and all-encompassing. From within his room, he uttered these words:

"Before the Buddha appeared in the world and before the Patriarch came from the West, there was originally no such thing as the names 'Buddha-dharma' or 'worldly dharma. How would you express that single phrase which transcends the ghost-caves of the Black Mountains?

Furthermore, since the Buddha has appeared in the world and the Patriarch has come from the West, the Buddha-dharma and worldly dharmas have been established in relation to one another. Without violating the gate of transformation, how do you speak?"

Bring forth a single phrase. Furthermore, the Buddha’s arising among ordinary beings and sages is a gate of dualistic opposition; worldly dharmas and Buddha-dharmas are merely names established by force. Set all of these aside for a moment.
Try bringing forward a single phrase that is the fundamental portion of a monk’s own task. Moreover, in the midst of ordinary life—
His speech and responses were exceedingly plain and easy, yet profoundly inconceivable. Whenever someone asked him, "What is this Buddha-nature that you inherently possess?
why was it that he would instead turn his eyes upward and remain speechless?

Furthermore, since he was a son of the Buddha and aspired to the stage of Buddhahood, for what reason was he most averse to hearing even the single word "Buddha"? In his later years, he retired to the capital.
Liuyang passed away on the sixteenth day of the first month of the辛巳 (Xinsi) year of the Wanli era. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa outside the Xiaoxi Gate.
He was seventy years of age and forty-eight years of monastic seniority.
Chan Master Dajian of Mount Lu in Jiujiang Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Hanyangyan. He was the son of the Hao family of Xiangyang. In his youth, he paid respects to Guzong;
he received the tonsure under Meilin Zong. Together with Guyan, they both emerged from the school of Tianqi. While Guyan resided at Zhongnan, [Dajian] became a dragon-elephant [of the Dharma].

The Emperor’s prestige was such that all submitted to him. Consequently, he sent the Master to the cliff to study under him. Upon his arrival, the Master spoke a single word that struck the core of the truth, whereupon [the Emperor] immediately bestowed upon him the robe and bowl.
Later, he dwelt on Mount Lu for thirty years; his reputation for the Way spread far and wide, and the people of Chu served him with particular reverence.

Wang Boyu of Xindu once followed the Master to inquire about difficult points, receiving many enlightening instructions. On the first day of the fifth month of the Jiyu year of the Wanli era, he preached...
He passed away in verse. His disciples built a stupa beside his hermitage to enshrine his relics.
He was seventy-three years of age at death and had fifty years of monastic seniority (*bhikṣu-varṣa*).

One day at dawn, Chan Master Baoying of Longshu Hermitage on Mount Wutai in Taiyuan Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Hong of Shizhou, attained realization upon beholding the morning star.
He composed a verse, saying: "The sun rises from the eastern mountains; The moon sinks behind the western peaks. Yesterday and today— They have never been two."
For example:
Chan Master Chufeng of Wutai Mountain in Taoyuan Prefecture resided at Bumo Rock for over ten years. He lived on wood and drank from mountain streams;
others could not endure such hardship, yet the Master remained as serene as ever. One day, upon hearing the sound of a firecracker exploding, he attained great enlightenment and composed this verse:
It is said: The eyeballs protrude from the head of dead wood; its brilliant divine light illuminates the four continents. It manifests wherever it touches, yet people do not comprehend it;
how many times has spring passed and autumn returned?
A monk asked Master Yutang, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Look beneath your feet. The monk asked, “How should one practice it?
The Master said, “Go straight ahead.”
Chan Master Wuhuan Guzhan Xingchong of Chexi in Suzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jingwu. He was the son of the Zhang family of Xiushui.
Initially, he met Chan Master Wuqu and attained a realization. Soon thereafter, he left home to follow Wuqu and received the tonsure. One day, Wuqu raised the *Jingshan San*...

The Verse on the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries: "A single phrase that penetrates to the bone and marrow; a phrase where the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are beyond all obstruction or protection.
A question was asked: "Of these two phrases, I, this mountain monk, wish to take one as my dharma.
Which one would you say is better to take? The Master said: "Which phrase did you ask about just now? The questioner narrowed his eyes and scolded him: "How can you be so indeterminate?"
Xing said, "It is precisely because you, Master, have penetrated to the very bone and marrow. Qiu said, "That is not so.
It may be acceptable for you alone, but what about the great assembly? The Master said, "I would not decline to take it, yet I would betray the former sages and lose my future followers."
Wumen inclined his head in assent. While Wumen was at Mount Jing, he had compiled the *Recorded Sayings* (*yulu*) of Wuquan.
One day, Wuzhun returned to pay his respects. Wuquan asked, "What have you been doing lately? Wuzhun replied, "I have purchased a plot of land and obtained the original deed;
I have come specifically to request the Master’s signature. He then presented the manuscript. Wuquan took it, unfolded it, and looked at it, saying, "This..."
"This is mine; what about yours? Yunju said. "Master, you must not encroach upon another's path or snatch away their trade.
He then took the manuscript and threw it down. Yunju immediately stepped out. After a short while, Xuedou presented a verse. Yunju asked, "Is this something you composed?
Xuedou replied, "I do not know how to drum up the 'gruel-and-rice' breath. If you say there is something I have produced, I would be failing the Master by no small measure."
Qiu nodded his head and stood at the rear to address the assembly: "The Great Way has no front or back; the ultimate principle transcends all verbal expression.

It stands far beyond the Three Vehicles and towers high above the Ten Stages. Where the ten thousand dharmas cannot reach, it shines with singular brilliance. Before the distinction between birth and Buddhahood had arisen—"
The spiritual source shines alone; it does not fall into seeing or hearing, nor does it follow sound or form. Directly beneath, there is not so much as a single hair’s breadth.

Throughout the entire world, the extraordinary matter is fully manifest. Even if one attains realization through the staff or takes responsibility under the shout, this is still merely a concession to the times.
Furthermore, even if light and objects are both forgotten and the mind accords with equality, in the final analysis, this is also not the ultimate point. Therefore:
The Way is the single path pointing upward; it has not been transmitted by a thousand sages. Students weary their bodies, like monkeys grasping at reflections.

Here, there is no practice and no understanding; no illumination and no function; no principle and no phenomenon. It is like a long sword leaning against the heavens, its divine majesty awe-inspiring;
it is like the mechanism of an iron ox, which cannot be ensnared. Today, before those with clear eyes, I dare not conceal it within my breast.
The shroud is opened wide in eight characters. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Venerable elders, do you understand? Shining through antiquity and soaring through the present, it is just this.
Within the great chiliocosm of dust-motes, there is but one idle body. He addressed the assembly: "Atop the solitary peak..."

Taking broad strides across the great chiliocosm, ten out of ten remain on the street. Rarely meeting those who truly understand, he neither paid homage to Vimalakīrti nor revered the Great Master Fu.
After a long silence, he said: "Look out beyond the heavens; who is such a person? To the assembly, he showed:
"The substance of the Great Way is vast; the long sky leaves no trace. Pressing down the clouds, another message is conveyed: born together and dying together, the wind blows."

The grass bends down. Now tell me: is it better to hold fast for the sake of others, or is it better to let go for the sake of others? After a long silence, he said: "Heaven and earth are one joined piece of earth-cake;
the sun and moon are two wheels of the sky-ball. He addressed the assembly: "Clearly manifest at the tips of the hundred grasses, clearly manifest is the meaning of the Patriarchs.
It makes old Master Pang laugh to death; even now he is still dozing. When Luzu saw someone, he would simply face them."
The wall does not understand cold or warmth. As soon as Bimā reaches it, he raises his trident; there is no courtesy or righteousness here at all.
Nanshan’s Turtle-Nose is no better than a dead eel; Xiyuan’s Tweezer is just like a blunt saw. But tell me: how did Dabeī act for the sake of others?
The Wheel-Turning King has never cast aside his three-inch blade; throughout the world, the sound of axes and hatchets is first heard. Addressing the assembly: "The three realms are mind-only;
the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. He strikes the meditation staff and says: "Last night, the seasonal rain dripped upon the empty steps; a single sheet of green moss was soaked through.
On the occasion of the Buddha-Bath ceremony, he ascends the hall: "In the Lumbinī Garden, he once displayed his ugliness; before the Hall of the Ancient Buddhas, again..."
"His body is exposed; it is not by the power of the *sūryaprabhā-samādhi* that his body can be washed clean.
O assembly, the Elder Śākyamuni has been born today; I wonder if he has yet touched the ground? A monk stepped forward and said:
[The monk] said, "It has already landed. The Master asked, "Whom did you see say this? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "A ladle divining by listening to empty sounds.
A monk asked, "When the principle of pure emptiness ultimately has no body, what then?
The Master said, "A practitioner should be like this. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "The snow hides the egret; only when it flies does one see it."
Only when Liuzhang spoke the words of the parrot was it known. A monk asked, "After the Master passes away, where will you go?

The Master said, "Beneath a thousand pine trees, at the tips of a hundred grasses. While the Master was burning firewood, a monk asked, "What is the self-nature, the true and heavenly Buddha? The Master said, "Bring me a bundle of firewood. When the monk carried the wood on his shoulder back to him, he asked again. The Master said: *The parrot’s words were only known when Liuzhang spoke; Where shall I go after a hundred years? "Under a thousand pines, amidst the tips of a hundred weeds," he replied.

While tending the fire, a monk inquired: "How is the self-nature, the true and heavenly Buddha? "Bring me a bundle of firewood," he said. When the monk returned with the wood upon his shoulder, he questioned him once more. The Master said:*

"This fellow! He does not know good from bad, so he beats him. [The Master] asked, "What is the Supreme Vehicle? The Master said, "A rattan vine passes through; bamboo splints bind it. In the place of deliberation, no sound is known; look at the household talk beyond a hundred or a thousand years.

I empty my belly and pour out my heart to tell you: when the thought arises to seek the mind, the mind is itself the thought. Suddenly, there is no thought, and where there is no thought, there is no mind. Within the nine layers [of the palace], one is always the sovereign;
penetrating past and present, one is the Immovable Honored One. Exerting every ounce of heart and strength, perform the practice; search within and without for the reality.
"Total non-existence. At such a moment, there is no calculation that can be made. Suddenly hearing the cry of a woodcock within the village, "This mind is Buddha" is a statement through the skin;
"Neither Buddha nor mind" is also a provisional teaching. If you truly wish to know the point of reality, you must spit out all the fox-slobber.
The Master lived in seclusion in his hermitage for over twenty years. In the *Gengxu* year of the Wanli era, he accepted an invitation from Mount Jing. He did not...
After several months, his illness flared up again, and he returned to Chexi. In the winter of the Xinhai year, he manifested parinirvāṇa; his body was cremated and a stupa erected at Mount Jing.
He was seventy-two years of age and had thirty years of monastic seniority.
Chan Master Huiji Cizhai Zhiji of Mount Gaoyang in Yiyang, Guangxin Prefecture, was a successor of Chan Master Xinxin of Gehu. He was the son of the Cheng family from Yueyi in Raozhou.
He was born on the third day of the eleventh month of the Wuzi year of the Wanli era. At birth, he made no sound; it was only when the full moon [of his month] arrived that he began to cry.
At the age of twenty-five, he fell gravely ill and suffered greatly. A practitioner of Chan told him that as long as one does not understand birth and death, suffering exceeds even this.
He then resolved to leave the secular world and went to Yungu Hui to receive the tonsure. At twenty-seven, he visited Guo’an Xian at Ehu.

While contemplating the phrase "Who is reciting the Buddha's name? he attained realization. One day, when Master Hu raised the story of the two mice gnawing at the vine, the Master asked, "The withered vine is severed;
where will you find a place to settle and establish your life? Hu immediately splashed hot tea across his face.

The Master was suddenly and completely enlightened, and subsequently received the formal transmission of the Dharma. In the *jiashen* year of the Chongzhen era, he founded Gaoshan. In the *jichou* year of the Shunzhi era...
He moved to the mountain peak. In the year *dingyou*, at the request of the assembly, he ascended the hall at Gaoshan to open the session and inaugurate the retreat.

He ascended the hall and said: "Today we tie the mouth of the cloth bag; forty-nine days have passed since the beginning. If you leave this aside to seek elsewhere, you will remain oblivious to the jewel in your robe and wander outward.
He gave a shout and said, "Is this the howl of a jackal, or the roar of a lion? He then ascended the hall.
The Buddha-dharma has been fundamentally manifest from the beginning; it truly accords with our daily lives.
It is only because we fail to pluck the eyebrows that the entire earth is pure gold, yet we do not recognize the gold. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said:
"To call this a 'staff' is to encounter resistance (touch); not to call it a 'staff' is to turn one's back (ignore). Tell me, what shall you call it? He struck the floor once and said: [Silence].

Opening the eye of a thousand sages, one transcends the myriad functions before they arise. A monk asked, "What is the lineage of Miu-yang? The Master said, "Deeply hidden, it is not permitted to be revealed;
father and son are careful of their tradition. "How is the Linji lineage? The Master said, "In a single blow of the staff, there is the patience of non-arising;
in the moment of action, the teacher is not seen. "How is the Caodong lineage? The Master said, "A golden needle passes through..."
"A jade thread embroiders a pair of phoenixes. What is the Yunmen school? The Master said: "Its solitary standard rises loftily beyond reach; even Buddhas and Patriarchs find it difficult to equal.
"What is the Fayen school? The Master said: "White clouds return to the azure peaks; the red sun shines upon the green mountains.
"Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ultimate teaching, I ask the Master to bring it forth. The Master said: "The wind blows and the tally-sticks move."
