Compiled by the Patriarch-Succeeding Śramaṇa Xingtong of Xichu at Potalaka in the South Sea.
The details regarding his dharma heirs are unknown.
Chan Master Yun’an Qing of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a native of Jianyang. A monk asked Yangqi, “What is the Buddha?
Yangqi said, “A three-legged donkey prancing on its hooves. The monk asked, “Is it not just this very thing? Yangqi said, “The lake...”
To Elder Nanyuan. The verse says: A donkey of Yangqi, its eyes flashing like lightning;
it tramples all people underfoot—what need is there to speak of three legs?
Formerly, Chan Master Jingzhao asked a lecturer: "The sutras state that if one can turn objects, one is identical to the Tathāgata;
if one is turned by objects, one is called an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*). Now, regarding this Shengyuan Pavilion—how would you turn it? The lecturer had no reply.
Master Gōngqī was on his way to Luóhàn when he encountered a young gentleman riding an ox along the road.
The Master asked, “Where does the path to Luóhàn lead? The gentleman slapped the ox and said, “Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, “You beast!
The gentleman replied, “Where does the path to Luóhàn lead? The Master then slapped the ox and said, “Speak! Speak! The gentleman said, “Straight ahead.”
"Even so, you still lack hooves and horns. The Master then struck him. The young nobleman slapped his ox and ran off.
During the Tang Dynasty, when Chan Master Yin was in his youth, while he was once using a mallet to strike the earth, he saw a large clod of soil. In jest, he struck it violently with the mallet;
it shattered upon impact with his hand, and he attained great enlightenment.

Chan Master Yunding of Mount Dongshan in Fuzhou Prefecture was a native of Quanzhou. Having failed the imperial examinations for a second time, he went to Yuntai Dahou Temple to shave his head and receive full ordination.
He then visited Daguizhi and Shendingyin; later, upon meeting venerable elders under Luohan, he finally attained thorough realization of his own fundamental matter.
His reputation for the study of the Way spread widely, and the monastic community hailed him as "Dingsan" (the Third Dings). A monk asked: "If..."
"What are the daily activities of the Master? The Master said, "I eat my fill while you suffer from hunger.
[The monk] asked, "If every dharma does not reach another, how is this so? The Master said, "Whatever sins you commit, I know them all.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s single fly-whisk? The Master said, "It shatters the cave of spiritual cultivation. [The monk] said, "In that case, there is originally not a single thing."
The Master said, "Who is it that knows there is nothing? [The Layman] said, "It is the student's fault. The Master said, "Reflect on this further.
The Layman asked, "Dongshan said, 'There is one thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth. I do not know what kind of thing this is."
The Master said, "Carrying an iron cangue and eating an iron staff. A man said, "Heaven and earth turn black; mountains and rivers flee.
The Master said, "One more ghost is added before the Hall of King Yama; he shall lie beneath Mount Beimang for a thousand years. The scholar cried out, "What joy! What joy!
The Master said, "This too is merely a wild fox swallowing a mouse. The Daoist of Jiulong Guan and three scholars invited him to ascend the hall. The Confucian [scholars]... [text ends].

The Gate of the Eight Trigrams (Bagua) draws talismanic seals, yet it does not rescue those in the cycle of transmigration through the six realms. The Daoist Gate venerates the Nine Sovereigns to refine the true qi, yet it does not comprehend the kalpas of the three great asankhyeyas.
Our Śākyamuni, the World-Honored One, penetrates the kalpas of the three great asankhyeyas and rescues those in the cycle of transmigration through the six realms.
With his Great Vow, he gathers in humans and devas, like the wind-circle supporting the sun and moon; with his Great Wisdom, he shatters birth and death.
Even if the kalpa-fire were to incinerate the finest autumn hair, those who have entered my gate naturally transform heaven and earth and perceive the hidden spirits and ghosts.
They cause Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the great earth, and the vast oceans to enter into a single pore, while all sentient beings remain unaware and unknowing.
I say that this Dharma-gate is like space, which contains all myriad forms; the one becomes the infinite, and the infinite becomes the one.
The measure is one. If a person attains this one, then all matters are finished. Take care.
Chan Master Yunyou Zhongyun of Jinhuafu first visited Xuefeng and subsequently relied upon Shishuang, where he attained awakening.

He returned to his hometown and lived in seclusion at Yunyou, covering his body with nothing but a single robe. After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and said: "Yunyou’s single arrow pierces through empty space."
It has no front or back; it shoots away throughout the ten directions, yet for the time being, no one sees it.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the single arrow of Yunyou? The Master said, "All the people of the great earth have no skulls. (Yunyou has now been changed to Fayun.)
Chan Master Da’an Ruyu of Hangzhou Prefecture was styled Shuangxi Bunuo. His secular surname was Xianqing and his courtesy name was Song. The poet Xiyi lamented him in verse, saying:

“To succeed to the Patriarchate in our own generation, His life’s conditions and conduct are worthy of emulation. Throughout his life he remained ever within the Way; Recognizing his ailment, he declined to seek a physician.
His ancient appearance is difficult for a brush to capture; His lofty spirit is unknown to the world. Where shall the clouds of compassion spread? The solitary moon shines on its own.”

"It is fitting," the Master said. Having finished reading it, he took up his brush and replied: "With whom else could my lifelong path of the Way be in accord? You, Xianqing, know me most intimately at heart.
Had I not wished to part from you at this time, I feared I might have missed composing this one poem for my fellow practitioner. He then threw down his brush and sat until he passed away.
Sixty years later, the door of his stupa opened of its own accord; his true countenance was there, solemn and vivid.
A monk asked Chan Master Toudi Tong of Tengtou in Anqing Prefecture, "How was it before Bodhidharma had not yet arrived?
The Master said, "On both banks, monks sing songs. The monk asked, "And after he had arrived? The Master said, "The great ocean surges with wind and waves. [End of] Question.
"What is it like atop a solitary peak? A long-pined pine of steadfast character. The Master said, "It is able to be the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet does not wither with the four seasons.
Question: "What is the Buddha-dharma here in the Master’s place? The Master said, "Striking the west wall from the east wall."

At the request of the authorities, Chan Master Fahai of Chuzhou Prefecture was ordered to convert his temple, Fahai, into a Shenxiao Palace. The Master ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying:
"It is precisely because one has not yet attained thorough penetration that one speaks of right and wrong; it is because of a lack of truth that one distinguishes between 'that' and 'this.
Even my own body does not truly exist—how could anything external to the body suffice as the Way? Viewed with the correct eye, all is one."
This is a source of laughter. Now, with the Sage Ruler bestowing his decree, to convert monasteries into temples of the Shenxiao [Celestial Palace] is like adding a crown atop a Buddha’s head;
when one calculates it, what is there that is improper? This mountain monk today cannot help but shoulder my staff crosswise and hang up my alms bowl;
I shall find refuge and establish my life within the seamless stupa, and beneath the rootless tree, I shall whistle at the moon and chant with the wind.

Let it be left entirely to the immortal guests who ride the clouds and the lofty recluses who drive their cranes, to come here to chant incantations over water, write talismans, and perform rites by clenching their teeth.
In years to come, when they have attained the Way and ascended on white days, they shall be able to repay unrequited kindness and assist in the transformation of non-action.
"I only fear it is not jade; were it jade, it would be truly marvelous. Although this is so, tell me: how shall the mountain monk turn his body?
How do you say it? Do you understand? Having cast down his whisk, he suddenly passed into stillness.
The Prefect submitted a memorial regarding these events, and by imperial decree the temple was restored, with the plaque inscribed "True Body" (Zhen-shen).

On the day Chan Master Ming of Tianning Monastery in汝州 (Ruzhou) was ordained as a *deśaka* (lay practitioner), the Master ascended the seat. Having finished expressing his gratitude for the Imperial Grace, he said:
"The wooden tally is grasped by the hand; the sitting cloth is laid down according to the occasion. Clouds disperse and waters flow away; all is silent, and heaven and earth are empty.
He then closed his eyes and passed away.
A monk asked Zen Master Renwang Qin of Xishu, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Hearing the name is not as good as seeing the face.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A monkey playing in a bamboo grove. The monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "A tiger watching the water mill."

Master Louzi was a man of unknown origins. One day, while wandering through the marketplace, he happened to be adjusting his socks and girdle beneath a wine tavern when he heard a song being sung by someone on the upper floor:
"Since you have no heart, I shall also cease. At this, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and was thus given the name Louzi (Tavern Master).

The Dharma Master Shenzhao Benru once requested further instruction on the essential meaning of the sutras from the Venerable Siming. The Venerable called out in a thunderous voice, "Your name is Benru (Inherently Thus).
The Master suddenly attained awakening and presented this verse: "Everywhere I encounter the path back home; At every turn, I reach my native land."
Originally accomplished and manifest—why must one wait for deliberation?

On the day of the *jiǎzǐ* year of the Jiàyòu era during the Rénzōng reign of the Song dynasty, Chan Master Pǔjué Chún péng of Língyǐn Monastery in Hángzhōu Prefecture was commanded by imperial decree to reclaim the road occupied by Jíqìng Monastery at Jiùlǐsōng.
He ascended the hall and said: "Before the mountain lies a vast expanse of idle field."
The Ground: For vast kalpas past, there has been no boundary; this morning it is restored and returned. Sitting, one cuts off both head and tail;
east is so, west is so—north, south, vertical, and horizontal, all are not otherwise. Yet, how shall one ultimately repay this debt of gratitude?
Ten li of lotus flowers, nine li of pines; before the Hall of Direct Pointing, a single incense stick burns.
At the age of sixteen, Chan Master Yiweng Koguan of Shengshou Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture entered the monastic order under Nanping. Following Chexi, he attained a profound realization.
At the beginning of the Shaoxing era of the Song dynasty’s Gaozong Emperor, he presided over Shengshou in Jiahe and later moved to Dezang in Danghu.

He retired to a bamboo hermitage, where his single room was serene and tranquil. He would often delight himself, saying, "The wind through the pines and the moon over the mountains are my inexhaustible robes and alms bowl.
In the *Xinmao* year of the Qiandao era of Emperor Xiaozong, Chancellor Wei Shu invited him to preside over Beichan Temple in Wu.

On the day he entered the monastery, it happened to be the ninth day of the month; pointing to the seat, he said: "An inch of ash within my breast has long since grown cold; on my head, a thousand strands of snow have fallen."
[The previous] has not yet been digested. An old man’s steps should only suit level ground; I know not for what reason you have climbed so high again.
Chan Master Fojue of Qingzhou (of the Yunmen lineage) offered this verse on the story of Mount Yangshan’s “Snow Lion”:

"A single color, nothing surpasses it for pointing it out to people; Within a world of white silver, he groans and sighs. Transcendently he topples [it], then raises it up again— How can this compare to..."
The eastern wind warms the new sun.
National Teacher Shantong (of the Yunmen school, successor to Fo-jue) was the Buddha-Sun. From Jiangyou he traveled to Yanjing and stayed at Dashing'an Temple.
One night, while conversing with Fo-jue and Huidang, the Master [Shantong] was twelve years old and stood in attendance to the right of their seats. At that time, the Sun—[Fo-jue]—[spoke].
Yangqi said, "I have come from the South, and with this staff of mine, I have never once struck upon a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma.
The Master joined his palms and stepped forward, saying, "It is simply that your staff, Reverend, is too short.
Yangqi was greatly startled and said, "I pray you, let this man continue my Linji lineage. The Master replied, "How could there be two [lineages]—Yunmen and Linji? Yangqi praised him incessantly.
Emperor Jin Shizong visited the Hall of the Auspicious Image at Sheng’an Temple and asked the Master, "Is it right to perform prostrations, or is it right not to?
The Master replied, "To prostrate is to show mutual respect and honor; not to prostrate is for each person to claim their own dignity. The Emperor was greatly pleased.
Later, while residing at Yansheng Temple, he addressed the assembly, citing Dongshan’s discourse upon the conclusion of the retreat: "In early autumn and late summer, brothers may go east or west..."

"Go! You must go directly to the place where there are ten thousand miles of land and not a single blade of grass. He asked again, "As for 'ten thousand miles of land with not a single blade of grass,' how does one go there?
Shishuang said, "Stepping out the door, it is already grass. Dayang said, "Even if you do not step out the door, it is still a vast expanse of grass.
The Master said, "Now tell me, what is the phrase beneath everyone's feet right now?"
How would you say it? If you say, "Ten thousand miles, not a blade of grass," I grant that you have seen Dongshan.

If you say, "Stepping out the door is already grass," I grant that you have seen Shishuang. If you say, "Even not stepping out the door is a vast expanse of grass," [I grant that you have seen Xuefeng].
"I permit you to see the Sun; if you still cannot speak, I permit you to see Yansheng. Why?
Because 'only a fine breeze comes upon the mat, and no idle talk falls to the world. He addressed the assembly, citing the story of Yunmen and Guanyin buying fried cakes.
The Master said, "The old man of Shaoyang may indeed be said to have sung ever more loftily, yet his response has become ever more rare. As it is said:
Now, turning back toward the tip of the whisk at Yansheng, I enter the Fangwang Samādhi:

entering meditative concentration in the east and arising in the four directions, and so on, until entering concentration in a male body and arising in a female body. Do you understand? The wild landscape has no further breaks between mountains.
The heavenly light connects directly with the water.
Imperial Envoy dispatched by Emperor Kinghyeonjong to Zen Master Eon-woo Yum (Yunmen school; successor of Wontong) of Gyeongsu-sa Temple in Seongdeok, Sundeung Commandery.
He took a sheet of paper, wrote the two characters "Mind-Buddha" (xīn fó), and asked the Master, "What kind of characters are these? The Master replied, "Not mind, not Buddha. This pleased him.
The following day, the Emperor bestowed upon him a poem of eleven lines, which said: "If one can thoroughly understand the causes and conditions of all phenomena, what need is there to ask?
In daily life, act without effort; throughout the twelve hours of the day, do not harbor further doubt. One must always [be self-reliant]..."
To perceive that from the beginning there has been no obstruction—though Buddha after Buddha and mind after mind may rely upon the Buddha, such reliance is still a defilement.

The Master replied: "To recognize 'non-action' (wuwei) as being non-action is itself a bondage. When illumination and function are simultaneous, like a flash of lightning or a shooting star, it is already too late.
To call 'neither mind nor Buddha' 'neither mind' is still to remain within the realm of objects. When both person and environment are empty, ten thousand..."
The elephant forest is reflected in a single mirror.
When Master Ding of Gaoyou Prefecture (of the Yunmen school; successor to Xuanwu) first visited Xuanwu, Xuanwu posed the following koan in his room:
A monk asked Xuansha, "What is the pure dharmakāya? Xuansha replied, "It drips with pus. At this, the Master...
There was a realization. A monk asked, "What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? The Master replied, "A dry dung pellet.
The late Head Seat Sushou had spent his life deeply hidden behind a single barrier; few recognized him.

During the Tianli era of the Yuan Mingzong, a monk who had lived with him obtained three *shuhui* (verses on expressing one's inner state) written by his own hand. He traveled to Zituo to seek out Zhu Yuandao.
Zhu Yuan remarked, "In all quarters, people have long regretted that [the Master] did not appear in this world nor preach the Dharma.
Now, having read these three verses, it is as if a great bell has been struck once and all other sounds are silenced. Can one still say he did not preach the Dharma?

The verses are as follows: "The lamp of transmission has been passed; my hair already shows the first signs of gray. My achievements, though vast, still vie with but a few *lakṣas*. Having just risen from my midday nap..."
Dust fills the desk; half a eaves-length of slanting sun sets upon the courtyard flowers. This pointed-roofed hut is not built too low; above it are tall forests, below it lies a pond.
Through the long night, a startling wind sweeps across yellow leaves; one suspects the onset of rain from beneath the reeds. In this floating world, the light of time has already slanted;
I have composed this poem merely to respond to the passing years. Today I am here beneath the tall pines, my back turned—
A few scattered crows stand against the western wind.
At Lohan Temple on Mount Yan in Wenzhou Prefecture, the Head Seat Zheng realized the Way with clarity.
Every morning, he personally swept the grounds. Someone asked him, "Have you swept this patch of ground clean yet? The Head Seat held up his broom to show him.
He asked again, "In the realm of true purity, there has never been a single speck of dust. What is there to sweep? The Master also held up a broom to show him.
He once composed a verse on Mount Jiuniu, which says: "For four or five years they have known how to herd together; Spring comes and autumn goes, satiated by wind and smoke.
The clear stream has water, yet they have no mind to drink; The green fields are unplowed, and they sleep forevermore. Each and every one of them has feet...
His feet tread upon the earth, yet his waist, head, and nostrils all reach toward heaven. Usually he dwells atop the thousand peaks;
when people from all over the world come, they dare not pull him down.
Chan Master Chang of Xuedou in Ningbo Prefecture was a senior disciple of Hengshan; he was illiterate and specialized solely in [Chan practice].

He practiced meditative concentration (*dhyāna*). His peers called him Chang Damo. The verses and hymns he composed were perfect in both principle and phenomena, and their prosody was harmonious and flowing.
One of his hymns on the "Iron Ox" says: "Forged a hundred times in the red furnace, it emerges; Its horns are towering, its body utterly free of dust."
Striking him was of no avail, nor could he be pulled; this time, he truly did not enter the womb. A verse by Haimen says:
"Fierce winds blow up waves like mountains; How many fishermen find it difficult to set foot [therein]? Only by risking one's life and casting away the body can one force one's way in;
Then one knows that the jade door has never been locked. A verse on the bitter bamboo shoots says: "The purple robes are stripped away until white as silver; In the cauldron of a hundred boils..."

One attains a body through this intermediate turning; from this point on, those who labor in earnest will not believe it otherwise. When one casually chews upon it, the flavor is entirely true. Xichan’s verse says:
"Having reached the top of a hundred-foot pole, cease asking for the way. On a solitary peak, at the very summit, nurture a leisurely body.
Although the dilapidated hut has no roof to cover it, It is difficult to speak of one's private possessions to others."
Chan Master Qinggu of Songjiang Prefecture was known as Oyang Beizi. His surname was Jiang. It is uncertain where he was born.

He was well-versed in the classics and histories; his speech was concise and his expressions profound. At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, he arrived in Songjiang and sat in the Yuantao Room (the "Ancient and Perfect" chamber). Thereafter, he would enter the marketplace.
Shen settled upon a meditation cushion and established a hermitage on the ground. His room was vast and open, yet his feet never crossed the threshold.

Someone asked him, "In the *Jin si lu*, it is said that after one attains stability, there is subsequently radiance; is this the Golden Elixir? The Master replied, "Virtuous one, go for now and savor the *Zhongyong*.
He once showed Shen a verse, saying: "The myriad purples and thousands of reds are all spring; Why need one trouble the Lord of the East with further words? Silence!"
"When a person has a dream, to whom do they tell it? They raise an empty fist and point toward the white clouds. He also said: "Neither leaning nor biased, standing in the center;
not clinging to the west, nor clinging to the east. Transcending the emotional and intellectual measures of past and present, one hooks the azure dragon upon the tip of a single hair.
One day, Jin Shen approached him and said, "I have exhausted my journey through transformation. You all must strive with diligence. Having spoken these words, he passed away peacefully.
However, he passed away.
Later, the Great Master Yuanfan Huihong of the Tiele Monastery on Mount Wutai in Taiyuan Prefecture, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, reached the passage:

"When one person gives rise to true awakening and returns to the source, the ten directions of empty space all vanish. At this point, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and subsequently traveled to the Yellow River.
Shuowen was residing there. Chen recounted what he had seen, and Wen approved. As he was nearing death, he spoke a verse, saying: "Sixty years of springtime, plus eight more;
the floating clouds have cleared, revealing the blue sky. As I depart, I shall kick over Mount Sumeru; on the mountain peak in the late night, the moon is perfectly full.
He changed his robes and passed away while sitting upright.
Chan Master Hui-kong Yuan-mo of Mount Jiangshan in Jianning Prefecture was the son of the Su family of Gutian.

In the gengzi year of the Dade era during the reign of Emperor Chengzong of the Yuan dynasty, while in a state of meditative concentration, he traveled to Mount Jiangshan. This mountain had formerly been the site of the Chan master Xuan-jang’s practice hall.
An old man came forward to greet him and said, "I have guarded this mountain for five hundred years. Having finished speaking, he transformed into a black dragon and departed.
Upon waking, he said, "I have often returned to this mountain. He then went to establish a hermitage there.

One day, he said to the assembly, "In the past, in the presence of the Buddha, I was called Bodhisattva Huikong (Wisdom-Emptiness). Now that my karmic conditions for transformation are exhausted, I shall enter nirvana.
Thereupon, he spoke a verse for the assembly, saying: "For over forty years I dwelt amidst the dust of the mundane world; Now, at last, I manifest the Honored One within this very midst. Yantou...
One night an east wind arose, blowing the blossoms open so that spring filled every tree. An iron ship without a rudder and without a sail was steered into the nature-sea of the golden lotus.
This final pivot of the teaching is now revealed: white clouds have never been separate from the vast sky.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth cannot be found anywhere; when the void is struck through, the ultimate reality is revealed.
Even if an iron wheel were to spin upon the crown of one's head, the numinous clarity of one’s original nature remains forever undiminished. He spoke again:

"The third patriarch of India, the Venerable Śāṇakavāsin, dwelt on Mount Gajaśaila and manifested the Dragon-Exertion Samādhi (*nāgavikrīḍita-samādhi*), preaching the Dharma to subdue all non-Buddhists. Thereafter...

He transformed himself into fire and self-immolated. "I shall now do likewise before the Elephant Trunk Rock," he said. Having finished speaking, clouds and mist rose up on all sides and a great storm of thunder and rain broke forth;
he transformed himself into fire and self-immolated. His stupa was erected to the west of the hermitage.
Chan Master Foguang Daowu of Puzhao Monastery in Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, was the son of the Kou family from Lintao in Lanzhou.
While staying overnight at Wanzi Inn, he heard the neighing of a horse and attained a sudden, great awakening. Upon returning home, he told his mother, "I have picked up something on the road.
His mother asked, "What thing? The Master replied, "That which has been unseen since beginningless time. His mother gave him a slap.

He said, "What joy is there in this? He then took leave of his mother to travel in all directions. His mother asked, "Where will you go? The Master replied, "Water flowing must reach the sea; a crane emerges from atop the white clouds. He then went to visit Baiyun Hai, who gave him the seal of approval. In the Jiachen year of the Jin Dading era, he emerged to preside over Puzhao Monastery.

After a long time, he retired to Zhuge Hermitage. In his later years, he lived a life of ease and obscurity in Luochuan. Thus it was said of him: The Master’s name was Zhenjue; his secular surname was Zhao. He was a native of Xianzhou. From childhood, he possessed a spirit that transcended the mundane. At the age of twenty-one, he left home to study under the guidance of Chan Master Daoyuan of Mount Shuangfeng in Xiangzhou. There, he received the full precepts and subsequently traveled to various regions to seek out the dharma. One day, while traveling through the Huai region, he encountered a monk who asked him, "What joy is there in this?

The Master then took leave of his mother to wander in all directions. His mother asked, "Where will you go? The Master replied, "Water flowing must reach the sea; a crane emerges from atop the white clouds. He then went to visit Baiyun Hai, who granted him the seal of transmission. In the Jiachen year of the Jin Dading era, he emerged to preside over Puzhao Monastery. After a long period, he retired to live in seclusion at Zhuge Hermitage. In his later years, he lived a life of drifting and sinking in Luochuan. People...
No one could fathom him. He once said: "If you say I am an ordinary person, I have come from among the ranks of the sages.
If you say I am a sage, I have gone back into the ranks of the ordinary. If you say I am neither ordinary nor a sage, I am instead wandering head-over-heels within your very eyes and nostrils.
On the thirteenth day of the fifth month in the year of Yichou (1205) during the Taihe era of the Jin dynasty, he passed away without illness at the age of... [years].
55. At thirty-nine years of ordination, Chan Master Lai of Jia Mountain in Zhending Prefecture asked, "Where is the stupa of Iron Ox Worthy?
The Master pointed his finger toward it. The monk was suddenly enlightened and uttered this verse: "Iron Ox, Iron Ox! Seek nothing else further. If there is someone..."
When asked a question, he would simply raise a finger.
The Abbot of Kuai-an on Mount Tianmu in Hangzhou Prefecture was a native of Suzhou. By nature quick-witted, he was well-versed in both Buddhist and secular classics.

He was a close friend of Pingshi Di. Dwelling in secluded mountain valleys, he did not associate with the world; there were only a few disciples at the foot of the mountain, such as Hong... [text fragment].
The descendants of the clan came and went to offer ritual provisions. One night, a woman of the Hong family dreamed that a spirit-general arrived in a palanquin;
upon waking, she gave birth to a son. The following morning, she climbed the mountain to await him, but the general had vanished. She therefore named him Yingkui (應魁) and styled him Shiyuan (士元).
In his youth, he studied the classics and was admitted to the local school. When he reached the age of thirty, he suddenly experienced a profound awakening.
He abandoned his home and built a thatched hut on the summit of East Peak, where he practiced the Way with diligent devotion day and night.

One day, while traveling from Mount Jing to his hermitage to avoid bandits, Kōshitsu observed that his deportment was serene and elegant, and his responses were composed and unhurried. Upon questioning him about these qualities, he came to understand [the depth of his realization].
It was said that he was the reincarnation of a certain mountain man. Therefore, [the master] addressed him, saying:
"In your previous life, you were an inseparable friend with the old man of the Flat Stone. This year, the old man is nearly ninety, yet his hearing and sight remain sharp.
Why have you not sent him word? Is it that one dream and two awakenings are seen as being exactly the same? The mountain man, delighted, took up his brush and composed a verse to send to him.
It is said: A message to the old master Pingshi of Tiantong: A single thought is neither now nor of the past.
If you wish to hear the midnight bell of Hanshan, the Wu River remains as ever, its waters merging with the azure sky.
Chan Master Seng’an Si of Lingyun in Wenzhou Prefecture was by nature upright and resolute. A native of Ninghai in Taizhou, he was the eldest of four brothers.
They all simultaneously resolved to leave the household life and traveled extensively to seek instruction from various masters. Later, the Master emerged into the world at Lingyun.

Next, he moved to Lingyan. During the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "The Great Perfect Enlightenment—ox-horns and horse-horns—are my monastery’s melon-basket, gourd-basket, and vegetable-basket.
He then ascended the hall and presented the story of Zhaozhou’s "The dog has no Buddha-nature," offering this verse:
"The dog has no Buddha-nature; The dog has Buddha-nature. The monkey worries, scratching its head; The dog runs, shaking its mouth. In the evening...
In the year [of the cyclical cycle], he retired to the mountain in front of Lingyun. In the Jia-shen year of the Yuan Zhi-zheng era, Kongshi Tong went with several monks to pay him a visit.
At that time, the Master was already ninety years old; with bushy eyebrows and white hair, he came out dragging his sandals, walking as he asked, "Where have you come from?
Tong replied, "From the heart of the river. The Master said, "How many fathoms deep is it? Tong replied, "You cannot deceive an old monk like me."
The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea. On the wall hung a poem cursing a monk, its style closely resembling the verses of Hanshan:
"The Five Pestilences do not strike his head, yet he has shaved it bald; A yellow cloth covers his body, and that is what makes him a monk.

He understands neither the Buddha-dharma nor the worldly dharma; Eating pigs and eating dogs—he is quite capable of it. Having read it through entirely, [the visitor] was struck with awe. Shortly thereafter, he took his leave and did not dare [to remain].
He once again encountered that sharp edge.
The attendant Yuwang Mian of Ningbo Prefecture was a distant cousin of Kongshi. A youth with great aspirations, he was unfortunately cut short by an untimely death.
He once composed a verse for a fellow monk traveling to Mount Tiantai and Mount Yan, which began: "The bird’s nest blew the cloth-hair; the attendant..."
He immediately attained awakening. Although it did not involve verbal explanations, it had already become a public proclamation: "The clouds atop Mount Tiantai; the trees within Mount Yandang.
Hereafter, let us deliberate well; do not touch upon the taboo that stands before one.
His verse at the time of death says: "Birth is fundamentally not born; death likewise is not dead. Bimi holding his staff; Jueyi pointing upward."
Upon hearing the crowing of a cock, Chan Master Yongning Guyuanqing of Jiangning Prefecture attained awakening. He composed a verse, saying:
"The golden rooster crows aloud as dawn breaks; Were it not for its sound, how could one know? The three-thousandfold world-system is entirely like snow;
A mud-snake at the bottom of the well dances the *zhèzhī*."
The Verse Sent by Chief Seat Xuan-an Shi of Yuyang Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture to Master Wo-yun: Horses gallop together within the Golden Garden;

A mere inch often gives rise to suspicion that one is clutching a sword. When the moon shines upon a thousand trees of plum blossoms like snow, It is the moment one returns from a dream upon the pillow of the Cloud-Reclining.
A verse by the Chief Seat Huàn’ān of Tiāntóng Monastery in Níngbō Prefecture, paying respects at the ancestral pagoda of Yìng’ān:

"A majestic slumbering tiger; though one glimpses its markings through a tube, One takes Zhōngfēng as a mountain to lean upon. Without even a single broken sand bowl, It would be difficult for descendants to seek their livelihood."
The West Hall Abbot Mozhong Weixi of Tiantong Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture composed a verse on silkworms, which says: "The mulberry trees are empty and the *zhè* trees are exhausted;

only then does the mind rest. Through the subtle and dense process of practice, all is gathered into a single cocoon. Even if one must enter the glowing embers and the boiling cauldron, for the sake of others, it depends upon that single thread."
The verse "Listening to the Rain" by Chan Master Fulong Ke of Yixing, Changzhou Prefecture, says: "Drops dripping from the eaves are perfectly clear;

Sentient beings, deluded of themselves, call them 'sound. I too have spent many years chasing after external things; Through the consecutive nights, leaning on my pillow, sleep has been hard to attain."
The verse of the passing of the Head Seat Shou of Jiufeng in Ruizhou Prefecture says: Seventy-two years, here and there;
I have long been accustomed to eating the food of the ten directions, Without studying the Chan of Bodhidharma. This morning, with one cast, I turn my body and depart;
My laughter shatters the half-smile of the onlookers.
Chan Master Baiyun Mingxing of Wugong Mountain in Jixian Prefecture was a native of the Zhang family of Changting in Min.

Having set his heart upon the inner scriptures, he followed Longgui Tong to tonsure his head and receive full ordination. He specialized in the cultivation of *śamatha-vipaśyanā* (calm abiding and insight).

One day, he sighed to himself, saying, "A man of great purpose, yet my path of the Dharma remains unaccomplished; what shall I do with birth and death? Thereupon, he resolved to travel to various quarters to seek instruction, visiting renowned masters everywhere.
When the karmic conditions were ripe, the Master was startled; he could not bring himself to say, "Is the Way truly like this?

He then went to see Kuanglu Benyuan and presented his insights, but Benyuan would not grant him approval. The Master became despondent, neglecting both sleep and food. Later, hearing of Panlong Yang, he went there to seek resolution.
Upon seeing him, his lingering doubts and obstructions were suddenly dispelled. He remained there for a long time, until Yang transmitted the lineage of the robe and whisk to him.

He was entrusted with this and lived in seclusion at Mount Xiao for over twenty years. The Prefect invited him to emerge from retreat and take charge of a monastery, but the Master firmly declined on account of his old age.

He moved once more to a remote thatched hut; after a long time, it too became a magnificent temple. One day, manifesting a slight illness, he gathered the assembly and expressed his gratitude, saying, "I am departing.
The assembly asked, "Where will the Master go? The Master showed them a verse, which began: "The bright moon falls into the heart of the waves. White..."

"Clouds span across the mountain ridges; if you wish to recognize the mechanism of coming and going, it is like an iron ox swallowing a great elephant. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain. He was eighty-four years of age.

When Chan Master Deng of Changlu in Yangzhou Prefecture had completed the renovation of the monastery buildings, he dreamed one night that a divine being requested to serve as the local guardian deity (tudi).
The Master said to the divine being, "You seem fond of seeing the faults of monks; I fear I cannot grant your request. The divine being replied:

He made a solemn vow and eventually severed one of his arms, placing it before the master. Moved by his sincerity, the master granted his request. The following day, he proceeded to construct the shrine and commission the statues;
however, once the image of the local deity (Tunchi) was completed, the missing arm repeatedly fell off, and no matter how often it was repaired, it could not be restored.
To this day, the local deity still lacks one arm.

The Chan Master Ta-liu of Sichuan was so named because he had a goiter on his neck. He once lamented that the Buddha-dharma was becoming muddled and that heterodox views were arising like swarms of bees.
He then said, "I have attained realization through the study of Chan; I shall no longer spare my verbal karma. Thereupon, he devoted himself single-mindedly to prostrating at the stupa of Mazu.
After a long time, the stupa suddenly emitted light, and he attained great enlightenment. From then on, wherever he went, he made it his business to test and examine others. As he passed by...
Xuedou said, "This old fellow has his mouth dripping with water. Xuedou asked, "Do you not approve of me, monk?
The Master replied, "Indeed, your mouth is dripping with water. He then struck him once with his sitting cloth and departed.
The temple steward, feeling resentful, pursued him halfway and injured the Master's foot. The Master said, "This was brought about by that old fellow himself. In days to come..."

"You must break off one leg to repay me," he said. Duoguo followed these words exactly. Later, while the Master was wandering through the market stalls in the capital, an official invited him to stay at his home with great respect.
He would frequently have an ugly concubine serve the Master food. When the Master declined, the official became even more reverent.

One day, when the official arrived, the Master intentionally flirted with the concubine, thereby managing to take his leave. Not long after, he passed away while sitting in meditation amidst the bustling marketplace.
Chan Master Fachai of Changqing in Shangyu, Shaoxing Prefecture, usually sat in meditation within a single room.

Scholars and officials delighted in visiting him to engage in profound discussions on the principles of the Nameless. At the beginning of the JiaTai era, he suddenly declined visitors and closed his door.

One day, during the height of the summer heat, after bathing and changing his robes, he sat upright and passed away. His disciples cried out in urgency, "Since the Master has reached such a state, why..."

After leaving behind these verses as an instruction for posterity, the Master said: "Since beginningless kalpas, nothing has ever been born; today, on this very stage, who is there to be extinguished? Who is there to be extinguished?
White snow flies through a scorching blue sky ten thousand leagues away. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Chan Master Daoxuan Jue of Tanzhe in Shuntian Prefecture was styled Songxi. He was the son of the Nan family of Fufeng.

His mother dreamed that the Dharma Master Tan bestowed upon her a jade image, which she swallowed and subsequently conceived. On that very day, Tan had passed away. From birth, he possessed extraordinary qualities;

he delighted in sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*). During the Mongol military incursions, he was captured and taken to Wuchuan. The military commander was pleased with him and ordered his ordination as a monk.

He went to Qingshan Temple on Mount Gui to shave his head and receive the precepts. He traveled between lecture halls with great renown; however, he realized that while he preached, food rarely filled his belly.
Thereupon, he hurried to see Shengyin, who asked him, "What have you come here for? The Master replied, "The matter of birth and death is great.

Shengyin said, "Since I recognized the path of Caoxi, I have known that birth and death are not concerned with me. How do you understand this? As the Master was about to deliberate upon it, Shengyin gave a shout.
The Master hurried out. Yinyuan then summoned the Head Seat; the Master turned his head back, and Yinyuan said, "Receive this clearly. At that moment, the Master was suddenly enlightened.

The next day, he informed Yinyuan, saying, "Yesterday, upon receiving your shout, I have attained a point of realization. Yinyuan said, "Try to express it. The Master shook his sleeves and went out. Yinyuan approved of this.
In the first year of the Xianzong era, the Magistrate of Fenshan sent a letter to Shengyin, requesting him to serve as abbot.

Regarding "Spiritual Mountain" (Lingshan): because the Master responded to this command, he entrusted him with a verse, saying: "For ten years your will was like iron; The profound barrier has been thoroughly penetrated.
Leaping out from the thicket of thorns, You have trodden through the moon upon the clear pool. It is well for you to travel now upon the summit of the solitary peak."

The Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past all transcended [this world]. In the Guiwei year of the Zhiyuan era, when Hui-tan of Longquan Temple at Tanzha retired to the West Hall, the Master was appointed to fill his seat.
Later, he passed away while seated in meditation; his stupa was erected on the mountain itself.
Chan Master Fuyan of Tanzhe Guyuan in Shuntian Prefecture was granted the honorary title Foxing Puming. A native of the Li family of Taiyuan, his grandfather held official rank.
From childhood, the Master delighted in studying Buddhism; his parents sent him to Miaojue, from whom he received the tonsure under Lang.
During the Xingding era, he took refuge from the chaos in mountain valleys. Later, he went to Xiniu in Zhending to attend upon Kuòlè Yī, serving in the Directorate of Attendants.

Subsequently, he attended upon Yuánmíng Zhào. Zhào cited a monk’s question to Yúnmén: “What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and tapping? Yúnmén replied: [“The hen has already broken the shell.”]
Xiang said, "How do you understand this? The Master replied, "Today I have thoroughly received the Master’s one question.
Xiang asked, "What is its meaning? The Master said, "Where all voices harmonize as one, the intent is clear for a thousand ages.
Zhaojie then went to see Kuole. Kuole said, "Have you come? Speak a single phrase at the point of intimacy. The Master stepped forward and said, "On this day, I respectfully wish the Master..."
I hope you are enjoying excellent health. [The Master] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master replied, "A mouth full of teeth, all bone; two ears, mere skin. Yueze said, "When did you ever see the Perfectly Bright One?
The Master instead asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Yueze shouted. As the Master hesitated, Yueze struck him, saying, "A mouth full of teeth, all bone; two ears..."

Upon hearing the words "two pieces of skin," the Master attained great enlightenment; Layi was pleased and granted him formal certification (*inka*). He subsequently appeared in the world, moving through three major monasteries, his reputation being highly esteemed throughout all quarters.
Haiyun once praised him with the utmost effusion. During the Zhizhi era of the Yuan dynasty, he passed away while seated in meditation. His stupa was erected at Tanzhe.
Chan Master Daoheng of Taigu Monastery in Suzhou Prefecture, whose courtesy name was Qingyin, claimed his secular surname was Yang.

At the end of the Song dynasty, he brought a macaque from Jinling to the Songjiang area; it was as large as a human and could perform various services for him. When the Master sat in meditation at night, there was light, and the people of Songjiang vied with one another to offer him food.
Whether the offerings were abundant or meager, he did not express gratitude, saying only, "It is fixed by destiny. People marveled at this and associated with him.
He constructed a hermitage to receive guests. The Master went barefoot into the marketplace to beg for rice on behalf of the assembly;
thus he was also known as the "Barefoot Immortal. Once, when soldiers were playfully roasting a monkey, the Master sighed deeply. Consequently, he took his leave of the assembly and spoke this verse:
"For eighty-one years I have been loquacious, Day after day, never ceasing to seek alms. On this Double Ninth festival, I return home; Along the way, there is only pure wind and bright moon."
He then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
Chan Master Xiaoshan Yuanliang of Baoding, in [blank] Prefecture, was the son of the Xiao family of Xinyang in Henan.

From childhood, he abstained from meat. Because his father held office in Tang, he settled there. Having gone to Baolin, he encountered Fuyou Dao, from whom he received the tonsure. Fuyou instructed him...

Through the essentials of dhyāna, he attained realization. He was then directed to visit the Guyu Valley in Guyu. Upon entering the inner chamber for instruction, his mind and the Master’s were like a needle meeting its eye.

In the Renzi year of the Hongwu era, he returned to Tang to establish Baoding Monastery; subsequently, by imperial decree, he resided at Ba’en and later at Daci. Imperial edicts were repeatedly bestowed upon him.

He earnestly requested to retire, and was consequently granted leave to return to the mountains. Previously, while serving as a Prince of Shu, he had also been invited to preach the Dharma within the inner court.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "How could a turtle ever escape from the jar? A shrimp’s leap never goes beyond the measure.

If one lacks a firm resolve for leaving the world, one will wander in vain through the cycles of the six realms. Brothers, you have now entered a mountain of jewels; is there anything therein that is not empty?"
As for those who return with their hands [empty], even if such exist, they must receive three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening.

On the thirteenth day of the tenth month of the Gengshen year, the sky was clear and cloudless; at noon, thunder suddenly shook the heavens three times, and three circles of light appeared in the void.
Thereupon, he passed away. Upon cremation, the *śarīra* relics fell like pouring rain.
Chan Master Bianrong Zhenyuan of Dajian Fosi in Shuntianfu was the son of the Xian family of Xinyang, Yingzhou, in Western Sichuan.

His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations; he could not forget anything once it passed his eyes, whether in writing or history. His kinsmen said, "This son will surely be the one who revives our clan."
When he reached the age of nearly thirty, moved by the impermanence of birth and death, he left his home and entered Yunhuashan.
There he paid homage to Master Ke as his teacher, shaved his head, and received the precepts. Upon arriving at the capital, he listened to lectures on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

When he reached the passage, "If one wishes to know the realm of the Buddha, one should purify the mind so that it is like empty space," he suddenly attained sudden enlightenment; his body transcended into empty space, and he was no longer conscious of the house as an obstruction.
I said to him: "The profound mystery of the Dharma-realm and the ocean of the nature of Vairocana do not lie beyond my own heart-mind.
Furthermore, tell me: apart from words, who can expound and who can listen? A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger; these words are indeed true.

The following day, he took up his staff and traveled eastward. Upon reaching Hongzhou, he resided at Mazu’s hermitage. At that time, those of like mind came to seek him out one after another. Seven... [years passed].
Zai then entered Mount Kuanglu, where he personally sold firewood to exchange for rice to provide for the assembly. For more than twenty years, he did not avoid wind, rain, cold, or heat.

While residing at Lion Rock (Shiziyan), he would often sit cross-legged with a staff across his lap at the mouth of the cliff; whenever a monk approached, he would strike them with the staff as soon as they arrived.
Alas, there was no one who could grasp his essential teaching. He entered the capital four times in total; first he resided at Longhua, and next...
He resided at Bailing Monastery. Later, he moved to Shichaha. Finally, Empress Dowager Cisheng established the Qianfo Conglin monastery and invited the Master to reside there.
Once, while the Master was lecturing on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* at Gaori Temple, a mad monk offended the Grand Chancellor and was imprisoned;

consequently, the Master was arrested along with him and brought before the cangue. As the Master recited the names of the Great Sūtra, the iron shackles and the wooden cangue were suddenly shattered into pieces.

The prison walls were torn asunder; all the people were moved by this marvel and followed one another in taking refuge [in the Dharma], so that within the circular gates there was nothing but the vast sound of the Buddha’s voice.

Within the prison of the Ministry of Justice, he faced ten thousand forms of suffering and oppression, yet the Master remained composed and at ease. Those undergoing punishment together with him were astonished by his extraordinary character.
The Master said: "There is no other method. If the mind abides in centrality and uprightness, then even while dwelling in hardship and calamity, one is unaware of such hardship and calamity.
Zhang Deyue submitted a memorial clarifying that the Master was innocent and was thus spared from punishment. Empress Cisheng ordered him to return to his residence at Shijia Hai.
Lu Wutai asked, "What is the wisdom of Mañjuśrī? The Master replied, "Not following external objects with the mind. He asked again:
"What is the practice of Samantabhadra? The Master said, "To harmonize all minds. "What is the Dharma-realm of Vairocana?
The Master said, "The non-obstruction of all phenomena. Lu sighed and said, "From this day forward, I understand that though things are myriad, they are of one essence.
Zhao Dazhou asked, "How does Confucius compare to the Buddha? The Master said, "Zhongni was a sage who governed the world."
The Buddha is indeed a sage who governs the world-transcending realm. In punishing evil and encouraging good, his principle is truly no different [from that of the sages].

When he analyzed the profound and subtle mysteries, the Buddhist school was only then fully exhausted [in its exposition]. At that time, Governor Zhou nodded in approval. In the ninth month of the Jia-shen year of the Wanli era of Emperor Ming Shenzong, the Master ordered the coffin to be sent without delay.
Just then, a solitary wild goose alighted at the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, "Have you come? On the ninth day...
He was still sitting on his corded meditation bench when he heard the evening recitation of the verses on aspiring for rebirth in the Western Paradise. Thereupon, he passed away peacefully.
He was seventy-nine years of age and fifty years since his ordination. His entire body was interred at the Universal Common Stupa outside Desheng Gate.
Chan Master Wunian Shen of Huangbo in Wuchang Prefecture was the son of the Xiong family from Macheng in Huangzhou.

While traveling to Mount Dangshan, an elderly monk said to him, "A single grain of rice from the ten directions is as heavy as Mount Sumeru; if you do not realize the Way, you shall return wearing fur and horns. The Master was struck with awe.
Later, he heard a monk cite a question asked of Daixiu: "What is it like? Daixiu replied, "It is like a man carrying a load of bricks on his head. The Master was further enlightened.

"What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? Xiu replied, "Yellow gourd, eggplant. The Master was greatly perplexed; he subsequently traveled to Mount Wutai and Mount Funiu, visiting various masters everywhere.
Upon reaching Mount Lu, he went to study under Da'an. An asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Wunian (No-Thought)."
An said, "Which one is non-thought? The Master was at a loss and had no reply. One night, hearing the sounds of laughter and weeping mingling together, he attained realization.
On another day, while opening a chest, he lost his balance and struck his head against the lid;
as sweat poured from his entire body, he clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "The whole earth is this very non-thought—what room for doubt? He then went to Longhu, where he stayed with Zhuo.
When I, the layman, arrived at Sima Mountain, a lecturer was present there. The layman asked the lecturer, "The fundamental nature is pure and still;

how did the mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? After the lecturer finished his exposition according to the text, the layman looked toward the Master and said, "You try to explain this.
As the Master was about to open his mouth, the layman gave him a push on the knee and said, "What about this? At that moment, the Master suddenly attained great awakening.
Wu (Awakening) spoke in verse: "For over forty years I did not rest in my practice; I exhausted it and exhausted it until no trace remained.

Now, having exhausted it to the point of having nothing to rely upon, I finally regret the effort I previously misapplied. Later, when he was staying [at a monastery], a monk asked him: "Does the Way have a fruit?"

"Is the fruit non-existent? The Master said, "To say it exists or to say it does not exist—both constitute slander. [The student] asked, "How then can one attain it? The Master said, "Seek nothing, and you will attain it.
[The student] asked, "What is the essence of the Way? The Master said, "It fills the mouth, yet words do not reach it.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when the four elements disperse? The Master held up his fist and said, "This does not belong to the four elements. A questioner asked, "The Ancients..."
The man said, "Expel [the obstruction from] your throat and lips; bring forth a single phrase. The Master asked, "How would you speak this one phrase?
The monk replied, "I have not expelled [the obstruction from] my throat and lips; you, first, try to speak a phrase. The monk had no response. The Master said:
“You have your mouth stuffed with sounds. [The student] asked, “Is it true that seeing one’s nature is attaining Buddhahood?
The Master said, “Yes. [The student] said, “Nature is formless; how can it be seen? The Master said, “Nature has form; you simply do not see it.
[The student] said, “Please, Master, point it out for me. The Master said, “I am telling you that you do not see it. [The student] asked, “How does one transcend birth?”
[The Master] died. He summoned the monks; the monks responded with "Yes. The Master said, "Come forth from here! [A monk] said, "I do not understand the words spoken by the Master.
The Master said, "When you do understand them, what would that avail? He further wrote in a letter to a friend:
The essential point of studying the Way is to seize the moment while the initial resolve is still sharp and vigorous, seeking immediate clarity and understanding.

Only when you can achieve liberation amidst the conditions and circumstances encountered during the day will it truly count; otherwise, as days and months pass, your diligence will gradually fade, and you will once again drift into worldly attachments.
Nowadays, students merely seek cleverness of speech and rely on their own intellectual acumen and cleverness, thereby forgetting [the true purpose].
This is the fundamental portion. When a terminal illness approaches the body, one’s hands and feet fall into a frantic turmoil; not even a single bit of [worldly effort] can be of use.

Yet, one refuses to blame one's own thoughts and lacks the resolve to apply oneself earnestly. Instead, one blames the ancient sages and Buddhas for the error. This is merely such slander against the True Dharma Wheel;
one has not yet awakened from one's own dream. Do not misunderstand this! As for those ancient sages...
A single word or half a phrase is like a hair-cutting sword, iron-nail rice, wooden-shavings soup, or a poison-smeared drum.
There is truly no place for you to prick up your ears, no place for you to take a bite, no place for you to apply your intent, and no place for you to draw near.
The moment you blink, you have already missed it. A true student of the Way must, during their practice, ensure that emotions are withered and thoughts are extinguished. Contemplate this.
Exhausting his spirit to its limit, he forgot both cold and heat, and neglected both sleep and food. In a state where nothing could be grasped or conceived, he suddenly attained a profound awakening;
the mind that had previously been driven by seeking was instantly stilled, all intellectual views vanished, and the traces of right and wrong were obliterated.
Upon reaching this stage, one naturally experiences joy and liberation. From then on, one never again follows after sounds or pursues forms.

Whatever intellectual understanding, capacities, or spiritual powers one possesses are surrendered to others; one is willing to remain for the rest of one's days as if dull-witted or like a simpleton.
To empty the belly and leave the mind at ease—throughout the world none can know it, and even ghosts and spirits cannot peer into it;
even that dark-faced Old Man Yan has no place to fix his gaze. This is precisely the true freedom of one who studies the Way.
The Great Master Yunqi Lianchi Zhuhong was a native of the Shen clan of Renhe in the prefecture of Hangzhou. At the age of seventeen, he enrolled in the local school (*xiang*).

He would always inscribe the four characters "the matter of birth and death" (*shengsi shi da*) upon his desk. One day, while handling a tea bowl, he dropped it and it shattered; at that moment, he attained a profound realization.

He recorded this experience with seven strokes of a brush to manifest his resolve. He then went to Mount Xishan to receive the tonsure from Master Xingtian and traveled north to seek further instruction.
Byeon-yong next visited Soran at Yulgang to seek instruction. Soran said, "You have come from three thousand *li* away to ask me for instruction.

What instruction do I have to give you? The Master was suddenly enlightened. He took his leave and returned home. While traveling on the road through Dongchang, he heard the sound of the watchtower drum and attained a vast, sudden enlightenment.
He composed a verse: "The matters of thirty years ago are questionable; The matters of thirty years later are doubtful."

What marvel is there in meeting someone a thousand *li* away? Burning incense and casting down a halberd are but trivial matters. Demons and Buddhas vainly contend over right and wrong. He returned to Zhejiang and established his banner at Yunqi.
When Minister Wang Zongmu asked, "Last night the mice were chirping; they recited the entire Avatamsaka Sutra," the Master said, "When the cat suddenly pounces out, what then?

Wang was speechless. The Master provided this on his own behalf: "Where the mouse goes, the cat follows; Where the cat goes, the mouse flees. The two do not meet for a thousand years; How could they ever know the meaning of the Avatamsaka?"
He said, "The Dharma Master has fled, leaving behind his lecture desk. He then recited this verse: "The mouse squeaks; the *Avataṃsaka* is clearly manifest. How extraordinary!
Official Wang, you have been deluded by a beast. A cat suddenly darts out before the painted hall;
at the head of the couch, the preaching of the Dharma leaves no trace. Yet there is a trace: the *Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra*, Chapter One, 'The Sublime Array of Worldly Rulers.'"

1. During a famine and pestilence, the roads were filled with those who had perished from hunger. The authorities released state granaries to provide relief and ordered physicians to offer medical aid.

The Master was appointed to oversee these matters. The Ministry Official Yu Chunxi recounted the story of Huiri’s treatment of five hundred ill monks and requested the Master to pass judgment upon it.
The Master took up the case and said: "Huiri accepted his own lot; the destitute son abandoned himself to follow another."
The Western Monastery. You have unjustly oppressed the common people, leading them from life to death. It is a pity that five hundred monks merely understand how to nod their heads and comply;
not a single one has remained aloof and refused to rise. This has caused the "Sun of Wisdom" to manifest strange wonders to delude the masses, bringing calamity upon your descendants.
Your Honor, you have deeply felt the sores of the people; this mountain monk hastened in haste due to the urgency of the moment. In the midst of this confusion, I lost my bamboo staff.
Staff-bearer! You cannot avoid brandishing empty fists. Upon the abscess of this layman, I strike the earth with one blow.
I dare guarantee that the chronic ailment will burst open, the poisonous blood will flow freely, the six pulses will harmonize, and the hundred limbs will relax and expand.
Even so, how can one person cause the multitude to arise? Have you not heard it said: "When a single leaf turns back toward the sun, spring fills the thousand forests"? This is the matter.
Let us set that aside for a moment. Suppose you were to hold a bamboo staff all day long, pointing east and waving it west;

this would not be as good as remaining constantly with a piece of wood, holding it in the morning and guarding it in the evening. Through this constant guarding, suddenly the withered wood will bloom again—this is the resurrection of the dead.
Forget about bamboo and wood; you can take it for granted that every blade of grass, tree, and forest throughout the entire world will all attain Buddhahood.
He departs. Why? For the essence of the empty void beyond the green and blue world is precisely the Tathāgata’s solid and real mind.
Question: Can the practice of *chan* (meditation) and the recitation of the Buddha's name be harmonized? The Master said: "If these were two separate things, one could speak of their harmonization.

[The Master] cited the World-Honored One remaining silent for a long while; the non-Buddhist [Māluṅkyaputta] said, "He has cleared away the clouds of my delusion," and Subhūti sat in quiet contemplation.
He did not speak. Śakra said, “You have well spoken these words on Prajñā. [The Master] held up his staff and said: “At the place where all is silent for a long time, one hopes to dispel delusion;

yet the gloom extends for ten thousand *li*. While sitting quietly at the side of the seat, one intends to hear the teaching of Prajñā, but much time passes. Nevertheless, by striking the horse’s head, one attains the essential meaning.”

The monk was at a loss. Again, a monk asked, "Where is the Great Being now? The Master said, "Setting aside the Great Being for a moment, where are you, Senior Monk, right now?

He said, "Come, please let the Master raise his foot to show me. Hao bowed in thanks. The Master showed him with a verse, saying: "A Zen practitioner asks for my old traveling gear;

The inexhaustible treasury of the Dharma radiates light from this source; [the Emperor] was greatly delighted and thus turned his attention toward it.

Direct and straightforward! This is indeed so. It is simply that no one can take your place in making the effort; you must still exert yourself for yourself. Do not fail the original aspiration of your study of the Way;

only by ultimately becoming a heroic and resolute man will you succeed. Throughout my life, I have composed many verses and gāthās on the picking up and commenting of cases (niansong), yet I did not allow any drafts to remain.
If anyone had privately recorded them, I would see them and burn them immediately. Written in the summer of the Jiachen year.
Suffering from a slight ailment, he said to the assembly, "This dream-like and illusory body will not endure for long; it shall ultimately return to extinction.

Initially, he visited Kouxie Yong at Tianning Temple; subsequently, he studied under Fangshan Bao. The master and disciple reached a state of mutual resonance, and he thereafter planted his staff [to remain there].
He resided atop Yunfeng Peak for fifty years, his shadow never leaving the mountain. On the eighth day of the second month in the Jiyou year of the Hongwu era, he manifested a slight ailment.

When the night was nearly half over, he looked to those around him and asked, "Is the sky beginning to brighten? They replied, "Not yet. Someone asked, "At such a moment as this, what do you intend to do, Master?
The Master broke into a smile and said, "Formerly, when Deshan was sitting in illness, a monk asked him, 'Is there still... [The text here ends abruptly].

At the beginning of the Wanli era, he visited Daqian again at Shaolin. One day, he requested further instruction from Daqian, who said: "Nine..."
"Facing the wall for years—was he sitting? Or was he not sitting? Qian said, "To say 'sitting' or 'not sitting' is talk of two extremes.

"All dharmas are fundamentally without coming or going; what is there to transition? Upon hearing this, the Master attained realization. He lived in seclusion on Mount Tai, where he received Manjusri’s empowerment by being touched on the crown of his head and granted a prophecy.

He then experienced a sudden and great awakening. His reputation for the Way became so eminent that it reached the point where a fierce tiger led him along the path and a Bodhisattva brought him a lamp.

Chan Master Fanyan Fangtan of Yifeng at Baima Temple in Kuizhou was the son of the Luo family of Dazhou.
He studied under Yun’an of Jinfoshan, who instructed him to contemplate: "What is the mechanism that ghosts and spirits cannot perceive? After three years, he attained realization.

One day at noon while cooking, he heard the sound of the steamer (*zeng*) and attained great enlightenment, composing a verse: "The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials have no origin; Exhausting all ingenuity, they are nowhere to be found.
Suddenly, with one sound—what was it that acted? White clouds and blue peaks nod their heads in unison. Nodding in unison! Nan Yue and Tiantai lose ground by one."
Chou said again: "When a maiden of sixteen marries her new husband, she spins hemp and twists thread just as usual;

One day, while pointing to a diagram of the Dharma-realm, he asked his teacher, "The ten realms arise from the mind; from where does the mind arise? The teacher was unable to answer.
At that time, Yifeng was building a hermitage on Mount Qingping. The master went there to consult him regarding the previous question. Yifeng said:
"You must understand this: it can only be attained through wondrous awakening. He then had him contemplate the word "Exposed" (Lù) from Yunmen.

Shu: The Master then took his ritual implements to Yunqi. Next, he visited Wuhuan and lived alone at Mount Fahu, where he observed the *śīla* (ascetic practice) beneath Baiyun Peak for ten years.
While consulting with the Dharma Master Liang regarding the karmic conditions concerning Mazu, he had not yet reached a resolution.

How could it stop at merely "falling into a trap with the whole body"? Nevertheless, though you seek him, you cannot find him. Yet, walking together and sitting together, his eyebrows remain only above his eyes;
a steamed bun is certainly made of flour. Even if you were to grasp it intimately, you would already have missed it face-to-face.
I tell you all my brothers in all sincerity: when the mud is thick, the Buddha is naturally large. If you wish to know further—how?
"Look at this old monk. [The Master] descended from his seat. Addressing the assembly at the Ordination Platform: "Virtuous ones, what is the precept? Who is it that receives it?

These constitute the path of concentration and the path of liberation; apart from the mind, there is no other "active" or "unmanifested" [action] to be found.
Venerable sirs, it is truly difficult for a blind tortoise to encounter a floating log; you should conceive of this as a rare opportunity and give rise to a heart of joy.
